πότνια.definition: poet.title of honour, used chiefly in; as Subst., = , mistress, queen , h.Cer.203: mostly c. gen., queen of wild beasts, of Artemis, Il.21.470; Pi.P.4.213; of Aphrodite, E.Fr.781.16 ; Arat.112, Call.Fr.anon.338: witho…

πότος.definition: drinking-bout, carousal, . . . .; Cratin.187; X.An.7.3.26; Theoc.14.17; over the wine, X.An.2.3.15, Smp.8.41; . . Pl.Prt.347c; Id.Smp.176a: pl., Ar.Nu.1073; Isoc.1.32, cf. Aeschin.2.47; Lys.16.11, cf. Pl.R.329a, Isoc.…

πουλβῖνον.definition: = Lat. pulvinus, cushion, bolster, Sammelb. 1.10 , dub.l. in Arr.Epict.3.23.35: also Dim. prob. in Gloss

πουλυβότειρα.definition: metri gr. for Hom. and Hes.; so all other compds. with may be lengthd. in hexameter verse to metri gr., v. however uses the licence only in this word, in the gen. sg. of and in the pr. n

πούς.definition: foot as that with which one runs, Il.1.215, al.; or walks, 8.443; freq. with reference to swiftness, . . Od.8.103; to race on foot, Il.13.325, cf. 23.792; 20.410, cf. Od.13.261; Il.9.124, etc.; Pi.O.12.15, 13.36, P.10…

πούστακος.definition: sine expl., Ar.Byz. ap. Hsch. s.v

πρᾶγμα.definition: Ion. Schwyzer 688 B16, C5; thing, concrete reality, Epich.171.1; opp. Pl.Cra.391b, 436a, And.4.27; . . . Pl.Cra.432b; c. inf., Ar.Pl.1; . . Arist.de An.432a3, cf. Mete.379a32, Ph.226b30, 227b28; Plu.2.1109d, cf. 1112d…

πρᾶγος.definition: poet. for Pi.N.3.6, Fr.108; = state-affairs, A.Th.2

πραιπόσιτος.definition: = Lat. praepositus, a military title, PCair.Preis.33.2 , etc.: hence PAmh.2.140.1 ; PLips.111.16

πραιτωρίδιον.definition: Dim. of sq., small house, Arr.Epict.3.22.47

πραιτώριον.definition: = Lat. Praetorium, official residence; praetorian guard: = praefectus praetorio, OGI707 , IG14.911, etc

Πράμνειος οἶνος.definition: Pramnian wine, Il.11.639, Od.10.235; also Hp.Mul.1.52, Ar.Eq.107, Fr.317. Phryn. Com.65; Ephipp.28 ; raisin-wine, Dsc.5.6

πράμνημα.definition: shoot of the Pramnian vine, Poll.7.150

πράξιμος.definition: of money, recoverable, Plb.21.43.17; practical aims, . . Supp.Epigr.6.802

πρᾶος.definition: of things, H.Hom.8.10; Pi.P.4.136; mild, Hp.l.c.; Id.Art.69; of sound, soft, gentle, X.Smp.1.10; AP6.349 ; ib.244 ; ib.229

πραότης.definition: mildness, gentleness, Th.4.108, Lys.6.34, Isoc.3.55, Pl.R.558a, etc.; opp. Id.Smp.197d; opp. Arist.EN1125b26; opp. Id.Rh.1380a6: pl., Isoc.5.116: later LXXPs.44.4, Ep.Gal.5.23 , CIG2788

Πραράτιος.definition: name of month at Epidaurus, IG42.105.10, 108.141, al.; once written ib.106.107: cf

πράσιος.definition: = Pl.Ti.68c; D.C.79.14; = 3, Id.73.4; vomitus, Cael.Aur.CP3.20; = Plin.HN37.113

πράσον.definition: leek, Allium Porrum, Batr.54; leek-like seaweed. Posidonia oceanica, Ligurian grass-wrack, Thphr.HP4.6.2, Plin.HN 13.135; also, riband-weed, Laminaria saccharina, Thphr.HP4.6.4

Πρασσαῖος.definition: mock-Ep. for , Leek-green, name of a frog, Batr.252:—so Leek-eater, v.l. ib.232

πρᾶτος.definition: Dor. for Epich.88, al., IG42.40.11 , etc.: Sup. Theoc.1.77, IG12.436, 540 , Berl.Sitzb.1927.161

πρεσβυτέριον.definition: honour or privilege of an elder, Thd.Su.50

πρεσβύτης.definition: Dor. age, seniority, Test.Epict.4.28, 6.29: opp. prob. rest. in IG5.1427.5

Πρέσβων.definition: pl. the Elders, name of a family or Abh.Berl.Akad.1909.17

πρηγορεών.definition: crop of birds, Ar.Eq.374 , Av.1113 ; from because birds collect their food there before it passes into the second stomach, Hsch., Poll.2.204, EM688.33, Suid., Apollonius ap.Zonar.: written EMl.c., cf. Suid

πρημαδίη.definition: name of a kind of olive, Nic.Al.87

πρημνάς.definition: a kind of tunny-fish, Pl.Com.44, Nicoch.11 , Opp.H.1.183; and in codd. of Arist.HA599b17

πρηστηροδόχος.definition: receiving thunderbolts, Orac.Chald. ap. Procl.in Cra.p.58 P

πρητήν.definition: yearling lamb, Ar.Byz. ap. Eust.1625.35, Hsch

Πρίαμος.definition: Priam, Il.1.19, etc.; Aeol. Alc.Supp.8.2; also Sapph.Supp.20a. 16:—Patron. metri gr.], Ep. gen. Il.3.356, 20.77: Adj. of or like Priam, Arist.EN1101a8; poet. fem. E.Hel.1158 , Or.1482 : Dim. and Sch.D.T.pp.375,376 H

πριβατάριος.definition: keeper of a private bath, Lat. balneator privatarius , MAMA3.259, al. ; written ib.557

Πριέπιος.definition: a month in Bithynia, prob. in Hemerolog.Flor

πρῖνος.definition: Arat.1047. Dsc.1.106.2 (also Amphis38; kermes-oak, Quercus coccifera, Eup.14, Amphis l.c.; Thphr.HP3.7.3, cf. Sign.45; . . Arat.1122

προαγών.definition: a ceremonial parade of actors, etc; preliminary contest, Pl.Lg.796d, cf.IG12.189.23 , Philostr.Gym.11: metaph., D.22.59

προαιτία.definition: prior cause, Dam.Pr.122, cf. 118; also ib.31 bis: Adj. Ammon.in Int.134.4

προαλής.definition: sloping, Il.21.262; the; metaph., = , heedless, Lysis ap.Iamb.VP17.77; wilful, LXXSi.30.8; rash, A.D.Pron.21.23, Adv.165.11. Adv. Comp., of dolphins, rather rashly, Str.12.3.19: is censured by Phryn.221

προβακχήϊος.definition: Ion. for of Dionysus, leader of the Bacchanals, E.Ba.412

προβαλάνειον.definition: ante-room before the bath, Archig. ap. Gal.13.168: pl., CIG3080

προβαλλός.definition: = II, shield, Hdn.Gr.1.158; cf. Phot., Hsch

πρόβασις.definition: property in cattle, abundance of; advance, Str.7.1.5; progression of musical sounds, Iamb.VP26.120; Sor.1.110: pl., Ph.1.595

πρόβλημα.definition: anything thrown forward; hindrance, obstacle, Hp.Nat.Mul.67, Mul.1.20, Ael.NA2.13

πρόβουλος.definition: deliberating beforehand or for; of the delegates of the twelve Ionian states at the Panionium, Hdt.6.7; of delegates appointed to consult on the mode of meeting Xerxes, Id.7.172

πρόβροτος.definition: former mortal, dub. in Epigr. ap. D.L.8.45

προγενής.definition: born before, primeval, S.Ant.938; generally, previous, prior, PSI8.904.6 ; PLond.1.77.59

πρόγλωσσος.definition: hasty of tongue, talkative; = foreg., Ruf. ap. Orib.25.1.23

προγόνη.definition: = abavia, privigna, Gloss., v.l. in Ph.2.303

πρόγραμμα.definition: public proclamation or notice; order of the day, agenda of or D.25.9, Arist.Ath.44.2

προγραφή.definition: public notice, advertisement; notice of sale, Thphr.Fr.97.2 , Plu.2.205c; public sale of confiscated property, Str.5.4.11

προγωνία.definition: a garment worn by cooks, Hsch

πρόδομος.definition: chamber entered immediately from the fore-court, Il.9.473; 24.673, Od.4.302: later, in temples, opp. SIG247 I 227 :— also Inscr.Délos370.14 , CIG2754

πρόδυσις.definition: earlier setting, Gem.16.16; Astrol., name of the sixth , Paul.Al.M.1, Procl.Par.Ptol.207, Antioch.inCat.Cod.Astr.8.117, Rhetor.ib.8.154

προδωσίκομπος.definition: boaster who breaks his word, Phot., Suid., Eust.710.12: in codd. wrongly written

προέγγονος.definition: great-grandson, CIG4380b1.7 , Ephes.3.17, Just.Nov.18.4 Intr.: also fem. great-granddaughter, Cod. Just.6.48.1.12

προέλευσις.definition: issuing forth, Sm.Ex.21.7, al; f.l. for in Luc.Prom.Es6

προηρόσιος.definition: before the time of tillage; the gods in whose honour it was performed, Plu.2.1119e; ib.158d

προθέλυμνος.definition: from the foundations, from; perh. close-packed, of shields overlapping in the phalanx, Il.13.130; expld. by Gramm. as = and so used by Nonn.D.22.183; also ib.2.374

πρόθεσις.definition: placing in public; of a corpse, laying it out , Pl.Lg.947b, 959a, 959e, D.43.64. 2. public notice, Arist.Pol.1322a9. 3. statement of a case, Id.Rh.1414b8; Id.Cat.11a21; theme, thesis, Phld.Rh.1.36, al. S.: generally, …

πρόθυμα.definition: preparatory offering, Ar.Pl.660, cf. Sch. ad loc.; IG22.1635.37, cf. 47.25: metaph., E.IA1311

προκάλυμμα.definition: anything put before, veil; covering, as a protection, Th.2.75; Ti.Locr.100b

προκάρδιον.definition: pit of the stomach, Ruf.Onom.95, Id. ap.Orib.inc.6.27, Poll.2.164, 165

προκάρπιον.definition: the part of the hand next the Poll.2.142

πρόκαυσις.definition: heating, stoking of a bath-furnace, CPHerm.66.7 , IG14.455

προκέλευθος.definition: conducting, dub.l. in Stratt.36; Mosch.2.151; AP5.244 ; Epigr.Gr.418.7 : abs., of persons, Nonn.D.11.419

προκελευσματικός.definition: proceleusmatic, a foot consisting of four short syllables, Heph.3.3 ; , , Aristid. Quint.1.15: , Heph.8.1, D.L.6.79; D.H.7.72

προκέφαλος.definition: with a sugar-loaf head, PGrenf.1.33.8; of verses, with a syllable prefixed , Ps.-Plu.Metr.2

πρόκλαστος.definition: broken off, of verses apparently defective in metre, Eust.1647.29

προκλίτης.definition: one who sits in the first place, Poll.6.12

προκνίς.definition: a sort of dried fig, Pamphil. ap. Ath.14.653b, Phot., Eust.1688.30; written in Poll.6.81

προκοθηλυμανής.definition: mad after the female like a Cerc.5.24

προκοίλιος.definition: = ventrosus, Gloss.: of a verse, having a syllable too many in the middle, Ps.-Plu.Metr.2; Eust.12.34,52.8

προκόλπιον.definition: part of a robe which falls; entrance into a gulf, Ach. Tat.1.1: dub. sens. in Sammelb.676.6

πρόκολπος.definition: distended, of a viper's belly, in Comp., Gal.14.265, Aët.13.23

προκόμιον.definition: forelock of a horse, X.Eq.5.6; false hair, false front, Ar.Fr.320.2, Arist.Oec.1348a30, IG11.203 B41 ; Poll.2.30; Ath.12.523a

προκόσμημα.definition: ornament in front, showy ornament, Longin. 43.3, D.L.Prooem.7; Id.6.72: pl., of a ceiling, J.BJ5.4.4

προκυμία.definition: breakwater, J.BJ1.21.6; prob. for in Id.AJ15.9.6

Προκύων.definition: the star Procyon, Arat.450; winds which precede the rising of Sirius, Adam.Vent.41

πρόλεσχος.definition: forward in talk, eager to begin, A.Supp.200

προλήνιον.definition: vat in front of a wine-press, LXXIs.5.2

προλιμνάς.definition: stagnant water left by a river overflowing, Arist.HA568a20 ), cf. Poll.9.49

πρόλοιπον.definition: arrears of a debt, Ostr.1032, al. , BGU48.15

πρόμαλος.definition: an unknown tree with supple springy branches, like prob. a kind of willow, Eup.14.5, Hp.Nat.Mul.75, A.R.3.201, Nicaenet. ap. Ath.15.673c

πρόμαστος.definition: with prominent breasts, Porph. ap. Eus.PE3.11

προμεσόζευξις.definition: figure of speech in which the principal verb is placed both at the beginning and in the middle of the sentence, Sacerd. p.456K

προμεσουράνημα.definition: Astrol. name of the ninth Paul. Al.M.4

προμήτωρ.definition: Dor. first mother of a; masc., maternal grandfather, Hsch

πρόμοιρος.definition: before the destined term, i.e; of persons, doomed to untimely death, AP11.159 ; in epitaphs, dead before their time, Epigr. Gr.418 , IG14.1386.3 , 1521 . Adv. ib.1932 , BMus.Inscr.794.10

προμολή.definition: approach, vestibule, A.R.1.1174: elsewh. in pl., Call.Dian.142, A.R.1.260,320, 4.1160; of the foot of a mountain, AP7.9 , Call.Dian.99; mouth of a river, AP7.246 , Opp.C.2.134

πρόμος.definition: foremost man, in Hom. always = Il.15.293, Od.11.493, al.; Il.5.533; opposed to another in the front rank, 7.75, 116, 22.85: later, generally, chief, A.Ag.200 , 410 ; . . Id.Eu.399; S.OC884 ; AP7.233 ; E.Tr.31; prob. i…

πρόμουλον.definition: or perh. embankment, quay, POxy.1911.167 ; as gloss on Hsch.; cf

προμύθιον.definition: moral prefixed to a fable, Aphth.Prog.1, Donat. ad Ter.Eun.232: title of a work by Sophron, Cod.Paris. in Cohn Zu den Paroömiographen82

προμυλαία.definition: goddess who presides over mills, Poll.7.180; expld. by Phot

πρόναος.definition: Subst. front hall of a temple, through which one passed to the BMus.Inscr. 481*.272,283 ; Ion. Luc.Syr.D.30; Att. dat. written IG12.237.58, ib.232.6 ; Ion. gen. Hdt.1.51: pl. as Adv., before the temple, AP6.281 : also…

πρόνοος.definition: contr. careful, prudent, A.Supp.969 , Hdt.3.36: Comp. S.Aj.119

προνουμηνία.definition: the day before a new moon, LXXJu.8.6

πρόουρον.definition: first juice from the grapes, Hsch

προούσιος.definition: prior to Being, Iamb.Myst.8.2, cf. 10.5; Anon.in Prm.inRh.Mus.47.613

προπαστάς.definition: vestibule, v.l. for in Sch.A.R.1.789; cf. · Hsch

προπάτωρ.definition: first founder of a family, forefather, Pi.N.4.89, Hdt.2.161,9.122, E.Or.1441 ; S.Aj.387 ; opp. Pl.Lg.931d; ancestor of a tribe, OGI446.3 ; Herm. ap. Stob.1.49.44, cf. Id.ib.3.11.31, IGRom.4.1213, 1215 ; D.Chr.39.8, cf…

πρόπειρα.definition: previous trial or venture, Lat.periculum facere in . . , Hdt.9.48; . . Th.3.86; Ael.NA8.22; of a trial in athletic exercises, IG14.1102.16

πρόπεμπτος.definition: only neut. pl. as Adv., five days before, Lex ap.D.43.75, Lys.Fr.26S.: c. gen., IG22.1237.61

πρόπλασμα.definition: rough draft, Cic.Att.12.41.4; sculptor's clay model, Plin.HN35.155

πρόπλοος.definition: contr. sailing before or in advance, Th.6.44; ib.46; the leading ships, Isoc.4.92, App.BC5.85, etc

προπόλεος.definition: lying before a city, Anon. ap. Suid.; gloss on Sch.Philostr.Im.Prooem. ap. Boissonade ad Marin.Procl.p.140

πρόπολις.definition: bee-glue, Varro RR3.16.24, Dsc.2.84, PMag.Par.1.2379, Aët.15.14, 15

πρόπολος.definition: going or acting before; servant that goes before one, attendant, minister, A.Ch.357 : abs., Xenoph.1.18, E.Hipp.200 , Ar.Nu.436; rower, Pi.O.13.54

πρόπομα.definition: drink taken before meals; = Plu.2.624c.—A form is cited by Hdn.Gr.2.935, Choerob.in Theod.1.339; cf

Προποντίς.definition: the Fore-sea, a name given to the Sea of Marmora, that leads into the Pontus, A.Pers.876 , Hdt.4.85, etc

πρόποσις.definition: drinking before or to one; drink itself, Simon.167.6; BMus.Inscr.1036

πρόπους.definition: one that has large feet, Phot; a star in the feet of the Twins , Gem.3.4, Ptol.Alm.7.5

προπραξία.definition: right of precedence in negotiation, IG9.442

πρόπρασις.definition: anticipatory sale: but, in a contract of marriage, conveyance of the husband's property to take effect on the dissolution of the marriage by death or otherwise, PMich.Teb.121r11 ii 1

προπρεών.definition: friendly, kindly, Pi.N.7.86 ; suppl. Herwerden in BCH23.302

προπρηνής.definition: stronger form of with the face downwards, Il.24.18; with the edge of the sword, Od.22.98: neut. as Adv., forward, opp. Il.3.218. [Hom. always makes first syll. long.]

προπρήων.definition: sine expl., perh. compd. of Choerob.in Theod.p.71 Gaisford, Theognost.Can.29

πρόρριζος.definition: by the roots, root and branch, utterly, Il.11.157; . . 14.415; Hdt.1.32; Id.3.40; . . E.Hipp.684, cf. ; S.El.765; And.1.146; A.Pers.812; S.El.512 ; . . Ar.Ra.587: neut. as Adv., Arist.HA616a2 , Lyc.214

πρόρυτος.definition: flowing forth or first, prob. in Gp.9.19.8

προσάββατον.definition: eve of the sabbath, LXXJu.8.6, Ev.Marc.15.42, Bull.Inst.franc. d'Arch.orientale30.5

προσάγιος.definition: capable of being brought into court, Mitteis Chr.96 iii 5

προσάλειψις.definition: besmearing, metaph. of a flatterer, Phld. Herc.1457.4

προσάλληλος.definition: one with or against another, X.Eq.4.3; congenial, prob. in Thphr.HP2.2.8

πρόσαλσις.definition: leaping against, of the pulse, Agathin. ap. Gal.8.937

πρόσαρσις.definition: Ion. administering or taking, Hp.Acut.26, cf. Aret.SD2.6, Gal. ap. Orib.inc.6.32

προσαφής.definition: touching upon, in communication with, Hp.Morb.4.56

προσβάρησις.definition: lying heavy or pressing upon, Gloss

προσβολή.definition: application, e.g. of the; in an auction, document recording the knocking down of a lot to a purchaser, PEleph.23.17 , PTeb.814.28

πρόσβορρος.definition: towards or exposed to the north wind, E.Ion11,937, Thphr.HP9.2.3, v.l. in Arist.GA783a31: Sup. Str.Chr.11.48

πρόσγειος.definition: keeping inshore, of fish, opp. Arist.HA525a15, 598a2; ib.598a7; ib.597a17; of islands, Id.Mete.368b33; of sea-plants, Thphr.HP4.6.2, Dsc.4.179

προσδεής.definition: needing besides, yet lacking, Pl.Ti.33d, Luc.Demon.4, Poll.5.170

πρόσδενδρος.definition: attached to trees, of creeping plants, Thphr.CP2.18.2

προσδοχή.definition: reception, Epicur.Ep.2p.38U; obligation, acceptance, debt, POxy.1223.25 ; dub. sens. in PTeb.209

προσδρομή.definition: charge, as a military evolution; sudden attack, Ptol.Tetr.116: pl., Plu.2.344a

προσείκελος.definition: somewhat like, c. dat., Hdt.2.12, 3.110; in sweetness, Id.4.177

πρόσειλος.definition: towards the sun, sunny, warm, A.Pr.451; Eup.378; Thphr.CP1.13.11, al., cf. Plu.2.649c; Philostr.VA2.18; Id.Gym.58

πρόσεργον.definition: earnings, interest upon money; extra work, i.e. to be paid for when completed, IG7.3073.8, al. .—The Adj. is dub.l.in AP6.288

προσεσπέριος.definition: towards the west, western, Arist.Fr.474, Plb.1.2.6, Scymn.157; D.H.1.13; D.S.14.34, cf. Str.9.5.10

προσευχή.definition: prayer, of the Temple; place of prayer, sanctuary, chapel, IPE12.176 , 2.52 ; esp. among the Jews. synagogue, PEnteux.30.5 , OGI726 , 96.6 , al., PTeb.86.18 , Ph.2.523, J.Vit.54, Apion ap. eund.Ap.2.2, Act.Ap.16.13, J…

προσέψημα.definition: late form for Ph.1.542, Dem.Ophth. ap. Aët.7.33, Philum. ap. Orib.45.29.55

πρόσηβος.definition: near manhood, X.Cyr.1.4.4, D.H.2.71, Ael.VH3.32, Chor.p.60 B.; Luc.Somn.1; also, near womanhood, Clearch.14, cf. Ruf. ap. Orib.inc.2.16

προσήλιος.definition: exposed to the sun, sunny, X.Cyn.4.6; Thphr.Od.40

προσήλωσις.definition: nailing on or to, Apollod.Poliorc.155.12, Gloss

προσήνεια.definition: mildness, softness, for the sake of ease or comfort, Hp.Acut.21; cj. in Herod.Med. ap. Orib.10.18.5; quietude, Sm.Ec.9.17; of language, S.E.M.1.194

προσήνεμος.definition: towards the wind, to windward, X.Oec.18.6; Arist.HA616b14; Id.GA783a32; Thphr.CP2.9.1, etc

προσηῷος.definition: Hellenistic for Dor. towards the East, Theoc.4.33; in Euboea, from the position of her temple, IG12.1189.5 , Plu.Them.8; D.S.5.55

πρόσθεμα.definition: = Ph.1.592, Socr.Ep.1; appendage: hence, = AP12.3 , Gloss

προσθεμέλιον.definition: additional foundation, IG 12.11.28 :—hence extend a foundation, ib.2, 8

προσθήκη.definition: addition, appendage; additional payment, PTeb.296.3 , etc

πρόσθιος.definition: foremost, opp. the fore-feet, Hdt.2.69; X.Cyn.9.19, etc.; Pl.Ti.91e, etc.; Arist.PA688a3; freq. alone, the front parts, opp. Id.HA493a11, al.; opp. Id.GA720a14; fitting the fore-feet to my hands, E.Rh.210; Arist.HA501…

προσθύμιος.definition: poet. according to one's mind, welcome, AP6.288

πρόσκαιρος.definition: occasional, extraordinary; opportune, Plu.Pel.15; Luc.Dem.Enc.31; Sch.Ar.Ach.274

προσκηδής.definition: bringing into alliance or; connected by marriage, Hdt.8.136; kinsfolk, AP7.444 , A.R.4.717

προσκήνιον.definition: entrance of a tent, LXXJu.10.22; porch of a house, PRyl.233.4

πρόσκοιτος.definition: for the bed or bedtime, Ph.1.635

πρόσκομμα.definition: result of stumbling, bruise, hurt, Plu.2.1048c, cf. Ath.3.97f

προσκόπιον.definition: shade for the forehead and eyes, visor, dub. in Posidon.2 J

πρόσκοπος.definition: foreseeing, sagacious, Pi.Fr.231; as Subst., outpost, vedette, X.Lac.12.6: pl., reconnoitring party, Id.Cyr.5.2.6, D.C.40.10, etc

πρόσκοψις.definition: friction, Arist.Mech.852a32, dub. cj. in Pr.940a12

πρόσκωπος.definition: at the oar, rower, Th.1.10, Luc.Cat.19

προσλάκκιον.definition: overflow-pit: metaph of the kidneys, Gal.19.362

πρόσλοιπος.definition: left over and above, IG22.1672.239; of time, for the future, Ephes.2.29

πρόσμειξις.definition: coming near to, and attack, assault, Th.5.72; D.C.40.2

παλαίφατος.definition: spoken of long ago, legendary, an oak of ancient story, Od.19.163

παλαίχθων.definition: that has been long in a country, an ancient inhabitant, indigenous, A.Th.104 ; Epigr. ap. Aeschin.3.190

παλαίωσις.definition: keeping for a long time, esp. of wine, Str.5.4.3, cf. Plu.2.656b, Ath.1.33b, Xenocr. ap. Orib.2.58.140; of drugs, maturing, Hp.Decent.10; dilapidated condition of a house, Stud.Pal.22.131.7 : metaph., LXXNa.1.15 ; And…

παλαμάομαι.definition: fut. Aeol. Alc.72; manage adroitly, Ar.Ach.659, cf. Nu.176, E.Fr.918 ; plan a daring deed, Ar.Pax94; Philostr.VA2.33.—Act. only in aor. part. Hsch

παλάμη.definition: Ep. gen. and dat; hand as used in deeds of violence, by the hands of Ares, Il.3.128, cf. 5.558, A.Supp.865 ; Alc.60: hence, a deed of force, S.Ph.1206

παλαστή.definition: = palm of the hand: hence, as a measure of length, palm, four fingers' breadth, IG12.372.35, Cratin.133, IG22.1665.10, 1666 A67, 70, al. , 11 .287 A95 , CIG2860.14 , cf. Phryn.264, PLit.Lond. 183:—also Hp.Nat.Mul.33, …

παλαστιαῖος.definition: a palm long, broad, or high, Hdt.1.50, cf. IG22.1675.13, 1693,2492.44; later

παλεονυμφάγονος.definition: where nymphs were born of old, ib.120

παλεύτρια.definition: fem. of Arist.HA613a23: as Adj., Ael.NA13.17: metaph., of courtesans, Eub.84.1:—also Phot

παλεύω.definition: act as decoy-birds, Ar.Av.1083, 1087:—Pass; metaph., decoy, entrap, Plu.2.52b, Sull.28, etc.; Philostr.VA4.25: abs., Ph.1.654

παλέω.definition: to be disabled, Hdt.8.21: elsewh. only in Hsch., also in shortd. forms, Id., Phot.; Id

παλιγγέλως.definition: mutual mockery, prob. l. in Ph.1.528

παλιγγενεσία.definition: rebirth, regeneration, of the world; in Stoic Philos., rebirth of the Chrysipp.Stoic.2.191: pl., ib.187, Boeth.Stoic.3.265; so later, M.Ant.11.1, cf. Procl.in Ti.3.241 D

παλιγγενής.definition: born again, Nonn.D.2.650; generated anew, PMag.Lond.121.510

παλίγγλωσσος.definition: contradictory, false; of strange or foreign tongue, Id.I.6.24

παλίγγναμπτος.definition: bent or doubled back, Tryph.523; written in Opp.C.2.305, H.1.54

παλιγγραφία.definition: revision of a III, Jul. Laod.inCat.Cod.Astr.5.191

παλιγκαπηλεύω.definition: to be a retail dealer, D.56.7

παλιγκάπηλος.definition: retailer of imported produce, Ar.Pl.1156 : metaph., D.25.46

παλιγκοτέω.definition: of wounds, grow malignant, fester, Id.Fract.11,25

παλίγκοτος.definition: spiteful, malignant, resentful; of persons, hostile, malignant, Ar.Pax390, Euph.51.12, etc.; Theoc.22.58; adversaries, Pi.N.4.96, A.Supp.376. Adv., . . it fared ill with him, Hdt.4.156; to bear accidents not resentful…

παλιγκρισία.definition: revision of a II.1, Jul.Laod.inCat.Cod. Astr.5.191

παλιλλογέω.definition: repeat, recapitulate, Hdt.1.118, cf. 90, Arist.Rh.Al.1433b31, Phld.Po.5.26, Ph.2.358, J.AJ17.5.5, App.Mith.14, Simp.in Ph.1159.4

παλιμβάκχειος.definition: a reversed Heph.3.2, Aristid.Quint.1.22, Eust.1551.54:—hence Adj. Heph.13.1

παλίμβαμος.definition: walking back, of women working at the loom, since they had to walk to and fro from side to side, Pi.P.9.18

παλίμβιος.definition: living again, Keil-Premerstein Erster Bericht p.9, Hsch., Phot., Suid

παλιμβλαστής.definition: sprouting or growing again, of the hydra, E.HF1274; Thphr.HP7.2.4

παλιμβολία.definition: change of mind, fickleness, AP5.301.12 , Agath.2.6

παλίμβολος.definition: reversed, Sch.Ar.Nu.298: hence, untrustworthy, unstable, Pl.Lg.705a, cf. D.Chr.31.37, Aristaenet.1.28; Plu.Crass.21; = Aeschin.2.40; of a slave, = Men.445; turned or patched sandals, Nic.Fr.85. Adv. Poll.3.132

παλιμβορέας.definition: a wind counter to the prevalent north wind, Thphr.Vent.28

παλιμπετής.definition: falling back, Nonn.D.3.30; recurrent, Theol.Ar.57: in early writers only in neut. as Adv., back again, Il.16.395; . . Od.5.27, cf. Call.Del.294, A.R.2.1250, etc

παλίμπηξις.definition: patching up or cobbling of shoes, Thphr.Char.22.11

παλίμπισσα.definition: pitch reboiled, dry pitch, Dsc.1.72; cf

παλιμπλανής.definition: wandering to and fro, AP6.287 ; Epigr.Gr.491.5

παλίμπλυτος.definition: washed up again, vamped up: metaph., of a plagiarist who retouches the works of others and passes them off for his own, AP7.708

παλίμπνοος.definition: breathing again, Nonn.D.37.295; poet. eddying, cj. in Opp.H.1.771

παλίμπορος.definition: going back, Tim.Pers.174, cf. Opp.H.4.529, Nonn.D.2.247

παλίμπους.definition: gen. going back, returning, Lyc.126, AP5.162 ; J.BJ4.1.6

παλίμπρατος.definition: sold again or by retail, of a good-; generally, good-for-nothing, Ph.2.523, Poll.4.36; also of things, D.Chr.31.37, Poll.7.12

παλιμπροδοσία.definition: double treachery, Plb.5.96.4, D.H.8.32, D.S.15.91, etc

παλιμπροδότης.definition: traitor to both sides, Din.Fr.89.26, D.S.15.91, App.BC5.96

παλίμπωλος.definition: = v.l. in Poll.7.12; esp. of works not completed by the first contractor and given to another, IG7.3073.26 , BCH20.324

παλίμφημος.definition: Dor. back-speaking; = Tryph.423, cf. Hsch.; Ph.2.301; ib.55

παλιμφυής.definition: growing again, of the hydra, Luc.Am.2

παλίμψηστος.definition: scraped again, palimpsest, Plu.2.779c: as Subst., ib.504d, cf. Catull.22.5, Cic.Fam.7.18.2

παλινάγγελος.definition: bringing messages to and fro, Hsch., Phot., Suid

παλινάγρετος.definition: to be taken back or; retracting his words, of the philosopher Arcesilaus, Id.ib.14.5

παλιναίρετος.definition: removed from office and re-; of buildings, pulled down and rebuilt, patched up, Pi.Fr.84, cf. Harp. s.v., Hsch., etc.; also IG12.313.131

παλιναυτόμολος.definition: deserting back again, double deserter, X.HG7.3.10

παλινδικέω.definition: go to law again, bring a fresh action, BGU613.17 , Hsch

παλινδικία.definition: second action, new trial, Hdn.7.6.4; Plu.Dem.6; . . Tab.Heracl.1.157

παλινδίνητος.definition: whirling round and round, AP9.73 ; ib.1.19 , cf. 9.505.14

παλινδορία.definition: mending of shoes: hence in concrete, mended shoes, Pl.Com.164, cf. Poll.6.164

παλινδρομέω.definition: run back again, J.BJ3.2.3; Medic., go back without coming to a head, of an abscess, dub. in Hp.Prog.18; strike inwards, ib.23

παλινδρομία.definition: Ion. running back, going backwards, AP6.307 , Iamb.in Nic.p.76P.; D.L.7.152; restoration, Aret.CD1.3; striking inwards, of an abscess or eruption, Hp.Prorrh.2.7: in pl., relapses, Id.Epid.4.42

παλίνδρομος.definition: running back again, Luc.Tim.37; recurring, Secund.Sent.6; recurring, Epigr.Gr. 233.7 ; . . back again, D.L.2.65: metaph., uncertain, S.E.P.2.203

παλινλιθηγία.definition: return of rejected blocks to a quarry, Supp.Epigr.4.453.30

παλινοδέομαι.definition: retrace one's path: hence in Math., recur, of numbers, Theol.Ar.22

παλίνορσος.definition: backwards, back, Il.3.33, cf. Emp.35.1; . . A.R.1.416; retrograde movement, Aret.SA2.5; recurrent, Id.CD1.5: neut. as Adv., back again, AP7.608 : Att. with a backward wrench, Ar.Ach.1179

παλίνουρος.definition: making water again, with play on pr. n. Palinurus, Mart.3.78.2

παλίνσκιος.definition: shaded over again, thick-shaded, Archil.34, Plu.Num.10, cf. Is.Fr.112; Arist.HA556a24; Luc.Am.12; dark, S.Fr.289:—also h.Merc.6, h.Hom.18.6; Thphr.HP1.8.1, cf. Od.40; Max.Tyr.5.1

παλινστατέω.definition: return from secession, of the Roman plebs, f.l. for Lyd.Mag.1.38

παλινστομέω.definition: = speak words of ill omen, A.Th.258

παλίντιτος.definition: done in requital; Act., requiting, Emp.111.5

παλιντοκία.definition: demand for repayment of interest, Plu.2.295d

παλίντονος.definition: bent backward, i.e. the opposite way; back-stretched, Ar.Av.1739

παλιντριβής.definition: rubbed again and again, of the ass; knavish, crafty, . . S.Ph.448

παλιντροπία.definition: turning about: in pl., changes of mind, A.R.3.1157

παλίντροπος.definition: turned away, averted; changing to the other side, contrary, S.Fr.576.5 ; Plb.14.6.6; exactly contrary to their original expectations, Id.5.16.9, cf. 9.21.1; D.S.15.85, cf. App.Mith.88; Onos.27 ; changeableness, Id.35.4

παλιντυπής.definition: beaten back, neut. as Adv., A.R.3.1254

παλιντυχής.definition: with a reverse of fortune, A.Ag.464

παλινῳδέω.definition: recant an ode: hence, generally, revoke; repeat an ode: hence, generally, repeat, Ph.1.586, S.E.M.7.202

παλινῳδία.definition: palinode, recantation, first used of; generally, recantation, ib.257a, Cic.Att.4.5.1, Ph.1.260, Plu.Alex.53

παλιρροέω.definition: ebb and flow, Str.1.3.8, 3.3.3; flow back, of perspiration, Diocl.Fr.147

παλιρρόθιος.definition: back-rushing, refluent, Od.5.430; of the wave caused by the rock thrown by the Cyclops, 9.485; Luc.Epigr.2.12: generally, = Arat.347; = A.R.1.1170

παλίρροιβδος.definition: dashing back with a roar, Opp.H.5.220

παλίρροος.definition: metaph., recurring, returning upon one's head, E.HF739 , cf. El.1155

παλίρροχθος.definition: roaring with ebb and flow, of Aulis, prob. in A.Ag.190

παλιρρύμη.definition: or rush backwards, back-flow, Plu.Flam.10; a reverse of fortune, Plb.15.7.1, D.S.3.51

παλίρρυτος.definition: = flowing in retribution, prob. for in S.El.1420 ; of honey, dub. in Philox.3.8

παλισσυτέω.definition: rush quickly back, of waves, D.S.1.32, 3.22

παλίσσυτος.definition: rushing back, hurried flight, S.OT193 ; E.Supp.388; Plb.15.12.2, cf. Aret.SD1.15; recovering, Id.CA2.3

παλιτραχηλίζω.definition: to be stiff-necked, refractory, contumacious, PPetr.3p.136

παλλακή.definition: = Hdt.1.135, cf. 84, 2.130, al., Ar.V.1353, Antipho1.14, Lexap. D.23.53, Lys.1.31, Pl.Ion538b, Lg.841d, D.59.122, LXXJd.19.1, etc.; Mitteis Chr.284.4

παλλακίς.definition: concubine, opp. lawful wife , Il.9.449,452; Od.14.203, cf. LXXJb.19.17, Heroph. ap. Sor.2.53 , etc.; AP3.3 ; of ritual prostitution, BCH7.276

παλτάζω.definition: throw a dart, in aor. 1 Hsch

παμβασίλεια.definition: queen of all, all-powerful queen, Ar.Nu.357, 1150, A.R.4.382; of Persephone, IG12.310.15

παμβασιλεύς.definition: absolute monarch, Alc.5, LXXSi.50.15 ; of Hadrian, Epigr.Gr. 990.3

παμμαχία.definition: in pl., contests of all kinds, B.12.76

πάμμαχος.definition: ready or sufficient for every battle, A.Ag.169 ; epith. of Athena, Ar.Lys.1321; esp. = fighting by all means, with all one's resources, Pl.Euthd.271c, Theoc.24.114, APl.4.52 , D.Chr.8.19; Sammelb.6222.22 ; so ib.26; A…

παμμελής.definition: in all kinds of melodies, LXX3; with all the limbs, entire, Poll.1.29

πάμμετρος.definition: a book of verse in all kinds of metres, D.L.7.31

πάμμηνος.definition: through all months, through the live-; = Plu.2.936a, Doroth. ap. Heph.Astr.3.9; at full moon, cj. in Philod. Scarph. 114

παμμήτωρ.definition: mother of all, A.Pr.90, Ph.1.32; a very mother, S.Ant.1282

παμμιγής.definition: mixed of all sorts, all-blended, A.Pers.269 ; Tim.Pers.188; LXX2 Ma.12.13; D.S.29.19; Lyc.5

πάμμικτος.definition: = A.Pers.53 ; ib.903 , cf. Aq.Ps.77.45, Vett. Val.15.15

πάμμορφος.definition: assuming all forms, of Proteus, Theol.Ar.7; Dam.Pr.311

πάμμουσος.definition: all-musical, Ph.1.625, 526; Calder Philadelphia and Montanism35

παμπαθής.definition: wholly passive, Plot.1.8.3; sens. obsc., = Man.4.311

παμπάλαιος.definition: very old, Pl.Tht.181b, Arist.Metaph.1074b1, cj. in ib.983b28; opp. Plu.Cat.Ma.1

παμπησία.definition: entire possession, full property, A.Th.817, E.Ion1305, Ar.Ec.868

πάμπλειστος.definition: in large quantity, number, Hdn.5.6.5; Ael.NA10.50; D.C.76.16

παμπληθής.definition: in or with their whole multitude; = very numerous, multitudinous, Pl.Lg.782b, cf. Tht.156b; D.19.145; Id.21.19; prob. in D.S.14.13; POxy. 1242.54 : c. gen., Isoc.12.169: with sg., Arist.HA567b2; a vast amount of . . ,…

παμποίκιλος.definition: all-variegated, of rich and varied; metaph., of the universe, Ph.1.651, cf. 654; manifold, Pl.Ti.82b

παμπόνηρος.definition: thoroughly depraved, Ar.Ach.854; of things, very bad, Epich.87; Phld.Ir.p.77 W

παμπρασία.definition: unreserved sale of property, Poll.7.196, al

πάμπρωτος.definition: the very first, first of all, Il.7.324, 9.93: neut. as Adv., Od.4.577; Pi.P.4.111: also in pl. Il.4.97, 17.568: Sup. A.R.4.1693

παμφάγος.definition: all-devouring, voracious; omnivorous, Arist.Pol.1256a25, cf. HA488a15, 593b25; Jul.Or.6.192d: Comp., Arist.GA786a34: Sup., Thphr.HP9.15.4

παμφαής.definition: all-shining, radiant, of fire, S.Ph.728 E.Tr.548 ; of the sun, Id.Med.1251 , cf. Ar.Av.1709, IG12.891.3 , etc.; of honey, bright, pure, A.Pers.612

παμφαλάω.definition: redupl. form like , gaze in astonishment, Ion. word, Hippon.131, Anacr.160, Herod.4.77; Eryc. ap. Sch.A.R.2.127: aor. 1 Hsch.:—Med., Lyc.1433

παμφάρμακος.definition: skilled in all charms or drugs, of Medea, Pi.P.4.233

πάμφθογγος.definition: with or of all sounds, Hsch

πάμφιλος.definition: beloved of all, prob. in A.Eu.536 : Sup. PGrenf.2.92.11

πάμφυλος.definition: of mingled tribes or; one of the three Dorian tribes, Hdt.5.68, IG42.71.49 , SIG1025.8 , etc.: gen. pl. IG4.598 ; SIG1027.4

πάμφυρτος.definition: mixed of all sorts, Ph.1.148, cf. 2.53, Longin.9.7, Opp.H.1.779: neut. pl. as Adv., confusedly, S.Ichn.232

πάμφωνος.definition: with all tones, full-toned or many- toned, Pi.O.7.12; Id.P.12.19; Id.I.5.27; Id.P.3.17: generally, expressive, APl.4.290 ; noisy, Philox.16

πάμψυχος.definition: in full life, of Amphiaraus, S.El.841

παμωχέω.definition: own, possess, Tab. Heracl.1.168:—also Hsch.; and Dor. for owner, Id

πανάγαθος.definition: also absolutely good, Cratin.434, Pl.Ep.354e, Simp.in Epict.p.76 D

παναγής.definition: all-hallowed, Call.Fr.1.36P; under an Philonid.5, Man.4.120

παναγόρσιος.definition: = name of month at Tegea, IG5.3.30

πανάγρετος.definition: taking all kinds of game, AP6.75

πανάγριος.definition: quite wild or savage, Opp.C.2.45, dub. in Ps.-Phoc.202

πάναγρος.definition: catching all, of a large fishing-net, Il.5.487; Ath.1.25b: metaph., Tryph.674

παναθέσμιος.definition: utterly lawless, cj. for sq. in Man.4.56

πανάθλιος.definition: all-wretched, A.Ch.695, S.OC1110, E.Hec.658, Timocl.25: in late Prose, Ph.1.542

παναισθησία.definition: full vigour of the senses, D.L.10.65

πάναισχρος.definition: = D.Chr.31.35, Ptol.Tetr.172: Sup., AP6.163 . Adv. Plb.4.58.11, Tz.H.6.44

παναίτιος.definition: cause of all, A.Ag.1486; to whom all the guilt belongs, opp. A.Eu.200

πανάκεια.definition: universal remedy, panacea; name of a healing herb or its juice , Call.Ap.40, etc.; Gal.14.156; Hercules' woundwort, Opopanax hispidus, Thphr.HP9.15.7

πανακής.definition: all-heal, Ferulago galbanifera, Hp.Mul.2.201, Thphr.HP9.7.2, etc.; Aesculapius' all-heal, Echinophora tenuifolia, ib.9.8.7, 9.11.1; = I.2a, ib.9.11.3, Dsc.3.48; Centaury, Centaurea salonitana, Plin.HN25.33, Sch.Nic.Th…

πανάκτειος.definition: in Nic.Th.626, expld. by Sch. either as or as a poet. form of cf. Hsch

παναληθής.definition: of things, absolutely true or real, Pl.R.583b, cf. Iamb.Protr.4

παναλκής.definition: all-powerful, v.l. for A.Th.166 : Sup., of a poultice, Aët.3.177

παναοίδιμος.definition: sung by all, APl.4.71, Dioscorus in PLit.Lond.100C6

πανάπαλος.definition: all-tender or delicate, . . , Od.13.223 metri gr.]; Ph.2.432

παναπήμων.definition: gen. all-harmless, Hes.Op.811; of Apollo, AP9.525.17

πανάπυστος.definition: all-unheard of, Phot., Suid., restd. in Philic. in Stud.Ital.9.48

παναρκής.definition: = Id.Th.166 ; the sun that shines on all alike, Call.Fr.48.1, cf. Suid. s. v.: Sup., of a poultice, Lycus ap. Orib.9.26.1; cf

παναρμόνιος.definition: embracing all modes or scales, in; metaph., complex, elaborate, opp. Pl.Phdr.277c, cf. Iamb.Myst.5.21; Luc.Salt.72; of Homer and Plato, Olymp.Vit.Pl.p.4 W

πανασφάλιος.definition: giving security, epith. of Zeus and Poseidon at Mytilene, Ath.Mitt.24.358

πανατρεκής.definition: all-exact, infallible, Keil- Premerstein Erster Bericht p.9 ; AP7.594 : neut. as Adv., A.R.4.1382

παναώριος.definition: doomed to an untimely end, Il.24.540; AP5.263.5

πανδαισία.definition: Ion. complete banquet at which no one and nothing fails, Hdt.5.20, Ar.Pax565, Is.Fr.100, Plu.2.1102a, Supp.Epigr.4.304.6 , Alciphr.3.18:—also Phot., Suid

πανδακέτης.definition: biting all, of Cato, Epigr. ap. Plu.Cat.Ma.1

πανδαμάτωρ.definition: the all-subduer, all-tamer, of sleep, Il.24.5, Od.9.373; of time, Simon.4.5, B.12.205, Epigr.Gr.1050 ; S.Ph.1467 ; Luc.Tim.2, etc.:—pecul. fem. Orph.H.10.26, Epigr.Gr.434.6 , IG12.303 ; Arist.Pepl.43

πάνδεινος.definition: all-dreadful, terrible; very able, c. inf., Pl.Plt.290b; ironically, D.19.120

πανδερκής.definition: seen by all, B.16.70; Act., all-seeing, AP9.525.17, Q.S.2.443, Orph.Fr.62

πανδέτης.definition: secure fastener, prob. name of a knot, PMag.Leid.V.5.23

πανδεχής.definition: all-receiving, Pl.Ti.51a; Ph.1.386; Ocell.2.3; Plu.2.1014d; Orph.Fr.315.3

πανδημία.definition: the whole people, Pl.Lg.829b; of Theseus in Attica, Arist.Fr.384, Plu.Thes.25; as Adv., = A.Supp.607

πανδήμιος.definition: of or belonging to all the people, public beggar, Od.18.1; a draught of all kinds of fish, AP9.383.2

πάνδημος.definition: Dor. = (esp. in; vulgar love, opp. Pl.Smp.180e sq., cf. X.Smp.8.9; Pl.Smp.181a, IG22.659, SIG 1014.57 , Paus.1.22.3, Luc.DMeretr.7.1, etc. ; Pl.Smp.181e; common, vulgar music, Aristox.Fr.Hist.90; ordinary speech, Phld…

πανδῖος.definition: all-divine, = Ps.-Dsc.2.180 : pecul. fem., Max.146; alone, Id.123

πανδοκεία.definition: trade of an innkeeper, Pl.Lg.918d, Poll.7.16

πανδοκεῖον.definition: Hsch.), inn, Ar.Ra.550, D.19.158, Aeschin.2.97, IG22.1638.30, Philippid.25.2, Com.Adesp.159, Plb.2.15.5:—later Thphr.Lap.53 codd., Aen.Tact.10.10 codd., Str.5.3.9, 12.8.17, etc., condemned by Phryn.276

πανδοκεύς.definition: one who receives all comers, innkeeper, Pl.Lg.918b, Plb.2.15.6, Arr.Epict.1.24.14, Plu.2.234e, etc.: metaph., Pl.R.580a; Lyc.655:—later Ev.Luc.10.35; of the all- containing, Pythag. ap. Procl.in Ti.3.107 D.; also Pyth…

πανδοκεύτρια.definition: hostess, Ar.Ra.114, Pl.426, Eup.9, D.C.46.6: metaph., a sea-monster ready to take all in, Ar.V.35

πανδοκεύω.definition: entertain as a host or innkeeper, Timocr.1.10, Hdt.4.95, Pl.Lg.918e: abs., keep an inn or lodging-house, Thphr.Char.6.5:—Pass., to be furnished with inns, D.H.4.53

πάνδοκος.definition: or all-receiving, common to all, of Hades, A.Th.860; of the sacred places at Elis and Delphi, Pi.O.3.17, P.8.61; Id.O.4.17; S.Fr.274: c. gen., A.Ch.662

πάνδοξ.definition: = gen. MAMA3.576, al. ; gen. ib.459 : nom. sg. in Hsch

πάνδοσις.definition: an unknown article of household equipment, PLond.2.191.6

πανδοῦρα.definition: or three-stringed lute , Poll.4.60, Ath.4.183f:—also Euph. ap.Ath.4.183f, MAMA3.24 :—Dim. Hsch. and Phot. s.v. Hsch.,Gloss.:—hence play the Hist.Aug.Elag.32; one who plays it, Euph.Fr. Hist.8, JRS18.177

πανδρόσειον.definition: temple of Pandrosos, daughter of Cecrops and Agraulos, IG12.372.45, 171, al

παράδοσις.definition: handing down, bequeathing; transmission of legends, doctrines, etc., tradition, Pl.Lg.803a; Arist.SE184b5; Plb.12.6.1, etc.; treatment, exposition, HeroBel.73.12; the subject of botany, Dsc.Praef.1; Phld.Rh.1.78 S.; s…

παραδοτέος.definition: to be handed down, Pl.Lg.802e; one must hand over, Id.Alc.1.132c; Iamb.Protr.2

παραδοχή.definition: that which has been received, hereditary custom, E.Ba.201; tradition, Hippod. ap. Stob.4.1.95; S.E.P.1.146; A.D.Adv.168.9

παραδρομή.definition: running beside: hence concretely; running by, traversing, Plu.Alex.17; cursorily, Arist.Pol.1336b24; Plb.21.34.2

παραδρομίς.definition: place for taking the air, IG22.1035.56 , 12.234.34 , Inscr.Perg.252.32, PCair.Zen.764.34,44 , Vitr.5.11.4, POxy.502.19 , 2146.9

παράδρομος.definition: that may be run through, spaces; running alongside, Stad.67

παραδρύπτω.definition: scratch, scrape at the side, Lib.Decl.28.12

παραδυναστεύω.definition: reign beside or with another, Th.2.97; have great influence or authority with, c. dat., Id.75.14, Jul.Mis.365a

παράδυσις.definition: creeping in beside, encroachment, Id.17.27; Plu.2.727a; J.BJ3.7.9; ib.4.7.4

παραδωσείω.definition: Desiderat. of to be disposed to deliver up, Th.4.28

παραζεύγνυμι.definition: and aor. 2 Pass; generally, associate, Phld.Mus.p.71 K..:—Pass., to be associated in a task, PRyl.237.4 ; the associated lameness, Apollon.Cit.3

παραζηλόω.definition: provoke to jealousy, LXX3 Ki.14.22; fret, be vexed, LXXPs.36.1

παραζητέω.definition: inquire into, search amiss, M.Ant.12.5, Al.Le.27.33

παραζωγραφέω.definition: paint beside or in the same picture, App.Mith.117

παραζωνίδιον.definition: dagger worn at the girdle, Posidon.2 J

παραζώννυμι.definition: and hang at the girdle; gird along the side, of clouds hanging on a mountain-side, Thphr.Sign.51

παραθάλλω.definition: pf. grow beside, cj. for in Philostr.Im.2.6

παραθάπτω.definition: bank up at the sides, BGU1121.24

παραθαρσύνω.definition: Att. fut. Plu.Alc.26:—embolden, encourage, Th.4.115, 8.77, X.An.3.1.39, etc.; Pl.Criti.108c: c. acc. pers. et inf., Plu. l.c

παραθεάομαι.definition: inspect side by side, compare, Pl.Ep.313c; Thphr.Char.Praef.2

παραθεμιστεύω.definition: transgress a law, Herm. ap. Stob.1.49.45

παραθερίζω.definition: graze in passing, in poet. aor. 1 A.R.2.601, Q.S.6.629

παραθερμαίνω.definition: warm, cheer, Ath.5.185c:— Pass., to be heated, Arist.Pr.876b3: metaph., of a man, become quarrelsome in his cups, Aeschin.2.157; LXXDe.19.6

παραθέσιμος.definition: that which is deposited, stored, PSI5.463.13

παράθεσις.definition: Gramm., juxtaposition, opp. com- position , as in opp. EM278.25,649.14; also, addition, addition of prepositions, A.D.Synt.333.7, cf. Pron.23.12, al

παραθεωρέω.definition: examine a thing beside another, compare; keep in mind, take into account, . . Epicur.Ep.1p.29U.; Phld.Rh.1.373 S

παραθήγω.definition: whet, sharpen upon; metaph., exasperate, provoke, D.H.8.57; Ph.2.575, cf. 543; incite, Plu.2.1145f

παραθηκαρία.definition: receipt for an object taken in charge, POxy.144.17

παραθήκη.definition: anything entrusted to one. deposit, Hdt.6.86, 9.45, BGU1004.15 , LXXLe.6.2 , Ps.-Phoc.135, Ostr.Bodl.i 274 , SIG742.51 ; of persons, hostage, Hdt.6.73

παραθηλάζω.definition: nurse at the breast as well as another child, BGU1106.30 , etc

παραθητεύω.definition: serve for hire, Epic. ap. Plu.2.761e

παραθιγγάνω.definition: aor. 2 touch at the side or in passing, Him.Or.23.12

παράθλιψις.definition: pressure at the side, Gal.18.69, Sor.1.119 cod., Cass.Pr.28

παράθραυμα.definition: anything broken off, fragment, in pl., Ar.Fr.366

παραθραύω.definition: break, smash, of ships and pottery; break off, metaph., Demad.44; Gal.4.623, cf. 9.931; infringe, violate, Porph.Abst.3.1:—so in Pass., Pl.Lg.757e

παραθριγκίζω.definition: edge as with a cornice, make a row along, prob. in Thphr.HP3.18.12:—hence Subst. cj. ibid

παραθρῴσκω.definition: run or leap past, Oikonomos p.39 , D.P.286

παραθυμιάω.definition: burn incense beside, fumigate, D.S.3.47; Agatharch.99

παράθυρος.definition: = PMich.Zen.38.11; stone forming part of a side-door, Milet.7p.56

παραιγιαλίτης.definition: haunting the shore, of certain fish, Clearch.73, St.Byz.:—fem. close inshore, Eust.116.6

παραιθύσσω.definition: poet. aor. Pi.O.10.73:—move or; whizz past, A.R.2.1253

παραίνεσις.definition: exhortation, address, A.Eu.707, Hdt.9.44, Th.2.45, etc.; ib.88: c. gen. pers., advice or counsel given by a person, Hdt.5.11, 51: c. gen. rei, advice given for, of, or towards a thing, Th.4.59; to recommend an opinion…

παραινέω.definition: advise or recommend publicly, propose, Id.1.139, cf. IG12.90.43, etc.; Th.2.13; advise not . . , c. inf. , ib.18

παραινίττομαι.definition: indicate enigmatically, Ath.13.604f; simply, hint at, suggest, allude to, Phld.Piet.91, Lyd.Ost.44

παραίρεσις.definition: taking away from, stripping one of, Th.1.122; Pl.R.573e; Arist.Pol.1311a12

παραιρέτης.definition: one that takes away or diminishes; a planet which is out of its proper Paul.Al.S.2, Sch.Ptol.Tetr.100

παραίρημα.definition: edge or selvage of cloth: generally, band, strip, Th.4.48; prob. for or in Hp.Off.12; expld. by Hsch

παραισαβάζω.definition: poet. for , to be inspired by Sabazius, i.e. Dionysus, Hsch., Phot

παραισθάνομαι.definition: remark or hear of by the way; misperceive, be subject to illusory perceptions, Pl.Tht.157e, Aret.SD1.6, Iamb.Protr.2

παραΐσσω.definition: Att. dart past, Il.5.690; 8.98; 20.414; Ar.V.988, cf. 837: c. acc., Il.11.615: in later Prose, Plu.2.774f. in Hom.]

παραιτέομαι.definition: beg of or from another, ask as a favour; having obtained the king's leave, Hdt.6.24: generally, intercede with, appeal to a person, Id.3.132, 5.33; E.Heracl.1026, cf. Ar.V.1257; . . entreating them and saying that . .…

παραίτησις.definition: supplication, entreaty; deprecating, Th.1.73; excuse, apology, Plb.39.1.5, Jul.Or.2.64a , Chor.inRev.Phil.1.73, etc.; pardon, Ph.2.296, cf. 223

παραιτητέος.definition: to be deprecated, Ph.1.275; to be; one must decline, S.E.M.10.118, Ath.10.421a, 11.464a; Ph.1.161; one must avoid, D.S.21.14, Sor.2.24, etc.; one must reject, Sch.Il.3.230; ib.2.8

παραιφάμενος.definition: Ep. part. Med. of talking over, persuading, Il.24.771, h.Cer.336, Hes.Th.90

παραιφασίη.definition: = sq. I, Musae.Fr.Epic.5, A.R.2.324; consolation against . . , Poet. ap. Orion s.v

παρακαθάπτω.definition: fasten, hang by the side, Poll.1.252

παρακαθεύδω.definition: sleep beside, of a dog, Ael.VH1.13; of persons, keep watch by, LXXJu.10.20

παρακάθημαι.definition: inf. to be seated beside or; of an army, encamp beside, Plb.9.11A.2

παρακαθιδρύω.definition: in Pass., to be placed by or near, Plu.Caes.9

παρακαθίζω.definition: pf. Arr.Epict.2.6.23:—set; Med. with aor. 1 let another sit down beside one, Lycurg.141, cf. J.AJ19.4.5; also make him assessor or co-arbiter, D.33.14

παρακαθίημι.definition: let down beside, of the nautilus; intr. , sink down, Plb.35.1.4

παρακαθίστημι.definition: also J.AJ14.15.7:—set down beside, station or establish beside, D.4.25; Isoc.4.104, cf. IG12.46.9; D.S.16.38, cf. PCair.Zen.199.7 , PRev.Laws54.15 :—Pass., being made his colleague, D.S.16.47

παράκαιρος.definition: = foreg., Epich.260, Men.Mon.217, Clearch.5, Luc.Nigr.31; Lib.Or.64.100. Adv. immoderately, Isoc.1.9

παρακαλέω.definition: Att. fut. later LXXJb.7.13; call in, send for, summon, Hdt.1.77, Ar.V.215, etc.; Hdt.7.158, cf. Th.1.119, Pl.Phd.89c, etc.; And.4.14; Hdt.7.205, cf. D.18.24; X.An.1.6.5; Pl.La.186a; Aeschin.2.184; invoke the gods, D.1…

παρακαλπάζω.definition: run beside a trotting horse, Plu.Alex.6

παρακάλυμμα.definition: anything hung up beside; metaph., veil, cloak, Antiph.167; LXXWi.17.3; J.AJ16.8.1; Plu.2.654d; excuse, pretext, Id.Per.4; Id.2.27e, cf. Ph.2.186

παρακαλύπτω.definition: cover by hanging something beside, cloak, disguise, Plu.Demetr.52:—Med., cover one's face, Pl.R.439e, Plu.Alc.34; Id.Pomp.60 : metaph., veiling itself, Pl.R.503a, cf. Plu.2.370f; Ph.2.196; set aside, ignore, ib.189

παρακαμμύω.definition: for give a side wink at, Phot. s.v

παρακάμπτω.definition: bend aside: hence, avoid, shun, D.S.5.59

παρακανθίζω.definition: to be somewhat prickly, Thphr.HP1.10.6, al

παρακαταβαίνω.definition: fut. dismount, of mounted; disembark from a ship, D.S.3.40

παρακατάβασις.definition: in Law, perh. rejoinder, or appearance of the defendant in court, Pl.Lg.956e

παρακαταβολή.definition: money deposited in court by; the process in which such a deposit was required, Poll.8.32

παρακαταγωγή.definition: a method of throwing in wrestling, Sch.T Il.23.730

παρακαταθάπτω.definition: Ep. aor. I bury beside, Q.S.1.804

παρακαταθήκη.definition: deposit of money or property; of persons entrusted to guardians, ward, Hdt.2.156; of children, D.28.15; of persons under the protection of the state, sacred trust, Din.1.9

παρακατάκειμαι.definition: Pass., lie beside or near, esp. at meals, X.Cyr.2.2.28, Pl.Ep.360b, etc

παρακατακλίνω.definition: lay down beside, put to bed with, Aeschin.2.149, Luc.DDeor.6.4, Artem.4.61

παρακαταλείπω.definition: leave with one, Th.6.7; leave as deputy, D.C.46.37

παρακαταλέχομαι.definition: Pass., lie down beside, lie or sleep with , Il.9.565, cf. 664

παρακαταλογή.definition: in Music, recitative, melodramatic delivery, Arist.Pr.918a10, Plu.2.1141a

παρακατασκευάζω.definition: gloss on EM637.29; v.l. for Sch.Pi.O.6.1

παρακατατίθημι.definition: expose to risk, Aeschin.3.180; Med., trust, c. dat., BGU326.16

παρακαταχράομαι.definition: use beside, use for a purpose, Arist.PA690a1, cf. 659a21

παρακάτειμι.definition: go farther down, farther down he says, Steph.in Hp.2.327 D., Sopat.inRh.5.144 W.; Sch.Od.11.90; v.l. in Sch.Theoc.1.4

παρακατέχω.definition: keep back, detain, Plb.1.66.5, etc; retain possession of, Plb.18.45.12

παρακατοικίζω.definition: make to dwell or settle beside, Isoc.6.28; make fear and watching their companions, Plu.Per.11:—Med., settle near oneself, Isoc.6.87:—Pass., Aristid.Or.46.26

παρακατορύσσω.definition: aor. I bury or plant in the earth beside, Hp.Art.47

παρακαττύω.definition: sew on beside, patch up:—in Med., generally, put in order, set straight, Ar.Pl.663

παρακαυλίζω.definition: shoot out at the side, Thphr.HP6.2.8

παρακέλευμα.definition: precept, maxim, Pl.R.407b, cf. Lg.688a, al

παρακελεύομαι.definition: recommend an action to one, prescribe; exhort, encourage, Isoc.9.79, Pl.Phd.60e, etc.; having delivered this address, Th.6.69: abs., encourage one another by shouting, Hdt.9.102; X.An.4.2.11; . . Th.4.25

παρακέλευσις.definition: cheering on, exhorting, Th.7.70; factious combination for elections, D.C.53.21

παρακελευστής.definition: one who calls out to or encourages, Gloss

παρακελητίζω.definition: Att. fut. ride by or past, Ar.Pax901

παρακενόω.definition: empty beside or near, void, vacuum, Placit.4.22.1, 5.15.3

παρακεντέω.definition: pierce or poke at the side; Medic., tap, for dropsy, Gal.Thras.23

παρακέντησις.definition: Medic., tapping for dropsy; couching for cataract, Gal.UP10.4 , Simp.in Cat.401.8

παρακεντητήριον.definition: instrument for tapping or couching, prob. in Gal.18.672

παρακεντητής.definition: one who taps or couches, Id.Thras.24, Gloss

παρακερδαίνω.definition: make incidental or unjust gain, Lib.Decl.2.7, Heliod.in EN81.22

παρακινδυνεύω.definition: make a venture, Hp.Aër.23, Ar.V.6; c. acc. rei, venture, risk a thing, Ar.Eq.1054, Pl.Lg.967b; I venture to say, Id.Tht.204b; a bold, venturous phrase, Ar.Ra.99; D.H.Comp.23, cf. Is.13; desperate battles, Id.9.30; Plu…

παρακίνδυνος.definition: risking dangers, temerity, daring character, Str.17.3.20. Adv. with great danger, Id.5.3.5

παρακινέω.definition: move aside, disturb, Pl.R.591e (unless; excite violently, madden, Thphr.HP9.19.1:—Pass., to be distracted, Arg.S.Aj.; to be violently excited or incited to . . , Luc.Hist. Conscr.1; Id.Cal.5; later, simply, urge, c. i…

παρακίνησις.definition: disturbance, Phld.Rh.2.5 S; gloss on Sch.Th.4.11

παρακίρναμαι.definition: Pass., to be mixed with, J.BJ4.3.7

παρακλάομαι.definition: Pass., to be broken off, f.l. for in Sch.Arat.785

παρακλείω.definition: Ion. shut out, exclude; shut up in prison, Plb.5.39.3 , LXX2 Ma.4.34

παράκλησις.definition: calling to one's aid, summons; imploring, appealing, of or on the part of one, Th.4.61; deprecation, Str.13.1.1

παρακλητεύω.definition: act as advocate or intercessor, Bull.Soc.Roy.des lettres de Lund 1928/9iv 16 , Ph.2.520

παράκλητος.definition: called to one's aid, in a court of; summoned, D.C.46.20, cf. BGU601.12

παρακλήτωρ.definition: one who encourages, comforter; suppliant, Sch.E.Hec.147; but = ib.345

παρακλίτης.definition: one who lies beside at meals, X.Cyr.2.2.28

παρακμάζω.definition: to be past the prime, of fruits, etc., X.Mem.4.4.23, Thphr.Od.34, etc.; of old trees, Id.HP9.4.7; of men compared to wine, Alex.45.5: metaph., of beauty, X.Smp.4.17,8.14; Arist.Rh.1389b13, cf. Pol.1275a17; Plu.Caes.37…

παρακμή.definition: point at which the prime is past, decay, Plu.2.453b; Ph.Fr.97 H.; Sch.Arat.1082; abatement, Plu.Marc.24, cf. S.E.P.2.238: metaph., of numbers, Iamb.in Nic.p.77 P

παρακνημόομαι.definition: Pass., go with difficulty, Hippon.130: Dor. impf. Hsch

παρακοιμάομαι.definition: Pass., lie or keep watch beside; lie beside, in death, IG14.1539

παρακοιμίζω.definition: make to lie with, Alex.Polyh. ap. Eus.PE9.21, cf. Artem.4.61, Cat.Cod.Astr.2.208 : hence Subst. in pl., panders to their own wives, Paul. Al.O.2

παρακοιτέω.definition: keep watch or ward beside, Plb.6.33.12: abs., Telesp.50 H., SIG731.15

παρακοίτης.definition: one who lies beside, bedfellow, husband, Il.6.430,8.156, Hes.Th.928

παράκοιτις.definition: acc. ), fem. of foreg., wife, Il.21.479, 3.53, Od.23.92, 15.26, etc. ; Ep. dat. 3.381, Hes.Sc.14, 46

παρακολλάω.definition: glue or fasten on, Hp.Mochl.2; unite directly by 'first intention', Heras ap.Gal.13.794, Antyll. ap. Orib.10.23.6,50.2.8

παρακόλλημα.definition: that which is glued on, perh; crimp or loop of string glued to a cylinder, HeroAut.23.7

παρακόλλησις.definition: glueing or fastening on; healing or closing up of sinuses, Heras ap. Gal.13.795, Antyll. ap. Orib.45.25.6, Leonid. ap. Aët.15.2

παρακολουθέω.definition: follow or attend closely, dog one's; make a succession of growths, Thphr.HP6.4.8

παρακολούθημα.definition: that which follows, Iamb.Comm. Math.8; accompaniment or attendant circumstance, Demetr.Lac.Herc.1012.46, Placit.1.22.5, Numen. ap. Porph. ap. Stob.1.49.25, Nicom.Ar.1.19, Plot.3.7.10, Hierocl.in CA15p.453M., Procl.in …

παρακολούθησις.definition: following closely; as an incidental result, Chrysipp.Stoic.2.336

παρακομιδή.definition: transportation, conveyance; going or sailing across, passage, transit, Th.5.5, cf. Plb.3.43.3, etc

παρακομίζω.definition: fut. PPetr. 3p.122; carry or convey over, transport, Arist.HA580a17; D.50.6: generally, convey, carry, Hdt.7.147, etc.:—Med., have a thing brought one, X.HG5.4.57:—Pass., ib.5.4.61, Plu.Oth.3

παρακομιστής.definition: one who transports or purveys, Gloss

παρακονάω.definition: sharpen or whet, Com.Adesp.599; generally, rub against the cheek, Hsch., cf. Phot

παρακονιάω.definition: whitewash, IG11 .144 A 69, al. , cf. Inscr.Délos 403.11

παρακοντίζω.definition: throw the dart with others, Luc.Par.61

παρακοπή.definition: metaph., infatuation; delirium, Hp.Aph.6.26: in pl., Plu.2.1123b

παράκοπος.definition: metaph., frenzied, frantic, distraught; counterfeit, Ph.1.261

παρακόπτω.definition: strike falsely, counterfeit, prop. of; Med., cheat or swindle out of a thing, Id.Eq.807; simply, cheat, ib.859:—Pass., to be cheated, Id.Nu.640

παρακοτέω.definition: to be angry besides, Phot.; cf. Hsch. )

παράκουσις.definition: defect of hearing, Gal.7.56; mishearing, Mich.in PN64.32

παράκουσμα.definition: thing heard amiss, false notion; in pl., defects of hearing, Gal.7.108

παρακούω.definition: hear beside, esp. hear accidentally, hear; eavesdrop, overhear from, Ar.Ra.750; Pl.Euthd.300d; overhear him, Luc.Merc.Cond.37; Ev.Marc.5.36

παρακρατέω.definition: detain, keep wailing, App.Hisp.35; compress, squeeze, Dsc.Eup.1.8

παρακρέμαμαι.definition: Pass., hang beside, Luc.Asin.23: metaph., to be dependent, the dependencies of an empire, Plb.5.35.10

παρακρίνω.definition: judge falsely, Hsch.s.v; Pass., to be drawn up in line opposite, Plu.Ant.39; the land force drawn up along the shore, Hdt.9.98; Id.8.70, cf. Plu.Cat.Mi.13

παρακροτέω.definition: pat, clap one, Luc.Anach.1; encourage, D.H.7.46, J.BJ1.19.5, 1.31.5:—Pass., ib.3.10.2

παράκρουσις.definition: striking falsely, false note; metaph., cheating, deception, D.23.175; Id.24.194

παρακρουσιχοίνικος.definition: striking off too much from the top of the measure , Com.Adesp.1104

παρακρούω.definition: Med., mislead, deceive, cheat, esp. by fallacies, Isoc.12.243; ib.271, cf.Pl.Cra.393c, D.2.5, 18.276, Din.1.40, Arist.Pol.1297a10, Metaph.1025a6, Men.Epit.329, PSI4.442.24 , etc.; D.43.39: pf. Pass. in sense of Med., …

παρακρύπτω.definition: hide one's sympathies, dissimulate, D.S.18.9:— Med., hide oneself, D.L.2.131

παρακρώζω.definition: croak beside, v.l. for in Dionys.Av.1.9

παρακυέω.definition: to be spuriously pregnant, dub. rest. in IG42.122.26

παραλαγχάνω.definition: pf. obtain as one's portion, Sch.Ar.Av.569

παραλαλέω.definition: talk at random, Men.923.4, LXXPs.43.17, D.C.69.4

παραλαμβάνω.definition: take upon oneself, undertake, Ar.Eq.345; undertakings, Hdt.1.38; take to oneself, admit, employ, Plu.2.988e:—Pass., ib.1027d

παραλανθάνω.definition: escape the notice of, Pl.Hp.Ma.298b, Isoc.10.14, 11.48, D.46.17: abs., lie hid, concealed, f.l. in Hdn.4.15.2

παραλαχανίζω.definition: defraud in the matter of vegetables, Com.Adesp.1108

παραλείπω.definition: leave to another, leave him time for speaking, Aeschin.3.71; permit, allow, Plu.Arat.28

παραλήγω.definition: to be next to the end, the penultima, A.D.Synt.255.5, etc. ; to have in the penultima, Hdn.Gr.2.926; in the last foot but one, Heph.5.1:— also in Med., A.D.Adv.175.20, cf. Hdn.Gr.2.927, Hermog.Id.1.6

παραληπτής.definition: later receiver of dues, Peripl.M.Rubr.19, OGI202.4 , BGU381.1 ; receiver of soldiers' allowances, Ostr.1135, al

παραλήπτωρ.definition: inheritor, Herm. ap; = dub. in PRein.42.12

παραληρέω.definition: talk nonsense, rave, Ar.Eq.531, Ra.594, Isoc.12.23, Pl.Tht.169a; . . , D.Prooem.4; . . even to crazy persons, Arist.Rh.1356b35

παραλήρημα.definition: piece of absurdity, of a person, D.C.59.26

παράληρος.definition: raving, delirious, ib.1.2, Ph.1.387; as Subst., = Suid. s.v

παραλιμπάνω.definition: collat. form of Arist.Pr.951a33, Aristox.Harm.p.35 M., Chrysipp.Stoic.3.200, Hermog.Inv.2.5, OGI519.18 , Olymp.in Grg.p.242 J

παραλίσκομαι.definition: Pass., to be put under restraint, Hsch. s.v

παραλιταίνω.definition: aor. do amiss, sin; c. acc. pers., . . didst sin against them, A.R.2.246

παράλλαγμα.definition: difference, variation, Epicur.Nat.Herc.908.1,al., Str.2.1.35 , Plu.Num.18; Gem.8.19, al.; departure from the normal, Metrod. Herc.831.5, 7

παράλλαξις.definition: alternation : overlapping of; alternating motion, Plu.Phil.6; Id.2.977b

παραλλάσσω.definition: change, alter, Hdt.2.49; Aeschin.3.192, cf. Arist.Top.119a15; esp. alter for the worse, S.Ant.298; twist, Chrysipp.Stoic.2.258:—freq. in Pass., to be altered, Plb.5.56.11, etc.; Id.7.17.7: hence strange, extraordinary…

παραλληλεπίπεδον.definition: body with parallel surfaces, parallelepiped, Euc.11.25, Plu.2.1080c

παραλληλεπίπεδος.definition: with parallel surfaces; number which is the product of three factors, two of which are equal, Nicom.Ar.2.16

παραλληλία.definition: being side by side, repetition of a letter, Eust.149.8; of words of identical meaning, pleonasm, Id.961.32

παραλληλίζω.definition: place side by side, Id.437.29, cf. 1539.58

παραλληλισμός.definition: equating of payments, PMasp. 58 ii; placing side by side, repetition of ideas in a compound , Eust.437.25

παραλογεία.definition: fraudulent exaction, extortion, in pl., PAmh.2.33.13 , UPZ113.10

παραλογίζομαι.definition: in keeping accounts, cheat, D.27.29; reason falsely, use fallacies, Arist.Ph.186a10, 239b5

παραλογισμός.definition: false reasoning, fallacy; weakness of reasoning power, Aristeas250

παραλογιστής.definition: one who cheats by false reckoning, Arist.EE1232a14; or by false reasoning, M.Ant.6.13, cf. Procl.Par.Ptol.225; cheat, Artem.4.57

παράλογος.definition: beyond reason, unreasonable, Plu.2.626e, etc.; App.BC2.146; Cleanth. ap. Arr.Epict.4.1.173. Adv. Plb.1.74.14, etc

παραλοξαίνομαι.definition: Pass., to be placed obliquely, Hp.Nat.Mul.40, Mul.2.141

παραλουργίς.definition: woman's garment edged with purple, Poll.7.56, Phot

παραλυκίζω.definition: to be changed and become salt, Antipho Soph.32

παραλυπέω.definition: grieve or trouble besides, . . no disease attacked them besides the plague, Th.2.51, cf. X.Vect.4.32, Thphr.CP1.7.8; annoy by a diversion, Th.4.89; . . Pl.Phd.65c; Plu.Per.35; the troublesome, the refractory, X.An.2.5…

παράλυσις.definition: secret or illicit undoing or; disabling of the nerves, paralysis, Thphr.Fr.11, Dsc.1.6, Ruf. ap. Orib.8.39.2, Gal.8.208; also of the eyes, i.e. nystagmus, Cels.6.6.36: generally, of the effect of strong wine, Com.Ades…

παραλυτρόομαι.definition: Pass., to be ransomed, name of a Comedy by Sotades, Ath.9.368a

παραλύω.definition: c. acc. rei, loose and take off, detach, Hdt.3.136 ; Ar.Fr.325; Plu.Ant.76:—Med., Id.Cleom.37; Id.2.646a:—Pass., Hdt.3.105

παραμαρτάνω.definition: err, trespass, Ar.Fr.692a, cf. Plu.2.89e, Hierocl.p.58A.: c. dat., damage, Ath.Mitt.30.327

παραμεθίημι.definition: let pass, Hp.Mul.1.67: c. gen. part., ib.25; ib.21

παραμείγνυμι.definition: and Ion. also in; c. acc. only, mix in, add by mixing, Hdt.1.203, 4.61; Hp.Morb.2.47, Mul.2.162; Alex.84:—Pass., Pl.R.415b

παραμελέω.definition: disregard, pay no heed to, Gorg.Pal.20, Th.1.25; Lys.9.1; X.Mem.2.2.14, etc. : abs., he recked little, Hdt.1.85; being negligent, Pl.R.555d; neglect a duty, Mitteis Chr.96 iii 4 :— Pass., to be slighted or abandoned, …

παραμετρέω.definition: measure one thing by another, compare; measure by a standard, Chrysipp.Stoic.3.188, Ph.1.147:—Pass., ib.92; supply a standard of measurement for, Plu.2.569c

παραμεύομαι.definition: Dor. form of will surpass the beauty of others, Pi.N.11.13: an Act. form Hsch

παραμηρίδιος.definition: along the thighs: armour for the thighs, cuisses, X.An.1.8.6; for horses, Id.Cyr.6.4.1, Arr.Tact.4.1

παραμήριον.definition: dagger, Just.Nov.85.4 (also Adj; inside of the thighs, Dsc.1.99, Ruf.Onom.119, Antyll. ap. Orib.10.31.1, Poll.2.188, Hsch. s.v

παραμιλλάομαι.definition: outvie, outdo, CIG2271.33 , J.BJ7.8.1; in a thing, Plb.12.10.4

παράμιλλος.definition: beyond rivalry, Astyd.Eleg.3; entering into competition, Iamb.Comm.Math.23

παραμιμνήσκομαι.definition: mention besides, make incidental mention of, c. gen. rei, Hdt.7.96,99, S.Tr.1124: abs., . . Phld.Ir.p.65 W.; cf. · Hsch

παραμολύνω.definition: aor. Pass. dub. sens. in Phld.Rh.2.27 S

παραμόνιμος.definition: poet. fem. Pi.P.7.18, cf; of slaves. trusty, X.Mem.2.4.5, prob. for ib.2.10.3; metaph. of a man, ib.3.11.11. Adv. Phryn.PSp.57 B

παράμονος.definition: poet. rarer form of foreg. , Plu.2.114f; Cat.Cod.Astr.8.207, cf. Vett.Val.292.30; Gp.1.12.32; Pi.N.8.17

παραμπέχω.definition: or cover with a cloak or robe; wrap a thing round as a cloak or disguise: metaph., use a cloak of words, E.Med.282:—Med., allege as a pretext, c. acc., Hp.Morb.Sacr.1

παραμπυκίζω.definition: bind with a headband, Ar.Lys.1316, in Lacon. form have one's hair so bound, Eust.1280.58

παραμυθία.definition: encouragement, exhortation, Pl.R.450d; consolation, Id.Ax.365a, Arr.Epict.1.1.18; diversion, distraction, Pl.Sph.224a

παραμύθιον.definition: address, exhortation, Pl.Lg.773e; assuagement, abatement of, S.El.130 ; of the fires of love, Theoc.23.7; Th.5.103; Pl.Lg.632e, cf. 704d; many consolations, Id.R.329e, cf. Phdr.240d, Phld.Mort.19; Epigr.Gr.298.7 , cf.…

παραμυκάομαι.definition: bellow beside or in answer, of thunder following on earthquake, A.Pr.1082

παραμφοδέω.definition: go astray, make a miscalculation, c. gen., Vett. Val.360.22

παραναβαίνω.definition: mount a chariot beside one, Callix.2

παραναβλαστάνω.definition: shoot or grow up beside, Ph.1.438: c. dat., ib.667

παραναγιγνώσκω.definition: later read beside; read publicly, Plb.2.12.4, al., LXX2 Ma.8.23, PGrenf.2.68.16 :—Pass., LXX3 Ma.1.12, cf. Ph.2.531

παραναγκάζω.definition: accomplish a thing by force, v.l. for in D.H.Lys.13. 2. Medic., force the ends of a bone together, Hp.Art.34

παρανάγω.definition: displace, v.l. in Hp.Mochl.4; remove, , Max. Tyr.16.3

παραναδύομαι.definition: Med., with aor. 2 and pf. Act., creep, crawl out, Plu.Alex.2

παραναιετάω.definition: dwell beside or near, c. acc. loci, S.Tr.635

παραναίω.definition: aor. 1 cause to dwell, settle; in Med., aor. 1 = . . D.P.776

παρανακύπτω.definition: emerge, come to light: hence, occur, Heracl. ap. Orib.48.8.2

παραναλίσκω.definition: or fut. spend amiss, waste, squander, throw away, D.Prooem.21; Id.13.4, cf. J.BJ3.7.13; ruin, ib.2.21.7:—Pass., of persons, to be sacrificed incidentally, Plu.Lys.28, cf. D.S.14.5; LXXNu.17.12: in Com., to be spent in…

παρανάλωμα.definition: useless expense, waste, Plu.Pyrrh.30, Cic.17; Ael.VH1.17; incidental waste, J.BJ4.5.2, 5.1.3; of persons, perishing incidentally, Aesop.345, cf. Demad.2; lest his death should involve that of . . , Ph.2.519; ib.600

παραναπείθω.definition: persuade one to change one's mind, BGU1141.40

παραναπίπτω.definition: fall back on one side, of dogs copulating, Artem.1.79

παρανατέλλω.definition: rise or appear beside, of stars, Ptol.Tetr.77, Vett. Val.8.15, Porph. ap. Eus.PE3.4, Serv. ad Virg. G.1.218; poet. of a building, AP9.614

παρανατολή.definition: simultaneous rising, in pl., Eudem. ap. Theon.Sm.p.200 H., Cat.Cod.Astr.8.207

παραναφωνέω.definition: in Pass., to be parenthetical, Sch.Il.Oxy.1086.43

παρανέομαι.definition: go or pass by, A.R.2.357, Ath.Mitt.17.272

παρανευρίζομαι.definition: to be ill strung, Arist.HA581a20, Pr.902b34

παρανεύω.definition: incline to one side, Hippiatr.33; AnatoliusinCat.Cod.Astr.8.188

παρανέω.definition: swim beside, Luc.DMar.8.2; Philostr.VA1.23: abs., Ael.NA9.38

παρανικάω.definition: subdue to or for evil, pervert, A.Ch.600

παρανίσσομαι.definition: aor. 1 = pass beside, near, or beyond, c. acc., h.Ap.430, A.R.2.1030

παρανίστημι.definition: fut. set up beside; Med. with aor. 2 Act., stand up beside, J.BJ2.21.1

παρανοέω.definition: to be deranged or senseless, lose one's wits, E.IA838, Ar.Nu.1480, Lys.Fr.74, Arist.Ath.56.6

παρανοίγνυμι.definition: and open at the side or a little, set ajar, D.25.28; Placit.4.22.1 ; half- closed eyes, Gal.18.300, cf. Dem. Ophth. ap. Aët.7.98: metaph., D.H.Rh.10.13

παρανομέω.definition: commit a crime or outrage, Antipho5.15, And.4.21, Aeschin.l.c., Arist.Pol.1307b31; Hdt.7.238, cf. Lys.3.17; D.59.126; D.S.16.61; also Plu.2.166b; Th.8.108; act illegally in public matters, Id.2.37:—Pass., a return ill…

παρανόμημα.definition: unlawful act, transgression, Th.7.18, Chrysipp.Stoic.3.71, Plb.23.10.2 , Plu.Cat.Mi.47 , Porph.Abst.1.2 , POxy.1119.10

παρανομία.definition: transgression of law, decency, or order, Antipho5.12, Th.4.98, Pl.R.537e, etc. ; loose and disorderly habits of life, Th.6.15, cf. 28; Plb.3.6.13; D.H.8.4; illegality, personified, Plb.18.54.10

παράνομος.definition: lawless, violent, E.Ba.997; of things, unlawful, Th.2.17; Ar.Th.684; Id.Pl.967; Pl.Ap.31e; illegality, Aeschin.3.197. Adv. illegally, Antipho5.94, Th.3.65; opp. Pl.Plt.302e: Comp. And.4.22: Sup. Antipho5.8

παρανυκτερεύω.definition: pass the night on guard, Plu.Pel.35, Arat.8,al

παρανύμφιος.definition: = sq., v.l. in Poll.3.40; correct acc. to Eust.652.41

παράνυμφος.definition: bridegroom's friend or best man; fem., bridesmaid, one of the dramatis personae in Ar.Ach., cf. Hsch.,EM145.31, Moer.p.269P

παραξηραίνω.definition: cause to dry up, in Pass., Hippiatr.9, 10

παραξιφίς.definition: knife worn beside the sword, dirk, LXX2 Ki.5.8, D.S.5.33, Str.3.3.6, Plu.Arat.25

παραξόνιος.definition: beside the axle: linchpin, Phryn.PSp.100 B.: metaph., expld. by Sch. audacious, venturesome quibbles, Ar.Ra.819

παραξονίτης.definition: linchpin, Phryn.PSp.100 B; nave of a wheel, Sch.A.Th.153

παραξύω.definition: = I.1, prob. in J.BJ3.10.9; Anon.Geog.Comp.50, cf. Procop.Aed.2.6; AP6.65 : metaph., graze the edge of vulgarity, Longin.31.2

παραπαιδαγωγέω.definition: help to train or form, Plu.2.321b; improve, reform gradually, Luc.Nigr.12

παραπαίζω.definition: jest by the way, Sch.Ar.Pl.811; epith. of Dionysus

παράπαισμα.definition: madness, Oenom. ap. Eus.PE5.25 :—in form Hsch

παραπαίω.definition: strike on the side, strike falsely; intr., strike a false note: metaph., to be infatuated, lose one's wits, Id.Pr.1056 ; Ar.Pl.508, cf. Pax90 ; Pl.Smp.173e, cf. Plb.12.8.1; Plu.2.963f; to be in error, Phld.Sign.32; co…

παραπάσσω.definition: Att. sprinkle beside or into, Thphr.CP5.6.10 ; Plu.2.954b, cf. Hp.Ulc.21, Damocr. ap. Gal.13.944; Dsc.3.23

παραπειράομαι.definition: make trial of one, so as to ascertain his will, . . Pi.O.8.3

παραπελεκάομαι.definition: Pass., to be hewn at the side with an axe, Thphr.HP4.16.2, CP5.4.7

παραπεμπτέος.definition: that must be dismissed, rejected; one must reject, Id.Adv.195.8; one must omit, Phld.Hom.p.60 O., Porph.Abst.4.10

παράπεμψις.definition: escorting, conveyance, of a person, D.S.34/35.39 codd

παραπέρνημι.definition: Aeol. sell at a reduced price, Bechtel Aeolica p.33 ; cf

παραπετάννυμαι.definition: the Bird hovers before it with outspread wings, Arat.312

παραπέτομαι.definition: poet. Call.Epigr.33.6: aor. 2; fly past, of specks before the eyes, Gal.1.363

παραπήγνυμι.definition: of Gramm., add by way of note, Eust.190.33, 300.22, etc; Pass., with pf. 2 to be fixed beside, of spears, Il.3.135; Hp.Fract.13; of the pegs in a I, Berl.Sitzb. 1904.102

παραπηδάω.definition: overleap, transgress, Aeschin.3.192. II. leap upon, of hounds, X.Cyn.6.22: metaph., Plu.Pomp.6; . . Crantor ap.S.E.M.11.53

παραπιέζω.definition: press from one side, press down, S.E.M.7.192, cf. Archig. ap. Orib.8.1.18, Heliod. ap. eund.50.9.3

παραπιεσμός.definition: = foreg., Heliod. ap. Orib.45.9.2, cf. Orib.46.17.1

παραπικραίνω.definition: embitter, provoke, c. acc., LXXEz.20.21; rebel against, ib.3 Ki.13.26: abs., ib.Ez.24.3, al. ; ib.La.1.20, cf. Ep.Hebr.3.16

παραπίμπραμαι.definition: Pass., to be inflamed, X.Eq.1.4, Thphr.Sud.15, Gal.11.234

παραπιπράσκω.definition: sell at a reduced price, BSA23.73; sell in addition, in Pass., ib.990

παραπίπτω.definition: Math., as Pass. of to be applied, Archim.Con.Sph.2; fall in one's way, Hdt.8.87, cf. Lys.27.15; X.Cyr.1.2.10; . . PCair.Zen.469.5 ; come in time to aid, Plb.31.5.2, etc.; as opportunity offered, X.Eq.Mag.7.4, cf. Th.4…

παραπλαγιάζω.definition: go obliquely, v.l. in LXX1 Ki.23.26, Hsch.:—Med., present oneself obliquely to . . , Sch.Od.5.440

παραπλανάομαι.definition: Pass., = foreg., Sch.A.Eu.104: intr. in Act., Sch.Ar.Eq.806

παράπλασμα.definition: piece of coloured wax stuck on; monster, Suid. s.v

παραπλασμός.definition: change of grammatical form; wax used to stop the holes of flutes, Hsch

παραπλάσσω.definition: Att. transform, in fut. Med; Med., append, S.E.M.5.70, cf. Phld.Rh.1.6S

παράπλαστος.definition: counterfeit, Sosith.2.4 ap. Tz.H.2.596; forged, BGU592.10

παράπλεγμα.definition: basket-work for a chariot, Hsch. s.v

παραπλέκω.definition: braid or weave in, Hp.Vict.1.14: metaph; braid or curl along the forehead, Poll.2.35; becurl himself, Plu.2.785e:—Med., Ael.NA16.11; Poll.l.c

παραπλεύριος.definition: at or in the side of anything, Tz.H.5.843

παραπλευρόω.definition: cover on the sides with a thing, Philostr.VA3.35

παραπλήξ.definition: stricken sideways or aslant; metaph., = mad, Ar.Pl.242, X.Oec.1.13, Demetr.Eloc.275

παραπληξία.definition: Ion. hemiplegia (opp; derangement, madness, LXXDe.28.28, al., Ph.2.556, Oenom. ap. Eus.PE5.22

παραπληρόω.definition: Gramm., fill up, of an expletive particle, Trypho ap.A.D.Conj.247.25; Dam.Pr.300

παραπλήρωμα.definition: expletive, words; Geom., complement of a parallelogram, Euc.1.43, etc

παραπλήσσω.definition: Att. strike at the side, of a harper, Philostr.Im.1.10:—Pass., to be palsy-stricken: hence, to be deranged, mad, Ar.Lys.831, Ec.139, etc. ; E.HF935; Plu.Aem.34; to be astonished at . . , Agatharch.103

παραποδίζω.definition: entangle the feet, fetter, tether: hence, generally, hinder, impede, Plb.2.28.8, 18.31.6:—Pass., to be entangled, hampered, Pl.Lg.652b, Ep.330b, Plb.16.4.10, Gal.9.575; Metrod.Herc.831.5; or S.E.M.1.171, 193; Hld.10.30

παραπόδιος.definition: poet. at the feet, i.e. imminent, Pi.N.9.38

παραποδισμός.definition: hindering, Artem.3.42, cf. MenoIatr.6.9, Gal.19.386; Hierocl.p.21 A., Iamb.Protr.21

παραποδύομαι.definition: Med., pull off one's clothes, strip so as to compare oneself with others, Pl.Tht.162b

παραποιέω.definition: make falsely, make false measures and weights, D.S.1.78; forgers, Just.Nov.73Praef.; having got a false seal made, Th.1.132 ; falsify his record, Philostr.VA2.30. 2. alter slightly, Paus.5.10.1, Jul.Or.2.70a; e. g. Ar…

παραποίησις.definition: imitation, adulteration, Gal.14.62.al.; forgery Just.Nov.73Praef.; slight alteration, Phoeb.Fig.1.3, cf. Eust.1403.60

παραπολαύω.definition: share the fruits of, Ph.2.15; J.BJ2.16.4; Luc.Alex.45; Dam.Pr.7

παραπόλλυμι.definition: destroy, consume or spend to no purpose, waste, lose, Plu.2.439e, cf. Gal.UP12.5; Charito1.7; D.C.74.2:—more freq. in Med. and Pass., with pf. 2 perish, Ar.V.1228; Dionys. Com.2.35; D.21.91; Men.835; Epicur.Sent. Vat.…

παραπομπή.definition: convoying, Decr. ap. D.18.73; escort, convoy, Arist.Oec.1351b24; Plb.30.9.13, 15.5.7; D.S.20.45, cf. PSI5.446.12 : pl., Ph.1.592; of a funeral procession, IG12.239.32 ; of athletes, being escorted by a body of support…

παραπόμπιμος.definition: attending, escorting, epith. of Hermes, Sch.E.Med.759

παραπορεύομαι.definition: with fut. Med. and aor. Pass., go beside; go past, pass by, PPetr.2p.36 ; Plb.3.99.5; Id.3.14.6; Id.2.27.5; Ev.Marc.2.23 , cf. 9.30; of stars, pass through the zodiac, Cat.Cod.Astr.8.210

παραπορθμεύω.definition: convey goods across a lake, CIG4302a

παραπράσσω.definition: help in doing, S.Aj.261; act unjustly, esp. exact money illegally, Plu.Agis16:—Pass., Wilcken Chr.238.6 , etc

παραπρεσβεία.definition: faithless or dishonest embassy, D.21.5; title of speeches by D. and Aeschin.; Phld.Rh.2.224 S

παραπρεσβεύω.definition: execute an embassy faithlessly or dishonestly, D.19.191, SIG167.5 ; Aeschin.2.94:—more freq. in Med. Pl.Lg.941a, Isoc.18.22; D.24.127

παραπροσποιέομαι.definition: dissemble, Cod.Just.1.4.34.15; pretend ignorance of the law, Just.Nov.113.3

παραπρύτανις.definition: perh. colleague or assessor of a CIG 3168

παράπταισμα.definition: f.l. for in Oenom. ap. Eus.PE5.25

παραπταίω.definition: stumble by the way, blunder, Placit.5.20.5 , Al.De.22.1

παράπτομαι.definition: Med., apply, of ointments, Asclep. ap; Med., touch in passing or slightly, Men.66.4, Plu.Cleom.37; Sor.1.108

παράπτωμα.definition: false step, slip, blunder; transgression, trespass, LXXEz.14.13,al., Ev.Matt.6.14, Ep.Gal.6.1, al

παράπτωσις.definition: falling beside, lying side by; falling from the right way, Plb.15.23.5: abs., = I, Id.16.20.5, LXXJe.22.21, Phld.Lib.p.17 O.; grammatical mistake, S.E.M.1.210

παραπυΐσκω.definition: impers. in infin., suppuration begins, Hp.Epid.4.11

παραπωμάζω.definition: cover with a lid, v.l. for Arist.Juv.470a9

παραρθρέω.definition: to be partially dislocated; trans., dislocate, v.l. in Pl.Ax.367b

παραριθμέω.definition: reckon in, PSI6.596.5 (iii; count over, check items in an inventory, PMich.Zen.31.12 , IG11.163 Bg19 , SIG874 A5 , v.l. in LXXTo.9.5

παραρράπτομαι.definition: Pass., to be sewn as a fringe along; of bandages, to be sewn on, Gal.18.917

παραρρέγχω.definition: snore beside or near, Lucil.Fr.1223 Marx

παραρρέω.definition: slip off or out, . . S.Ph.653; whom it did not slip off, X.An.4.4.11: metaph., many points escaped you, Pl.Lg.781a; having disappeared from memory, Gp.Prooem.4

παραρρήγνυμι.definition: metaph., break through, violate, Them.Or.15.190b, cf. Or.16.212d

παράρρηξις.definition: breaking of a line of battle, Arr.An.2.11.7

παραρριγόω.definition: 2sg. fut. freeze beside or near, AP5.42

παραρρίπτω.definition: later LXXPs.83.10; c. acc. rei, hazard, Id.Fr.555.5; expose them . . , D.S.13.79

παραρρυπόω.definition: mark with the in pf. part. Pass. Hsch

παραρτάω.definition: hang alongside, to, or upon, Ael.NA1.2; Plu.2.844e:—Pass., Id.Ant.4; to have it hung by one's side, Ael.NA5.3; Hdn.3.14.8; Luc.Peregr.15; parts appended, Artemo12

παραρτέομαι.definition: Ion. Verb only Med; trans., fit out for oneself, get ready, was engaged in preparing, Hdt.7.20, cf. 142, 8.76, 9.42; so Arr.Ind.27.10

παράρτυσις.definition: preparing, M.Ant. ap; seasoning, Ph.1.389, 604, etc

παραρτύω.definition: of food, season, Id.2.477,483; Med., get ready, Plu.Luc.7

παρασαλεύω.definition: shake to the foundations, sap, undermine, metaph., Ph.2.69 ; Just.Nov.135 1 Ep.; upset, disturb an agreement, PLond.1.113i51 :— Pass., PLips.34r19

παρασαρόω.definition: sweep beside or at the side, Hsch

παράσεισμα.definition: swinging of the arms in running, Hp.Vict.2.64

παρασείω.definition: shake at the side, swing one's arms in running, Arist.IA705a17: without Id.EN1123b31; Id.Pr.881b6, cf. Thphr.Char.3.6; hurried to the spot, prob. in UPZ119.30

παρασεύω.definition: drive past, aor. Hsch.:—Pass., rush past, Q.S.2.214, 8.44

παρασημαίνομαι.definition: Med., set one's seal beside another's; put one's seal on, seal up, D.42.2 ; . . of the witnesses, put their seals on the will of the deceased, Id.28.5

παρασημασία.definition: indication, Ptol.Tetr.93, Geog.2.1.7; honourable mention, Plb.22.20.1

παρασημειόομαι.definition: make a marginal note, POxy.34.14 (ii; countersign, BGU82.11

παρασημείωσις.definition: passing mention, Dsc.Ther.26; indication, Philum. ap. Aët.5.127

παράσημον.definition: marginal mark or note; distinguishing mark, in various senses : ensign of a ship, with the Dioscuri as the sign or emblem, Act.Ap.28.11, cf. Plu.2.162a; of a city, ib.399f; of patricians and plebeians, Id.Cor.20; Id.A…

παράσημος.definition: marked amiss or falsely; of words and phrases, false, incorrect, AP11.144 ; Gal.Libr.Propr.17; eccentricity of style, Demetr.Eloc.208

παρασιγάω.definition: pass by in silence, Str.12.3.26; Ion. Hp.Ep.19

παρασιτέω.definition: board and lodge with, Pl.La.179b; play the parasite, from the time I became a parasite, Alex.195, cf. Axionic.6.1, Diph.63, Luc.Par.4; Alex.201.1; Phld. Herc.223; Socr.Ep.1.4

παρασίτιον.definition: meeting-place of Crates Gramm. ap. Ath.6.235d, Poll.6.35

παράσιτος.definition: one who eats at the table of another; of priests who had their meals at the public expense, Clitodem.11, Polem.Hist.78

παρασιωπάω.definition: pass over in silence, omit mention of; keep silence, Plb.24.10.7, D.S.30.9: abs., LXXGe.34.5, al., Plb.22.4.16, al. ; stand by in silence, of the chorus, Hsch. s.v. also Id

παρασιώπησις.definition: passing over in silence, a; metaph., intermission, Sch.Ptol.Tetr.161

παρασκευάζω.definition: fut. X.Cyr.1.6.18 (but 3sg; provide, procure, contrive, Antipho1.28; Th.3.49; Pl.Smp.188d, etc. ; Lys.1.28: in bad sense, get up, D.28.17; v. infr. B. 1.2

παρασκευαστέος.definition: to be prepared, Nicostr. ap; one must prepare or provide, Pl.R.467b; . . Id.Grg.480e; X.Eq.Mag.1.7; Id.Mem.1.7.2

παρασκευή.definition: preparation, Hdt.9.82; with Preps., of set purpose, by arrangement, Antipho6.19, Lys.31.30; a pitched battle, Th.5.56; Id.1.133; Antipho5.22; at short notice, offhand, Th.4.8; Id.2.80; were engaged in preparing for it…

παρασκηνάω.definition: or pitch one's tent beside, X.An.3.1.28, in aor

παρασκήνιον.definition: in sg., use of one of the chorus as a fourth actor, Poll.4.109

παρασκηνόω.definition: throw a wide garment like a tent or canopy over one, v.l. in A.Eu.634

παρασκιρτάω.definition: leap beside or near, of fish, Ael.NA13.2 leap upon . . , Plu.Mar.38

παρασκώπτω.definition: intervene with jests, h.Cer.203; Plu.Cic.38, cf. Demetr.28

παρασοβέω.definition: scare away birds, Arist.Mir.841b22, as v.l; intr., stalk haughtily past, Plu.Cat.Ma.24

παρασοφίζομαι.definition: apply art wrongly, refine overmuch; c. acc., wish to be wiser than the physician, Arist.Rh.1375b21; Agatharch.49

παρασπάς.definition: shoot torn off and planted, Thphr.HP2.1.1, Gp.10.3.4 and 5; opp. Thphr.HP2.2.4

παράσπασις.definition: = sq., gloss on Sch.Th.1.122; dragging away of victims by beasts, Porph.Abst.1.10

παρασπείρω.definition: sow among, Thphr.CP3.10.3 , PCair.Zen. 269.35 , BGU591.14 : metaph., in Pass., Pl.Ax.366a; to be diffused over, Sch.Epicur.Ep.1p.21U., cf. Nat.Herc. 1420 Fr.1; to be interspersed in, Gal.1.345; Id.Nat.Fac.2.8; J.BJ7.3…

παρασπίζω.definition: bear a shield beside, i.e. fight beside, stand by, E.Ion1528; D.H.3.19: abs., E.Ph.1435: metaph., Id.HF1099: Arith., of numbers, place beside or on the flanks, Iamb.in Nic.p.40 P

παρασπιστής.definition: shield-bearer, companion in arms, E.El.886, Ph.1165, Cyc.6

παρασπόνδειος.definition: at or for a libation: , Ph.2.484

παρασπονδέω.definition: break a compact or treaty, D.7.36, 18.71; break faith with them, Plb.1.7.8, cf. Plu.Sull.3; IG 22.687.32:—Pass., suffer by a breach of faith, Plb.3.15.7, J.BJ1.19.4; Id.Vit.59

παρασπόνδημα.definition: breach of faith, IG7.411 , Plb.2.58.4, Plu.Caes.22, App.Gall.18

παρασπόνδησις.definition: breaking of faith, Plb.2.7.5; Str.7.1.4; App.BC2.110

παράσπονδος.definition: contrary to a compact or; of persons, breaker of treaties, forsworn, Lys.12.74, J.AJ10.8.2, Heraclit.Incred.15

παραστάζω.definition: drop upon, Hp.Mul.1.78, 84, D.S.2.4:—Pass., Menemach. ap. Orib.7.22.3
