παραστάς.definition: prop. anything that; space enclosed between the vestibule or entrance of a temple or house, in pl., E.Ph.415, IT1159, X.Hier.11.2, IG22.1672.131, 186, Poll.7.122: also in sg., E.Andr.1121, IG12.372.73, SIG307.12 , Sup…

παράστασις.definition: putting aside, removal, esp. relegation, banishment, Pl.Lg.855c; i.e. to ostracize them, Arist.Pol.1308b19; Hsch

παραστατέω.definition: stand by or near, abs., A.Ag.877

παραστάτης.definition: one who stands by or near; one's comrade on the flank , Hdt.6.117, cf. X.Cyr.3.3.59, 8.1.10; Polyaen.2.10.4

παρασταυρόω.definition: enclose by palisades, Anon. ap. Suid

παραστείχω.definition: aor. go past, pass by, c. acc; transgress, Herod.5.50

παραστέλλω.definition: draw aside, of a curtain, Hld.10.28; reduce a swelling, Hp.Epid.5.69

παραστίζω.definition: prick, mark the names of defaulters, Hsch., cf. Id. s.v

παραστιχίδιον.definition: Dim. of sq., v.l. in D.L.8.78

παραστιχίς.definition: anything written at the side, esp. = Id.5.93, Gell. 14.6.4; of a magical formula, PMag.Leid.W.21.22

παραστορέννυμι.definition: lay flat, lay low, . . Ar.Eq.481:—Pass., Hsch. :— so aor. J.BJ7.9.1

παραστοχάζομαι.definition: aim at, S.E.P.3.222 codd., cf. Herod.Med. ap. Orib.5.30.25: abs., estimate, Sor.1.20

παραστρατεύομαι.definition: march with an army, of camp- followers, Anon. ap. Suid. s.v

παραστρατηγέω.definition: issue orders interfering with those of; Pass., to be out-manoeuvred, Arist.Ath.6.2

παραστρατοπεδεύω.definition: encamp beside or opposite to, Plb.2.6.3; D.H.2.41: abs., Plb.3.17.4, Polyaen.5.2.10, etc. :—Med., c. dat., ChioEp.3.1

παραστρέφω.definition: turn asiae, alter, Pl.Cra.418a:—Pass., to; metaph., turn aside, esp. for the worse, pervert, E.Fr.491.3; Arist.Pol.1342a22

παραστροφή.definition: distortion, Erasistr. ap; selvage of a robe, Gal.18.776, Hsch. s.v

παραστύφω.definition: to be rather astringent, Diph.Siph. ap. Ath.3.73a, Sor.1.95, 2.13

παρασυγγραφέω.definition: break contract with, D.56.28: abs., ib.34, PPetr.3p.161 ; PTeb.105.34 , etc

παρασυκοφαντέω.definition: cavil at, Ph.1.340: abs., find fault, Plu.2.73b

παρασυμβάλλομαι.definition: Pass., to be compared, to be like, LXXPs.48.12, 20

παρασύμβαμα.definition: in the technical language of the Stoics, secondary accident or circumstance, Chrysipp.Stoic.2.59: Gramm., impersonal verb governing a dative, A.D.Pron.115.12, Synt.300.4,6

παρασυνάγχη.definition: inflammation of the muscles of one side of the throat, Gal.8.248, Cael.Aur.CP3.1

παρασυνάπτομαι.definition: Pass., to be connected by a causal particle, CrinisStoic.3.269; Ph.1.321, cf. A.D.Synt.8.10

παρασύνθετος.definition: formed from a compound, A.D.Synt.330.5, EM131.42, 155.56, 493.18. Adv. An.Ox.3.182

παρασύνθημα.definition: sign which accompanies the password, Aen.Tact.25.1, Plb.9.13.9, Onos.26

παρασυνίσταμαι.definition: to be at one's side, as an amanuensis, Sammelb.5676.5

παρασύρω.definition: fut. Hsch.:—Pass., pf; sweep off the oars of the ships by brushing past them, Plb.16.4.14, cf. D.S.13.16 : intr., grazing it obliquely, Hp.VC11

παρασφάζω.definition: wound in the side, Anon. ap. Suid. s.v

παρασφαλίζω.definition: fortify next in order, in Med., LXXNe.3.8

παρασφήνιον.definition: side-block for wedging, IG11.159 A 38 , PCair.Zen.759

παρασφηνόω.definition: wedge in, Sor.2.31 , Hsch. s.v. , Aspasia ap. Aët.16.22

παρασφραγίζω.definition: set a seal upon:—Med., Telesp.38 H; counterfeit a seal, Hsch. s.v

παρασχηματίζω.definition: change from the true form, transform; in Gramm., form from another word by a slight change, Porph.in Cat.69.20, Sch.Ar.Ach.424, etc.; dub. sens. in Phld.Rh.2.97 S.; forming a derivative word from Hierocl.p.50 A.:—Pass…

παρασχηματισμός.definition: formation by a slight change; malposition of the foetus, Paul. Aeg.3.76

παρασχίζω.definition: rip up lengthwise, slit up, Hdt.2.86; open fish, Alex.133.4:—Pass., D.S.1.91; Polyaen.6.49

παρασχιστής.definition: or or one who rips; mutilators, Plb.13.6.4

παρασχοίνισμα.definition: cord drawn beside or along, Poll.7.160

παρασῴζω.definition: keep a criminal for delivery to the officer of the law, PLond.2.422.1

παραταιναρίζω.definition: celebrate the Taenaria like the Laconians, Hermipp.32

παρατάνυσμα.definition: anything stretched out, covering, Aq., Sm.Ex.27.16

παρατάσσω.definition: Att. place or post side by side; Med. and Pass., stand prepared, Pl.Prt.333e; Epicur.Fr.489: c. inf., refuse obstinately, Arr.Epict.1.5.3, cf. M.Ant.8.48

παρατείνω.definition: stretch on the rack, torture, Plu.2.135d: metaph., X.Cyr.1.3.11:—Pass., to be tortured, Pl.Smp.207b; to be worn out, c. part., X.Mem.3.13.6; I am nigh dead with eating dainties, Ar.Fr.506.1; . . Pl.Euthd.303b; . . Id.…

παρατέμνω.definition: fut. Lacon. Ar.Lys.116cod; cut amiss, make a wrong cut, Thphr.HP6.3.2

παρατεχνολογέω.definition: introduce incidentally into a treatise, Demetr.Eloc.178

παρατηρέω.definition: observe carefully, Arist.Rh.1405b33:—Med , observe religiously, Ep.Gal.4.10; J.AJ14.10.25: generally, D.C.53.10

παρατήρημα.definition: observation, D.H.Amm.2.17; condition to be observed, Alex.Aphr.in Top.515.9

παρατήρησις.definition: observance of rules, etc., D.T.629.21; remark, note, Longin.23.2, cf. Sch.Ar.Ra.1258; bare notice, A.D.Pron.41.8

παρατίλλω.definition: fut. Ar.Eq.373:—pluck the hair from; Med., pull up weeds, Gp.2.38.2

παρατίλτρια.definition: female slave who plucked the hairs from her mistress's body, Cratin.256, Philostr.VA4.27

παρατιτρώσκω.definition: wound besides: metaph., do violence to, Men.Prot.p.116D.; violate, Lyd.Mag.1.41

παρατολμάω.definition: pf. to be foolhardy, Plb.Fr.66; overbold phrases, Longin.8.2

παρατραγῳδέω.definition: use mock-tragic style, Poll.10.92; ut paratragoedat carnufex! Plaut.Pseud.707

παρατρέφω.definition: aor. 1 Hdn. :—Pass; bring up alike, Hdn.3.15.5

παράτρητος.definition: pierced at the side, of a flute used for mournful airs, Poll.4.81; an injecting tube, Ruf. ap. Orib.8.24.62; Antyll.ib.50.3.3

παρατριβή.definition: rubbing against one another; metaph., friction, Plb.2.36.5; Ath.14.626e

παρατρίβω.definition: rub beside or alongside; rub on or against, Ael.NA17.44; Pass., rub oneself against, Arist.HA540b12; dub. in Sor.1.7

παράτριμμα.definition: abrasion caused by friction in riding or walking, intertrigo, Dsc.1.39, Antyll. ap. Orib.10.24.10, Gal.13.395, al

παράτριψις.definition: rubbing against one another, friction, Epicur.Ep.2p.45U. , cf. Arist.Mu.395b5, Thphr.Lap.45, Ph.Bel.78.10, D.S.3.36, Placit.3.3.11 , M.Ant.6.13; Chrysipp. ap. S.E.P.1.70

παρατροπή.definition: turning away, means of averting; slight alteration, ib.376a, cf. Suid. s.v. f.l. for A.D.Synt.167.3; TryphoTrop.Praef

παράτροπος.definition: turned aside : turned from the right; strange, unusual, Opp.H.1.515, 4.18, cf. Plu.Lys.12

παρατροχάζω.definition: poet. for run past; pass by or over, leave unnoticed, APl.4.169: metaph., Puchstein Epigr.Gr.p.10

παρατρυγάω.definition: pluck grapes, Aristaenet.1.3: metaph., of love, Id.2.7

παρατρύζω.definition: coo beside or near, Hsch., Phot

παρατρώγω.definition: fut. Suet. Galb.4: aor. Hp.Epid.5.86:—nibble at, take a bite of, Hp. l. c.; Ar.Ra.988, cf. Pax415: metaph., August. ap. Suet. l. c.; Philostr.VS2.15.1

παρατρωπάω.definition: poet. for . . turn away the anger of the gods . . , Il.9.500

παρατυπόομαι.definition: counterfeit, Poll.8.27; to be constantly changing one's method, Sor.1.4

παρατυπωτικός.definition: misrepresenting as by an illusory copy, S.E.M.8.67, Gal.7.107. Adv. ib.104, 8.225

παραυγάζω.definition: present the appearance of; Med., shine, of the sun, Str.2.1.18:— Pass., to be illuminated, Id.2.5.42

παραυλέω.definition: play the flute beside, or play it ill, Poll.4.67

πάραυλος.definition: dwelling beside; dub. sens. in Michel832.18

παραύξησις.definition: waxing, Gem.6.29; progressive increase of parallel series, Vett. Val.295.6

παραυχενίζω.definition: bend the neck aside, cut the throat, Hsch. , Phot

παραφαιρέω.definition: c. gen., detract from, v.l. in Artem.3 Pr

παραφάσσω.definition: feel gently with the finger, Hp.Nat.Mul.6:—Med., Id.Mul.1.13:—hence interior of the pudenda muliebria, ib.2.171, cf. Gal.19.128

παραφέρω.definition: poet. fut. S.OC1675; bring forward, allege, cite, Antipho3.4.8, cf. PFlor.48.8 ; Hdt.9.26; E.IA981, cf. S.OC1675 ; Aeschin.1.126, cf. 132; . . D.H.7.27; Eust.ad D.P.306, cf. PAmh.2.81.12 , etc

παραφθέγγομαι.definition: add a qualification, in replying; say casually, let drop, Hyp.Eux.32; . . Is.8.23; . . Plb.28.17.13; Philostr.VA1.19

παράφθεγμα.definition: qualification added; incidental remark, Aristid.Or.28 tit

παραφθορά.definition: corruption, A.D.Adv.164.24; of music, Plu.2.1131f; of language, Hermog.Meth.3, St.Byz. s.v. Eust.1936.23

παραφίημι.definition: put out at the side, Thphr.HP7.4.12; release, discharge from service, BGU1011 iii 10 , PGen. 51.17

παραφλυαρέω.definition: keep on chattering, Gal.18.763, Eun.Hist.p.265 D

παραφορά.definition: Ion. Dor. going; movement to and fro, Sor.1.73: pl., Id.2.14

παράφορος.definition: borne aside, carried away; reeling, staggering, E.Hec.1050; Plu.2.501d; of a drunkard, Luc.Vit. Auct.12; Corn.ND30: c. inf., unsteady for sowing seed, Pl.Lg.775d

παραφορτίζομαι.definition: cram as an additional load into, Plu.2.8e, cf. Poll.2.139

παραφράζω.definition: say the same thing in other words, paraphrase, Ph.2.140; Hermog.Prog.4, cf. Gal.15.467; Eust.1406.19: abs., Hermog.Meth.24, cf. Gal.5.678; Eust.239.23

παραφράσσω.definition: Att. barricade, Hdn.4.1.5, etc. :—Pass., Plb.10.46.3, . . Hdn.3.3.2

παραφρονέω.definition: to be beside oneself, deranged; to be delirious, v.l. in Hp.Prog.10

παραφρουρέω.definition: keep guard beside, guards the frontier beyond the Douro, Str.3.4.20:—Pass., Hld.8.3

παραφρυγανίζω.definition: bank up, revet a canal with brushwood, PPetr.3p.108 :—hence Subst. ib.p.100, PTeb.180 , prob. in PCair.Zen.296.3,19

παραφρύγομαι.definition: Pass., metaph., go into raptures, Eun.VSp.503 B

παραφρυκτωρέω.definition: make secret signals to the enemy, Din.Fr.9.3

παραφυάς.definition: in plants, sucker, off shoot, opp. Thphr.HP2.2.4, cf. 1Enoch26.1: metaph., Arist.EN1096a21, cf.Ph.1.330

παραφυλακή.definition: guard, garrison, Plb.2.58.1,4.17.9; keeping securely, safeguarding, D.S.17.71, cf. Peripl.M.Rubr.19, POxy.2121.75 ; watchfulness, Hierocl.in CA10p.436M

παραφυλακίτης.definition: soldier of a garrison, OGI338.17 , IGRom.4.896 , CIG4366x

παραφυλάσσω.definition: Att. watch beside, guard; watch, observe narrowly, . . Pl.Plt.297a; . . Democr.87; . X.Lac.4.4; . . watch for a time at which. . , Plu.2.775e; keep one in sight, of a dog following and watching a person, ib.969f

παραφύω.definition: with fut. and aor. 1, produce at the side; Pass., with pf. and aor. 2 Act., grow beside or at the side, Hdt.2.92, Arist.PA658a26, Thphr.HP3.17.3, Plu.Dem.31, Plot.5.2.2; Ael.VH3.1; Men.407; Anaxil.22.13; Gal.18.980, c…

παραφωνέω.definition: interrupt and say, Plu.2.183c; gloss on Hsch., Phot

παραχάραγμα.definition: perh. false coinage, Supp.Epigr.3.565.17 : metaph., Hippiatr.115

παραχαράσσω.definition: Att. re-stamp, i.e. re-; esp. debase the currency, D.Chr.31.24:—Pass., Harp.s.v

παραχειμάζω.definition: pf. part. Act.Ap.28.11:—winter at a place, Hyp.Fr.260, D.34.8, 56.30, Peripl.M.Rubr.32, etc.; Plu.Sert.3

παραχειμασία.definition: wintering in a place, Plb.3.35.1, SIG762.16 , D.S.14.38, Act.Ap.27.12; D.S.20.28

παραχειρογραφέω.definition: violate a written agreement, PLond.2.359.1 , PFay.42 a ii 14 , POxy.2112.19 :—hence Subst. PGnom.218

παραχελῳίτης.definition: dweller by the Achelous, Str.9.5.10 :— fem. , country along the Achelous, Id.10.2.19

παραχέω.definition: pour on, Gal.6.328; of solids, . . Hdt.1.185

παραχορήγημα.definition: part of a subordinate chorus; part taken by a fourth actor, Poll.4.110

παραχράομαι.definition: deal wrongly or unworthily with them; treat with contempt, disregard, c. acc., Id.1.108, 4.159, 8.20: part. abs., of combatants, fighting without thought of life, setting nothing by their life, Id.7.223

παραχρίω.definition: daub, Hippon.50, cf. Suid. s.v. to be used for ointment, Gal.12.183

παράχρωσις.definition: use of the chromatic scale; colouring, metaph. of character, Simp.in Cat.216.5

παράχυσις.definition: pouring in, i.e. fraudulent watering of wine, BCH50.214

παραχύτης.definition: one who pours in, esp. who; prob. attendant at the religious ceremony PCair.Zen. 176.38

παραχώννυμι.definition: throw up beside, Hdt.1.185; bank up

παραχωρέω.definition: fut. D.23.105, later LXX2; give way, yield, submit, to one, Pl.Prt.336b; in respect of . . , ib.c. c. acc. cogn., should concede this, Arist.de An.410b25: c. acc. et dat., Pl.Lg.959e

παραχώρησις.definition: retiring. Str.10.2.12; c. gen., retiring from, giving up, surrender, BGU1127.13 ; ib.1171.12 ; of a holding of land, surrender, PPetr.3p.40 , cf. PTeb.30.12 : generally, cession, withdrawal from, D.S.13.43, Plu.Cat.Mi…

παραχωρίζω.definition: hand over, condemn to death, SIG684.20

παραψάλλω.definition: touch, pluck lightly, Plu.Demetr.19, cf. 2.133a: c. dat., Philostr.Im.2.1: c. gen., Onos.10.3

παραψελλίζω.definition: stammer out somewhat of the truth, Str.2.1.9

παραψηλαφάω.definition: grope about, fumble, Phld.Rh.1.240S.: c. acc., fumble with, Id.Po.5.32

παραψιδάζω.definition: dub. sens. et l. in Hippon. in PSI9.1089.9

παραψίδιον.definition: written for Dim. of small dish, PLond. 1.124.2

παραψυχή.definition: cooling, refreshment, consolation, E.Hec.280; Id.Or.62; Is.2.13; Aristid.Or.44.12; Iamb.Protr.20; D.60.32: in pl., . . Timocl.6.4

παραψύχω.definition: cool, v.l. in Placit.5.25.1; metaph., console, soothe, Theoc.13.54 , cf. Call.Cer.46

παρδαλέη.definition: leopard-skin, Il.3.17, 10.29, Hdt.7.69: prov., of a shifty person, Eust.374.44; Dor. Pi.P.4.81; Att. contr. Ar.Au.1250, Anaxandr.65, Corn.ND27

παρεάω.definition: let pass, neglect, Olymp.in Alc.p.117 C.; fail; gloss on , Sch.E.Ph.508

παρέγγραπτος.definition: illegally registered, intrusive citizens, Aeschin.2.177; of deified heroes, Luc.JTr.21: metaph., assumed, Plu.2.3c; interpolated, Eust.1379.62

παρεγγράφω.definition: write by the side, subjoin; in bad sense, interpolate, Aeschin.3.74, cf. Plu.CG17, Gal.15.9 , 17.606; Str.9.1.10; Luc.Ind.19; enrol illegally among the citizens, Id.Bis Acc.27; Aeschin.2.76

παρεγγυάω.definition: hand over to another, entrust or commend; of things, recommend, Men.487, cf. POxy.1101.15 , Olymp.Alch.p.94 B. ; Phld.Rh.1.137 S

παρεγγύησις.definition: passing on the word of command; instruction, exhortation, Oenom. ap. Eus.PE5.28

παρεγκάπτω.definition: swallow besides, Eub.15.9; prob. cj. in Plu.2.130b

παρέγκειμαι.definition: Pass., to be interpolated, Gal.18.178, al., Simp.in Ph.44.22

παρεγκελεύομαι.definition: exhort, c. acc. et inf., Plu.2.188e

παρεγκεράννυμι.definition: mix in besides, in pf. part. Pass., Poll.3.86

παρεγκεφαλίς.definition: cerebellum, Arist.HA494b32, Herophil. ap. Gal.UP8.11, etc

παρεγκλίνω.definition: cause to incline sideways; intr. in Act., Arist.HA498a16: c. gen., deviate from, Id.Ath.41.2: c. acc., not far from their prime, Thphr.CP6.17.3: abs., of the sun, pass the meridian, Id.Vent.16

παρέγκλισις.definition: flexure of the womb, Sor.2.7, Paul. Aeg.3.64; alteration, Plu.CG5; Dam.Pr.440

παρεγκύκλημα.definition: something added to a drama; stage-direction, in the margin of a play, Sch.Ar.Nu.18, al

παρεγχειρέω.definition: interfere with, Ph.Fr.49 H; interpret symbolically, Asclep. Tragil.3 J.; Artem.4.72

παρεγχείρησις.definition: encroaching on other people's business, Cic.Att.15.4.3; interference, BMus.Inscr.481*.402

παρεγχέω.definition: pour in beside, Arist.EE1235b39:—Pass., Id.Mete.359a2, Gal.18.469; v.l. in Plu.2.82e

παρεγχυματίζω.definition: drop in liquid, Gal.12.740:—Pass., have a little liquid dropped into the eye, Alex. Trall.2

παρέγχυσις.definition: pouring in beside, of dropsy, Aret.SD2.1, Gal.8.350; esp. of cataract, Ruf.Fr. 116; accumulation of fat, Sor.2.7

παρεδρεύω.definition: wait, attend upon; frequent, attend, IG5.734 ; ib.14.1728.6; ib.22.1028.35; SIG695.27 ; . . Plb.29.27.10

παρεδρία.definition: Ion. attendance, Memn.60; of things, its association, constant presence, Arist.PA652a32; persistence, Hp.Praec.8

πάρεδρος.definition: sitting beside, as at table; Subst., assessor, coadjutor, folld. by dat. or gen., of Themis, Id.O.8.22, cf. Ar.Av.1753, Phylarch.24J.; of Rhadamanthys, Pi.O.2.76; . . S.Ant.798 ; E.Med.843; Epigr.Gr.783 , cf. 817, IG2…

παρεικάζω.definition: liken, compare, Pl.R.473c, Plt.260e; make like, Sch.E.Ph.1185

παρείργω.definition: keep off, shut out, in aor. Hsch

παρείρω.definition: thread in, insert, A.Fr.281.3; X.Smp.6.2; Plb.18.18.13; is corrupt in S.Ant.368

παρεισάγω.definition: pf. Phld.Piet.32:—lead in; with a notion of secrecy, introduce, admit them into the city, Plb.2.7.8, cf. 1.18.3

παρείσακτος.definition: introduced privily, Ep.Gal.2.4: nickname of Ptolemy XI, Str.17.1.8

παρεισβάλλω.definition: throw in beside or secretly, Suid. s.v; intr., gloss on Phot., Suid.; cf. Hsch

παρεισβιάζομαι.definition: force one's way in, Iamb.in Nic.p.14 P

παρεισδέχομαι.definition: take in beside or as well, S.Tr.537; Arist.PA662a9

παρεισδύνω.definition: slip in, penetrate; Med. Hp.Epid.5.86, cf. Sor.1.101, Gal.2.653; . . Epicur.Ep.2p.48U.; Hdn.2.12.1, etc.; Arist.Pr.933a16; of a leech's bite, penetrate into, Aret.CA2.6; of customs, Plu.2.216b, Agis3, etc

παρεισέρπω.definition: aor. creep in secretly, Ph. ap. Eus.PE8.14

παρεισέρχομαι.definition: with aor. and pf. Act., come or go in; occur, suggest itself, of an idea, Vett. Val.357.9

παρεισκρίνω.definition: bring in, introduce beside, of a digression, Eust.1397.63:—Pass., to be introduced, Id.263.5, Hsch

παρεισπίπτω.definition: get in by the side, steal in; fall in the way of, Id.Luc.17

παρεισπράσσω.definition: Att. exact beside what is due, i.e. illegally, of tax-gatherers, Poll.9.32

παρεισρέω.definition: flow or stream in, Thphr.Fr.174.7; glide or slip in, Plu.Lyc.17,27:—Pass., in lit. sense, glide in by the side or imperceptibly, Arist.PA664b5, cf. Agathin. ap. Orib.10.7.28

παρεισφέρω.definition: bring in beside, propose an amending law, D.20.88, cf. 99 ; smuggle in, PTeb.38.12 : generally, introduce, A.D.Conj.213.9; Aps.p.243H.; apply besides, 2 Ep.Pet.1.5; interpolate, Sch.D.T.p.29H.:—Pass., to be brought in…

παρεισφθείρομαι.definition: steal in to the hurt of another, Ph.2.341, J.BJ4.2.1, 4.3.3

παρεισχέω.definition: pour in beside, metaph., in Pass., Eun.VSp.477B

παρεκβαίνω.definition: step aside from, deviate from, c. gen; c. acc., overstep, transgress, A.Ch.645 ; Arist.Pol.1310b19; Id.EN1160b20; Id.GA771a12; Id.Pol.1309b23; Phld.Po.5.15; Thphr.HP3.1.5

παρεκβάλλω.definition: throw out at the side, Sch.E.Hipp.237; extract and compile the remarks of others, Eust.3.1

παρέκβασις.definition: going aside from: metaph; esp. of the deviations of constitutional forms, as is a of monarchy, oligarchy of aristocracy, democracy of Id.EN1160a31, cf. Pol.1279a20, 1283a29, al

παρεκβολή.definition: digression, Iamb.Bab.8; compilation of a set of critical remarks, as those of Eust. on Homer, Pindar, and Dionysius Periegeta, cf. eund. ad D.P.426; title of Sch.D.T.inCod.BMus.Add.5118

παρεκδέχομαι.definition: take in a wrong sense, misconstrue, M.Ant.5.6, Anon.in Tht.19.46

παρεκδίδωμι.definition: give in marriage secretly: name of a play by Antiphanes

παρεκδοχή.definition: in pl., varieties of interpretation, Ph.Bybl. ap. Eus.PE1.10

παρεκδύομαι.definition: Pass. with aor. 2 Act., slip out secretly, Luc.JTr.41

παρέκθεσις.definition: insertion of part of a metrical system intermediate between and Sch.Ar.Ach.1007, Pax458

παρεκκαθαίρω.definition: clear up, explain incidentally, Epicur.Nat.119 G

παρεκκλίνω.definition: turn somewhat aside, Archig; alter slightly, of the form of a word, D.H.5.47

παρεκλείπω.definition: leave out, Aristid.1.171 J; run short; c. acc., fail, v.l. in LXXJu.11.12

παρεκμανθάνω.definition: learn incidentally or gradually, Phld.Mus.p.105 K

παρεκνέομαι.definition: sail past, c. acc. loci, A.R.2.941

παρεκπεράω.definition: go past, c. acc. loci, A.Fr.31

παρεκπυρόομαι.definition: Pass., take fire by the way, Arist.Mete.341b30

παρεκπύρωσις.definition: taking fire by the side, Phlp.in Mete.75.7

παρεκρίπτω.definition: throw up, of the sea, prob. in Cyran.33

παρέκτασις.definition: stretching out, extension; projection of the false ribs, Ruf.Oss.25

παρεκτείνω.definition: stretch out in line, deploy an army into; intr., extend, of Place, LXXEz.47.19; D.S.14.22; . . Str.13.4.17; of Time, Thphr.CP1.13.9; of semi-tertian fevers, Agathin. ap.Gal.7.367; Phld.Mus.p.109K

παρεκτρέπω.definition: turn aside, E.Supp.1111:— Pass., to be turned aside, deviate, Arist.GA773a15; . . Plu.2.114d; Sch.Ar.Ach.81

παρεκτρέχω.definition: run out past, in aor. part; metaph., forms derived from the nominative, A.D.Adv.171.25; of the outcome of astrological influences, Vett. Val.185.2

παρεκτροπή.definition: turning aside, diverting, of a stream; swerving aside, deviation, divergence, Demetr.Eloc.84; A.D.Synt.167.3; Simp.in Ph.232.35

παρεκτροχάζω.definition: pass by, IG12 p.vii; run from the path, yield the road, Tz.H.10.84

παρεκφέρω.definition: abuse, prob. in; to be excreted with, Aët.5.28

παρεκχέω.definition: pour out by degrees, S.E.M.7.90:—Pass., Gal.18.447; of rivers and lakes, overflow, Str.16.2.33, D.S.5.47; also become obese, Sor.1.32

παρέκχυσις.definition: overflowing, of rivers; effusion, Gal.19.124; of humours, Cass.Fel.76; = Cael.Aur.TP3.8

παρελκυσμός.definition: protraction of disease, Aët.9.28; prolongation of sound, Eust.1005.6

παρεμβαίνω.definition: fit in, Ph.Bel.66.39; go in beside another, Plu.2.593f; to be mounted beside another on . . , D.H.2.34; Id.5.47, etc

παρεμβάλλω.definition: fut. Ar.V.481:— put in beside or; in Tactics, insert troops in a line of battle, Plb.1.33.7, al.; insert men in the ranks, Ascl.Tact.10.17, etc

παρεμβλέπω.definition: look askance, E.Hel.1558, cf. Phld.Vit.p.37 J., Sm.Ca.1.6, Hsch. s.v

παρεμβολή.definition: insertion, interpolation; Gramm., parenthesis, Alex.Fig.25, Tib.Fig.48

παρεμβολοθέτης.definition: one who fixes a camp, Gloss

παρεμμαίνομαι.definition: Pass., to be somewhat mad, Tim.Lex. s.v

παρεμμίγνυμι.definition: mix in besides, Ael.NA3.30, Olymp.in Alc.p.7 C. , Tz.H.2.347:—also Ps.-Dsc.4.137

παρεμπάσσω.definition: sprinkle or mix in besides, Dsc.5.76, Damocr. ap. Gal.14.121; Gp.2.34.1:—Pass., c. dat., ib.3.9

παρεμπίπλημι.definition: fill secretly with, Plu.Marc.18:—Pass., to be overfull, Erasistr. ap. Gal.7.538

παρεμπίπραμαι.definition: Pass., to be chafed by rubbing, Str.15.1.52

παρεμπίπτω.definition: fut. Arist.APo.95b23:—creep in; in Logic, of a term, to be inserted, Id.APr.42b8, APo.l.c

παρεμπλέκω.definition: insert men in ranks, Ascl.Tact.10.17; mingle, Orib.Fr.41:—Med., prob. in Phot. : metaph., interweave, Eust.2.2, al. :—Pass., to be blended with, contained in, Diph. Siph. ap. Ath.2.57c; to be involved, Vett. Val.181.35

παρεμπλοκή.definition: fitting in, inclusion; in Tactics, = 2, Ascl.Tact.10.17

παρεμποδίζω.definition: to be a hindrance, Luc.Am.15: abs., Gal.4.504, 10.63

παρεμποδισμός.definition: obstruction, Erot. s.v. Gal.14.776, Aspasia ap.Aët.16.72

παρεμπολάω.definition: traffic underhand in a thing, smuggle it in, dub. in E.Med.910; an intrusive citizen, Com.Adesp.96

παρεμπόρευμα.definition: in pl., merchandise of small; metaph., appendix, = Luc.Dem.Enc.10,22, M.Ant.3.12, etc

παρεμπορεύομαι.definition: traffic in besides: metaph., Alciphr.Fr.6.16; yield delight besides instruction, Luc.Hist.Conscr.9

παρέμπτωσις.definition: influx, entrance; insertion of words, A.D.Synt.16.11,al.; parenthesis, D.H.Amm.2.2

παρεμφαίνω.definition: aor. Phld.Piet.18:—display; generally, suggest, indicate, Arist.Aud.801b13, Chrysipp.Stoic.2.52, 245, Plb.12.24.2, Phld.l.c., D.H.Comp.6, Plu.Per.16, 2.107e, A.D.Adv.204.22, Synt.9.22:—Pass., Ph.1.488, A.D.Pron.11.28

παρεμφερής.definition: somewhat like, v.l. in Arist.HA524b10, cf. D.S.1.35,98, etc. Adv. Zos.5.16

παρεμφράσσω.definition: Att. block up beside, Id.6.768; Cass.Pr.60

παρεμφύομαι.definition: Pass., grow in beside, hang upon, Luc.Fug.10

παρέμφυσις.definition: point of attachment, Heliod. ap. Orib.45.9.3

παρενδείκνυμαι.definition: Med., exhibit, of actors, Poll.4.98; denote , ib.145: generally, display, Dam.Pr.116:—Act. in Olymp.Alch.p.79 B

παρενδημέω.definition: take up residence in a place, Sammelb.5223.2

παρενδίδωμι.definition: give in, Plu.2.813d, App.BC1.12; relax, remit, of acute disease, Gal.12.494

παρενδύομαι.definition: Pass. with aor. 2 Act., slip in, PCair.Zen.534.50 , Plu.2.479a

παρενείρω.definition: put in by the side, Sor.2.60: metaph., intrude oneself into everything, Plu.2.793d; Alex.Aphr.in Top.521.34, cf. Eust.7.39

παρένθεσις.definition: putting in beside : giving besides; insertion, of a tent in a wound, Aët.8.27: Gramm., of letters, Eust.30.43: in Tactics, of men in a rank, Ascl.Tact.6.1; Eust.100.33

παρένθετος.definition: interpolated, Eust.67.29; a 'man of straw', Sammelb.5248.7 , etc

παρενθήκη.definition: something put in beside, addition; smaller wares taken as an addition to the cargo, opp. Plu.2.151e, cf. Poll.1.99, Hsch

παρενθυμέομαι.definition: disregard, Ph.1.78, M.Ant.5.5, etc. : aor. Pass. in act. sense TAM2.245.13 ; Sammelb.7404.39

παρένθυρσος.definition: false sentiment or affectation of style, Theod. ap.Longin.3.5

παρενοχλέω.definition: cause one much annoyance, Hp.Ep.13; c. acc., annoy, Plb.16.37.3, OGI139.16 , Hierocl.in CA8p.431M.:—Pass., D.18.50; Plb.3.53.6; of disease, OGI331.10

παρενσαλεύω.definition: swing to and fro, Ar.Pl.291; Philostr.VA2.13

παρενσπείρομαι.definition: to be strewn among, pf. part. Procl. ap. Simp.in Cael.656.14

παρενστάζω.definition: let drop in besides or by mistake, Sor.1.86, Gal.12.794, Aët.4.9

παρενσφηνόομαι.definition: to be wedged in beside, 'impacted', cj. ib.31

παρένταξις.definition: in Tactics, insertion, e.g. of light-armed troops among hoplites, Ascl.Tact.6.1

παρεντείνω.definition: stretch beside, in Med; strain, exert, it, ib.623b, cf. D.H.Dem.54; aggravate, Ruf.Sat.Gon.43

παρεντίθημι.definition: insert, Dsc.5.120 , Sor.1.84; interpolate, Gal.18.179, Longin.27.1:—Pass., Hermog.Id.2.10

παρεξαιρέω.definition: take out, Tz.inAn.Ox.3.321; Med., take by choice, SIG1106.107

παρεξαίρω.definition: thrust up, Str.11.14.4:—Pass., to be lifted up, Scymn.343

παρεξαλλάττω.definition: change, changed her tone somewhat, Men.Sam.42: pf. part. Pass. different, strange, gloss on Sch.S.Ant.849

παρεξαμείβω.definition: go or sail by, c. acc., A.R.1.581

παρεξαυλέω.definition: pf. part. Pass. worn out by being played upon: hence, generally, worn out, having lost voice and strength, Ar.Ach.681; Suid., cf. Hsch., Phot

παρέξειμι.definition: pass by or alongside of; turn aside, metaph., Pl.R.503a; deviate from, Paul.Aeg.3.45

παρεξειρεσία.definition: outrigger, oar-box, a closed structure built out from the sides of a ship, through which the oars passed, Th.4.12, 7.34 , Plu.2.347b, Arr.Peripl.M.Eux.3 , Fr.160 J., Polyaen.3.11.13

παρεξέλεγχος.definition: confutation on a side-issue; super-refutation , Gal.17.618

παρεξελέγχω.definition: confute on a side-issue, Arist.Top.112a8 , Alex.Aphr.in Top.172.10

παρεξετάζω.definition: put one thing by another, compare them; examine, Procop.Gaz.Ep.78

παρεξευρίσκω.definition: find out besides, find out a law which neutralizes another, Hdt.3.31; Ph.2.46, cf. Polystr.Herc.346p.80V

παρεξίημι.definition: allow to pass through, D.C.40.2, cf; aor. inf. divulge, dub. in h.Cer.478; cf. II

παρεξισόω.definition: place beside as equal, rank with, Archestr.Fr.59.6, cf. Hsch. s.v

παρεξίστημι.definition: remove from its place; Pass., with aor. 2, pf. and plpf. Act., undergo a change, Epich.170.16; went mad, Plb.32.3.6, cf. Fr.192: abs., LXXHo.9.7; wine that has turned, sour wine, Lyc.Fr.2.3

παρέξοδος.definition: side-way, Et.Gud. s.v; passage of injections, Mnesith. ap. Orib.8.38.2

παρέξω.definition: outside, c. gen., v.l. in LXXLe.8.17

παρεπαίρομαι.definition: to be puffed up, pf. part. Vett. Val.9.18, cf. 201.10

παρεπέχω.definition: aor. inf. suspend for a time, PTeb. 29.16

παρεπιβοηθέω.definition: come in addition to help, c. dat., v.l. in D.S.2.6

παρεπιγραφή.definition: something written in the margin; incidental statement, as a rhetorical figure, Tz.ad Lyc.1

παρεπιγράφω.definition: write by the side of an inscription, i.e. correct it, Str.14.5.14; write in the margin, in Pass., PCair.Zen. 147 , PTeb.30.25, al., Sch.Ar.Av.222

παρεπιδείκνυμι.definition: point out beside or at the same time; display, Gal.8.600

παρεπιδημέω.definition: Boeot. pres. part. Supp.Epigr.3.364 :—sojourn as a stranger in a place, Macho ap.Ath.13.579a, Plb.27.6.3, IG7.190 , 2712.15 , PCair.Zen.368.20 ; travel, . . . . Plb.13.8.3

παρεπιδημία.definition: Dor. residence in a; metaph. of life, Pl.Ax.365b, cf. Hipparch. ap. Stob.4.44.81

παρεπίδημος.definition: sojourning in a strange place, esp. as Subst., LXXGe.23.4, PPetr.3 p.14 , Callix.2, Plb.32.6.4, etc

παρεπικουρέω.definition: to be a help to, S.E.M.5.75

παρεπινοέω.definition: invent besides, Sch.Ar.Av.454:—Med., v.l. in D.S.12.11. II. Pass., to be conceived or apprehended at the same time, Plot.6.6.10

παρεπιπλέκομαι.definition: Pass., of stars, to be in conjunction, Gal.19.557

παρεπισκοπέω.definition: examine besides or also, Arist.MM1197b32, Plu.2.129e

παρεπισπάομαι.definition: Med., draw to oneself, claim, v.l. in Ph.1.540

παρεπιστρέφω.definition: intr., turn aside, Eratosth. ap.Str.17.1.2, cf. Marcian.1.11. II. Pass., turn in passing and look at, Plu.2.521b, D.L.2.23

παρεπιτείνομαι.definition: Pass., become intensified, of the action of drugs, Archig. ap. Orib.8.2.4

παρεπιτηδεύομαι.definition: practise as well, Philum. ap. Aët.5.78

παρεπιφαίνομαι.definition: Pass., appear beside, Herod.Med. ap.Orib.10.17.2. II. incidental, Phld.Po.5.33

παρεπιχέω.definition: add by pouring, HeroAut.2.4, cf. Sor.1.100, Heras ap.Gal.12.430, Sammelb.7350

παρέπομαι.definition: accompany, attend, Hp.Epid.1.8, etc.; of an; the lands appertaining to a village, POxy.1134.15

παρεργάτης.definition: workman in addition, i. e. argumentative too, E.Supp.426:—later assistant in a trade, POxy.1731.19

παρεργολαβέω.definition: convert to one's own use, Ph.1.541

παρερεθίζω.definition: irritate, J.Vit.45 , cf. Sm.Pr.24.19, Thd.Ps.36.1, Aët.16.61, Simp.in Epict.p.66 D

παρέρπω.definition: creep secretly up to, Theoc.15.48: aor. 1; Dor. = Schwyzer177.8 ; IG 5.514.3 : aor. subj. ib.8, Theoc.15.60; IG5.1390.36 ; appear in public, Dialex.2.9. 2. pass by, APl.1.11 , Epigr.Gr.195

παρεσθίω.definition: eat besides, Hp.Dent.16. II. gnaw or nibble at, c. gen., . . Ar.Eq.1026; Jul.Gal.229c. 2. metaph., carp, sneer at, c. acc., D.L.2.66

παρετάζω.definition: put beside and compare, Hsch. II. approve, . . IG5.6.28 . 2. Med., aor. part. c. acc., after obtaining the consent of, ib.3.20 . 'regard as admissible'.)

παρετοιμάζω.definition: make ready besides, metrical version of Aesop.62

παρετυμολογέω.definition: allude to the etymology of a word, Ath.1.35c, Ach.Tat.Intr.Arat.15

παρευδιάζομαι.definition: live at peace with one's neighbours, Plb.4.32.5

παρευδιαστής.definition: of a kind of water-fowl that comes on land in fine weather, prob. for Clearch.73

παρευδοκιμέω.definition: surpass in fame, etc., Plu.Pomp.37, etc.; Lib.Or.62.44; D.H.Vett.Cens.3.1; Alciphr.1.39:—Pass., to be surpassed, Telesp.26 H., Luc.Herm.51, Ach.Tat.Vit.Arat.6, Philostr.Ep.9

παρευημερέω.definition: flourish, abound, Ph.1.19,al. :—Pass., to be surpassed, D.S.20.79

παρευλαβέομαι.definition: beware at the same time, . . Sch.S.Tr.1

παρευμαρέω.definition: aor. 1. think lightly of, hold cheap, Hsch

παρευναστήρ.definition: one who sleeps beside: hence, chamberlain, Men.Prot.p.10 D., Agath.3.16

πάρευνος.definition: lying beside or with, bedfellow, Ion Eleg.2.9: metaph., A.Th.1009

παρεύρεσις.definition: pretext, pretence, Decr. ap. D.18.37, cf. PEleph.1.9 , IG9.694.109 , Test.Epict. 2.15, SIG581.45 , etc.; Sammelb. 4638.10 ; = Lat. fraus, Supp.Epigr.3.378C16 : prov., Str.9.2.4, Zen.4.37

παρευρίσκω.definition: discover besides, invent, Hdt.1.26; Pass., . . be discovered in them, Hdt.3.31

παρευτακτέω.definition: perform one's duty regularly, of; serve as a BCH55.439

παρεύτακτος.definition: member of a particular class of , ibid., Lucil.321, 752 Marx, IG3.107, fem. prob. in Varro ap. Non.p.93 L

παρευτρεπίζω.definition: put in order, arrange, make ready, E.IT725:—Med., Plb.5.108.4:—Pass., E.Cyc.594

παρεφάπτομαι.definition: touch on the side, c. gen., Plu.2.573f; touch upon, allude to, Phld.Mus.p.96 K., al

παρεφεδρεύω.definition: lie near to guard : keep guard; stand immediately behind, Ael.Tact.13.3

παρηγορέω.definition: console, comfort, A.Pers.530, E.Ph.1449; consolations, emollients, D.60.35; appease, Musae.l.c

παρήγορος.definition: c. gen., assuaging them, M.Ant. ap. Justin.M.Apol.1.71

παρηδύνω.definition: sweeten or season, Dorio ap.Ath.7.309f: metaph., of language, D.H.Dem.45

παρηθέω.definition: filter through, Hp.Dent.14 and 17 :— Pass., Gal.UP6.16

παρημερεύω.definition: pass the day with one or in doing a thing, Poll.1.65

παρήμερος.definition: Dor. coming day by day; every other day, Poll.1.65 cod. B

παρηχέομαι.definition: resemble in sound, Sch.Ar.Pl.586; Eust.139.31; to be derived from a word by such resemblance, Id.87.24

παρήχημα.definition: succession of similar sounds, alliteration, Suid. s.v

παρθενεία.definition: virginity, E.Heracl.592, Tr.980:—more freq. Ep. Sapph.102, Pi.I.8.48, A.Pr.898 , E.Ph.1487 , Arist.Pr.894b35, A.R.2.502, LXXJe.3.4, Parth.26.2, Sor.1.30; or Ev.Luc.2.36, IG12.395.20 ; Plu.Brut.13, PSI1.41.5 ; of a man…

παρθένειος.definition: poet. also of or belonging to a maiden, Pi.N.8.2; the maiden's life, A.Ag.229 ; E.Tr.676; later in Prose, PRyl.435.2 ; St.Byz. s.v

παρθενεύω.definition: bring up as a maid; intr. in Act., = Pass., Hld.7.8

παρθενίας.definition: son of a concubine: the youths

παρθενική.definition: poet. for Il.18.567, Od.11.39, Hes.Op.699, Alcm.26, Alc.Supp.11.5, Sapph.Supp.20a. 15, Pi.P.9.99, B.16.11, E.El.174 ; Od.7.20; E.Epigr.2

παρθένιος.definition: the son of an unmarried girl, Il.16.180; Pi.O.6.31; but the husband of maidenhood, first husband, Plu.Pomp.74

παρθενίς.definition: pecul. fem. of name of a flower used in garlands, Poll.6.106; = Plin.HN25.73

παρθενοκόμος.definition: taking care of maidens, An.Ox.2.398:—also ibid

παρθενοπίπης.definition: one who ogles maidens, seducer, Il.11.385

παρθενόσφαγος.definition: streams of a slaughtered maiden's blood, A.Ag.209

παρθενοτροφέω.definition: bring up from girlhood, Suid. s.v; Pass., keep virgin, Sor.1.32

παρθενών.definition: maidens' apartments in a house; in sg., the western cella of the Parthenon or temple of Athena at Athens, IG12.301.13, al., D.22.76, etc.; also, of the cella of the temple of Artemis at Magnesia on Maeander, SIG 695.2…

παριαμβίς.definition: air set for the harp; a kind of harp, Poll.4.59

παριδρύω.definition: set up beside, Hsch.:—Med., AP9.315 , Ph.2.347:—Pass., ib.151, al

παριππεύω.definition: ride along or over, E.Hel.1665; ride; ride up to, Plb.3.116.3

πάριππος.definition: riding beside, Plb.11.18.5; keeping pace with a horse, Poll.5.40

πάρισος.definition: almost equal, evenly balanced; in Rhet., of the clauses of a sentence, exactly balanced and even, Arist.Rh.1410b1, cf. Phld. Rh.2.258 S.; D.S.12.53; Plu.2.350d; parallel in structure, D.H.Comp.22, cf. 23; ib.9; Hermog…

παριστάνω.definition: = sq. , Plb.3.96.3, 3.113.8, Phld.Sign.29, Ep.Rom.6.13, etc. :—also A.D.Synt.272.13 , S.E.P.2.42, 108, etc. :—Pass., Parm.16.2; cf

παριστορέω.definition: inquire by the way, Cic. Att.6.1.25; narrate or notice incidentally, Placit. 2.24.4, Dam.Pr.123

παροδεύω.definition: pass by, Theoc.23.47, AP9.341; c. acc., pass by or through, D.S.32.27, Plu.2.973d, Herm. ap. Stob.1.49.44, Luc.Nigr.36, IG14.881 : Astron., pass through or across, Plu.2.67oc, Ptol.Tetr.109; Vett. Val. 145.9:—Pass., t…

παρόδιος.definition: by or on the roadway, Hyp.Fr.261; Subst. frontage, IG22.2561, 2566

παροδίτης.definition: passer-by, traveller, Hp.Ep.17, AP9.249 , IG 14.494 :—fem. AP7.429 , 9.373

παροδύρομαι.definition: lament beside or along with, D.C.43.19

παροίγνυμι.definition: or open at the side or a little, half-open, E.IA857, having opened a bit of the door, put it ajar, Ar.Pax30

παροιδέω.definition: = foreg., Herod. Med. in Rh.Mus.58.88, Antyll. ap. Orib.6.27.2, Dsc.Alex.27: metaph., Ph.1.276

παροικέω.definition: dwell beside, c. acc; live in a place as D.S.13.47, cf. SIG709.9 ; Ph.1.416; sojourn in, Ev.Luc.24.18

παροικία.definition: sojourning in a foreign land, LXXWi.19.10, Act.Ap.13.17; = LXXSi.Prol

παροικίζω.definition: place near, Sm.Ez.12.25:—Med., Call.Epigr.26:—Pass., settle near, dwell among, Hdt.4.180; settled upon, Luc.Am.6

παροικοδομέω.definition: build across or past, Th.2.75; build up, narrow them by building, Arist.HA623b32; keep it off by a wall, D.55.17

παροικοδόμημα.definition: building beside a road, prob.cj. in D.C.68.15

παροιμιάζω.definition: the Proverbs of; Med., speak in proverbs, Pl.Hp.Ma.301c, Arist.EN1129b29; people who quote proverbs, Pl.Tht.162c

παροιμιαστής.definition: author of proverbs, of Solomon, Sm.Ec.12.10

παροινία.definition: drunken behaviour, Lys.1.45, X.Smp.6.1 sq., Amphis29, D.10.198, Aeschin.1.61; Id.2.4

παροίνιος.definition: f.l. for Id.Ach.981. II. befitting a drinking party, Ath.14.629e, cf. Luc.Salt.34; Ph.1.353; drinking songs, Sch.Ar.V.1217, 1231; drinking songs, ib.1232; Plu.Dem.4

παροινοχοέω.definition: pour out wine ready for one, Q.S.4.279

παροιστράω.definition: and = LXXHo.4.16, cf. Ez.2.6, D.S.34/5.28a. II. trans., provoke, incite, Pap.in GerckeNorden Einleitung 31p.42, cf. Hsch.:—Pass., Jul.Ep.89b

παροκλάζω.definition: = Tim.Gaz. in Ar. Byz.Epit.147.11, Hsch., Phot., Suid

παρολιγωρέω.definition: neglect, disregard. X.HG7.4.13, Plb.4.46.6, etc.:— Pass., to be neglected, Pl.Epin.991d, Plb.5.27.6, Phld.Ir.p.42 W., Ph.2.319

παρολκή.definition: spinning out of time, delay; Gramm., redundancy, A.D.Synt.327.4, cf. Adv.207.4 ; so in Logic, Stoic. 2.79

πάρολκος.definition: tow-rope, Ostr. Bodl. ii 72; Adj., = lentus, Gloss

παρομαρτέω.definition: accompany, Plu.Ant.26, Aret.SA2.2, Jul.Caes.312c, etc.; Junc. ap. Stob.4.50.85; Luc.Tim.55, cf. Im.9, Porph.Abst.2.49, CPHerm. 6.15

παρομοιόω.definition: compare, describe by a comparison, Anon.Geog.Comp.53, Philum.Ven.35.1, Dion.Byz.109: —Pass., assume the form of, PMag.Leid.V.2.2

παρομοίωσις.definition: assimilation, esp. of sounds in; comparison, Arist.Rh.Al.1430b9

παρομολογέω.definition: grant or admit besides: generally, = Plb.3.89.3, 7.3.7:—so in Med., PPetr.3p.129

παρομολογία.definition: partial admission, a rhet. figure; agreement, OGI607.7

παρονομάζω.definition: call with a slight change of name; added the epithet 'virilis' to 'Fortuna', Plu.2.318f

παρονομασία.definition: play upon words which sound alike; use of a word first in its proper, then in a derived sense, Hermog.Id.2.5

παροξίζω.definition: have a somewhat sharp smell, Dsc.1.19

παροξύνω.definition: pf. inf. Plb.31.1.3, but; provoke, irritate, E.Alc.674; Th.1.84:—Pass., to be provoked, at a thing, Id.5.99; Id.6.56; OGI48.15 , Plb.4.7.5; X.HG6.4.6, D.57.2; Arist.Pol.1302a39; Lys.l.c. ; Plu.Them.31: c. dat., Lycurg…

παροξυσμός.definition: irritation, exasperation, D.45.14; severe fit of a disease, paroxysm, Hp.Aph.1.11,12, Gal.17.387, etc

παροξυτονέω.definition: pronounce paroxytone, Eust.1600.18 :— hence Id.1409.54, al

παροπλίζω.definition: pf. D.S.4.10:—disarm, Plb.2.7.10, etc. :— Med., 2sg. Ep. aor. Numen. ap. Ath.7.306c:—Pass., Plu.Cat.Mi.68

παροπτάω.definition: roast slightly, half-roast, toast, Plb.12.25.2 , Agatharch.47; as medical treatment, Herod.Med. ap. Orib.10.10.2

παροπτέος.definition: one must overlook, Men.53, cf. D.26.16

παρόπτησις.definition: half-roasting or -baking, Herod.Med. ap. Orib.10.10.4, Sor.2.15, Cael Aur.TP3.4

παρόραμα.definition: oversight, error, Phld.Sign.29 , Plu.2.515e , 1123c, Procl.in Prm.p.556 S.; opp. Longin.33.4

παρόρασις.definition: false vision, Ruf.Fr.116; overlooking, Plu.Aem.3, cf. LXX2 Ma.5.17, Luc.Jud.Voc.3, etc

παροργίζω.definition: fut. LXXDe.32.21:—provoke to anger; Pass., to be or be made angry, Thphr.HP9.16.6, prob. in Str.7.2.1; v.l. in D.26.17

παρόργισμα.definition: provocation, cause of anger, LXX3 Ki.16.33, 20.22

παρορίζω.definition: limit, define, Longin.2.2, 10.6; outstep one's boundaries, encroach on a neighbour's property, AP11.209 , AB293:—Pass., have the boundaries extended, Inscr.Prien.37.142, al. ; have one's land encroached upon, BGU615 i…

παρορμάω.definition: urge on, stimulate, incite, X.Cyr.2.4.10; ib.2.2.1; ib.8.1.12; Arist.MM1206a9, Phld.Rh.2.60 S.; Phld.Mus.p.35 K.: c. acc. rei, Dsc.2.140, 3.129; Id.1.16: c.inf., X.Cyr.8.1.43, Arist.EN1179b7:—Pass., to be eager, Plb.2…

παρορμέω.definition: lie at anchor beside or near, D.S.14.49.50, PFlor.155.8 ; Plu.Ant.32

παρόρμησις.definition: urging on, incitement, X.Eq.Mag.1.25, v.l. in Cyr.1.6.19, cf. Plb.6.39.8, Phld.Mus.p.98 K., Andronic. Rhod.p.572 M.; Iamb.Protr.5; ib.1

παρορμίζω.definition: bring to anchor alongside the shore, Lys.13.25

παρορύσσω.definition: Att. dig alongside or parallel; dig one against another, D.L.6.27:—Med., Arr.Epict.3.15.4, Epict.Ench.29.2

παρορχέομαι.definition: represent in dancing out of season, . . Luc.Salt.80

παροσφραίνω.definition: hold for one to smell, Gp.13.17

παρουσία.definition: presence, of persons; arrival, S.El.1104, cf. E.Alc.209, Th.1.128; D.H.1.45; esp. visit of a royal or official personage, etc., PTeb.48.14 , IPE12.32A85 , etc.; of a god, IG42.122.34

παροχέομαι.definition: Pass., sit beside in a chariot, X.Cyr.8.3.14, Luc.DMar.15.3, D.C.63.20

παροχετεύω.definition: turn from its course, divert, Plu.Them.31:—Med., Id.2.779f: metaph., E.Ba.479; Pl.Lg.844a:—Pass., to be diverted, Thphr.CP5.17.4

παροχεύς.definition: provider, purveyor, of Hermes, Cyran.15, cf. Hdn.Epim.116; gloss on Sch.E.Or.1650

παροχή.definition: supply, furnishing; payment, furnishing, PLond.3.1159.2 , etc

παρόψημα.definition: dainty side-dish, Ath.9.367c; i.e. other fruits planted among the vines, Philostr.Her.Prooem.1:—Dim. Poll.6.56

παροψίς.definition: dish on which such meats are served, Antiph.60, Alex.86, Archestr.Fr.6, Ev.Matt.23.25, Juv.3.142, Artem.1.74

παροψώνημα.definition: addition to the regular fare, dainty: metaph., a new relish to the pleasures of my bed, A.Ag.1447

παρρησία.definition: outspokenness, frankness; in bad sense, licence of tongue, Isoc.11.40, cf. Pl.Phdr.240e, Cic.Att.1.16.8

παρρησιαστής.definition: outspoken person, Arist.EN1124b29, Phld.Lib.p.62 O. , D.S.14.5, Luc.Deor.Conc.3

παρυβρίζομαι.definition: insult, Salač & Škorpil Několik Archeol. Památek z Vychodniho Bulharska p.57

παρυγραίνω.definition: moisten or soften a little, Herod.Med. ap; Pass., to be relaxed, of the bowels, Sor.1.122, Mnesith. ap. Orib.inc.19.5

παρυπαντάω.definition: come into the way of, meet, J.BJ1.31.4

παρυπονοέω.definition: suppose incidentally, Phld.Lib.p.49 O.; conclude as well, Gal.16.537; suspect besides, Dam.Pr.118

παρυπόστασις.definition: coordinate or parallel existence, Porph.Sent.44 , Procl.in R.1.38 K., al.; by-product, Simp.in Cael.429.34, cf. in Ph.1262.8

παρυπτιάω.definition: of the stomach, to be turned , Sor.1.36

παρυφαίνω.definition: pf. Ph.Byz.Mir.2.5:—weave beside; excel in weaving, Philostr.Im.2.28

παρυφή.definition: border woven along a robe, IG22.1514.29, Clearch.9, Phylarch.45 J., Plu.2.239c, Gal.18.791: metaph., Jul.Gal.238b

παρυφής.definition: with a border, bordered robe, Ar.Fr.320.7, Poll.7.53, Phot. s.v. also Men.479, Poll.7.46

παρυφίστημι.definition: place close beside:—pres. Act. only in; Pass., with aor. 2 subsist coordinately with, Stoic. 2.48, S.E.P.1.205, D.L.9.105, Plot.2.9.14, Porph.Sent.43, Ascl.in Metaph.371.2: abs., Simp.in Cat.110.5

παρῳδέω.definition: write by way of parody, D.L.4.52, Luc.Cont.14, etc.; Philostr.VS1.5; . . Ath.8.364b, cf. Sch.Ar.Pl.253, etc

παρωκεάνιος.definition: near or on the ocean, Plu.Caes.20

παρωνυμέω.definition: = Eust.84.28 , etc; intr., to be of like signification with, Ph.1.486, 2.39

παρωνυμία.definition: by-name, nickname, Plu.2.401a, 421e; alternative name, Dam.Pr.61

παρωνυμιάζω.definition: call by a derived name, Arist.Ph.245b11:—Pass., = Id.EE1228a35

παρωνύμιος.definition: deviating from the sense, slightly; as Subst. name formed from another by a slight change, derivative, Id.Sph.268c, Chrysipp.Stoic.3.198, A.D.Adv.160.3; in full, Id.Conj.253.22

παρώνυμος.definition: formed by a slight change, derivative; Subst. by-name, Pherecyd.25 J

παρωνυχία.definition: whitlow, Hp.Epid.2.6.27, Plu.2.43b; plant reputed to be a cure for whitlow, Dsc.4.54, Gal.12.96, Paul.Aeg.7.3

παρωνυχίς.definition: = foreg. I, Hierocl.Facet.199, 200, Gloss., v.l. in Paul.Aeg.7.3, interpol. in Suid

πασιδάμεια.definition: universal queen, epith. of the moon-goddess, prob. in PMag.Lond.121.694

πασιθέα.definition: magical plant, PMag.Leid.V.12.13; festival at Ephesus, Ephes.3 p.103

Πασικράτεια.definition: universal queen, a goddess of the underworld, IG14.268 , PMag.Par.1.2774:—also Dor

πασιμεδέουσα.definition: ruling over all, of Hecate, PMag.Par.1.2775

πασιμέλων.definition: a care or interest to all, world-famous, Str.1.2.40; esp. of the ship Argo, Od.12.70

πασιφαής.definition: shining on all, Orph.H.8.14, Man.3.346:—fem. Epigr. in Arist.Mir.843b29

πασίφιλος.definition: = foreg., ib.221 , Sammelb. 6160.10, al. ; ironical in PCair.Zen.454.12 :—fem. Sammelb. 7254 : as pr. n., Archil.19

πασσαλεῖον.definition: Att. Dim. of peg, rivet, EM323.9: metaph., Plb.29.8.10

πασσαλίσκος.definition: Dim. of Plb.Fr.163; used to force open the mouth, Hp.Mul.2.203; esp.peg or pin in musical instruments, Sch.Ar.V.572; = EM525.31

πασσαλιστής.definition: one who plays with pegs, Hsch.s.v

πασσαλοκοπέω.definition: Att. drive in pegs, Dosith.p.432 K

παστιλλόω.definition: make into a paste, Orib.Fr.102, Alex.Trall.5.4:— Pass., Aët.8.74

παστοφόριον.definition: chamber assigned to PPetr.2p.1 , UPZ119.25, al. , SIG977a , Hsch.; used of the priest's chamber in the temple at Jerusalem, LXXJe.42.4, J.BJ4.9.12

παστοφόρος.definition: bringing the marriage-bed, Epigr. in Stob.1.5.14

πασχητιάω.definition: feel lust, Erot. s.v. D.C.79.16; esp. of unnatural lust, Luc.Am.26, Ath.5.187c, Cat.Cod.Astr.2.175.6

παταγέω.definition: Aeol. impf. Alc. Supp.25.9:—; trans., beat drums, Luc.Syr.D.50:—Pass., Lyr.Adesp.121; Luc.Tim.3

πατερίζω.definition: Att. fut. say or call father, Ar.V.652

πάτησις.definition: treading of grapes, Corn.ND30, PLond.2.163.32 , Gp.8.36.2

πατησμός.definition: treading on, trampling, A.Ag.963; threshing of corn, PFlor.388.7

πατητήριον.definition: place where grapes are trodden, CIG2694a10 , Androtion or Philippus ap.Harp. s.v

πατητής.definition: one who treads grapes, POxy. 1340 , Hsch

πατραγαθία.definition: virtue of one's father or ancestors, opp. Plu.2.183d, 534c

πατραδελφεός.definition: poet. and Dor. for Pi.I.8.72, Michel995 C 44

πατραδέλφεια.definition: cousin by the father's side, A.Supp.38

πατραλίτωρ.definition: one who sins against a father, dub. in Tz.H.6.443

πατραλοίας.definition: gen. and voc. :—one who slays or strikes his father, parricide, Ar.Nu.911, 1327, Ra.274, Lys.10.8, Pl.Phd.114a, Sph.241d, etc. : as fem., Hld.10.38:—sts. written or in codd., as 1 Ep.Ti.1.9, J.AJ16.11.1

πατριά.definition: Ion. lineage, descent; = II.2, clan, Hdt.1.200, Michel195.1 , 995 A 26

πατριάρχης.definition: father or chief of a race; title borne by the Bishops of Rome, Constantinople, Jerusalem, Antioch, and Alexandria, Just.Nov.3.2, etc. :—Adj. of or belonging to him, ib.7 Praef.1, cf. Cod.Just.1.5.12.22

πατρογενής.definition: begotten of the father, Orac. ap. Dam.Pr.206

πατρογέρων.definition: hereditary member of the Ephes. 2.20 iii 4

πατροδίδακτος.definition: taught by a father, Sch.ad Tz.H.7.959 in An. Ox.3.370

πατροκόμος.definition: taking care of her father, Nonn.D.26.103

πατροκτονία.definition: murder of a father, parricide, Hipparch. ap. Stob.4.44.81, Plu.Rom.22, Iamb.VP17.78

πατροκτόνος.definition: murdering one's father, parricidal; a father's murdering hand, E.IT1083

πατρολάθησις.definition: neglect of one's father, PMasp.97 B 51

πατρομήτωρ.definition: mother's father, Luc.Alex.58; fem., grandmother, Lyc.502

πατρομύστης.definition: one whose father was a hereditary IGRom.4.1393

πατρονομέω.definition: hold office of IG5.18 B 4; Pass., to be under a patriarchal government, Pl.Lg.680e, Plu.Dio10

πατρονομία.definition: paternal government, Luc.Dem.Enc.12; office of at Sparta, IG5.311, al.; ib.541.17

πατρονόμος.definition: member of the council instituted by Cleomenes III at Sparta, IG5.32,al., Plu.2.795f, Paus.2.9.1, Philostr.V.A.4.32; IG5 .311

πατροπαράδοτος.definition: handed down from one's fathers, inherited, D.H.5.48; D.S.17.4; 1 Ep.Pet.1.18; OGI331.49 , CIG 2134b4 , cf. IG 12 .860.4

πατροπάτωρ.definition: father's father, Pi.P.9.82, N.6.16, A.R.1.170, IG12.303 ; as title of gods, Sammelb.5802.4 , cf. 1570.4

πατροποίητος.definition: adopted as a father, Supp.Epigr.6.77 , Klio 24.61 (Galatia, written

πατρόπολις.definition: coined by Antiph.220 in the line

πατροτυπία.definition: act of beating one's father, Corp.Herm.9.3

πατροτύπτης.definition: one who beats his father, Is.Fr.166, Ph.1.135, S.E.M.2.44, TheonProg.13

πατροφονεύς.definition: Ep. murderer of one's father, . ., Od.1.299, cf. 3.197

πατροφόνος.definition: slaying a father, A.Th.783; Subst., parricide, Pl.Lg.869b

πατρῴζω.definition: = Hdn.1.7.1, Alciphr.3.14, Them.Or.5.71b: c. acc. modi, Philostr.VA6.16; Id.VS2.9.3

πατρωνεία.definition: or = Lat. patronatus, D.H.2.10, Plu.Rom.13, Paul.Al.L.3

πατρωνεύω.definition: to be a patron, GDI2688.7 :— Pass., D.S.40.5, PMasp. 151.229

πατρωνίκιον.definition: in pl., rights of a patron, PMasp.29.5

πατρωνυμέομαι.definition: Pass., have the patronymic formed, Eust.13.41

πατρωνυμία.definition: name taken from one's father, patronymic, as Id.1388.24

πατρώνυμος.definition: named after his father, Quarterly of Dept. of Antiquities in Palestine 1.155

παυσικάπη.definition: projecting collar worn by slaves while grinding corn or kneading bread, to prevent them from eating any of the Ar.Fr.302, cf. Ael. Dion.Fr.276; also by animals, Suid

παυσίλυπος.definition: ending pain, S.Fr.425 ; E.Ba.772; i.e. the grave, IG14.2136

παυσίπονος.definition: ending toil or hardship, c. gen., E.IT451 , Ar.Ra.1321 ; Epigr.Gr.244.10

παυστήρ.definition: one who stops or relieves, S.Ph.1438, cf. El.304, Alex.240.9

παυστήριος.definition: fit for ending or relieving; alleviation, Nic.Th.746; Ar.Byz.Arg.S.OT11

Παφλαγών.definition: Paphlagonian, Il.2.851, al.; of Cleon , Ar.Eq.2,6, Nu.581, al. :—Adj. X.An.5.4.13: the country, ib.6.1.15

πάφλασμα.definition: boiling: metaph., in pl., blusterings, Ar.Av.1243

παχύδερμος.definition: thick-skinned, Arist.GA783a2: Comp; metaph., dull, stupid, Men.Epit.574, Luc.Tim.23

παχύθριξ.definition: gen. with thick hair: Comp. Arist.GA782b5

παχύκαυλος.definition: with a thick stalk or stem, Thphr.HP6.2.6

παχύκνημος.definition: with fat or thick legs, Ar.Pl.560, D.L.7.1

παχυμέρεια.definition: thickness of parts, S.E.M.9.86; opp. Theo Sm.p.97 H

παχυμερής.definition: consisting of thick or coarse parts; metaph. in Adv., loosely, broadly, roughly, Str.1.4.7, cf. 8 , Ach. Tat.Intr.Arat.18; cursorily, Just.Nov.53.4.1

πάχυνσις.definition: thickening, Arist.Mete.383a11, Thphr.CP6.11.7; hardening of eggs by boiling, Gal.6.707

παχύπους.definition: gen. thick-footed, v.l. in Arist.HA557a23, cf. Adam.2.48

παχυσμός.definition: a growing fat, Hp.Epid.6.8.11; thickening, Damocr. ap. Gal.13.988

παχύστομος.definition: thick at the brim, Henioch.1; metaph., speaking with a broad accent, of the Str.14.2.28:—hence ibid

παχύφλοιος.definition: with thick rind or bark, Thphr.HP1.5.2, Dsc.1.13, Gal.6.270, Gp.10.75.2

παχυχειλής.definition: thick-lipped, of shell-fish, Arist.HA528a29:—also Ruf.Fr.70; Gal.13.491

παχύχυμος.definition: with thick juices, Id.6.261, Alex.Aphr.Pr.1.52, etc

πεδαρτάω.definition: Pythag. word for = Iamb.VP31.197; D.L.8.20, cf. Suid.; . . Iamb.VP22.101, 33.231

πεδέρχομαι.definition: v. III, IV.5: aor. imper. = Id.; subj. = Id

πεδοιχνέω.definition: = go in search of, pursue, B.15.9

Πεδοσείων.definition: earth-shaker, coined as etym. of Corn.ND4

πεδοστιβής.definition: earth-treading, opp; on foot, opp. A.Pers.127

πεζεύω.definition: go or travel on foot, walk; go or travel by land, opp. going by sea, X.An.5.5.[4], Plb.16.29.11; Id.10.48.6; land-forces, Arist.Pol.1327b10; of Xerxes passing by his bridge over the Hellespont, Isoc.4.89; pass it like…

πεζίδιον.definition: Dim. of II.2, ribbon, to be read for EM749.37, Suid

πειρασμός.definition: trial, LXXDe.4.34, al., 1 Ep.Pet.4.12; worry, LXXEc.5.2

πελεκητής.definition: hewer of wood or stone, Gloss. , restd. in IG12.349.20

πελταστής.definition: one who bears a light shield; in pl., generally, light troops, Id.HG4.4.16, IG12.97.17, 99.5, etc

πεμπάδαρχος.definition: commander of a body of five, X.Cyr.2.1.23 , Eq.Mag.4.9 : Hsch. s.v

πεμπάς.definition: the number five, Pl.R.546c, Phd.104a; group of five, X.Cyr.2.1.22 and 24, HG7.2.6, Dam.Pr.203; cf

πένθιμος.definition: also D.S.11.57:— = foreg; sorry, wretched, E.Alc.622: of death, Epigr.Gr. 204.7

πεντάκλινος.definition: of a room, with five couches, Chares2 J., Callix.1; PSI5.533.3 : as Subst., Arist.Mir.842b21, PCair.Zen.445.13

πενταμοιρία.definition: arc of five degrees, Paul. Al.S.3

πεντάμυρον.definition: a kind of ointment, Orib.Fr.70, Alex.Trall.7.8:—written perh. rightly, Aët.12.61

πενταναΐα.definition: squadron of five vessels, Hell. Oxy. 2.4, Polyaen.3.4.2

πεντανούμμιον.definition: a piece of five sesterces, Zonar

πενταπάλαιστος.definition: five handbreadths wide, long, etc., X.Cyn.9.14, 10.3; cf

πενταπλασιάζομαι.definition: Pass., to be multiplied by five, interpol. in Nicom.Ar.1.21

πεντάπλοκος.definition: five times twisted, Hp. ap. Paul.Aeg.6.78

πενταπρωτεία.definition: board of the first five men, Lat. quinqueprimi, Cod.Just.12.28.2.1

πεντάπυλος.definition: with five gates: a quarter of Syracuse, Plu.Dio29

πεντάρραβδος.definition: or consisting of five; = Lat. praetor quinquefascalis, IGRom.1.971

πεντάσκαλμος.definition: with five sets of tholes , Ephipp.5.17

πεντασπίθαμος.definition: five spans long, broad, or high, X.Cyn.2.4,7, Str.15.1.57; BCH54.97

πενταστάδιος.definition: of five stades, Str.7.6.1, 15.1.21: distance of five stades, Id.7.6.2

πενταστάτηρος.definition: five in weight, Sosicr.1 codd. Poll

πεντάστιχος.definition: of five lines or verses, AP9.173

πεντάστομος.definition: with five mouths or openings, of the Nile, Hdt.2.10; of the Ister, Id.4.47; of the Rhone, Str.4.1.8

πενταφάρμακος.definition: consisting of five drugs or ingredients : pentapharmacum, Hist. Aug.Hel.5

πεντέγραμμος.definition: consisting of five lines, draughts played on a board with five lines, S.Fr.429; cf

πεντεδραχμία.definition: sum of five X.HG1.6.12, Din.1.56; coin worth five cj. in Polyaen.3.10.14

πεντεκαιδεκαετηρίς.definition: term of fifteen years, Sch.Th.1.18: as Adj., fifteen-year cycle, Men. Prot.p.49 D

πεντέλοιπος.definition: remaining out of five, last of five, Cic. Att. 14.21.4, 15.2.4

πεντεμυριομέδιμνος.definition: of fifty thousand medimni burden, Tz.H.2.108

πεντεσύριγγος.definition: with five holes, pillory, Ar.Eq.1049, cf. Poll.8.72: metaph., of palsy, Polyeuct. ap. Arist.Rh.1411a22

πεντετάλαντος.definition: worth or consisting of five; weighing five talents, Simp.in Ph.1104.10

πεντετηρίς.definition: term of five years; festival celebrated every fifth year , Id.6.111, Th.3.104, IG 12.84.6, 32, 22.1172.27

πεντετριάζομαι.definition: Pass., to be conquered five times, AP11.84

πεντηκοντάδραχμος.definition: worth fifty drachmae; weighing fifty drachmae, IG 7.3498.26

πεντηκονταετής.definition: of or lasting fifty years, D.S.4.58, etc.: fem., Th.5.32 codd

πεντηκονταετία.definition: the age of fifty years, D.H.4.32; period of fifty years, ib.532, Sch.Th.1.97

πεντηκοντάπαις.definition: consisting of fifty; having fifty children, Id.Supp.321

πεντηκοντάπλεθρος.definition: fifty plethra large, Eust.776.60: poet. Nonn.D.25.504

πεντηκόσταρχος.definition: chairman of the company which farmed the AB297, Phot

πεντηκοστεύομαι.definition: Pass., to be charged with a tax of two per cent. on any articles, D.35.29; also of the articles, to have the tax paid upon them, . . ib. 30

πεντηκοστολόγιον.definition: office of IG 11 .154 A 38 , Anon. ap. Suid

πεντηκοστολόγος.definition: collector of the at Athens, D.21.133, 34.7, Eub.122; at Delos, SIG 975.10 ; at Cyparissia, ib.952.9

πεντηκοστύς.definition: body of fifty, as a division of the Spartan army, Th.5.68; X.An.3.4.22

πεντηκοστώνης.definition: farmer of the prob. in AB 297 , cf. Ostr. 43 , Theb.Ostr. 130

πέντοζος.definition: with five branches: as Subst., of the human hand, Hes.Op.742, Hsch. s.v

πεντόροβος.definition: = Dsc.3.140, Plin. HN 25.29; an architectural ornament in this form, IG 11.161 B 19 : BCH 32.11 , IG 22.1451.29, 1452.7

πεντώροφος.definition: with five stories, D.H.Rh.1.3, D.S.1.45, etc

πεπαίνω.definition: aor. :—Pass., fut; metaph., soften, assuage, Ar.V.646: Plu.2.102a: X.Cyr.4.5.21: AP12.80 ; of a person, E.Heracl.159

πεπλογραφία.definition: description of the peplos, or the subjects worked on it, title of work by Varro, being a sort of 'Book of Worthies', Cic.Att.16.11.3

πεπλοποιία.definition: making of the peplos, metaph., Dam.Pr.339

πεποίθησις.definition: trust, confidence, boldness, LXX4 Ki.18.19, Phld.Lib.p.22 O., Ph.2.444, Ep.Eph.3.12, Philum.Ven.2.4; J.AJ1.3.1: ib.10.1.4: in pl., Babr.43.19

πεπονθέω.definition: to be affected, in aor. Dam.Pr.60

πεπόνθησις.definition: passivity, modification, Simp.in Cat.130.1, Dam.Pr.58, al.; opp. ib.176

περαίνω.definition: Pi.P.10.28, Philol.1, etc.; poet; limit, Iamb.Comm.Math.3:— elsewh. Pass., to be limited or finite, Arist.Ph.207a16: Id.Cael.273a4; esp. in part. opp. Id.Ph.266b22, Cael.272a15

περαῖος.definition: Comp., anything further, PFay.124.8; Subst., the country on the other side of the river, etc., Str.4.1.12; SIG588.29 : freq. with gen. whether partitive or objective, the part of Boeotia over against [Chalcis], Hdt.8.…

περατής.definition: = Suid. s. h. v; wanderer, emigrant, LXXGe.14.13: expl. of Ph.1.439

περδίκειος.definition: of a partridge, Poll.6.33, cf. Suid

περδίκιον.definition: Dim. of Eub.123, Ephipp.15.8; a plant, Polygonum maritimum, Thphr.HP1.6.11; = Dsc.4.85

περδικοθήρας.definition: partridge-catcher, name of a species of hawk, Ael.NA12.4

περιαγγέλλω.definition: announce by messages sent round; abs., send or carry a message round, Id.7.119; v.l. for in D.21.4

περιαγόραιος.definition: haunter of the market-place, Hsch., Phot., Suid

περιάγω.definition: fut. Men.532.13, etc. :—lead or draw; cause to revolve, Pl.Lg.898d, cf. Plot.5.1.2:—Pass., rotate, Pl.Ti.79b

περιαγωγή.definition: Dor. turning round; metaph., distraction, Plu.2.588d

περιάθρησις.definition: looking at on all sides, Ph.1.142, al

περιαίρεσις.definition: taking away a person's goods, etc., Stoic.3.96

περιαιρετέος.definition: to be done away with; neut. one must remove, Antyll. ap. Orib.50.2.10; Gp.5.29.4; Aët.7.26; one must do away with, Arist.Oec.1345b26; Id.Rh.Al.1427a7; D.S.19.8

περιαιρέω.definition: aor. Hdt.3.159, etc.:—take away; make void, cancel a vow, LXXNu.30.13

περιακολουθέω.definition: follow about, Heraclid.Pol.44; encircle, Polem.Phgn.9, al

περιακοντίζω.definition: dart at from all sides, Plu.Galb.26

περιαλγέω.definition: to be greatly pained at a thing, Antipho Soph.54; Th.4.14; Pl.Hipparch.229d; Ael.VH2.4, cf. Ph.2.178; Id.Fr.57 H.: c. acc., Id.2.436

περιαλγής.definition: feeling extreme pain, mental or; very painful, Nic.Th.497. Adv. D.C.78.24: Comp. Aret.SD1.13

περιαλείφω.definition: fut. SIG1097.7 :(smear all over, Ar.Eq.907; overlay it with silver, Pl.Criti.116d; whitewash, SIGl.c., cf. IG22.1672.140: metaph., Gal.5.535:—Pass., of the mouth of the hive, Arist.HA624a14

περιαμάομαι.definition: Med., gather from all sides, Gp.1.14.8, cf. Hsch., Phot

περιαμαρτίζω.definition: make a sin-offering, Aq., Sm., Thd.Ex.29.36

περιαμπέχω.definition: cover all over, Id.Phd.98d; later Ph.l.c.: metaph., Philostr.VS2.22

περιαμύνω.definition: defend or guard all round, Plu.Alc.7

περιαμύσσω.definition: Att. prick or wound on all sides, Pl.Ax.365c: gloss on Gal.19.130

περιαναγκάζω.definition: force round, Hp.Art.62, Gal.18.336:—hence Subst. Apollon.Cit.3

περιανίστημι.definition: rouse up, dub. in Ph.2.552:—Pass., with aor. 2, pf., and plpf. Act., arise from sleep, start up, Id.1.672, al., Apollod.2.1.4

περιαντλέω.definition: pour all over, Dsc.2.114 , Archig. ap. Aët.3.194: metaph., Plu.2.502c:—Pass., to be completely drowned, Sch.Opp.H.1.155: metaph., LXX4 Ma.15.32; Gal.10.469

περιαπλόω.definition: unfold and spread around, f.l. in Placit.5.26.4

περίαπτος.definition: hung round, appended, i.e. an; as Subst. = amulet, Pl.R.426b, Thphr.HP9.19.2, etc.; adventitious charm, Arist.EN1099a16: pl., ornaments, Ph.1.608

περιάπτω.definition: fut. Lys.21.24, etc.:—tie, fasten, hang; metaph., X.Cyr.1.5.9; Id.Mem.2.6.13; Phld.Rh.1.208S.: mostly in bad sense, attach to one, Simon.97 , Ar.Pl.590; Lys.l.c., cf. Pl.Euthd.272c; Id.Ap.35a; X.Cyr.8.4.32; D.20.10 ; …

περιαράσσω.definition: break all in pieces, Nic.Th.842 , Poll.1.111,114

περιάργυρος.definition: set in silver, Chares4 J., cf. LXXEp.Je.8; App.BC1.106

περιαργυρόω.definition: case, plate with silver, Theopomp.Hist.40:—Pass., IG11 .161 B77 , LXXEx.27.11, Diog. ap. TheonProg.5, PRyl.110.14

περιαρμόζω.definition: fasten, fit on, Pl.Ax.366a; intr., fit closely round, Arist.Mech.854a22

περιαρόω.definition: fut. Id.5.25:—plough round, l.c., Plu.2.820e, etc

περιαρτάω.definition: hang round or on, Poll.1.242; Max.Tyr.36.2:—Pass., of persons, having it hung round one, S.E.M.2.105; Philostr.VS2.1.8; of things, to be hung round, Plu.Per.38, cf. Poll.5.101

περιασθμαίνω.definition: breathe round, Ach.Tat.4.4; breathe hard, Hld.8.9

περιαστράπτω.definition: flash around, Act.Ap.9.3, cf; dazzle, is dazzled with beauty, Junc. ap. Stob.4.50.95, cf. Gal.19.220

περιασχολέω.definition: keep busy about a thing, v.l. in Luc.Bis Acc.11

περιαυγάζω.definition: beam round about, illuminate, Ph.1.364, Hld.8.9

περιαυγέομαι.definition: Pass., to be surrounded with light, Str.16.4.6 , Longin.17.2

περιαυγής.definition: beaming round about, Ph.1.570: Sup., ib.443; Metop. ap. Stob.3.1.115

περίαυλον.definition: courtyard, enclosure, Keil-Premerstein Zweiter Bericht No.87 , Supp.Epigr.2.481

περιαυτίζομαι.definition: Med., to be busy about oneself; speak much on one subject, Hsch., Phot., Suid

περιαυτολογέω.definition: speak about oneself, brag, Phld.Hom.p.60 O., S.E.P.1.62, Iamb.Myst.2.10, Eust.100.37

περιαυτολογία.definition: speaking about oneself, bragging, Plu.2.41b, al., Alex.Rh.p.4S

περιαχυρίζω.definition: free from husks, Dieuch. ap. Orib.4.7.21

περιβιάζομαι.definition: use great force, Aesop.103: c. acc., do violence to, Gal.17.177

περιβιβάζω.definition: put astride, mount a rider on a horse, Plu.Crass.31

περιβιβρώσκω.definition: gnaw all round, pf. Diph.34; Plu.2.1059e:—Pass., of leaves, Dsc.2.133; D.S.2.4: to be corroded by ulcers, Dsc.1.71, 2.74, Gal.12.875

περίβλεπτος.definition: looked at from all sides, admired of all observers, E.Andr.89; Antiph.175.5; X.Eq.10.1 ; Isoc.10.17; mostly of persons, E.HF508, cf. Epicur.Sent.7, LXXPr.31.23, etc.; . . X.HG7.1.30; Id.Smp.8.38, etc.; Carneïsc.Herc.1…

περιβλεπτότης.definition: celebrity, as a title, BGU547.3 , Gloss

περιβλέπω.definition: look round about, gaze around; trans., look round at, X.Cyr.5.1.4:—Med., M.Ant.7.55, cf. Ev.Marc.3.5

περίβλεψις.definition: looking or gazing about; close examination, Plu.Alex.23

περίβλημα.definition: garment, Arist.Pr.870a27; = II.2, Ph.2.148; enceinte, fortification, Pl.Plt.288b

περιβόητος.definition: in bad sense, notorious, scandalous, Lys.3.30: Antiph.25: . . D.18.297, cf. Din.2.15. Adv. notoriously, Aeschin.1.113, D.17.5

περιβοθρόομαι.definition: Pass., have a trench dug round, Thphr.CP5.13.1

περιβόλαιον.definition: that which is thrown; = II.2, CIG4590

περιβολή.definition: covering, garment, Pl.Plt.280b; dress; circumnavigation, Luc.Ner.1

περιβομβέω.definition: buzz, hum round, Luc.Lex.16,Im.13, Alciphr.2.4; Max.Tyr.23.4:—Pass., Agath.1.17,3.18

περιβόσκομαι.definition: of beasts, fishes, etc., feed on all round, Nic.Al.391, Th.611, Luc.Asin.17; of tribes, D.P.383: metaph., Call.Ap.84

περιβρέμω.definition: roar or bellow round about, A.R.2.323, cf. Orph.A.689:—Med., c. dat., D.P.132, Opp.C.2.67

περιβρίθω.definition: intr., to be exceeding heavy, droop, Nic.Al.180, Th.851; bear a heavy crop, Arat.1049; with leaves, Nic.Al.143

περιβρομέω.definition: = Ep. impf. A.R.4.17: c. acc., buzz about, Id.1.879

περιβυρσόομαι.definition: Pass., to be covered with hides all round, Ath.Mech.25.1

περιβώμιος.definition: round the altar, Suid. s.v. Subst., images placed about the altar, LXX2 Ch.34.3:—but , space round a Rev.Hist.Rel.97.275; functionaries attached to Asiatic cults, IG12.1126 : hence Peribomius, name of an Archigallus, …

περιγελάω.definition: deride, A.D.Synt.284.21; smile all around , ib.311.27, cf.Phot. s.v

περιγληνάομαι.definition: turn round the eyeballs, glare around, of a lion, Theoc.25.241

περιγληνής.definition: having eyes all round, i.e. the Milky Way, Arat.476

περιγλύφω.definition: peel, Aristid.Or.47 .45; trim, of papyrus, Heliod. ap. Orib.50.9.11

περιγομφάομαι.definition: Pass., to be pierced by nails, f.l. for in Lib.Or.56.20

περίγραμμα.definition: that which is written around or; enclosed space, ring, Luc.Anach.38

περιγράφω.definition: draw a line round; Geom., circumscribe, Euc.4.3,5, cf. Archim.Sph.Cyl.1.3,al.; ib.40

περιδαπανάομαι.definition: to be wasted away all round, Philum. ap. Aët.5.127

περιδειπνέω.definition: cause one to eat a funeral feast, LXX2 Ki.3.35 :—Pass., Artem.4.81

περίδειπνον.definition: funeral feast, D.18.288, Aen.Tact.10.5, Men.367, Hegesipp.Com.1.11, PTeb.118.1 , Phld.Acad.Ind.p.35 M., etc.; Anaxipp.1.42; title of work by Timo, D.L.9.115

περιδέραιος.definition: passed round the neck; Subst. necklace, Ar.Fr.320.5, Com.Adesp.146, Arist.Po.1454b24, Plu.Sert.14, Luc.Pisc.12, etc

περιδεσμεύω.definition: tie round, Sch.Ar.Ec.118, 319 :—also Gp.17.19.3, Sch.Opp.H.2.34:—Pass., Zos.Alch.p.233 B

περιδέω.definition: bind, tie round or on, Hdt.1.193; bind round, bandage with, Hp.Fract.13: Arist.HA623a14

περιδηριάω.definition: fight about, Ep. part. Q.S.6.287:— Med., Id.4.165

περιδιαιρέω.definition: part off, remove all round, Heliod. ap. Orib.44.8.24, Gal.2.296

περιδιαρθρόομαι.definition: to be articulated on all sides, Gal.18.433

περιδίδωμι.definition: only in Med., stake, wager, c. gen. pretii, let us make a wager of a tripod, i.e. let us wager a tripod , Il.23.485; I will wager myself, i.e. my life, Od.23.78; . . lay a wager whether . . , Ar.Ach.1115; Id.Eq.791: w…

περιδινεύω.definition: hover around, prob. for sq. in S.Fr.334 ; revolve round, D.S.18.27

περιδινέω.definition: whirl, wheel round, Aeschin.3.167: D.Chr.1.56: Men.Rh.p.442 S.; Luc.VH1.9: set in motion all round, Alciphr.1.39:—Med., AP7.485 ; also, take a stroll, Luc.Lex.2:—Pass., to be whirled round, Ph.1.145, Ti.Locr.97c, Iamb…

περιδίνησις.definition: whirling round, rotation, revolution, Plu.Flam.10, cf. Plot.2.2.1, Theol.Ar.60; Arr.Tact.38.3, Philostr. Jun.Im.10; Heliod. ap. Orib.46.11.12

περιδινήτειρα.definition: fem., causing to revolve, of Aphrodite, PMag.Par.1.2918

περιδινητής.definition: one who causes to revolve, Hsch

περιδιώκω.definition: pursue on all sides, Str.6.1.8, S.E.M.1.227 , Aq. Jb.13.25

περιδονέω.definition: v.l. for D.H.1.19 ; of a wounded elephant, Agath.3.27

περίδραξις.definition: grasping with the hands, Plu.2.392b, cf. 979d

περιδράσσομαι.definition: Att. grasp, Ph.2.136, Hierocl.p.37 A., Plu.Cam.26, Lys.17: c. acc., Phld.Mort.18: Iamb. ap. Simp.in Cat.375.9: abs., Ph.2.353; arrogantly claim, Phld.Rh.1.214 S

περιδρομή.definition: running round, encircling, Plu.Aem.20; revolution, E.Hel.776

περιδρομίς.definition: circular track on the top of the walls of Babylon, prob. in Ph. Byz.Mir.5.2

περίδρομος.definition: running round, encircling; wandering, roaming, A.Supp.350 ; Ar.Ra.472: gadabout woman, Thgn.581

περιεγκεντρίζω.definition: fut. surround with beams laid in cuttings in rafters, IG22.463.62

περιείλημα.definition: that which is wrapped round, Poll.7.91, Sch.Ar.Nu.10

περιείλησις.definition: wrapping round, Herod.Med. ap; revolution, Poll.4.156

περιείλω.definition: wrap up, swathe, Ath.15.672d:—Med., swathe oneself, Ar.Ra.1066:—Pass., to be wrapped up, Ath.15.672e; to be coiled, of a snake's tail, Gal.14.265, cf. OGI56.63 ; to be concentrated, Ach.Tat.Intr.Arat.3

περιεκλεπτύνω.definition: reduce to extreme smallness or fineness, in Pass., Zos.Alch.p.223 B

περιελαύνω.definition: fut. Ar.Eq.290, etc. :—drive round; draw or build round, Il.18.564; Od.7.113; A.Pers.872 ; Plu.Rom.11

περιελίσσω.definition: intr., wind about, of a guide, Plu.Crass.29:—Pass., rotale, Emp.46 ; of troops, wheel, Arr.Tact.21.3: so intr. in Act., ib.39.3

περιέννυμι.definition: Ep. Verb used in aor. Act. and Med., put round, Il.16.670,680; 18.451:—Med., to put on one's cloak, Hes.Op.539

περιέπω.definition: impf. Hdt.7.181, X.Mem.2.9.5: fut. Id.Cyr.4.4.12, Luc.Tim.12: aor. Hdt.1.73, al. ; inf. ib.115: fut. Med. Id.2.115: aor. Pass. Id.5.1 :-treat, handle, whether well or ill, usu. with an Adv. or some modal word to deter…

περιεργάζομαι.definition: c. acc., to be busy about 'some new thing', Ar.Ec.220; Philostr.Im.2.12; meddle, interfere with, Chilo ap.Stob.3.1.172; Plb.18.51.2: abs., to be a busybody, D.26.15, 32.28, Men.Epit.358, Lib.Ep.1068.3

περιέργω.definition: Att. enclose, encompass, Hdt.2.148, Th.1.106, 5.11; X.HG4.1.15; Ar.Lys.810

περιέρπω.definition: walk about, IG42.121.7, 34; creep round, Gal.2.549

περιέρχομαι.definition: impf. Ar.Th.504 cod.:—go; c. acc. pers., in Hom. , encompass, of sounds, . . Il.10.139, cf. Od.17.261; . . 19.444; of the effect of wine, 9.362

περιεσθίω.definition: eat all round, nibble at, Luc.Merc.Cond.26: metaph., Id.Lex.23: aor., D.S.5.33

περιζέω.definition: boil round, Plu.2.567c, Luc.Tox.20, Gal.7.707; metaph., Eun.VSp.463 B

περίζωμα.definition: girdle worn round the loins, PRev.Laws94.7 , Plu.Rom.21 , Poll.7.65, etc.; worn by athletes, Paus.1.44.1; by priests, Plu.Aem.33; by smiths, Arr.Epict.4.8.16; wear the apron, of a cook, Hegesipp.Com.1.7: hence Plu.2.1…

περιζωματίας.definition: affecting the waist, of shingles, etc., Orib.Fr.102

περιζώννυμι.definition: gird upon a person, J.AJ6.9.4, cf. App.Hann.20, Nonn.D.40.460 ; gird, prob. in Ruf. ap. Orib.inc.20.1:—more freq. in Med. with pf. Pass., gird oneself with, Theopomp. Com.37; Plu.Rom.16, Cor.9; put him on as a defence…

περιζώστρα.definition: apron, Anaxandr.69; ribbon twined round a garland, dub. in Theoc.2.122

περιηγέομαι.definition: abs., explain, describe, Luc.Cont.1, D Mort.20.1; Pass., to be made to revolve, Philol.[21]

περιήγησις.definition: leading round and explaining, as; geographical description, Str.9.2.6; Ath.7.278d; Aristid.Or.26.102, cf. Porph.Antr.2 ; title of poem by Dionysius of Alexandria; title of work by Crito, Suid

περιηγητής.definition: one who guides strangers, cicerone; author of geographical descriptions, as Dionysius also of Polemo, Ath.5.210a, cf. Plu.Them.32

περιήκω.definition: to have come round to one; of Time, to have come round, Plu.Ages.35; Aristid.Or.50.1, cf. Parth.30.2

περιημεκτέω.definition: to be aggrieved, chafe, etc., Hdt.1.44,164, 4.154, al.: c. gen. pers., to be aggrieved at or with him, Id.8.109: abs., Id.1.114

περιθελόω.definition: fumigate thoroughly, Hsch., Phot.: prob. in Men.530.22

περιθέλωμα.definition: in pl., fumigations, gloss on Hsch

περιθέσιμος.definition: to be put round or on, J.AJ15.8.2

περίθεσις.definition: putting round, putting on, in the act of application, Heraclas ap. Orib.48.12.1; 1 Ep.Pet.3.3; Philum.Ven.7.8; S.E.P.3.15: pl., J.AJ19.1.5; Sor.1.85

περίθετος.definition: also put round or to be put round, a mask, Aristomen.5; a mask with a wig attached, Ar.Th.258, cf. Sch.; false hair, wig, Plb.3.78.2; Ael.VH1.26, EM790.19; Ath.12.523a; alone, Amphis2, Men.359

περιθέω.definition: run or gad about, Ar.Eq.65, Pl.R.475d: metaph., Plot.2.2.2,5.1.4, al

περιθεωρέω.definition: go round and observe, Luc.Herm.44; survey, consider thoroughly, Diog.Oen.24

περίθλασις.definition: crushing, contusion, Plu.2.609e. Herod.Med. ap.Orib.10.37.6, Sor.1.80, Gal.18.468

περιθλάω.definition: bruise or crush all round, Plu.2.341a , Sor.1.118 , Gal.18.640

περιθλίβω.definition: press all round, Nonn.D.10.370; squeeze out, Nonn.D.17.361

περιθνήσκω.definition: of flesh, mortify round a wound, Hp.Fract.33

περιθραύω.definition: break small, grind down, Arist.Pr.935b2:—; metaph., crush, Ph.1.564,al

περιθριγκόω.definition: edge or fence all round, Plu.Mar.21

περιθρομβόομαι.definition: Pass., to be clotted up, of blood, Heliod. ap. Orib.50.52.3, Gal.10.345

περιθρύπτω.definition: and , rub or pound in pieces, l.c. ; Ph.1.501; Id.2.527

περιθυρέω.definition: to be about the door, Ael.NA1.11,14, Phot

περίθυρον.definition: door-way, i.e. door-posts and lintel, Ephes.4No.28

περιιάχω.definition: ring around, re-echo, Od.9.395: Ep. impf. for Hes.Th.678

περιιδρόω.definition: sweat all over or excessively, S.E.M.11.159, Aët.8.7

περιιδρύομαι.definition: to be set up around, Philostr.Im.1.12

περιίζομαι.definition: sit round about, Hdt.1.202, 6.78: c. acc. objecti, Id.5.4, cf. 41

περιικνέομαι.definition: reach on all sides, Arat.473, cf. Sch.Arat.862

περιιππάζομαι.definition: Med., = sq., Polyaen.4.3.29, Zos.1.53, PMag. Leid.V.7.10

περιίπταμαι.definition: later form for Arist.HA542b24, D.C.58.5, Alex.Trall.Febr.4

περιιστάνω.definition: later form of sq., Vett.Val.285.33:—also Chamael. ap. Ath.1.21e

περικαθαίρω.definition: cleanse on all sides or completely; metaph., purify completely, Arist.Fr.496, cf. Thphr.Char.16.14; Pl.Criti.120a; LXXDe.18.10; D.Chr.48.17

περικαθάπτω.definition: fasten or put on; = Str.16.4.6; Dsc.5.95; Id.Eup.2.45; enclose, Ps.-Callisth.3.31

περικάθαρμα.definition: expiation, ib.Pr.21.18; = I.2, 1 Ep.Cor.4.13, cf. Arr.Epict.3.22.78

περικάθημαι.definition: Ion. Ion. 3pl. impf. or Hdt.8.111 :—to be seated all round, at table, Id.3.32 codd.: mostly c.acc., invest, besiege a town, Id.1.103, al., cf.LXXJd.9.31; also ib.3 Ki.15.27; of ships, blockade, Hdt.9.75: c.acc.pers., …

περικαθίεμαι.definition: Pass., have hung round one, Ph.2.266

περικαθίζω.definition: cause to sit around or over, Hp.Mul.1.51; invest a city, J.AJ8.14.1, cf. 13.5.5

περικαθίσταμαι.definition: take up position around, invest, Iamb.Bab.3

περικαίω.definition: Att. scorch, Thphr.CP2.3.8; metaph., inflame, excite, LXX4 Ma.16.3:—Pass., And.2.2

περικακέω.definition: to be in extreme ill-luck, Plb.1.58.5; Id.3.84.6

περικάλυμμα.definition: covering, garment, Pl.Plt.279d: metaph., pretext, Ph.1.608

περικαλύπτω.definition: cover all round; put round as a covering, . . put sleep as a cloak around him, Il.14.359; Pl.Ti.34b; LXX3 Ki.8.7: metaph., throw a veil of darkness over the deeds, E.Ion1522

περικαμπή.definition: bending round, a sharp curve, Hp.Art.46

περικαμπής.definition: bent round, Aq.Is.40.4, Ho.6.8; by zigzag paths, Vett.Val.263.13

περικάμπτω.definition: bend round, Hp.Art.18; make; intr., turn round a corner or bend, Pl.Euthd.291b: c. acc. loci, Arist.Aud.802a35; Ael.VH1.15: abs., bend or sweep round, App.Pun.95

περικαταβάλλω.definition: only in Ep. aor. , throw down around or upon, A.R.3.707; lay him prostrate on . . , Nonn.D.37.582; wrap a sheepskin round it, Orac. in Damocr. ap. Alex.Trall.1.15: metaph., Q.S.1.819, 5.469

περικατάγνυμι.definition: break all round, Thphr.HP3.7.4 , Ph.1.657 ; break it about his back, Ar.Lys.357; Alciphr.3.45; Ath.1.17c: intr. in pf. part. D.H.8.67

περικατακλάω.definition: break all round about, Apollon.Lex. s.v

περικαταλαμβάνω.definition: embrace, enclose, hem in on all; overtake, Thphr.HP4.2.5, cf. 3.4.5, 3.16.1, D.S.4.54, 20.74, al.; J.AJ2.16.3:—Pass., Archyt.1, J.AJ20.4.1; to be overtaken by . . , Thphr.CP2.81; Arist.Mu.400b1, Plb.14.4.10; compelled…

περικατάλαμψις.definition: Doricized form of = of planets, Ti.Locr.97b

περικαταλείπω.definition: leave behind in, Nic.Th.809; f.l. in Plb.4.63.10

περικατάληπτος.definition: overtaken and surrounded; detected, LXX2 Ma.14.41, D.S.4.76, Theodor. ap. Stob.4.20.71

περικαταπίπτω.definition: only Ep. aor. fall down upon, A.R.3.543; Q.S.5.502, cf. 9.168; esp. fall upon so as to be pierced, A.R.2.831, cf. Tryph.576

περικαταρρέω.definition: fall in and go to ruin, Lys.30.22

περικαταρρήγνυμι.definition: tear off round about, strip off, D.H.9.39, Nic.Dam.62 J.:—Med., she tore off and rent her outer garment, X.Cyr.5.1.6

περικατάσσομαι.definition: Pass., late form of Sch.Il.11.631; cf

περικαταστρέφω.definition: turn round over, Dsc.2.61:— Pass., to be overturned, Str.16.2.13

περικατέχω.definition: shut in all round, J.BJ3.7.3, 6.4.5:—Pass., aor. 1 part. v.l. in Ph.1.657

περικάτω.definition: Adv. upside down, Stratt.34 ; Epicur.Nat.87 G., cf. Nat.Herc.1420.4; headlong, Plu.2.943d

περίκαυσις.definition: burning all round; spray, douche, f.l. for in Thphr.Sud.16

περικείρω.definition: aor. inf. Philostr.Ep.61: pf; metaph., shear of its walls, Ael.VH7.8

περικεράννυμι.definition: temper acrid humours, Alex.Trall.7.3:—Pass., f.l. in Plu.2.924b; cf

περικεφάλαιος.definition: round the head: hence; Subst. covering for the head, helmet, cap, Call.Com.1 D., Aen. Tact.24.6, PPetr.3p.328 , etc.; IG 11.161 B77 , cf. 22.1478.16, 12.647.30 , Plb.3.71.4, J.AJ6.9.4, Antyll. ap. Orib.6.36.3

περικέφαλον.definition: top of an upright in an engine, Ath.Mech.23.3,al

περικίδναμαι.definition: Pass., spread round about AP5.291 ; ib.9.765 ; ib.651

περικινέω.definition: move round, gloss on Hsch. , cf. Dosith.p.434 K

περικιόνιος.definition: a name of Dionysus at Thebes, Orph.H.47.1, Mnaseas18

περικίων.definition: gen. surrounded with pillars, E.Fr.369.5 ; Id.IT405

περίκλασις.definition: breaking round or on something, Id.Lys.12; Gal.18.436; wheeling round of an army, Plb.10.23.6,11.23.2; Plu.Flam.8

περικλείω.definition: Ion. old Att. , shut in all round, enclose, Hdt.3.117, cf. 7.129,198; Th.2.90: abs., Ph.2.544:-Med., get them surrounded, Th.7.52:-Pass., Id.2.100. II. metaph., in Pass., to be confined, reduced, D.S.16.35; S.E.M.11.1…

περικλίνω.definition: decline, of the sun, Posidon.28; Pass., to be deflected, distorted, Phld.Rh.1.157 S

περικλονέω.definition: stir up all round, Q.S.2.649:—Pass., to be massed together, of clouds, Id.3.707

περικλύζω.definition: wash all round, Arist.Mir.837b21:— Pass., to be washed all round by the sea, of an island, Th.6.3; of a boat, Plu.Mar.36; i.e. venture not on the sea, Arat.287: metaph., to be overwhelmed, Lib.Decl.30.61; Gal.15.584

περίκλυσις.definition: = Ael.NA16.15; spray, douche, cj. in Thphr.Sud.16

περίκλυστος.definition: also A.Pers.880 :—washed all round by the sea, of islands, h.Ap.181, cf. A.Pers.596 , E.HF1080 , Ephipp.5.3 ; Str.16.2.13; 'belvederes', Plu.Comp.Cim.Luc.1; Str.2.5.24; D.H.5.13

περικλώζομαι.definition: Pass., to be hooted off on all sides, Eust.1504.31

περικνημίς.definition: covering for the leg, gaiter, D.H.4.16, Plu.Phil.9, Thd.Da.3.21, PLond.1.191.13
