περικνίζω.definition: scratch all round v.l. in Poll.9.113: metaph., keep nibbling at a thing, D.H.9.32, Plu.2.10e: aor. Med. of bees, AP9.226

περικνύω.definition: scratch or rub all round, Phot

περικοκκάζω.definition: cry cuckoo all round, Ar.Eq.697 ap.Phot

περικολάπτω.definition: trim all round, v.l. for in Hippiatr.8

περικολλάω.definition: glue all round, IG12.374.132, 136; Gp.12.33 , cf. Aët.7.106

περικολούω.definition: cut short, clip all round; metaph., humble, Plu.2.139b

περικολπίζω.definition: sail round a bay, Peripl.M.Rubr.57: c. acc., ib.34

περικομιδίζω.definition: carry round, Th.7.9:—Pass., go round, Id.3.81

περικομμάτιον.definition: Dim. of foreg. I, Ar.Eq.770, Alex.132, Athenio1.31

περικομπέω.definition: sound round about, LXXWi.17.4. II. declare loudly, J.BJ1.25.2

περικονδυλοπωροφίλα.definition: loving chalk-stones on the knuckles, epith. of the gout, Luc.Trag.202

περικοπή.definition: cutting all round, mutilation, e.g. of the Hermae at Athens, Th.6.28, And.1.15, Plu.Alc.18, etc.; lopping of a tree, Thphr.CP5.4.7; docking of hair, Plu.2.42b; trepanning, Id.Cat.Ma.9

περικόπτης.definition: mason, POxy.1146.15; thief, robber, Hsch., Phot

περικόπτω.definition: pf. Lys.14.42:—cut all round; lay waste , D.8.9: hence, plunder a person, Id.9.22:—Pass., PCair.Zen.44.24, 145.4 , D.H.10, 51, Str.11.13.2, etc.; Plu.Ant.68: abs., D.S.4.19: hence, simply, intercept, cut off, D.H.10.4…

περικορδακίζω.definition: dance the around, gloss on Sch.Ar.Eq.694

περικοσμέω.definition: deck all round, App.BC4.94, interpol. in J.Ap.2.35: in tmesi, Phoronis4:—Pass., LXXPs.143 .12

περικράζω.definition: croak or scream all round, Dionys.Av.1.9

περικρατέω.definition: have full command of : hold fast; lord it over, Carm.Pop.46.24, cf. Iamb. ap. Simp.in Cat.375.17; prevail over, Ph.2.383; controi, LXX4 Ma.1.9; J.AJ11.3.4; of an actor, Simp.in Epict.p.125 D.; master with the mind, Ph…

περικρατής.definition: grasping, tenacious, Simm.1.11; having full command over, Act.Ap.27.16, cf. Thd.Su.39 ; cf

περικράτησις.definition: predominance, Iamb. ap. Simp.in; prevailing signification, - EM584.4

περικρεμάννυμι.definition: hang round, AP11.66 , Nonn.D.26.254:—Pass., hang round, cling to, cj. in Plu.2.924b : c. dat., AP9.78

περικρεμής.definition: hanging, cj. for in; c. dat., hung round with, Luc.Trag.142

περικρούω.definition: strike off all round, having stones and shells knocked off, stripped of them, Pl.R.611e; when the headlands are broken away, by the river overflowing, Str.12.8.19. 2. strike all round, ring a metal or earthen vessel, …

περικρύπτω.definition: late impf. Ev.Luc.1.24: —conceal entirely, Luc.DMort.10.8, Eun.Hist.p.248 D., etc.:—Med., conceal oneself from, D.L.6.61

περικρώζω.definition: caw all round, of crows, D.C.58.5

περίκτησις.definition: acquisition, A.D.Synt.278.8, cf.S.E.M.7.166, 11.146, App.Prooem.11, Vett.Val.41.21, etc

περικτυπέω.definition: sound around, Hymn.Is.33, cf. Eun.Hist.p.246 D

περικυκλέω.definition: move in a circle, move around; intr., revolve, c. acc. cogn., Epicur.Ep.2p.53 U

περικυκλόω.definition: encircle, encompass, Arist.HA533b11; intr., go round, Luc.Ocyp.63

περικυλινδέω.definition: later fut. Vett.Val.115.21: aor. 1 round, Ar.Pax7; D.H.9.21, cf. D.S.18.34:— Pass., of an infant, Sor.1.85; of the shoulder in reducing dislocation, Gal.18.327: abs., roll about, Pl.Lg.893e: metaph., to be involved in…

περικυμαίνω.definition: heave or surge around, c. acc., Orph.H.83.3

περικυρτόομαι.definition: Pass., to be quite convex, Parth. ap. Ath.11.783b

περικυφόομαι.definition: Pass., to be bent all round, Apollon.Lex.s.v

περιλαλέω.definition: chatter exceedingly, gossip, Ar.Ec.230; describe, Philostr.Im.2.9

περιλάλητος.definition: much talked of, famous, of things and persons, Agath.2.15, 4.26, Hsch

περιλαμβάνω.definition: encompass or surround an enemy, Hdt.8.7,16, Plb.2.29.5, etc. ; intercept them at sea, Th.8.42; Plb.1.48.10; when you get hold of him, catch him, Hdt.5.23; Id.8.106; Pl.Sph.235b; cover it over, Phylarch.41 J.; also of …

περιλαμπής.definition: very brilliant, Ph.1.485 , cf. Max.Tyr.39.4 : metaph., Plu.Fab.19: neut. as Adv., Id.Crass.24, etc

περιλάμπω.definition: shine around or brightly, Id.Cam.17; c.acc., light up, Demad.39; illuminate, Ph.1.634; shine around, Plu.Cic.35; Act.Ap.26.13, cf. Ev.Luc.2.9:—Pass., to be illumined, Plu.Per.39, Dio46; Luc.Dom.8

περιλάπτω.definition: suck or lick all round, Pherecr.23

περιλείπομαι.definition: Med. and Pass., remain over, survive, Il.19.230; Hdt.1.82; Ar.Nu.725; E.Hel.426, cf. Pl.Ti.23c , Arist.Oec.1350a29, etc

περιλείχω.definition: lick all round, Ar.Pl.736; lick off, Arist.HA605a4; Luc.Icar.30

περιλεπίζω.definition: = sq., Ph.Bel.88.47, Diench. ap. Orib.4.7.15, Paul. Aeg.1.81, Sch.Ar.Lys.736

περιλέπω.definition: strip off all round, Il.1.236; Hdt.8.115; peel, Thphr.HP6.4.10 ; v

περιλεύκιος.definition: name of a stone, Herm. Trism. in Rev.Phil.32.274

περίλευκος.definition: edged with white, Callix.2; garment edged with white, Antiph.297

περιλιμνάζω.definition: surround with water, insulate; intr., become a lake, Ael.NA16.15

περιλιμπάνω.definition: later form of Simp.in Epict.p.119 D. , Sch.Ar.Pl.554, etc

περιλιχμάομαι.definition: = foreg., Theoc.25.226; lick up, Plu.Pyrrh.31; Luc.Prom.10

περίλυπος.definition: very sad, deeply grieved, Hp.Acut.42; opp. Isoc.1.42, Arist.EN1124a16; Demad.17, cf. LXXGe.4.6, al

περιλύω.definition: loosen round about, Aq.1 Ki.5.9; cancel, PLips.10ii31 , cf. POxy.323 , etc

περιμαίνομαι.definition: rage round about, rush furiously about; to be madly in love with, Ael.Ep.7: c. dat. rei, to be mad for, Naumach. ap. Stob.4.23.7

περιμάσσω.definition: Att. wipe all round; wipe off, Dsc.5.94

περιμάχητος.definition: fought about, fought for, Ar.Av.1404; Th.7.84; not a thing one would fight for, X.Smp.3.9, cf. Pl.R.521a, Lg.678e; Isoc.8.65, cf. 7.24, 10.17; such as are matters of contention, highly prized, Arist.EN1169a21, cf. Pol…

περιμελαίνομαι.definition: Pass., to be black all round, to have bright parts shaded off into dark. Plu.2.368c

περιμενεαίνω.definition: wish for ardently, in tmesi, A.R.1.670,771

περίμετρον.definition: circumference, Hdt.1.185, 2.15,41, Arist.Mir.840b34, Luc.VH2.40; Hdt.2.149; Ach.Tat.Intr.Arat.29

περίμετρος.definition: very large, Hom., only in; well fitting, of a garment, Aristaenet.1.1

περιμήκετος.definition: poet. for sq., very tall or high, Il.14.287; Od.6.103: c. gen., Arat.250

περιμηρύομαι.definition: Dor. Med., wind round, Ph.Bel.65.39, cf. 46:—Pass., to be surrounded by a cord, of a temple, prob. in Abh.Berl.Akad.1928.33

περιμοτόω.definition: dress a wound with lint, Heliod. ap. Orib.44.10.18, 47.15.8:—Subst. dressing with lint. Id. ap. Orib.46.19.4

περιναιέτης.definition: one of those who dwell round, neighbour, Il.24.488, A.R.4.470

περινέμομαι.definition: Pass., spread round, of fire, Plu.Dio46

περινεύω.definition: bend forward and look round timidly; incline first to one side then to the other, sway, Arist.Phgn.808a15; of a chariot, = Phryn.PSp.40 B

περινέω.definition: swim round, Hp. ap. Gal.19.130; Arist.HA621a18; Hdt.6.80: aor. part. Id.4.164

περινήχομαι.definition: swim or float about, D.H.1.15; Plu.2.977a; swim round . . , Q.S.14.548

περινίζω.definition: wash off all round, Il.24.419, cf. Hp.Fist.9:—Med., Id.Mul.2.158; D.S.4.51

περινίσομαι.definition: go round about, as the cups go round, Phoc.11; revolve, Orph.Fr.247.11; come round, of time, E.Alc.449

περινοέω.definition: contrive cunningly, Ar.Ra.958; consider on all sides, consider well, study carefully, Epicur.Nat.11.6; Plu.Brut.13, cf. Hierocl.in CA23p.469M.; understand a thing, M.Ant.1.7, S.E.M.2.9

περινόησις.definition: shrewdness, subtlety, Plu.2.509e; sustained thought, Plot.6.9.11

περινοστέω.definition: go round, visit, inspect; abs., go about, stalk about, Pl.R.558a; of vagrants, Ar.Pl.121,494, D.19.255; Alex.28, cf. Alciphr.1.10 , Jul.Ep.89

περινοτίζω.definition: moisten all round, Sor.1.22 ; Alex. Trall.1.15

περινότισις.definition: wetting all round, Archig. ap. Aët.3.194

περιξηραίνομαι.definition: become dry all round, Arist.GA758b25, Pr.870a24

περιξυράω.definition: Ion. shave all round, v.l. in Hdt.3.8:—Pass., Luc.Merc.Cond.33

περιξυστήρ.definition: surgical instrument for scraping or smoothing bones, Heliod.ap.Orib.46.11.29

περιξύω.definition: scrape all round, Hp. ap. Gal.19.130; scrape off or away, LXXWi.13.11, cf. Gal.2.653; nibble at, . . Opp.H.3.525:—Med., scrape oneself, Diocl.Fr.141, Alex.Aphr.in Top.455.25:—Pass., Hp.Mul.2.192; drilled out by a bore…

περιοδευτής.definition: traveller, Eust.1382.59; medical practitioner, Gal.12.844, Steph.in Hp.2.457D

περιοδεύω.definition: go all round, LXXZa.1.10; in military sense, patrol, Aen.Tact.22.10; Id.26.2; of dyke-watchers, PPetr.2p.17 ; of an inspector, go round vineyards, PCair.Zen.300.7 ; march round, App.BC1.58,al

περιοδίζω.definition: to be periodical, esp. in pres. part., Str.7.2.1; of fevers, intermittent, Ph.2.576, Gal.10.627

περιοιδέω.definition: swell round about, Hp.Vict.3.82, Herod.Med. ap. Orib.6.20.24

περιοικέω.definition: dwell round persons or places, c. acc., Hdt.1.57, al., X.An.5.6.16: abs., Hdt.5.23, Lys.7.28:—Pass., to be inhabited all round, Arist.Mete.354a4, Scyl.107, Scymn.766

περιοίκιον.definition: space round a dwelling, Is.Fr.102, Aristid.Or.51.55

περιοικίς.definition: pecul. fem. of dwelling; as Subst. , country round a town, as of Sparta, Th.3.16; of Elis, Id.2.25

περιοικοδομέω.definition: build round, D.55.11; enclose by building round, D.55.3; ib.29; UPZ10.16 :—Pass., to be built up, walled in, Th.3.81; X.Cyr.1.4.11; space built round, enclosure, Hdt.7.60

περιοικοδόμημα.definition: wall built round, IG11.161 A56 : but in pl., surrounding buildings, SIG685.75

περιοκέλλω.definition: prop. of a ship, run aground: metaph., fall into the worst habits, D.S.12.12

περιολισθάνω.definition: slip about. Hp.Art.47; slip away all round, Id.VM22. cf. D.H.14.10; slips off the engine, Plu.Marc.15; glance off them, J.BJ3.7.10: metaph., Plu.2.1089d: later metaph., wander, stray from the point, Plot.2.2.1

περιολίσθησις.definition: slipping away, in pl., Plu.Cam.26, Id.2.930e; Antyll. ap. Orib.45.24.9

περιονυχίζω.definition: fut. pare a person's nails, LXXDe.21.12

περιοράω.definition: impf. Ion. Hdt.3.118; abs., take a look round, Thphr.Char.25.3

περιοργής.definition: very angry or wrathful, Th.4.130, J.AJ18.8.1, D.C.39.19. Adv. A.Ag.216

περιοργυιόομαι.definition: Med. with pf. Pass., clasp in the arms, Ctes.Fr.57.6

περιορίζω.definition: mark by boundaries : set a limit; draw up the description of the boundaries of a property, OGI225.30 :—Pass., SIG1231.9

περιόρισμα.definition: anything surrounded by boundaries, enclosed place, Sch.Pi.O.13.62, Phot. s.v

περιορισμός.definition: marking out by boundaries, D.H.8.75; boundary, HeroGeom.4.12

περιορμέω.definition: anchor round, blockade, Th.4.23, 26, Poll.1.122, D.C.59.17

περιορμίζω.definition: bring round [a ship] to anchor, D.51.4, 7, PCair.Zen. 343.3 , Plu.Ant.35:—Med., come to anchor, Th.3.6

περιορύσσω.definition: Att. dig round, dig; dig up around, Plu.Rom.20

περιορχέομαι.definition: dance around, Thphr.HP9.8.8, Luc.Salt.8: c.acc., Call.Dian.240

περιουσία.definition: ) that which is over; residuum, Hp.Cord.11

περιουσιάζω.definition: have more than enough, of persons; expend one's means, Phalar.Ep.69.2

περιούσιος.definition: having more than enough, wealthy; especial, peculiar, LXXEx.19.5,al., Ep.Tit.2.14

περιοχέομαι.definition: Pass., to be traversed in all directions, . . Arist.Mu.397a25

περιοχή.definition: a containing, enclosing; compass, circumference, Placit.3 Prooem., cf. J.BJ5.4.3, Cleom.1.11, 2.3, Diog.Oen.24; opp. BGU492.10 ; of the body, Arist.Col.797b22, cf. Pr.870a10, D.S.1.91; according to their extent, Id.17…

περίοχος.definition: Aeol. superior, Sapph.92: Boeot. pre-eminent, restd. in Corinn.2.68

περιπαθέω.definition: to be in a state of violent emotion or indignation, Conon38.3, Plu.2.168d, etc.; . . Ph.2.176, etc

περιπαθής.definition: deeply moved, Plb.1.81.1; passionate, Longin.8.3; Luc.Hist.Conscr.26: Comp., Ael.Fr.123: Sup., Sch.Par.A.R.2.257. Adv. LXX4 Ma.8.2, Luc.Tim.46; Ael.NA9.8: Comp. Plu.2.456a

περιπάθησις.definition: intensity of emotion, Ph.2.26: pl., expressions of emotion in Rhetoric, Id.1.158

περιπαλάσσομαι.definition: to be hurled about, of atoms, cj. for in Democr.168 and for in Thphr.Sens.66: Hsch

περιπάλλομαι.definition: Pass., tremble all round, Q.S.10.371,14.44; Hymn.Is.156

περιπαμφανάω.definition: only Ep. 3pl. beam all around, D.P.530

περιπαπταίνω.definition: look timidly round, Mosch.4.108 : c. acc., Arat.297

περιπάσσω.definition: Att. strew, sprinkle all round, Sotad. Com.1.28; Alex.84.4; Thphr.HP9.1.7, cf. Arist.Mir.845a32:-Pass., to be sprinkled, Id.HA534b22; with a thing, Gal.6.533

περιπατέω.definition: walk up and down, as in a cloister, opp; walk about while teaching, discourse, Pl.Ep.348c, D.L.7.109; dispute, argue with them, Philostr.VA1.17, cf. 7.22

περιπάτησις.definition: walking about, A.D.Synt.19.10, Sor.1.112 tit., S.E.M.1.74, D.L.7.98

περίπατος.definition: walking about, walk; place for walking, esp. covered walk, X.Mem.1.1.10, Plu.Luc.39, IG22.2639; . . Plu.Alex.7; cf. infr. 2,3

περιπαχνόομαι.definition: Pass., to be congealed all round, Orph.L.526

περιπέζιος.definition: lowly, 'earthy', Herm.in Phdr.p.102 A., p.128 A., Procl.in Cra.p.69 P., etc.; Simp.in Epict.p.126 D. Adv. in common language, Eust.899.56

περιπέσσω.definition: Att. bake a crust round: only metaph., disguise, Ar.Pl.159; deck themselves out. with false hair, Id.Fr.321; Bato7.6; cover Marius without hurting him, Plu.Mar.37 :—Pass., Com.Adesp.338; dressed up, Pl.Lg.886e; X.Oec.…

περιπετάννυμι.definition: also X.Oec.19.18: pf. Pass. spread or stretch around, E.Hel.628 ; spread bathing-drawers over . . , Theopomp.Com.37 ; Dsc.5.75; spread them out, Aeschin.3.76; . . X.l.c.:—Pass., covered with . . , D.S.31.8; is spread …

περιπέτεια.definition: turning right about; esp. sudden reversal of circumstances on which the plot in a Tragedy hinges, such as Oedipus' discovery of his parentage, Arist.Po.1452a22, cf. 1450a34

περιπετής.definition: surrounded by, wrapped in, A.Ag.233; the sword round which he has fallen, S.Aj.907

περιπέτομαι.definition: fly around, Ar.Av.165: c. acc., ib.1721; Ant.Lib.16.3; Luc.Halc.1; Id.Hist.Conscr.1: the form occurs in codd. of Arist.HA609a14; cf

περιπετρίζομαι.definition: Pass., to be dashed upon a rock, Hsch

περιπήγνυμι.definition: make to congeal round, Plu.2.433b:—Pass. with pf. intr. are frozen on the feet, X.An.4.5.14; Str.12.5.4; Dsc.5.1; of a coated tongue, Gal.17.277: metaph., Dam.Pr.70

περιπηλόω.definition: encase in clay, Gal.12.727, Pholm.8.34, Olymp.Alch.p.76B

περιπηχύνω.definition: aor. part. take into one's arms, Call.Fr.344

περιπιλέω.definition: cover thick all round, LXX3 Ki.6.20

περιπίμπλαμαι.definition: Pass., to be filled full of. Pl.Tht.156e: abs., X.HG3.2.28

περιπίμπρημι.definition: set on fire round about: impf. X.Cyn.10.17 codd.; Th.3.98:—Pass., aor. D.C.51.24

περιπίπτω.definition: fut. Ar.V.523, etc.: Ep. pf. part; fall around, i.e. upon, a weapon, Ar.V.523; Antipho3.3.6

περιπλανάομαι.definition: wander about, Hdt.4.151; abs., wander, Luc.Herm.59, D.C.47.21, etc.: metaph., to be in this state of uncertainty, X.Cyr.1.3.5; . . Phld.Ind.Sto.13; erratic, irregular, D.H.Dem.50

περιπλάσσω.definition: Att. plaster one thing over; plaster over with a thing, Arist.Pr.924b37; Eub.98.1

περιπλαστεύω.definition: surround with a bank of clay, in Pass., Sammelb. 4481.8

περίπλεκτος.definition: intertwining, crossing, of the feet of dancers, Theoc.18.8

περιπληθής.definition: very full of people, Od.15.405; very full or large, Id.Mar.34, cf. Luc.Anach.25: Comp. Id.VH2.40

περιπλήθω.definition: to be quite full, c. gen., Tryph.595, Q.S.11.160: also c. dat., Theoc.25.13; Opp.H.5.591:—Med., abs., ib.678

περιπλίσσομαι.definition: put the legs round or across, . . Stratt.63, cf. Eust.1564.49, Hsch

περιπλοκή.definition: twining round, interlacing; in the philos. of Epicurus, interlacing of atoms, Ep.1p.8 U., 2p.44 U. , al.; Arist.Fr.208

περίπλοκος.definition: entwined, AP9.362; Tryph.300; coiled, of a snake, Nonn.D.22.34: c. dat., twined about, ib.6.195

περιπλύνω.definition: wash clean, scour, D.54.9, Plu.2.69c; Diocl.Fr.141, etc.:—Pass., have a thing washed off one, Arist.HA591a28; also of the thing, Thphr.CP4.14.4

περίπλυσις.definition: thin discharge from the bowels, Hp.Coac.600; Id.Prorrh.1.2, Aret.SA1.5

περιπνέω.definition: breathe round, c. acc., Pi.O.2.72, cf. Luc.VH2.5: abs., D.S.3.19:-Pass., Arist.Mu.397a34; MyiaEp.4. II. exhale a scent of, Eun.VSp.483 B

περιπνιγής.definition: suffocated, choked, Nic.Th.432, J.AJ7.13.3; Agatharch.76; D.S.38.4:—also Sch.Nic.Th.432

περιπνοή.definition: blowing round about, D.S.3.19; ventilation, Gal.7.393

περιποιέω.definition: cause to remain over and above, keep safe; of money, food, etc., save up, lay by, X.Oec.11.10; ib.2.10; part of the revenues, Is.6.38, cf. POxy.2148.17

περιποίησις.definition: keeping safe, preservation; concrete, those who are saved, Ep.Eph.1.14

περιποικίλλομαι.definition: Pass., to be variegated, Apollon.Lex. s.v

περιπολαῖος.definition: open all round, flat, of eyes, Arist.Phgn.810a1

περιπολεύω.definition: later form for sq., Phylarch.25 J. ; Sch.Nic.Al.339

περιπολέω.definition: go round or about, wander about, S.OT1254; c. acc. loci, traverse, Pl.Phdr.246b; Id.Tht.176a; prowl about it, E.Rh.773; Philostr.Ep.5, etc

περιπόλησις.definition: revolution, of the stars, Ph.1.10 ; Theo Sm.p.120 H., cf. Iamb.VP15.65; of the sun, Porph. ap. Eus.PE3.12; of metempsychosis, Max.Tyr.38.3, D.L.8.4

περιπολίζω.definition: wander about, Str.14.5.15; move in society, PMed. in Arch.Pap.4.270

περιπόλιον.definition: station for guard-house; suburb or township, LXX1 Ch.6.71 , IG12.1033 , etc.; the quarter round her temple, CIG2715.16

περιπόλιος.definition: lying round a place, c. gen., Str.7.7.6, cf. 14.2.22, 17.3.21

περιπορεύομαι.definition: travel, go about, Pl.Lg.716a, Ceb.7; c. acc. loci, go round, Arist.Oec.1353b20; etc., Plb.3.7.3,9.6.3, etc.; Id.4.54.4; D.S.40.1, cf. Corn.ND17

περιπορπάομαι.definition: fasten with a clasp round oneself, App.Hisp.42

περιπόρπημα.definition: that which is so fastened, Cyr

περιπόρφυρος.definition: edged with purple, Crates; garments with a purple border, of the Roman toga praetexta or laticlavia, Id.6.53.7; D.H.2.70, Plu.Rom.26; and alone, ib.25, 2.283a; , pueri praetextati, Id.Publ.18

περιποτάομαι.definition: poet. for hover about, S.OT482 : c. acc., Hld.2.22

περιπταίω.definition: stumble upon, c. dat., Polyaen.1.3.2; fall; fall in with, f.l. for in Arist.Fr.487

περιπτίσσω.definition: strip off the husk or skin, Thphr.HP9.16.9, Dieuch. ap. Orib.4.7.21:—Pass., Thphr.HP4.4.10, Sor.1.122: metaph., free from the chaff, clean-winnowed, Ar.Ach.507; clean-built, taper of form, Philostr.Her.3.4

περίπτυξις.definition: folding oneself round, embracing, Plu.Cat.Mi.11 ; Plot.4.7.8

περιπτύσσω.definition: enfold, enshroud, S.Ant.886; as military term, outflank, X.An.1.10.9:—Pass., Id.Cyr.7.1.26

περιπτυχή.definition: that which enfolds, used in pl. in; enfolding, embracing, E.Supp.815 ; in all that the sun embraces, i.e.all the world, Id.Ion1516

περιπτυχής.definition: folded round, S.Aj.915; fallen around his sword, ib.899

περίπτωσις.definition: Ion. encountering, falling; experience, . . Hp.Praec.1; Plu.2.918c tit.; ib.440a; Stoic.2.29, al., cf. Phld.Rh.2.164S., Diog.Oen.10

περιπυκάζω.definition: encompass thickly, with foliage, Ach.Tat.1.15:— Med., have thick round, Ctes.Fr.57.11

περιπωμάζω.definition: cover with a lid all over, Hp.Loc.Hom.47; Pass., to be shut up in, Id.HA592a22

περιρραίνω.definition: besprinkle, Thphr.Lap.13; esp. in sacred; generally, moisten, . . ib.14.48

περιρραντήριον.definition: utensil for besprinkling, esp; the parts of the market-place sprinkled with lustral water, Lex ap.Aeschin.1.21, cf. 3.176, Luc.Sacr.12, 13

περιρραντής.definition: sprinkler, temple-official at Sardes, BMus.Inscr.1031 .117, i B. C.)

περιρραντίζω.definition: = LXXNu.19.13, al.; v.l. for in Alex.Trall.1.15

περιρραπίζω.definition: lash round about, of fish, Plu.2.977b

περιρράπτρια.definition: she who sews or stitches: title of priestess at Piraeus, IG22.2361.12

περιρρέμβομαι.definition: wander, roam about, Zos. Alch.p.244 B., cf. Gloss.; · Hsch

περιρρεπής.definition: falling over on one side, opp. Hp.Art.50; cause the organs to press on the bladder, Ruf.Ren.Ves.11

περιρρέπω.definition: incline to one side, Hp.Fract.4, Gal.18.828

περιρρήγνυμι.definition: and , break off; cause a stream to break or divide round a piece of land, Isoc.11.31:—Pass., Hdt.2.16, cf. Ael.NA7.24; kept breaking round a place, Plu.Crass.19

περιρρηδής.definition: falling away, or sloping on each side, Hp.Art.16; of the body in bed, Id.Mul.2.158, Gal.18.420

περίρρηξις.definition: breaking away all round, as of; open wound, Hippiatr.100,104

περιρρήσσω.definition: collat. form of Gal.11.138, f.l. in Q.S.8.332:—also D.S.17.35, Ph.2.230, Dsc.2.107

περιρρητινόομαι.definition: to be treated with resin, dub. in Gal.12.659

περιρρίπτω.definition: cast around or over, . . prob. in Q.S.8.332:—Pass., aor. 2 inf. Sch.A.R.2.1210; to be thrown about, Agath.2.1, 23

περίρροια.definition: = foreg., Plu.2.1128c; fluid discharge in dysentery, Hp.Epid.1.5 ; cf. II.2

περιρρομβέω.definition: cause to spin round like a top, Plu.Ant.67, Tz. ad Lyc.310

περιρρύπτω.definition: scour all round, Gal.11.129, Orib.Eup.2.1 s.v

περίρρυτος.definition: Act., flowing round, c. gen., over the barren plains that flow round Sicily, i.e. the sea, E.Ph.209

περισαλπίζω.definition: sound trumpets around:—Pass., or has never had the trumpets sounding round him, Eudamid. ap. Plu.2.192b

περισαρκίζω.definition: make an incision all round, Heliod. ap. Orib.46.22.12, Philum.Ven.3.5, Paul.Aeg.5.3

περίσαρκος.definition: surrounded with flesh, fleshy, Arist.Phgn.809b7 , Adam.2.2 : Com. metaph., Clearch.Com.2

περισαρκόω.definition: surround or cover with flesh, Gal.10.324, 336

περισάττω.definition: heap up all around, Arist.Pr.924b4, cf. a28 ; Thphr.CP5.6.5; block up, Plb.21.28.14:—Pass., cj. in Antyll. ap. Orib.6.10.12

περισβέννυμι.definition: quench all round, Plu.2.997a: metaph., J.BJ3.7.18

περισήπομαι.definition: Pass., decay all round, Thphr.HP3.9.3; Hp.Morb.2.36

περισιαλόομαι.definition: Pass., to be broidered round the edge, LXXEx.36.13

περισιδηρόομαι.definition: Pass., to be cased with iron, Bito49.5, Stud.Pal. 20.67r.6

περισκάλλω.definition: hack round about, Gal.6.619: aor. 1 imper. Gp.5.42.1

περισκάπτω.definition: dig round, Thphr.HP4.14.7, CP5.9.3; turn up all round, D.H.2.31

περισκελασία.definition: harshness in action, of hellebore, Orib.Fr.80 II.2)

περισκέλεια.definition: hardness, harshness; difficulty, Arist.Fr.29. ap. Orib.8.6.6,al., Paul.Aeg.6.112.)

περισκελής.definition: metaph., obstinate, stubborn, Id.Aj.649; M.Ant.4.28; AP9.578 : Comp. Simp.in Epict.p.62 D. Adv. Comp. to bear more unflinchingly, Men.6.3

περισκελίς.definition: leg-band, i. e. anklet, bangle; ornament round the stem of a cup, IG22.1407.38, 1408.17

περισκέλλω.definition: pf. part. dried up : wiry, lean, Philostr.Gym.35

περισκεπάζω.definition: cover, screen all round, AP5.103 , cf. Gp.2.4.2:—Pass., Thphr.HP4.5.3, Dsc.2.76

περισκεπής.definition: covered all round; covering or screening all round, Call.Del.23; Thphr.HP7.1.4

περίσκεπτος.definition: to be seen on all sides, far-seen; worth seeing, Call.Epigr.6.8; admired, AP12.91

περίσκεψις.definition: Delph. , consideration, Eudor. ap. Stob.2.7.2; Str.4.4.2, Chrysipp.Stoic.3.115

περισκήπτω.definition: prop or press all round, Hsch

περισκιάζομαι.definition: Pass., to be overshadowed, Plu.2.1129d; of the moon, to be obscured, Id.Nic.21

περίσκιος.definition: throwing a shadow all round, of the inhabitants of the polar circles, Posidon.76 J., Cleom.1.7

περισκιρτάω.definition: leap round or about, c. acc., Ael.NA14.28, cf. AP12.181 , Luc.Bacch.2, etc

περίσκληρος.definition: very hard, Hp.Aff.59, Epid.6.1.10: metaph., very rough, strong, Antiph.202.17; of persons, very tough, Heliod. ap.Orib.44.14.4

περισκληρύνω.definition: make hard all round, Hp.Aph.5.20, Liqu.6

περισκοπέω.definition: fut. pf. in act; examine, observe carefully, Th.1.36; Plu.Pomp.80; Arat.199; Luc.VH1.32

περισκόπησις.definition: = J.AJ17.9.1: pl. in concrete sense, Sch.Opp.H.1.364

περισκορπίζω.definition: scatter on all sides, Olymp.in Mete.108.19,26

περισκουτλόω.definition: cover or surround with marble slabs, Jahresh.3.206

περισκυθίζω.definition: scalp in Scythian fashion, LXX2 Ma.7.4; as a surgical operation, Gal.18.790 : —hence Id.14.784; PMed. in Arch.Pap.4.270 ; cf

περισκυφίζω.definition: make an incision round the scalp:—hence Aët.7.56 ,93, Paul.Aeg.6.7

περισμαραγέω.definition: rattle all round, Anon. ap. Luc.Hist.Conscr.22, D.P.844

περισμάω.definition: wipe all round, Hdn.Gr.1.468, f.l. in Dsc.3.45

περισμήχω.definition: wipe over, Sor.[2.88], f.l. in Dsc.3.45

περισμύχω.definition: consume by a slow fire, Orph.L.602; of love, AP5.291.11

περισπαίρω.definition: quiver round, Q.S.1.624; struggle convulsively, Lyc.68, Nic.Th.773, etc

περίσπασις.definition: = sq. II, PGen.56.15; = sq. III, Ephor.108 J., Eust.630.28

περισπασμός.definition: wheeling round, Plb.10.23.3,12.18.3; distracting circumstances, distraction, Metrod. Herc.831.7, Plb.3.87.9 , Phld.Mus.p.98K., Plu.2.831f ; Plb.4.32.5, etc.; D.S.12.38; Chrysipp.Stoic.3.77: rarely in sg., LXXEc.2.23, …

περισπάω.definition: strip bare, E.IT296; wheel about, of a general, Plb.1.76.5; intr. of the troops, Id.3.116.5; esp. wheel twice through a right angle, Ascl.Tact.12.6,al. ; of a horse's bit, not pulling it violently round, Luc.Merc.Cond.21

περισπειράω.definition: wind round, Plu.Cam.25:— Med., . . having concentrated his troops around . . , Id.Ages.31:—Pass., form round, Id.Cic.22; of serpents, etc., twine, coil round, D.S.4.48: c. dat., Luc.Hist. Conscr.29; Id.Dips.6: metaph.…

περισπείρω.definition: spread all round, Apollod.Poliorc.145.13 , Ach. Tat.Intr.Arat.1:—Pass., Gal.7.314

περισπερχής.definition: very hasty, a rash; goaded by pains, Opp.C.4.218, H.5.145

περισπέρχω.definition: intr., to be in great agitation, ib.2.334; Pass., to be agitated, angered, Hdt.7.207

περισπεύδω.definition: pursue on all sides, dub. in; go in search of a thing, Arat.1122

περισπογγίζω.definition: sponge all round, Hp.Morb.2.13, Thphr.Char.25.5, Gal.13.357

περισπούδαστος.definition: much sought after, much desired; diligent, eager, PMasp.20ii 11 . Adv. with due care, Phylarch.30 J., Ath.4.164b

περίσπουδος.definition: very eager, Poll.6.29, etc.; for . . , Simp.in Epict.p.51 D

περισσάρτιος.definition: odd and even: Arith. of numbers which become uneven when divided by some power of two, such as 24 , Nicom.Ar.1.10, Poll.4.162

περίσσευμα.definition: Att. superfluity; = excrement, Sor.1.108, f.l. in Plu.2.962f

περισσεύω.definition: to be more than enough, remain over, Id.Smp.4.35; Id.Vect.4.7; . . Pl.Lg.855b; SIG672.19 ; Arist.HA619a20; Ev.Matt.14.20; such abundance of reason had Pericles for his belief, Th.2.65; J.AJ19.1.18; D.H.3.11

περισσογονία.definition: production of odd numbers, Iamb.in Nic.pp.21,34 P

περισσοδάκτυλος.definition: with more than the usual number of fingers or toes, Gp.14.7.9

περισσοειδής.definition: partaking of the nature of odd numbers, of the Theo Sm.p.24 H., Theol.Ar.19, Iamb.in Nic.p.31 P

περισσολογέω.definition: Att. speak superfluously, Simp.in Ph.770.14; gloss on Hsch., Suid

περισσολογία.definition: over-talking, wordiness, Isoc.12.88; elaborate writing, D.H.Pomp.2

περισσομελής.definition: with superfluous limbs, Heph.Astr.1.1, Man.4.464, Vett.Val.18.33, al

περισσόμυθος.definition: = superfluous, E.Fr.52. Adv. in form , Phld.Rh.1.101 S

περισσόπους.definition: gen. with a foot too many, Nonn.D.7.43

περισσοσυλλαβέω.definition: to have one syllable more than, or EM35.41, 131.57: abs., A.D.Pron.28.11, etc

περισσοσύλλαβος.definition: with a syllable more, Id.Adv.166.26, St.Byz. s.v. Adv. Id. s.v. Sch.E.Or.18, etc

περισσοταγής.definition: put in a series of uneven numbers, opp. Nicom.Ar.1.22

περισσότης.definition: in style, redundancy, Hermog.Meth.5; ex abundanti, Aps.Rh.p.223 H

περισσόφρων.definition: in good sense, extremely clever, Vett.Val.17.22

περισσωνυμέω.definition: of numbers, to be odd, Iamb.in Nic.p.22 P.:—Adj. odd, ib.p.84P

περίσσωσις.definition: Att. superfluity; = Arist.HA489a7, GA717b6, al., Thphr.Sud.20

περιστάσιμος.definition: filled with people standing round, crowded with hearers, Lyr. ap. Timae.80 10)

περίστασις.definition: surrounding, Arist.Pr.869a21: in concrete sense, environment, Epicur.Ep.2p.50 U., cf. p.48 U.; surrounding space, Plb.6.31.1, 6.41.2; esp. free space round a building, OGI483.123, al. , IG14.352i8, 70

περίστατος.definition: surrounded and admired by the crowd; Act., standing round and wondering, agape, Theopomp. Com.41

περισταυρόω.definition: fence about with, palisade, Th.2.75:— Pass., X.An.7.4.14:—Med., having entrenched themselves, Id.HG3.2.2

περιστεγνόω.definition: solder a pipe all round, HeroSpir.2.23

περιστέγω.definition: retain heat, etc. by covering, Hp.Acut.21, Thphr.Ign.19; contain a fluid, Gal.15.709:—Pass., Arist.Pr.900a1, Thphr.CP1.19.2

περιστενάζω.definition: lament round:—Pass., filled with lamentation, Plu.Ant.56

περιστενοχωρέομαι.definition: Pass., to be confined within a narrow compass, Apollon.Lex.s.v

περιστερά.definition: common pigeon or dove, Hdt.1.138, S.Fr.866, Democr.164, etc.; specifically, Columba livia domestica, and so distd. from Arist.HA562b5, 593a16; ib.544b3: cock-pigeon, Pherecr.33 , Alex.214; censured by Luc.Sol.7

περιστερεών.definition: dovecote, Pl.Tht.197c, 197d; = II, Ps.-Dsc.4.59, prob. in Plu.2.614b; holy vervain, Verbena supina, Ps.-Dsc.4.60

περιστεριδεύς.definition: young pigeon, PCair.Zen. 354.5 , etc. 4 ), Sch.Ar.Ach.866, Eust.753.56

περιστερίδιον.definition: Dim. of PGoodsp.Cair.30 v 20, al. , PLips.97 xxvi 9 , f.l. in LXXLe.1.14, interpol. in Ath.14.654a

περιστέριον.definition: = foreg., Pherecr.135, Phryn.Com.51; vervain, Verbena officinalis, Dsc.4.59

περιστερίς.definition: = foreg.I, BGU594.9; a woman's ornament, Com.Adesp.1115

περιστεροτροφεῖον.definition: place where doves are reared, Varro RR 3.7

περιστεφανίς.definition: coronary vein of the hoof, Hippiatr.117

περιστεφανόω.definition: put round in a circle, D.H.3.30; Id.8.66:—Pass., Arist.Mu.393b17, cf. Ph.2.324

περιστεφής.definition: wreathed, crowned, with a; Act., twining, encircling, E.Ph.651

περιστηλόομαι.definition: to be set up as round about, Jahrb.Ergänzungsheft10.64

περιστίζω.definition: prick or dot all round; Gramm., mark with dots, Gal.16.800; EM169.37, cf. 462.39 : pf. part. Pass. marked with dots, Sch.Il.p.xliii Dind., etc. ; etc., D.L.3.66

περιστίλβω.definition: glitter all round, D.S.3.45, Plu.2.693d; Eun.VSp.459B

περιστιχάω.definition: stand round in rows, Nic.Th.442, Nonn.D.26.223

περιστλεγγίζω.definition: scrape all round with a Hsch

περιστοιχέω.definition: = sq., comprehend within limits, Men.Rh.p.348S. ; f.l. for sq. in D.C.60.30

περιστοιχίζω.definition: surround as with toils or nets, of a besieging army, interpol. in Plb.8.5.2, etc. ; dub. in Sm.Ps.47.13, Quint.Ho.8.13: metaph., J.AJ17.2.4:—Med. , D.4.9, cf. D.C.39.3:—Pass., Id.49.30, al., Aristaenet.1.9; Ph.Fr.104 …

περιστολή.definition: laying out, of a corpse, D.H.3.21, BGU896.7; Medic., peristaltic action of internal organs, Gal.8.440; Id.7.219; Id.Nat.Fac.2.1

περιστολίζομαι.definition: Med., wrap oneself up, Suid. s.v. Dsc.Eup.2.115

περιστόμιος.definition: round a mouth or aperture; Subst. mouth of a vessel, Plb.21.28.12

περιστομίς.definition: wooden gauge or spanner for; iron clamp, Apollod.Poliorc.155.11

περίστομος.definition: presenting a front all round, Ascl.Tact.11.6

περιστοναχέω.definition: groan all around, cj. in Hes.Sc.344; cf

περιστορέννυμι.definition: aor. inf. Med. Pass. spread all round or over, Orph.A.1335 , Nonn.D.18.81, etc. ; cf

περιστρατοπεδεύω.definition: encamp about, invest, besiege, Lycurg.128, Plb.1.30.5, 2.2.7, D.H.6.29, Plu.Fab.22:—used by X. in Med., abs., HG3.1.7, Cyr.3.1.6, al.:—Pass., HG4.7.1

περιστροβέω.definition: cause to revolve, Herm. ap. Stob.1.49.44

περιστροφή.definition: turning or spinning round, Pl.R.521c; courses of the stars, S.Fr.432.8; Euc.Phaen.p.8 M.; Hld.1.18, etc.; amidst them, LXXSi.50.5: pl., contortions, Gal.15.126; whorls in hairgrowth, Heph.Astr.1.1

περιστροφίδιον.definition: name of a garment, dub. in BCH29.432

περίστροφος.definition: turning round : turning in a socket; Subst., twisted rope, f.l. for in X.Cyn.2.6

περιστρώννυμι.definition: aor. = Duris49 J., cf. Aq., Thd.Pr.7.16

περιστρωφάω.definition: ply hither and thither; intr., turn hither and thither, prob. in Q.S.6.504

περίστυλος.definition: surrounded with a colonnade; Subst. peristyle, colonnade round a temple or round the court of a house, LXXEz.42.3 , D.S.18.26, IG5.268.50 , J.BJ1.21.11 ; also, area surrounded by a colonnade, LXX3 Ma.5.23,al.:—so D.S.…

περιστυφελίζομαι.definition: Med., beat, dash all round, Opp.H.3.23

περισυλάω.definition: strip off all round, Ph.1.637; strip, plunder, Ael.VH1.20; strip of one's property, Id.Fr.48; ib.167:—Pass., Pl.Grg.486c, cf. Luc.Philops.20, JConf.8

περισυμπλέκω.definition: in Pass., to be wound round, of a screw, dub. in Bito47.4

περισυνάγω.definition: gloss on Sch.E.Hec.1139:—Pass., gloss on Sch.Opp.H.3.231; collected from all round, gloss on Sch.Them.Or.16.201a

περισυρίττω.definition: hiss on all sides, Eust.1816.46:—Pass., ibid., Id.1504.31

περισφάλλω.definition: cause to slip about, Apollon.Cit.1:—Pass., slip about, Hp.Art.6

περίσφαλσις.definition: Ion. causing to slip round, in reduction of a dislocation, Id.Mochl.15, cf. Art.25

περισφαραγέω.definition: to be ready to burst, Nic.Th.553

περισφηκόω.definition: tie tight all round, as one does a jar, Dsc.5.18:— Pass., to be tight bound, Hp.Ep.15, 16

περισφίγγω.definition: bind tightly all round; metaph., tighten up, make more stringent, Just.Nov.46Praef

περίσφιγξις.definition: tying tight all round, constriction, Herm. ap. Stob.1.49.69; Sor.2.40 , cf. Pall.in Hp.12.284C

περισχιδής.definition: slit all round, Dsc.4.119; Subst. a kind of shoe, Ephipp.Olynth. ap. Ath.12.537e; used by slaves, Phot., cf. Hsch

περισχίζω.definition: slit and tear off, Plu.Cic.36; Pass., of a river, to split round a piece of land, i.e. divide into two branches and surround it, Hdt.9.51; Plb.3.42.7, etc.: abs., of a stream of men, part and go different ways, Pl.Prt…

περισχοινίζω.definition: part off by a rope, Poll.8.20; ib.141; D.H.7.59:—Med., of the Areopagitic Council, part itself off by a rope, D.25.23:—Pass., Poll.8.123

περισχοίνισμα.definition: space marked off by a rope, Plu.2.847a, App.Pun.78, Alciphr.2.3; Poll.8.124

περισώζω.definition: save alive , save from death or ruin, X.HG2.3.25, etc.; ib.6.5.47:—Med., Alciphr.1.30:—Pass., escape with one's life, of a prisoner, X.HG2.3.32, cf. 4.8.21, Phld.Rh.1.28 S.; App.Sam.4.7; D.C.46.50; of things, survive,…

περισωρεύω.definition: heap up all round; Pass., to be heaped up with, Plu.Tim.29; to be buried under the shields, of Tarpeia, D.H.2.40

περιταφρεύω.definition: surround with a trench, Plb.1.48.10. Plu.2.191c; App.Pun.72; Phleg.36.18 J.:—Pass., X.Cyr.3.3.28; Plu.Mar.33

περιτείνω.definition: stretch all round or over, Hdt.1.194; Id.4.65; . . ib.73; Arist.Mete.355b28:— Pass., tight-stretched, Hp.Prog.2, cf. Arist.HA548b32, al.; being spread round . . , Pl.Ti.66b, cf. Arist.Mete.354b24; covered with a skin,…

περιτειχίζω.definition: build round, in Med., Themist.Ep.8:—Pass., X.HG5.3.22; metaph., fortify, Vett.Val.334.10

περιτείχισις.definition: walling round so as to blockade, circumvallation, Th.2.77, 4.131; but also for defence, Themist.Ep.4.3

περιτείχισμα.definition: wall of circumvallation; surrounding wall of a precinct, SIG818.5

περιτελέω.definition: complete in a circle, Od.10.470, cf. 19.153

περιτένεια.definition: tension of the skin, Antyll. ap; Archit., prepared surface, finished section, IG22.1670.17 , 7.3073.69

περιτενής.definition: stretched all round, distended, Hp.Art.46, Paul.Aeg.5.8; glossed by Erot., Greg.Cor.p.556 S

περιτεχνάομαι.definition: contrive with great cunning, Anon. ap. Suid

περιτέχνησις.definition: extraordinary art or cunning, Th.3.82; D.C.46.19

περίτηξις.definition: Ion. discharge of humour, as in dropsy, Hp.Coac.471

περιτίτραμαι.definition: Pass., to be trephined by a circle of perforations, Heliod. ap.Orib.46.11.34, Leonid. ap. Aët.15.12

περιτίω.definition: honour very highly, Il.8.161:—Pass., A.R.3.74. Il., A.R.]

περιτομή.definition: circumcision, LXXGe.17.13, Agatharch.61; section of a machine, Apollod.Poliorc.173.4

περίτομος.definition: cut off all round, abrupt, steep, Plb.1.56.4; D.H.5.19; steep places, Inscr.Prien.363.28

περιτόναιος.definition: stretched or strained over, esp. of; = Poll.1.92, cf. II ; but

περίτονος.definition: covered with something stretched over; Subst. = II.1, Eust.1533.41

περιτοξεύω.definition: overshoot, outshoot, Ar.Ach.712 (nisi; shoot to death with arrows, App.Num.3 ):— Pass., Aristid.1.125 J

περιτορνεύω.definition: turn as in a lathe, . . . . he framed a globe round it, Pl.Ti.73e; ib.69c: metaph. in Pass., to be well-turned, of style, D.H.Dem.21

περιτραχήλιος.definition: round the neck, Hsch. s.v; Subst. neckpiece, gorget, IG22.1492.54, Str.3.4.17 , Plu.Alex.32,Arr.Epict.3.14.12,POxy. 1273.7

περιτρέπω.definition: turn and bring round, divert; turn upside down, upset, Luc.Cont.7; capsized, Plu.2.831d; Id.Marc.7: metaph., Trag.Adesp.547.4; LXXWi.5.23; pervert, Ath.Med. ap. Orib.inc.21.1; . . Pl.Phd.95b; refute, Id.Ax.37oa, cf. A…

περιτρέφω.definition: pf. A.R.2.738:—cause, make to congeal around, l.c.: metaph., Nic.Th.299:—Pass., [the milk] forms curds as you mix it, Il.5.903; the ice froze hard upon the shields, Od.14.477; M.Ant.12.1, cf. Gal.2.504

περίτρησις.definition: trephining by a circle of perforations, Heliod. ap. Orib.46.11.35

περίτρητος.definition: perforated: Subst. perforated horizontal beam in a torsion-engine, Ph.Bel.55.5,al.: pl., HeroBel.93.9

περιτριβής.definition: worn all round by use, AP6.63 : metaph., worn with work, A.R.1.1175

περιτρίζω.definition: pf. creak all round, Q.S.12.431, prob. in 14.265

περίτριμμα.definition: anything worn smooth by rubbing; Medic., preparation for rubbing in, Crito ap.Gal.12.447

περιτροπή.definition: turning round, revolution; turning about, changing, by turns, one after another, Hdt.2.168,3.69; D.H.5.2, Aristid.Or.43.24, BGU149.9 , D.C.53.1; Id.54.19

περίτροπος.definition: turned round, whirled round, rotatory motion, prob.l. in Plu.Lys.12: Subst. Hsch

περιτρόχαλος.definition: = neut. pl. as Adv., to have one's hair clipped round about, Hdt.3.8, Plu.2.261f; Phot. s.v

περιτροχασμός.definition: f.l. for in Antyll. ap. Orib.6.22.10

περιτρόχιον.definition: wheel revolving round an axle, the wheel and axle, Papp.1060.9, cf. Tz.H.11.607

περιτρυπάω.definition: perforate with a circle of holes, Aët.9.38, Paul.Aeg.6.3

περιτρύπησις.definition: perforation with a circle of holes, ib.90

περιτρώγω.definition: fut. Luc.Gall.28: aor. Ar.Ach.258:—gnaw round about, bite off, v.l. in Arist.HA605a4, cf. Luc.Tim.8, etc.; Pherecr.13; nibble off, purloin her jewels, Ar.Ach.258; Id.V.672: metaph., carp at, ib.596

περιτυγχάνω.definition: mostly of persons, happen to be about, at, or near: hence, light upon, fall in with, c. dat. pers., Th.1.20, Lys.13.23, etc.; X.Mem.2.8.5: abs., Th.1.135, Pl.Smp.221a: c. dat. rei, And.1.37; Th.4.120; Pl.Phdr.268c; Id…

περίτυλος.definition: callous, Sor.2.16; surrounded with bead-moulding, Inscr.Délos504.14

περιτυλόω.definition: make callous, Crito ap.Gal.13.798:—Pass., become callous all round, Cass.Pr.13

περιτυμπανίζομαι.definition: Pass., to be maddened by drums, Plu.2.144d, 167c

περιτυπόω.definition: embrace, enfold, as the atmosphere does our bodies, S.E.P.3.75, M.10.95: Peripatetic term, Id.P.3.131

περιυβρίζω.definition: insult wantonly, Hdt.5.91, J.AJ7.6.1, Jul.Or.5.159a, etc.; Ar.V.1319, cf. Th.535; Plu.Cam.18:—Pass., to be so treated, or Hdt.2.152, 4.159; or Id.1.114, 3.137; Ar.Eq.727; Ph.1.488

περιύομαι.definition: Pass., to be rained round, Str.14.2.20

περιφανής.definition: seen all round, of a city, Th.4.102

περιφαντάζομαι.definition: frame an imaginative notion of a thing, Simp.in Epict.p.112 D., in Cael.313.8

περιφεγγής.definition: radiant, Ph.1.631; shedding light around, Id.2.505; of Zeus, Orph.Fr.168.22; Man.6.57; Cat.Cod.Astr. 1.109

περιφέγγω.definition: illuminate round about, in Med., Sm.Ez.1.27

περιφείδομαι.definition: spare and save alive, Isyll.26; to be careful, . . Archig. ap. Orib.46.25.2

περιφέρεια.definition: Ion. circumference; arc of a circle, Arist.Ph.264b25, Euc.3.28; marked on concave sun-dial , Sammelb.358.1

περιφερής.definition: rounded or curved; of surfaces and lines, Hp.Art.7; Pherecr.143.5; Ael.Tact.2.7; Hp.VC11; opp. Pl.Prm.137e, 138a, Arist.Ph.248a12, al.; circularity, Id.APo.73a39; but, circumference, Pl.R.436e, Dsc.3.6, 48. Adv. in a …

περιφέρω.definition: move round, bring the foot round in mounting a horse, X.Eq.7.2; hand round at table, Id.Cyr.2.2.2, al. ; Plu.Agis18; Id.2.737d

περιφεύγω.definition: flee from, escape; abs., escape from illness, come out of it alive, D.54.1, 28; v.l. in Hp.Prog.23, cf. Arist.HA604a10

περιφημίζω.definition: announce, publish; celebrate all round, EM517.17

περίφημος.definition: very famous, Archil.63; in bad sense, notorious, Paul.Al.N.3

περιφθέγγομαι.definition: speak with all kinds of people, Gal.4.448

περιφθείρομαι.definition: Pass., to be utterly destroyed; wander about in destitution, Isoc.Ep.9.10, Lycurg.40

περιφίμωσις.definition: disorder of the penis in which the prepuce cannot be drawn forward, Antyll. ap.Orib.50.5.2, Paul.Aeg.6.55: is f.l. in Gal.19.445

περιφλέγω.definition: burn, blaze all round, Id.2.648c; trans., burn up, wither, Ph.2.391; D.Chr.36.47: with acc. understood, Poll.10.51; overheat, Plu.2.651b, Sor.1.72:—Pass., of victims in the bull of Phalaris, Plb.12.25.2; to be singed,…

περιφλεύω.definition: or scorch, singe, or char all round, of lightning, Ar.Nu.396:—Pass., Hdt.5.77; Dsc.2.25; cf

περιφλίω.definition: to be almost bursting with, Nic.Al.62

περιφλοίζω.definition: strip off the bark, Thphr.HP9.5.3; Id.Ign.72, cf. Dsc.1.20:— Med., Id.4.148

περιφοβέω.definition: terrify, scare, Phot. and Suid. s.v. fear greatly, X.Cyn.9.17

περιφοιτάω.definition: wander about, prov; c. acc., Hp.Vict.1.6; Philostr.VSPraef

περίφοιτος.definition: revolving, Parm.10.4; of persons, wandering about, Call.Epigr.30.3,39.2, Nonn.D.3.297, al.; Ph.1.484; but f.l. for Id.2.248

περιφορά.definition: carrying round, of dishes at table; going round, circular or rotatory motion, revolution, of a wheel, E.Ba.1067; of the heavens and heavenly bodies, Ar.Nu.172, X.Mem.4.7.5, Pl.Phdr.247c, Lg.898c, Arist.Mete.341a2, Cae…

περίφραγμα.definition: fence round a place, Agath.2.4; place fenced round, enclosure, IG11.287 A117 , PMich.Zen.84.12 , Str.15.1.55 , BCH11.395 precinct, IG12.481.28

περίφρακτος.definition: fenced round: Subst. enclosure, IG3.1866, Plu.Thes.12, Luc.Bacch.6

περίφραξις.definition: fencing round, Agath.2.20 , dub. in SIG1231.17

περιφράσσω.definition: Att. fence, fortify all round; make a dam, Arist.HA603a9

περιφρίσσω.definition: c. dat., tremble for, Nonn.D.6.8; bristle with, ib.11.502

περιφρονέω.definition: compass in thought, speculate about; contemn, despise, Th.1.25; D.H.1.71, etc.: c. gen., Pl.Ax.372b; Plu.Thes.1, cf. Ael.Tact. Praef.3, etc.: metaph., of diseases or difficult patients, defy remedies, Alex. Trall.1.15…

περιφρουρέω.definition: guard on all sides, blockade closely, OGI199.17 , D.C.40.36:—Pass., Th.3.21: metaph., Vett.Val.271.8; but, to be protected, Paul.Aeg.6.105

περιφρύγω.definition: Pass. Steph.in Hp.1.175 D.), scorch, parch, Thd.Ca.1.6, Olymp.in Mete.292.33:—Pass., aor. 2 inf. Alex.Trall.Febr.4

περιφυλάσσω.definition: Att. guard all round, Ph.Bel.83.29 , J.BJ5.10.1codd., Sch.E.Hec.1209

περιφύρω.definition: throw into confusion, in Pass., Ph.2.656

περιφυτεύω.definition: plant round about, Il.6.419; Pl.Lg.947e: metaph., LXX4 Ma.2.21

περιφύω.definition: Pass., with fut. Med. pf. and aor. 2 Act. aor. 2 inf. part. round about, Od.9.141; Arist.PA654b27, cf. GA754a2; Thphr.CP5.5.4; . . there is rock all round, Plu.Cam.25

περιφώνησις.definition: sounding round about, prob. in Id.2.587c

περιφωτίζω.definition: shine round about, illuminate, Cleom.2.1; Plot.6.9.4:—Pass., Plu.2.953a, Dam.Pr.83

περιφωτισμός.definition: shining round about, Hld.9.22; but v.l. for in Str.3.1.5

περίχαλκος.definition: covered with brass or copper, Theodor.Hierap. ap. Ath.10.413b

περιχαλκόω.definition: cover with brass or copper, LXXEx.27.6

περιχαρακόω.definition: surround with a stockade, Aeschin.3.236; fortify, Plb.4.56.8; Ph.Bel.96.39; blockade, besiege, App.Hisp.90:—Pass., to be besieged, Polyaen.2.2.5 : metaph., Din.1.64

περιχαρακτήρ.definition: instrument for detaching the gums before drawing teeth, Cael.Aur.TP2.4, Aët.8.36, Pall.in Hp.2.174 D

περιχάραξις.definition: demarcation by incision, Orib.44.11.1; incision made for purposes of grafting, Gp.10.77.2

περιχαράσσω.definition: Att. entrench all round, Str.15.1.42: in Medicine, demarcate, Dsc.1.72, 2.112; also, detach from gums all round, Gal.14.431:—Pass., serrated, cj. Scalig. in Thphr.HP3.12.5, cf. 3.14.1

περιχάρεια.definition: excessive joy, Pl.Phlb.65d, Ph.1.460; opp. Pl.Lg.732c: in pl., Plu.2.83d, Gal.10.841, Plot.1.4.12:—incorrectly written D.C.44.8, Alciphr.3.38, Adam.2.38, etc

περιχάσκω.definition: aor. 2 and pf. (as if; open a girdle, Heliod. ap. Orib.48.58.5

περίχειρον.definition: armlet, bracelet, Plb.2.29.8:—Dim. Hsch. s.v. also Poll.1.185

περιχλαινίζομαι.definition: Med., wrap oneself in a cloak, Hsch. , Phot.:—Act., and also Subst. Hdn.Epim.149

περιχονδριάω.definition: to be swollen, cj. in Com.Adesp.1116

περιχορεύω.definition: dance round, E.Ph.316 ; Luc.DMar.15.3; Id.Salt.24: metaph., Epicur.Sent.Vat.52

περίχρισμα.definition: ointment, salve, Alex.Trall.7.8: metaph., of music used as 'jam to coat the pill', Phld.Mus. p.96K

περίχριστος.definition: ointment, Archig. ap. Orib.44.26.11 ; Dsc.1.77; Plu.2.102a

περίχρυσος.definition: set in gold, IG12.280.78; ib.22.1388.91, 1459.18, Chares 4J., Luc.Nec.12; cf

περιχρυσόω.definition: gild all over, Agatharch.Fr.Hist.2 J., v.l. for in Hdt.4.65:— but in Pass., = with a gold mount or setting, IG22.1388.88, cf. POxy.1449.22

περιχύτης.definition: attendant at baths, POxy.148 , cf. Ptol.Tetr.179, Cod.Just.3.43.1.4

περίχωμα.definition: embankment, dyke enclosing an; area enclosed by dykes, PCair.Zen.182.7, 362.24 , PTeb.13.12, 84.3

περιχωματίζω.definition: surround with a dyke, PLond.3.1170 B298 :—hence PRyl.172.22 , etc

περιχωνεύομαι.definition: to be fused in an amalgam with, Dsc.Eup.2.168

περιχώννυμι.definition: heap earth round, D.S.17.82; embank, PSI6.577.8 , cf. PLille 1 v 20

περιχωρέω.definition: rotate, Anaxag.9, 12; to be transferred to, come to in succession, Hdt.1.210; D.C.40.49

περίχωρος.definition: round about a place: the people about, D.19.266, Plu.Cat.Ma.25, Eum.15, etc.; the country round about, LXXGe.13.10,al., Ev.Matt.14.35; Palaeph.20

περιψάω.definition: wipe all round, wipe clean, Ar.Eq.909; Id.Pl.730; IG11.287 A 84 ; Zos. Alch.p.224B

περίψημα.definition: anything wiped off, offscouring, of a vile person , 1 Ep.Cor.4.13, Phot.; your humble servant, CIL8.12924 , LW2493 , Classical Studies in honor of J.C.Rolfe318 ; peripsuma su , Dessau ILS5725

περιψιλόομαι.definition: Pass., to be made bare all round, to have one's flesh all stripped off, Hdt.9.83

περιψοφέω.definition: sound loudly around, in Pass., J.AJ11.3.9; Plu.2.266d

περιψόφησις.definition: sounding all round, loud noise, ib.549c

περιψυγμός.definition: cold, chill, Pl.Ax.366d; excessive cold, as a cause of injury, Cat.Cod.Astr.8.188

περίψυκτος.definition: very cold, chill, of places; fanned all round: hence, fondled, beloved, Alciphr.3.59; Eun.VSp.455 B.; cf. · Hsch

περίψυξις.definition: shivering, Hp.Prorrh.1.134; chilling, cooling, Arist.Fr.231, Thphr.Ign.52, Chrysipp.Stoic.2.222, Plu.2.73c, etc

περίψυχρος.definition: cold all round or very cold, Hp.Epid.1.18 , Thphr.Sens.58

περιψύχω.definition: chill all round; metaph., refresh, revive, cherish LXXSi.30.7 , D.H.7.46 , Alciphr.1.39

περιωδυνάω.definition: suffer great pain, Dsc.3.23, Gal.12.603:—Med., v.l. in Hp.Aph.7.52

περιωδυνέω.definition: = foreg., ib.6.10, Morb.3.1, Epid.5.12, Herod.Med. ap. Orib.10.10.4

περιωδυνία.definition: excessive pain, Pl.R.583d; opp. Id.Lg.732c; of headache, Hp.Aff.2: in pl., Id.Acut.34; ib.4; Arist.Po.1452b12

περιώδυνος.definition: exceeding painful, of death; suffering great pain, Hp.Acut.34, D.54.12, Parth.5.5. Adv. Hsch. s.v

περιωθέω.definition: push, shove about; push or force round, Pl.Ti.79c, cf. e, Arist.Resp.472b18:—Pass., to be pushed away, Th.3.57; lose one's place in a person's favour, ib.67; D.H.7.25; App.BC1.45: abs., to be rejected, defeated, Arist…

περιωπέω.definition: gaze around upon, Philostr.Dial.2:—Med., Sch.D Il.14.8

περίωπος.definition: visible all round, Hsch. s.v. in Orph.A.14 . . is prob. f.l. for

περιωτειλόομαι.definition: to be cicatrized all round, Hp.Art.63

πέρκη.definition: a river-fish, perch, Epich.47,48, Philyll.13.3, Antiph.194.2, Arist.HA505a17, 599b8, Numen. ap. Ath.7.313c

περκίδιον.definition: Dim. of foreg., Anaxandr.27 :— also PCair.Zen.66.14

περνάω.definition: sell, aor. imper. Hsch.; cf. sq

περόνημα.definition: Dor. garment pinned or buckled on, Theoc.15.79

περονητρίς.definition: Dor. robe fastened on the shoulder with a buckle or brooch, Theoc.15.21: as Adj., cj. for in AP7.413

πέρπερος.definition: vainglorious, braggart, Plb.32.2.5, 39.1.2, Arr.Epict.3.2.14, S.E.M.1.54; gloss on Hsch

Πέρσης.definition: heterocl. acc. v.l. in; the city of Persepolis, Beros.16 , Arr.An.3.18.10; cf

Περσίζω.definition: speak Persian, X.An.4.5.34, Porph.Abst.3.5; imitate the Persians, Arr.An.7.6.3, cf. Str.11.11.8

Περσονομέομαι.definition: Pass., to be governed by the Persian laws or by Persians, A.Pers.585 :—from ruling Persians, ib.919

πεσσευτής.definition: Att. draught- player, Pl.Plt.292e; applied to Divine Providence, Id.Lg.903d

πεσσονομέω.definition: set the in order for playing: play; metaph., dispose, adjust, A.Supp.13

πεσσοποιέομαι.definition: make and apply a II.1 to oneself, Poet.de herb.103

πεταλία.definition: flat dish or crate, PCair.Zen.99.3 (iii; crown of leaves, Ostr. in Arch.Pap.6.220

πεταλίζω.definition: put forth leaves or strip off leaves, Hsch

πεταλισμός.definition: petalism, method of banishing citizens practised at Syracuse, like the at Athens, exc. that the name was written on olive- leaves instead of potsherds, D.S.11.87

πεταλόω.definition: cover with leaves or plates , LXX3 Ki.6.21 cod. A; cf. PLeid.X.89

πετάλωσις.definition: covering with gold-leaf, EM69.44; putting forth of leaves, Aristeas68

πετάομαι.definition: false form for f.l. in Arist.Metaph.1009b38, Str.16.4.11, AP14.63 :—also in Act., Cat.Cod. Astr.8.249

πετάσιον.definition: Dim. of Posidon.2 J.; Sch. Orib.2.745

πέτασος.definition: also Eratosth. ap. Ath.11.499e; from its shape, broad umbellated leaf, as of the lotus, Thphr.HP4.8.9; Dsc.2.106

πετευρίζομαι.definition: jump from a springboard, vault, perform acrobatic feats, Phld.Rh.1.74 S.: pf. Gloss

πετεύριον.definition: Dim. of IV, small notice- board, Jahresh.13 Beibl.23

πετευριστής.definition: = foreg., in Lat. form petaurista, Varro ap. Non.p.79 L.: metaph., of fleas and the like, Plin.HN11.115

πετρηρεφής.definition: o'er-arched with rock, rock- vaulted, A.Pr.302, E.Cyc.82

πετρίδιον.definition: Dim. of Arist.HA547b21, Fr.338, Thphr.Fr.160, AP9.570 , Porph.Abst.2.17

πετροβάτης.definition: one who climbs rocks, ib.56; of Pan, Poet. ap.Stob.1.1.31a

πετρόβλητος.definition: pelted with stones, Phot; affected by the stone, Id

πετροβολέω.definition: pelt with stones, in Pass., Sch.rec.A.Th.560

πετροβόλος.definition: throwing stones, X.HG2.4.12; Subst. engine for throwing stones, Plb.5.4.6, LXXJb.41.19, Ath.Mech.34.2, etc.; distd. from Plb.8.7.2 : neut. , opp. J.AJ9.10.3

πετροκατοίκητος.definition: having its abode in the rocks, Limen.15

πετροκόραξ.definition: raven of the rocks, nickname in IG14.1517

πετροκυλιστής.definition: rolling rocks or stones, Str.15.1.56: name of a play by Aeschylus, Anon.in EN145.25

πετροσέλινον.definition: parsley, Petroselinum sativum, Dsc.3.66, Gal.12.99, Alex.Aphr.Pr.1.110, POxy.2144.3 , Edict.Diocl.32.56

πετροφυής.definition: clinging to rock; Subst. = Ps.-Dsc.4.90, cf. 89

πεύκινος.definition: of, from, or made of pine or pine wood, E.Hec.575; S.Tr.1198; tear of the pine, i. e. the resinous drops that ooze from it, E.Med.1200; Dsc.1.71; pine-logs, Plb.5.89.1, cf. IG12.342.70

πευστήριος.definition: of or for inquiry, a sacrificial feast for learning the will of the gods, cj. for in E.El.835

πηγανέλαιον.definition: oil of rue, Herod.Med. in Rh.Mus.58.75, Alex.Trall.1.16

πηγανηρά.definition: rue-plaster, Antyll. ap. Paul.Aeg.7.17, Alex.Trall.5.4. :—also Aët.15.40

πηγανίζω.definition: to be like rue, Dsc.1.14, Gal.14.258

πηγανίτης.definition: wine flavoured with rue, Gp.8.13; fem., rue-juice, Sopat.18

πηδαλιόομαι.definition: to be furnished with a rudder, Simp.in Cat.187.14

πηδαλιουχέω.definition: steer, Ph.1.131: metaph., LXX4 Ma.7.1; of God, Ph.1.516; govern, Boeth.Stoic.3.266, Ph.1.370

πήδησις.definition: beating or throbbing of the heart, Pl.Ti.70c, Lg.791a, Arist.PA669a20, Phld.Irp.27 W

πηλακίζω.definition: etym. of EM669.49, cf. also found in PSI5.495.9

πηλικότης.definition: magnitude, size, A.D.Pron.26.13, Gal.1.333, Sch.Ar.Pl.377: opp. , Nicom.Ar.1.7

πηλοβάτης.definition: mud-walker, name of a frog, v.l. in Batr.241

πηλοπατέω.definition: trample in the mire, PMasp.87.9 (vi A. D; walk on clay or mud, Sch.Ar.Pax1148

πηλόπλαστος.definition: moulded of clay, of a man, A.Fr.369

Πηλοπλάτων.definition: Mud-Plato, nickname of the sophist Alexander, Philostr.VS2.5.1

πηλότροφος.definition: reared in mud or soft soil, Opp.C.1.288

πηλουργία.definition: in Ion. form working in clay, Aret.SD1.6

πηλοφορέω.definition: carry clay or mortar, Ar.Av.1142, Ec.310 , BGU 699.5

πηλοφόρος.definition: carrying clay or mortar, ib.1290.3 , Poll.7.130, Suid

πηλόχυτος.definition: moulded of clay, of swallows' nests, AP10.16

πηλόω.definition: coat or daub with clay, PMag.Berol.2.151, Gal.14.291:— Med., smear oneself with clay, IG42.126.11 , cf. Plu.2.980e:—Pass., to be covered with mud, J.AJ1.3.5, Plu.2.831a; Lyd.Mens.4.57; to be smeared with clay, Apollod…

πημονή.definition: = freq. in Trag., A.Pr.239 , 278, 308 , S.Tr.1189 , E.Fr.682; also with hostile intent, Foed. ap. Th.5.18

πηνήκη.definition: false hair, wig, Luc.DMeretr.5.3, 11.4, 12.5: distd. from and Phot., cf. Poll.2.30, 10.170

πηνηκίζω.definition: cheat, gull, Cratin.319, Hsch. , Suid.; cf

πηνίζομαι.definition: Dor. wind thread off a reel for the woof, Philyll.33, prob. in BGU1141.34 : generally, wind off a reel, Theoc.18.32:—later in Act., Orib.Fr.137

πήνισμα.definition: woof on the spool, AP6.283; Ar.Ra.1315, cf. Sammelb.5873.6

πηρομελής.definition: disabled in the limbs, maimed, Epigr. ap. D.L.5.40

πηρόω.definition: Dor. , maim, mutilate; metaph., incapacitate, . . Pl.Phdr.257a; Str.17.3.3:—Pass., incapacitated for practising virtue, Arist.EN1099b19; Anaxarch. ap. S.E.M.7.55, cf. 298; Thphr.CP1.5.5

πηρώνυμος.definition: named after a wallet, gloss on Tz.ad Lyc.183

πήρωσις.definition: maiming, disabling in the limbs or senses, Democr.296, cf. Arist.EN1131a9: freq. in pl., Hp.Art.61, Pl.Lg.874e, 925e, Arist.EN1148b17; ib.1145a31; Plu.2.633c, Luc.DMar.2.4 ; Plu.2.167c: generally, Aret.SD1.4; Man.4.51…

πήσσω.definition: Att. later form for LXXSi.14.24, Ph.1.420, Dsc.4.188, Arr.Epict.1.19.4, S.E.M.9.247, Str.4.3.5, D.H.3.22: impf. Satyr.1:—Pass. Antig.Mir.174, Str.13.4.14, 7.3.18

πηχισμός.definition: measuring by the cubit, Ostr.Bodl. i 90 , PTeb.164.14 , Sm., Al. l.c., Judeich Altertümer von Hierapolis No.262

πηχύνω.definition: take in one's arms, embrace, A.R.4.972, Nonn.D.25.177; ib.3.340: more freq. in Med., AP12.121 , Opp.H.4.286, Nonn.D.9.30; ib.14.152

πιαίνω.definition: fut. A.Th.587: aor. Id.Ag.276; increase, enlarge, Pi.P.4.150 ; Xenoph.2.22

πιδακῖτις.definition: growing at or about a spring, Hp.Ep.16

πιδάω.definition: = Arist.Mete.349b34, Hsch., Choerob. in An.Ox.2.249; prob. cj. in Hp.Epid.5.16, Theoc.8.42

πίεσις.definition: squeezing, compression, Arist.PA687b11 , Mete.387a16; pinching, Aret.CA1.2; pressure, close contact, Gal.18.398

πιεσμός.definition: = Hp.Nat.Puer.21 , Eust.1181.63: metaph., in pl., constraint, pressure of circumstances, Epicur.Nat.28.3

πιεστήρ.definition: squeezer : press, IG22.1672.304 , Dsc.4.64 , Gal.13.1044, Aët.12.55

πιθανολογέω.definition: use probable arguments, Arist.EN1094b26, D.S.1.39: —Med., Dam.Pr.405, Sch.E.Or.424:—Pass., Epicur.Ep.2p.36 U., Orib.49.22.22

πιθανολογία.definition: use of probable arguments, opp. demonstration , Pl.Tht.162e, cf.Ep.Col.2.4, Gal.17.619

πιθανολογική.definition: art of using probable or specious arguments, Arr.Epict.1.8.7

πιθανοποιέω.definition: sharpen the wits of one, Hsch. s.v

πιθανότης.definition: persuasiveness, plausibility, of; of arguments, Pl.Lg.839d, Cra.402a; Arist.EN1097a4, cf. Phld.Rh.1.209 S.; provided himself with plausible charges against . . , Plb.27.15.9, cf. 12.26c.2, Ph.1.94

πιθήκειος.definition: of an ape, ape-like, Gal.2.386, UP3.8, Suid

πιθηκίζω.definition: play the ape, of flatterers, Lib.Ep.424.1, 1397.5:—Med., Sch.rec.D.18.242 : barbarous form or cj. for in Ar.Th.1133

πιθηκισμός.definition: playing the ape, playing monkey- tricks, Ar.Eq.887, M.Ant.9.37

πιθηκοφόρος.definition: branded with the mark of an ape, Luc.Pisc.47

πικράζω.definition: = sq., S.E.P.1.211:—Pass., taste bitter; metaph., Epict.Gnom.22

πικραίνω.definition: make sharp or keen, esp. to the taste; metaph., embitter, irritate, LXXJb.27.2; affect it harshly, opp. D.H.Comp.12, 15; make harsh, cj. in A.Eu.693:—Pass., to be exasperated, embittered, Pl.Lg.731d, Theoc.5.120; vexe…

πικρασμός.definition: bitterness : bitter feeling, LXXEz.27.31: pl., Ph.1.441:—written Aq.Jb. 3.5

πικρία.definition: of taste, Thphr.CP6.10.7, Od.32, LXXJe.15.17, Placit.3.16.2, Dsc.1.61, etc

πικρίζω.definition: to be or taste bitter, Str.11.2.17, Archig. ap. Orib.8.1.37; Dsc.1.20

πικρόγαμος.definition: attaining a bitter kind of marriage , Od.1.266, al., Hld.5.30, 7.28

πικρόγλωσσος.definition: of sharp or bitter tongue, A.Th.787

πικρολόγος.definition: speaking bitter things, prob. in Epigr.Gr.288c4

πιλέω.definition: = (which is rejected by; generally, compress, close up, Ar.Lys.577; D.H.9.58; make firm or solid, Gal.11.758, 394; . . Id.6.417:—Pass., to be close pressed, Arist.Mete.366b13; . . made solid, A.R.4.678; kneaded, APl.4…

πίλησις.definition: compression of wool, felt; generally, compression, solidification, esp. of contraction by cold, Id.Ti.76c, cf. Xenoph. ap. Placit.3.4.4, Pl.Ti.58b, Thphr.CP5.8.3 ; compression of air, Ph.Bel.77.22; opp. Ph.1.385: pl.,…

πιλίδιον.definition: Dim. of Ar.Ach.439, Antiph.33.4, Pl.R.406d, D.19.255

πίλινος.definition: made of felt, IG5.1390.23 , cf. Poll.7.171

πιλίον.definition: Dim. of II, Arist.Fr.235; name of a bandage, Sor.Fasc.2

πιλοειδής.definition: like a cap, Cleanth.Stoic.1.113 , Heliod. ap. Orib.48.50.1 . Adv. Sor.1.14

πιλοφόρος.definition: wearing a cap, AP9.430 ; of the Dacian nobles, D.C.68.9

πιμελή.definition: soft fat, lard, Hdt.2.40,47, Hp.Aër.19, S.Ant.1011, Democr. ap. Ael.NA12.18, Alex.83: distd. from as being Arist.HA520a8, cf. PA651a20; of cream, Philostr.Im.1.31

πιμελής.definition: fat, Aq. Jd.3.17, Luc.Tim.15, Babr.100.1, etc.: Comp. Luc.Symp.43

πιμπλάω.definition: = imper. Xenarch.3 codd.; pres. part. LXXSi.24.25, Hp.Epid.6.8.7, v.l. in Id.Morb.2.12: impf. Lyr.Adesp.90:—Pass. Hp.Morb.1.32

πινακιαῖος.definition: of the size or thickness of a Hippiatr.104

πινακίδιον.definition: = Hp.Epid.6.8.7, Arist.Mir.834b12, Sm.Ez.9.2, Gal.7.855; writing- tablet, Plu.Eum.1

πινάκιον.definition: Dim. of small tablet on which; notice-board on which laws, decrees, etc. were written, Ar.Av.450, Plu.Per.30, etc.; IG22.1237.62, cf. 12.66.31; also for notices of charges against officials, Arist.Ath.48.4, cf. D.8.28…

πινακίς.definition: = foreg. I.3, Philyll.11, Macho; in pl., tablets, Plu.TG6, Id.2.47e, Arr.Epict.1.10.5

πινακίσκος.definition: Dim. of 2, Ar.Pl.813,Fr.532, Pherecr.108.14, Pl.Com.119, Lync.1.6

πινακογραφέω.definition: inscribe on a in Pass., Eust.633.25 , etc

πινακόγραφος.definition: map-maker, Id.ad D.P.4; maker of lists or catalogues, St.Byz. s.v

πινακοπώλης.definition: one who sells small birds plucked and ranged upon a board, Ar.Av.14, cf. Sch

πιναρόομαι.definition: Pass., to be dirty, Suid. s.v

πινόομαι.definition: Pass., to be dirty, Philet.17; of Alexander's complexion as painted by Apelles, Plu.Alex.4: metaph. , literae or scriptae, in archaic style, Cic.Att.14.7.2, 15.16; D.H.Dem.45

πινοτήρης.definition: pinna-guard, a small crab; metaph., of a diminutive person, 'baby-crab', Ar.V.1510; , posted to give warning, S.Fr.113

πινοφύλαξ.definition: = Arist.HA547b16, Isid.Char.20, Xenocr. ap. Orib.2.58.98, Artem.2.14

πινυτόφρων.definition: of wise or understanding mind, of Odysseus, Q.S.14.630, AP3.8 ; ib.7.22 ; APl.4.325 ; ingenious, Puchstein Epigr.Gr.p.10; Jul.Caes.319a; restd. in Epic.Alex.Adesp.7.19

πιπίσκω.definition: Hp.Mul.1.63, Luc.Lex.20: fut. Pi.I.6.74, Eup.115: aor. Hp.Mul.1.59, al., prob. in Arist.EN1111a14 , Pi.Fr.111 :—Med., aor. Nic.Th.573,877, etc.:—Pass., aor. ib.624:—causal of give to drink, Hp.Acut.2, Aret.CA1.1, etc.…

πισσάριον.definition: a little pitch, Archig. ap. Gal.12.978

πισσάσφαλτος.definition: Att. compound of asphalt and pitch, Dsc.1.73, Plin.HN24.41, etc

πισσέλαιον.definition: = Dsc.1.72; also, mixture of oil and pitch, Hippiatr.20,al

πισσίζω.definition: taste of pitch, Sch.Ar.Ach.189; f.l. for in Dsc.5.75

πίσσινος.definition: Att. of or from pitch, pitched, Ar.Fr.269, IG22.1648.27 ; like pitch, Luc.VH2.29

πισσίτης.definition: flavoured with pitch, Str.4.6.2, Dsc.5.38, Plu.2.676c

πισσόκαπνος.definition: soot obtained by burning pitch, lampblack, Hippiatr.34

πισσόκηρος.definition: a kind of propolis, with which bees line their hives, Arist.HA624a17, Plin.HN11.16

πισσοκοπέω.definition: Att. smear with; have the hair removed by pitch-plasters, Alex.264.1; Com.Adesp.339; title of play by Philemon :—hence Subst. Ion. Aret.CD1.2, POxy.1911.187 : Adj. and Poll.7.165

πισσοκώνητος.definition: daubed with pitch: fire blazing with pitch, A.Fr.118; the death of one who is pitched and burnt alive, Hsch. s.v

πισσουργέομαι.definition: Pass., to be made into pitch, D.H.20.15

πισσόω.definition: Att. pitch over, pitch; Med., remove the hair by means of a pitch-plaster, Theopomp. Hist.195, cf. Luc.Rh.Pr.23; Id.Demon.50, cf. Merc.Cond.33

πίσσωσις.definition: Att. a pitching over, PCair.Zen.271.9 , Gal.6.443, Archig. ap. Aët.3.180

πιστάκιον.definition: pistachio-nut, Nic.Th.891, Dsc.1.124, Gp.10.3.3: written Posidon.3 J.; v.l. in Nic. l.c

πιστοΐασπις.definition: true jewel, metaph. of Isis, POxy.1380.138

πιστολογευτής.definition: confidential agent for collection of dues, PCair.Zen.199.7

πίστωσις.definition: assurance, confirmation, Pl.Lg.943c , cf. Hermog.Meth.10; D.C.38.12

πιστωτέος.definition: to be affirmed as true, Luc.Hist.Conscr.60, cf. Plot.5.3.16

πίτνω.definition: poet. form of Pi.O.2.23, P.8.93; Id.N.5.42, cf. I.2.26, A.Ch.1056, Ag.1128 , E.Hec.23, al.: impf. poet. B.16.6, S.OC1732 , etc.: is given as pres. by Gramm., as Hdn.Gr.2.290, and is found in codd. of E.Heracl.77; but …

πιττακίζω.definition: attach a label to a thing, PMag.Par.1.2952

πιτύινος.definition: of or from the pine, pine-resin, Hp.Mul.2.203, Thphr.HP9.2.2; so alone, Orib.Fr.89, Paul.Aeg.7.17; Plu.2.677b; Gal.13.475

πιτυλεύω.definition: ply the sweeping oar, Ar.V.678; = sq. I, Com.Adesp.3 D

πιτυλίζω.definition: practise regular swinging of the arms, as; dart about, Anon. ap. Suid

πίτυλος.definition: sweep of oars, periphr; shower, torrent, E.Hipp.1464 ; of blows, Theoc.22.127, cf. Poll.2.147; E.Tr.1236

πιτυοκάμπη.definition: a stinging or urticating caterpillar; small pine-cone, Sch.Il.2.868

πιτυοκάμπτης.definition: pinebender, epith. of Sinis, who killed travellers by tying them between two pine-trees bent down so as nearly to meet, and then let go again, Str.9.1.4, Apollod.3.16.2, Plu.Thes.8:—also prob. for in AP11.107

πιτυρίας.definition: bread made with bran, Poll.6.72, Gal.6.481, etc

πιτυρίζω.definition: become coated with bran, PLeid. X.8, 25

πιτυρόομαι.definition: Pass., to be affected with Hp.Prorrh.2.30

πιφάσκω.definition: freq. v.l. for sq. in Hom., Il.10.478, al

πλαγιάζω.definition: hold aslant, Ach.Tat.Intr.Arat.21; Pass., let the holes be made obliquely, Apollod.Poliorc.151.6; Hierocl.in CA24p.474 M

πλαγιασμός.definition: obliquity, of the sun's course; in Obstetrics, oblique presentation of the foetus, Sor.2.60

πλαγίαυλος.definition: cross-flute, opp. flûte-à-bec, Theoc.20.29, BionFr.7, etc.; cf

πλαγιοβάτης.definition: walking obliquely, dub. cj. for Vett.Val.110.14

πλαγιόκαρπος.definition: having fruit at the sides, Thphr.HP1.14.2,3.18.12

πλαγιόκαυλος.definition: having stalks at the sides, ib.8.3.2

πλαγιόσκελος.definition: expl. of Lat. Varus, Blaesus, Lyd.Mag.1.23

πλαγιοφύλαξ.definition: guarding the flanks of an army on the march, D.S.19.82 ; esp. of the corner man in the of cavalry, Ascl.Tact.7.2, 6, Arr.Tact.16.5; cf

πλαγκτήρ.definition: either he that leads astray, the beguiler, or the roamer, epith. of Dionysus, AP9.524.17: fem. of the Zodiac, Hymn.Is.29

πλαδαρόομαι.definition: Pass., become soft and flabby, Aq.Is.19.3

πλαδαρότης.definition: flaccidity, Epicur.Nat.140 G., Herm. ap. Stob.1.49.69, Gal.14.770

πλάδος.definition: abundance of fluids, like water-brash, Hp.Epid.1.5, Acut.37, Gland.3, Aret.SD2.6

πλάδωσις.definition: = Aët.9.42, cf. Phot. and Suid. s.v

πλαθανίτης.definition: Dor. baked in a mould, prob. in Philox.3.17

πλάθανον.definition: dish or mould in which bread, cakes, etc. were baked, Theoc.15.115, Nic.Fr.70.2, Poll.7.22, etc.: hence the baking-woman in Ar.Ra. is called cf

πλάθω.definition: poet. form of used by Trag. in lyr., approach, draw near, S.Ph.728, cf.El.220: c. acc., E.Rh.14: abs., Id.Alc.119:—Med., Inscr. ap. Plu.Arat.14

πλαίσιον.definition: hollow rectangle, Th.7.78, cf. 6.67, X.An.1.8.9; = Ael.Tact.37.8, Arr.Tact.29.7; X.An.3.4.19, Arr.An.4.5.6; Aristid.Or.23.20; of the shape of the Acropolis of Alexandria, Aphth.Prog.12

πλάκινος.definition: made of marble slabs, CIG2846 ; a marble tripod, AP6.98

πλακίον.definition: Dim. of IG4.823.61 , POxy.921 Intr. ; small slab of marble ready for powdering, Aët.12.64

πλακίς.definition: bench, seat, couch of flowers, used at the Panathenaea, Hsch

πλακίτης.definition: fem. = a form of Gal.12.220; a kind of alum, ib.237

πλακουντάριος.definition: maker of cakes, pastry-cook, IG3.3445 , MAMA3.697

πλακούντιον.definition: Dim. of Arr.Epict.2.16.25, Aët.9.30, Sch.Porph.Abst.2.16:— written PLond.3.964.20

πλάκωσις.definition: facing with marble slabs, revetting, TAM2.408 , cf. CPHerm.94.2

πλάνη.definition: wandering, roaming, Hdt.1.30, 2.103, 116; discursive treatment, Pl.Prm.136e; Id.Lg.683a

πλάνης.definition: wanderer, vagabond, ib.1029; planets, X.Mem.4.7.5, Arist.Mete.342b28; and, simply, Id.APo.78a30,Fr.196, Plu.2.604a, etc.; Arist.Cael.290a19

πλανησίεδρος.definition: having a wandering seat, i.e. moving about freely, of the knee-pan, Arist.HA494a5

πλανήτης.definition: as Adj., E.Heracl.878, cf. Porph.Marc.22; Medic., = I.3, Gal.11.18

πλανῆτις.definition: fem. of Lyc.998, Phld.Acad.Ind.p.77 M., Poll.5.63, Ant.Lib.24.1

πλασματίας.definition: fabricated, fictitious; one addicted to invention, Plu.Cam.22

πλάσσω.definition: plaster, . . BCH15.209; generally, mould, form by education, training, etc., Pl.R.377c; Id.Ti.88c; Id.R.500d; Id.Lg.671c:—Pass., E.Ion830; of the voice, to be trained, Arist.HA536b19

πλαστή.definition: mud-wall or -enclosure, BGU1503 , PSI 2.171.19 , POxy.729.30 , etc

πλαστογραφία.definition: forgery, J.Vit.11, BGU388 ii 39 , Vett. Val.40.29 , Just.Nov.80.7

πλαστογράφος.definition: forger, Artem.1.51, Ptol.Tetr.161, Man.2.305, Cod.Just.4.20.13 Intr

πλαστοκόμης.definition: one who wears false hair, Man.4.304

πλαστουργία.definition: work of plastic art, of statues, Tz.H.7.932; of cakes, ib.13.325

πλαταγέω.definition: clap the hands, Theoc.8.88; of broad flat; beat, so as to make a loud noise, Bion1.4; BMus.Inscr.1084.6 ; AP6.218.6

πλαταγή.definition: rattle, Hellanic.104 J., Pherecyd.72 J.; Arist.Pol.1340b26; A.R.2.1055, AP6.309

πλαταγώνιον.definition: broad petal of the poppy or anemone, so called because lovers took omens from it, laying it on the left hand, and striking it with the right, and it was a good omen if it burst with a loud crack, Theoc.11.57, cf. Nic.…

πλατανιστής.definition: an unknown fish of the Ganges, Plin.HN9.46

πλατάνιστος.definition: earlier name for Il.2.307, 310, Hdt.5.119, 7.27,31, Theoc.18.44, al

πλατανιστοῦς.definition: contr. for grove of plane-trees, Thgn.882

πλάτανος.definition: later form of Platanus orientalis, plane, Ar.Eq.528, Nu.1008, Pl.Phdr.229a, Thphr.HP4.5.6, Nic.Th.584, Dsc.1.79

πλατάσσω.definition: slap or clap two flat bodies together, Suid. s.v

πλατειασμός.definition: broad Doric accent, pl. in form Quint.Inst.1.5.32

πλατόομαι.definition: Pass., to be made flat like an oar-blade, Ar.Ach.552

πλατυάμφοδος.definition: with broad streets, gloss on Sch.D Il.2.12, AB332, etc

πλατυγίζω.definition: of a goose, beat the water with its wings, splash about, Eub.115; prob. in Ar.Fr.22 D.: metaph., make a splash, swagger, Id.Eq.830

πλατύγλωσσος.definition: Att. broad- tongued, flat-tongued, Arist.HA504b3: Comp., Id.PA660a30

πλατύκαρπος.definition: with flat fruit, v.l. in Dsc.3.144

πλατυκέρως.definition: flat-horned, Dsc.Eup.1.21, cf. Plin.HN11.123, Poll.5.76: as Subst. , Dsc.2.75

πλατυκέφαλος.definition: a venomous beast or reptile, Philum.Ven.32.2

πλατυκορία.definition: Ion. a disease of the eye from dilatation of the pupil, mydriasis, Aret.SD1.7, Aët.7.54

πλατύλογχος.definition: Subst. partisan, Str.17.3.7, prob. in Hsch. s.v

πλατυμέτωπος.definition: with broad forehead, Ael.NA12.19, cf. Heph.Astr.2.2

πλατυμήλη.definition: broad probe, Antyll. ap. Orib.44.22.2, Heliod. ap. eund.44.11.2

πλατύνω.definition: widen, Ev.Matt.23.5; was opened wide, ib.1 Ki.2.1: hence, metaph., be puffed up, ib.De.11.16:—Med., talk big of oneself, Timo34.4

πλατυόφθαλμος.definition: widening the eyes, v.l. in Hp.Art.67, cf. Erot.: = Dsc.5.84

πλατυπήγιον.definition: broad-bottomed boat, punt, POxy.1652.2 , prob. in PThead.59.3

πλατυπρόσωπος.definition: flat-faced, PGrenf.1.27.8 , Peripl. M.Rubr.65, Arist.Mir.832b2, Ael.NA15.26

πλατυρημοσύνη.definition: breadth in speaking, i.e. prolixity, Timo35

πλατύρρυμος.definition: with broad streets, gloss on Eust.166.21

πλατύσημος.definition: with broad border, =; of those entitled to wear it, = tribunus laticlavius, IG4.588.4 , IGRom.3.554 , 889

πλάτυσμα.definition: flat object, e.g. tile, Herod.3.46; slab, Dsc.Eup.1.171; metal plate, HeroDioptr.5; Gal.12.831; plaster, Heliod. ap. Orib.46.29.3, Orib.Syn.2.59; flat cake, Gal.4.526; a muscle discovered by Galen, 18.930; blades, Eus…

πλατυσμάτιον.definition: Dim. of foreg., HeroSpir.1.21, Asclep. ap. Gal.13.675, Orib.Fr.99

πλατύστομος.definition: wide-mouthed, Dsc.1.30, Damocr. ap. Gal.13.40, Gp.9.24.1; of a cupping instrument, Sor.1.50

πλατύσχιστος.definition: with broad clefts, of a leaf, Thphr.HP9.10.1

πλατύφυλλος.definition: broad-leaved, Arist.APo.98b4, Thphr.HP3.8.2, etc.: Comp. Id.CP5.7.2

πλατυώνυχος.definition: with flat nails, of man, Pl.Def.415a, S.E.P.2.211; of the swan and goose, Ael.NA11.37

πλέγμα.definition: anything twined or twisted; plaited work, wicker-work, Pl.Lg.734e, etc.; Id.Ti.79d: hence, = X.Cyr.1.6.28: in pl., wreaths, chaplets, E.Ion1393; also, plaited hair, 1 Ep.Ti.2.9

πλεθριαῖος.definition: of the size of a X.Cyr.7.5.11; Id.An.1.5.4; Pl.Criti.116a; Str.16.2.17

πλέθρισμα.definition: race of a in length, Hsch., Phot

πλέθρον.definition: measure of length of 100 feet, Hdt.2.124; as a square measure, 10,000 square feet, Hdt.7.199 , IG12.376, 385, Pl.Tht.174e, Alc.1.123c, D.20.115, SIG306.13

πλειονομοιρέω.definition: to be further on in the zodiac, have more degrees, Paul.Al.H.1

πλειονοψηφία.definition: dominant astrological influence, Serapio in Cat.Cod. Astr.5.87 , Paul.Al.R.1

πλειστηριάζω.definition: raise the price of a thing, make dear, Lys.Fr.7, Pl.Com.18, Them.Or.21.261b:—hence Subst. Hsch

πλειστοβολέω.definition: throw highest at dice, Phot., Suid

πλειστογονέω.definition: produce many at a birth, Ptol.Tetr.126:—hence Adj. ib.110

πλειστοδυναμέω.definition: to be dominant, prevail, Heraclid.Erythr. ap. Gal.8.743; the greater part, majority, Sor.1.11, 126, Gal.18.324

πλειστονίκης.definition: victor in many contests, SIG 1073.3 , BSA26.167 , etc

πλειστοτόκος.definition: bringing forth most offspring, Man.4.102 cod

πλεκτανόομαι.definition: Pass., to be intertwined, interlaced, Hp.Oss.18

πλεονάζω.definition: fut. pf. D.S.1.90:-Pass., pf. Hp.Fract.7, etc.: aor. Id.Art.47: :-to be more, esp. to be more than enough, superfluous, opp. Arist.EN1106a31, Col.799a18; the excess, PRev.Laws 57.13 , LXXEx.26.12; c. acc., to be in ex…

πλεόνασμα.definition: superfluity, LXXNu.31.32; opp. A.D.Synt.133.14, cf. Gal.16.417; opp. A.D.Pron.59.7; surplus of production, PTeb.78.7 , 81.27 ; Ostr.Bodl. i 97 , cf. PTeb.344

πλεονασματίζω.definition: bring a surplus into account, PGiss.48.20

πλεονασμός.definition: superabundance, excess; surplus, PRyl.213.82 , Sammelb. 4296.7 , etc

πλεονεκτέω.definition: fut. Th.4.62, etc; also, gain or have some advantage, without any bad sense, Th.4.62, cf. 86; opp. Arist.Rh.1360a3; X.HG7.1.34: abs., Arist.Rh.1402b25, D.S.12.46; Plb.6.56.2: freq. with neut. Pron., etc., Th.4.61, etc

πλεονέκτημα.definition: advantage, gain, Pl.Lg.709c; act of overreaching, undue gain, D.21.60, 50.38, Ep.5.3, Arist.Pol.1311a5; = vitium, Gloss

πλεονέκτης.definition: = one who has or; making gain from their losses, Id.Cyr.1.6.27

πλεονοδάκτυλος.definition: having more than the normal number of fingers, Gal.19.454

πλεονοσυλλαβέω.definition: to be of more syllables, Eust.1769.56: c. gen., A.D.Pron.78.7

πλευμονία.definition: disease of the lungs, Com.Adesp.759:—also Mnesith. ap. Plu.2.918d, cj. in Hippiatr.6

πλευρά.definition: = rib, rare in sg; side, of things and places, Thgn.513; Pl.Sis.388e; D.P.833; of an army, X.An.3.4.22, cf. 28, Plu.Mar.25, etc.; Plb.5.26.6; opp. IG22.463.72

πλευριαῖος.definition: of the side, BCH20.324 ; cj. in Poll.6.52

πλευρισμός.definition: dub. sens. in BGU1270.14; = IIIc v.l. for in Theol.Ar.28

πλευρίτης.definition: connected with ribs, of vertebrae, Poll.2.178

πλευροτυπής.definition: with striking of the sides, of a cock crowing, AP12.137

πλευρωνία.definition: dub. sens. in Them.in PN11.24, Mich.in PN25.20

πληγή.definition: Dor. blow, stroke; stroke by lightning, Hes.Th.857 ; strokes of axe or sword, Pi.P.4.246, O.10.37; . . A.Th.796; beating of breasts, S.El.90 ; strokes from boars' tusks, X.Cyn.10.5; spearing of fish, Pl.Lg.824 ; of pi…

πλῆγμα.definition: = etc., S.Tr.522 , E.IT1366, Tr.794 , etc.; stroke of mattock, S.Ant.250; ib.1283; of a wasp's sting, Arist.HA627b27

πληγμός.definition: apoplectic stroke, Alex. Trall.12; bite, Heraclid.Tar. ap. Gal.14.181; Sch.Nic.Th.655

πληθοειδής.definition: having the form of plurality; numerous, Simp.in Ph.528.24

πληθύνω.definition: fut. 2 Ep.Cor.9.10: aor; make multiple, 'plurify', Dam.l.c.; Jul.Or.4.143b, cf. Or.7.222a

πληθύς.definition: Ep. dat. Il.22.458, Od.11.514, 16.105:—Ion. for throng, crowd, of people, Hom.ll. cc.; = Leg.Gort. 6.52; majority, IG9.333.18 : as Noun of multitude with pl. Verb, Il.2.278: in later Prose, Pl.Ax.366b, LXX3 Ma.4.17; P…

πληθυσμός.definition: a making multiple, pluralization, Procl.in Prm.p.577 S., in Ti.1.184 D., al., Simp.in Ph.88.22, Anon.in Cat.9.9, Dam.Pr.53, Eust.213.23

πληθύω.definition: aor. subj. Pl.Ti.83e:—intr. form of; increase in number, multiply, A.Ch.1057, Pl.Lg.678b; increase in time, S.OC930:—Med., possessing multiplicity in unity, Iamb.Myst.1.6

πληθώρα.definition: Ion. fullness, =; fullness, satiety, Hp.Acut.37; Hdt.7.49: pl

πλήκτης.definition: striker, brawler, Hp.Ep.19 , Arist.EE1221b14, 1 Ep.Ti.3.3; violent, fierce, Plu.Dio30, cf. Phil.9; of wine, Id.2.132d; of the sun, ib.920c, cf. 653f: Sup. Eust.1441.26, EM31.16

πληκτίζομαι.definition: bandy blows with one; beat one's breast for grief, AP7.574

πλῆκτρον.definition: Dor. anything to strike with; spear-point, S.Fr.152 ; of lightning, E.Alc.129 ; a bee's sting, Jul.Or.2.90a

πληκτροποιός.definition: maker of Poll.7.154:—hence manufacture of ibid.: Adj. ibid. Adv. ibid

πλημμέλεια.definition: prop. mistake in music, false note, but in usage, metaph., fault, error, esp. in taste or judgement, Pl.Ap.22d; Id.Lg.691a; faultiness in metre, etc., Plu.2.396d; Arist.VV1251a31 : freq. in pl., Isoc.8.56, etc

πλημμελέω.definition: prop. make a false note in music, but in usage, metaph., offend, err, E.Ph.1655, cf. Pl.Phd.117e, al.; D.21.42; Antipho3.3.6; Din.1.62; Pl.Lg.943e, cf. Rev.Phil.1929.142 , POxy.1119.18 ; Aeschin.1.167, cf. Phld.Ir.p.8…

πλημμέλημα.definition: fault, trespass, Aeschin.3.106 , cf. LXXJe.2.5, Phld.Rh. 1.188 S. , Gal.Anim.Pass.2.3 , etc

πλημμελής.definition: prop. out of tune, opp; wrongful, outrageous, E.Hel.1085; Id.Med.306; Pl.R.451b; Arist.EN1099b24, cf. Democr.181, Pl.Cri.43b, Sph.243a: Sup., Id.Lg.689b. Adv. ib.793c; wrongly, Id.Ti.30a

πλήμυρα.definition: = flood-tide, flood; Medic., accumulation, excessive flow, Lycus ap.Orib.8.25.39, Aret.SA2.9, SD2.2

πλημυρέω.definition: rise like the flood-tide, to be full or in flood, be redundant, Hp.Morb.Sacr.10,11, APl.4.134 , Plu.Caes.22, etc.: Medic., suffer congestion, Aret.SD2.3, CD2.1

πλημυρία.definition: Ion. = prob. f.l. in Aret.CA2.8 and in Sch.Pi.O.5.20

πλημυρίς.definition: rise of the sea, as at flood-tide; generally, flood, deluge, Arist.Mu.397a28 ; of tears, . . A.Ch.186; E.Alc.184

πλημύρω.definition: = overflow, Call.Del.263, AP5.203; swell, Archil.97; A.R.4.706

πληροφορέω.definition: bring full measure: satisfy fully; fulfil, 2 Ep.Ti.4.5; Arch.Pap.5.383 :—Pass., to be fulfilled, Ev.Luc.1.1, Vett.Val.43.18

πληροφορία.definition: fullness of assurance, certainty, 1; assurance given, Cod.Just.1.1.5.4

πληρόω.definition: c. gen. rei, fill full of, Hdt.3.123, etc.; , E.Ion1192, Cyc.29:—Pass., to be filled full, of a thing, Hp.VM20, Pl.R.550d, etc.; A.Eu.568; Porph.Sent.32

πλήρωσις.definition: filling up, filling; sensual satisfaction, gratification, esp. of eating and drinking, Pl.Grg.496e; ib.492a; Id.R.439d: as expl. of the origin of pleasure, Id.Phlb.31 esq., 35a sq.; of other passions, Plu.Lys.19; of t…

πλησιάζω.definition: Dor. Archyt. ap. Stob.1.41.2: pf; intr., abs., to be near, S.OT91: c. dat., draw near to, approach, X.Cyr.7.3.16, An.4.6.6.al. .304); Pl.Phd.97a; Amphis4; Pl.Smp.181d; enter on a career of public office, Thphr.Char.26…
