πλησίος.definition: Boeot. Rev.Ét.Gr.10.29; Adv. Aeol. Sapph.2.3, Supp.6.1; Dor. = near, hard by, c. gen., Il.3.115, cf. Od.14.14; Epich.101, cf. IG42.123.15 ; A.Pr.366; S.Tr.1076; Hdt.4.111; E.Hipp.1439; Id.Or.1159: c. dat., Id.IA1551; …

πλησιφαής.definition: with full light, of the moon, Ph.1.24, al., Man.1.208, Nonn.D.41.258, Epic. in Pap. ap. Kroll Analecta Graeca p.4, Eust.729.20:—also Theol.Ar.26

πλησιφωτέω.definition: to be waxing, of the moon, Anub. ap. Heph.Astr.2.5

πλήσμιος.definition: Hices. ap. Ath.7.298b, but Xenocr. ap. Orib.2.58.49:—filling, satisfying, Plu.Tim.6, cf. Philistion ap.Ath.3.115d, Ph.Bel.89.9, Hices.l.c., Xenocr. l.c., Dsc.5.8; of wine, Ath.1.32f; satiety, surfeit, Epicur.Fr.465, P…

πλησμονή.definition: a being filled, satiety, opp; abundance, LXXPr.3.10, Gp.1.10.8

πληστεύομαι.definition: to be full, gorged, opp. Eust.1382.64

πλινθεία.definition: brickmaking, LXXEx.1.14, al., J.AJ2.13.4; drawing up of an army in square, Suid.s.v

πλίνθευσις.definition: making of bricks, prob. in IG42.102.172

πλινθεύω.definition: make into bricks, Hdt.1.179; build of brick, Id.4.67

πλίνθινος.definition: made or built of brick; of clay, Thphr.HP5.9.8; Dicaearch.1.3

πλινθίον.definition: Dim. of small brick, Th.6.88; square of troops, Hell.Oxy.7.2, Plu.Crass.23, Arr.Tact.11.5, 29.8; J.AJ13.4.4

πλινθόομαι.definition: Med., build as with bricks, . . AP9.423

πλινθοφορέω.definition: carry bricks, Ar.Av.1149, IG22.1672.28, Polyaen.8.24.3, BGU699.6

πλινθοφόρος.definition: carrying bricks, Ar.Av.1134; name of a coin , Inscr.Délos461 Bb 49

πλοιαρίδιον.definition: = sq., POxy.602 , Ps.-Callisth.1.3, dub. in PGiss.11.6

πλοιάριον.definition: Dim. of skiff, boat; a kind of woman's shoe, Poll.7.93

πλοκαμίς.definition: poet. for sq., lock or braid of; = II, in pl., Opp.H.2.125, C.3.179

πλόκαμος.definition: lock or braid of hair, A.Ch.6,187; a constellation, Hsch., cf. Call.l.c.; Ptol.Tetr.26

πλόκανον.definition: plaited work, basket-work, Pl.Ti.78c; wicker fan for winnowing, Pl.Ti.52e, Poll.1.225

πλοκή.definition: twining, twisting, Epich.171; anything twisted or woven, web, E.IT817 , Pl.Lg.849c; mesh, PGiss.47.7

πλοκίζομαι.definition: Pass., have one's hair braided, Hp.Ep.15; Aristaenet.1.19:—Act., plait is prob. in PMag.Par.1.1336

πλόκιον.definition: Dim. of I, Phot; necklace or chain, IG22.1524.100, Plu.2.141d, Eun.VSp.455B.: title of play by Menander, Gell.2.23.6

πλόκιος.definition: twined, v.l. for Od.13.295; epith. of Orph.H.10.11

πλόκος.definition: lock of hair, braid, curl, A.Ch.197; wreath or chaplet, the parsley- wreath at the Isthmian games, Pi.O.13.33; E.El.778; Id.Med.841 ; ib.786

πλουδοκέω.definition: wait for a fair wind, Cic.Att.10.8.9

πλουτέω.definition: to be rich, wealthy, opp; c. gen. rei, to be rich in a thing, A.Fr.241; X.An.7.7.42; Arist.Pol.1257b13; . . IG12.442.8

πλουτίζω.definition: Att. fut. Timocl.4.8:— make wealthy, enrich, A.Ag.586, X.Cyr.8.2.22; Id.Mem.4.2.9; IGRom.3.199 : iron., A.Ag.1268:—Pass., S.OT30; X.Cyr.5.5.27; gain one's wealth from . . , Id.Mem.2.1.28, Vect.4.14

πλουτογαθής.definition: Dor. for delighting by or in riches, wealthy, A.Ch.801

πλουτοδοτήρ.definition: = sq., epith. of Apollo, AP9.525.17:—fem. of Demeter, Orph.H.40.3, cf. Fr.302, Luc.DMeretr.7.1

πλουτοδότης.definition: giver of riches, Hes.Op.126; Ph.1.232; Arch.Anz.45.147 ; epith. of Dionysus, Poet. ap.Sch.Ar.Ra.482; of Zeus, Orph.H.73.4; of Zeus-Helios-Sarapis, Not.Scav.1912.323; of Pluto, Luc.Tim.21:—in form epith. of Men, BCH23.389

πλουτοκρατέομαι.definition: Pass., to be in a state governed by the wealthy, Men.Rh.p.360S

πλουτοκρατία.definition: oligarchy of wealth, X.Mem.4.6.12, Men.Rh.p.359 S

πλουτοφόρος.definition: wealth-bringing, Archestr.Fr.45.5, Ael.NA12.43; Com.Adesp.8; of God, Ph.1.544

πλουτόχθων.definition: rich in treasures of the earth, in allusion to the silver mines of Laureion, A.Eu.947

πλυνός.definition: trough, tank, or pit, in which dirty; parox. washing, Suid.; Ostr.Bodl. i126 , cf. PHib. 1.114 : metaph., = II, Ar.Pl.1061; = Phryn.PSp.101 B

πλυντήριος.definition: of or for washing: , a festival at Athens , in which the clothes of Athena's statue were washed, IG12.842, X.HG1.4.12, Lycurg.Fr.44, Plu.Alc.34, Phot

πλυντηριών.definition: name of month at Thasos and elsewhere, BCH 50.214 , SIG987.10 , IG12.1010

πλύντης.definition: clothes-cleaner, Poll.7.37, rejected by EM785.35; cf

πλύντρια.definition: fem. of washerwoman, IG12.473, Poll.7.37; name of a Satyric drama by Sophocles and of a comedy by Philyllius

πλυντρίς.definition: a kind of fuller's earth, Menestor ap. Thphr.CP2.4.3, Nicoch.4

πλύντρον.definition: payment for cleaning clothes, Sammelb.7451.150 , PCair.Zen.176.252 , Poll.7.38

πλωΐζω.definition: sail on the sea, Hes.Op.634 ; began to use ships or practise navigation, Th.1.13:—Med., Sammelb.7332 , Str.17.1.6, Luc.Hist.Conscr.62: aor. inf. Pass. Just.Edict.13.6:—written in Sammelb.7169.20 , Plb.4.47.1, 5.88.7, …

πλώιμος.definition: or fit for sailing; of a ship, seaworthy, Th.1.29,50, 2.13, D.56.23, etc.; also, fit for ship-building, Plu.2.676a

πλωτεύομαι.definition: Pass., to be navigated, of the sea, Plb.16.29.11

πνευματίζω.definition: fan by blowing, in Pass., Antig.Mir.136; write or pronounce with the breathing, Eust.524.5, al

πνευμάτιον.definition: Dim. of a little breath or; flatulence, Damox.2.26

πνευματισμός.definition: use of the breathing, Eust.524.26, al

πνευματόμφαλος.definition: sufferer from umbilical hernia, supposed to be caused by wind, Gal.14.786:—also umbilical hernia, Id.19.445

πνευματοποιέω.definition: turn into air, vaporize; cause flatulence, Orib.Syn.9.43.8

πνευματόρροος.definition: contr. streaming with currents of air, Pl.Cra.410b

πνευματοφορέομαι.definition: Pass., to be borne as by the wind, LXXJe.2.24

πνευματοφόρος.definition: bearing the spirit, inspired, ib.Ho.9.7; ib.Ze.3.4

πνευματόφως.definition: epith. of a shining spirit, PMag.Par.1.593

πνευμάτωσις.definition: inflation, Dsc.1.8, cf. Gal.7.67; f.l. for Placit.5.8.2

πνευστιάω.definition: breathe hard, pant, Hp.Int.44, Sor.1.108; expld. by Arist.Rh.1357b21; Ep. AP11.382.4

πνιγῖτις.definition: a sort of clay, Dsc.5.157, Plin. HN35.194

πνίγω.definition: Sophr.68, al., Antipho4.1.6, Herod.4.31; impers. of great heat, it is stifling, Arist.Pr.941b4, 944a7

ποάριον.definition: Dim. of Thphr.HP3.3.6; in form ib.1.7.3, 9.10.2

ποάστρια.definition: weeder or grass-cutter, Archipp.44; title of comedies by Magnes and Phrynichus, cf. IG 22.2363.31

ποδάγρα.definition: trap for the feet, X.Cyr.1.6.28; foot disease of dogs, oxen, horses, Arist.HA604a5,14,23; gout, of human beings, IG42.122.133 , Dsc.1.104, Arr.Epict.3.22.40, Philostr.VA4.30: pl., Str.15.1.43

ποδαγράω.definition: have gout in the feet, Ar.Pl.559, Pl.Alc.2.139e; of a foot disease in oxen, Arist.HA575b8; in dogs, Ael.NA4.40

ποδαλγέω.definition: causal, produce gout, Ruf. ap. Orib.5.3.35

ποδαλγία.definition: gout in the feet, Ruf. ap. Orib.5.3.35, Poll.2.196, Lyd.Mens.4.8

ποδανιπτήρ.definition: vessel for washing the feet in, footpan, Stesich.30 , Hdt.2.172, Amips.2, Diocl.Com.1, IG12.313.137, 22.1425.393, 11.161B127 , CIG3071.8 , Plu.2.151d, etc.: is a later form, Ath.4.168f, Stesich.l.c

ποδάνιπτρον.definition: water for washing the feet in, mostly pl., Od.19.504; ib.343: sg., Ar.Fr.306; dub. in Com.Adesp.35 :—later Ph.2.472, J.AJ8.2.5

πόδαργος.definition: swift-footed, or acc. to others white- footed , Lyc.166: Swiftfoot or Whitefoot, a horse of Hector, also of Menelaus, Il.8.185, 23.295; fem. name of a Harpy, 16.150

ποδδατέομαι.definition: Dor. for assign, in aor. Tab.Heracl.2.54

ποδδέχομαι.definition: or in aor. part., Dor. for IG5.653a9

ποδεῖον.definition: sock or legging, puttee : in pl., CritiasFr.65D., Crates Com.34, IG22.1425.402, Thphr.HP7.13.8, etc.—On the accent, v. Theognost. l.c., Hsch.: written in Phot., codd. Thphr.l.c.; PCair.Zen.778.5

ποδεκμαγεῖον.definition: or cloth for wiping the feet, Gloss

ποδεών.definition: in pl., ragged ends in the; neck of the bladder, Poll.2.196, Phot

ποδηγετέω.definition: guide, Democr.173, cf. Lyc.12, Opp.C.4.360: abs., Ph.1.16, al.:—Pass., Id.2.442,421

ποδηγέω.definition: lead, guide, Pl.Lg.899a, Ep.340c, Lyc.965, Phleg.Fr.36.2 J.: abs., Ph.1.440, Muson.Fr.8p.37H.:—Pass., Clearch.9, D.C.63.9

ποδηνεκής.definition: reaching down to the foot, Il.10.24, cf. A.R.1.324, 4.180; Il.15.646; Hdt.1.195

ποδήνεμος.definition: wind-swift, epith. of Iris, Il.2.786, al. ; of a runner, B.l.c.: Com., Crates Com.29 , cf. Hsch

ποδιαῖος.definition: Math., side of one foot long, taken as the unit of length, Pl.Tht.147d, cf. Arist.Sens.446a6, Metaph.1052b33

πόδιον.definition: Dim. of Epich.57, Hp.Epid.7.52; foot of a vase, BGU781i15

ποδίς.definition: a kind of shoe. in pl., Poll.10.168

ποδιστήρ.definition: a foot-entangling robe; a kind of tripod, J.AJ8.3.7

ποδίστρα.definition: foot-trap, AP6.107 ; of a spider's web, ib.9.372

ποδοκάκκη.definition: stocks , Lex ap.Lys.10.16, Lex ap.D.24.105, Pl.Com.249, TheonProg.13, Sch.Ar.Eq.366

ποδοκτυπέω.definition: strike the earth with the feet, of dancers, Phot. s.v

ποδορραγής.definition: bursting forth at a stamp of the foot, of Pirene and Hippocrene, AP9.225

ποδοτρόχαλος.definition: one who turns a wheel with his foot, potler, Hsch

ποδοχέω.definition: guide a ship by means of the sheet , Antipho Soph.96, AB297.5 :—hence govern, is restd. by Dind.in A.Pers.656

ποδώκεια.definition: swiftness of foot, Il.2.792 , E.IT33, Plu.Rom.25:—written in A.Eu.37, X.Cyn.5.27 , Hld.8.16; Anacreont. 24.3

πόδωμα.definition: storage-charge for grain, PRyl.71 Intr. , PTeb.339.17 , etc

ποδώνυχος.definition: reaching to the toes , Poll.10.191, Hsch

ποηφαγέω.definition: eat grass or herbs, J.BJ2.8.8, al.:—written Hdt.3.25,100, Max. Tyr.29.4; Arist.HA593a15

ποηφάγος.definition: eating grass or herbs, opp. Hp.Vict.2.49, Arist.HA595a14, al.; Id.Fr.344, Max.Tyr.29.4; Arist.PA693a15

ποίημα.definition: anything made or done; work, Hdt.4.5, 7.84, cf. 2.135; Id.1.25; of the works of Daedalus, Pl.Men.97e; a lover's invention, Id.R.474e; product, of land formed by silting-up of rivers, Arr.An.5.6.4

ποιησείω.definition: Desiderat. of desire to do, Hdn.Epim.249

ποίησις.definition: fabrication, creation, production; of Poetry, Pherecr.145.10, Pl.Grg.502a, 502b, R.394c: abs., art of poetry, Hdt.2.82, cf. Ar.Ra.868, etc.; . . Id.Fr.254; i.e. tragedy and comedy, Pl.Tht.152e; Id.Phdr.245a; ib.278c

ποιητέος.definition: to be made or done, Hdt.1.191, 7.15; one must make or do, And.3.16, Onos.22.2, etc.:—from Med., one must deem, X.Mem.4.2.30

ποιητικεύομαι.definition: Pass., to be a poetic invention; Med., speak poetically, Eust.79.12, Sch.Arat.696, al

ποιήτρια.definition: fem. of Hld.2.8; poetess, Supp.Epigr.2.263 , cf. SIG532.4 , Str.17.1.33, Plu.2.300f, Luc.Musc.Enc.11, Ath.13.600f, etc.; par excellence, of Sappho, Gal.4.771

ποικιλάνιος.definition: Dor. for with broidered reins, Pi.P.2.8

ποικιλείμων.definition: gen. arrayed in spangled garb, in reference to the stars, A.Pr.24

ποικιλεύομαι.definition: to be versatile or artful, Vett.Val.4.9

ποίκιλμα.definition: broidered stuff, brocade; embroidery, Il.6.294; with various ornaments, X.Oec.9.2; . . Pl.Euthphr.6c; Id.Hp.Ma.298a; of the stars in heaven, Id.R.529c; CritiasFr.25.34D

ποικιλόβουλος.definition: of changeful counsel, wily, Hes.Th.521; APl.4.300.5; Orph.H.28.3

ποικιλόγηρυς.definition: Dor. of varied voice, many-toned, Pi.O.3.8

ποικιλόδιφρος.definition: with chariot richly dight, Orac. ap. Poll.7.112

ποικιλόθριξ.definition: gen. spotted, dappled, E.Alc.584 ; of birds, v.l. in Lyr.Adesp.94

ποικιλομήτης.definition: voc. full of various wiles, epith. of Odysseus, Il.11.482, Od.3.163, 13.293; of Zeus, h.Ap.322; of Hermes, h.Merc.155

ποικιλομήχανος.definition: full of various devices, Epigr. ap. Clidem.24

ποικιλόμορφος.definition: variegated, Ar.Pl.530; of many shapes, of Fortune, Lyr.Alex.Adesp.34.1

ποικιλόμυθος.definition: of various discourse, AP5.55 ; epith. of Cronus, Orph.H.13.5; of Hermes, ib.28.8

ποικιλόνωτος.definition: with back of various hues, Pi.P.4.249; E.IT1241 ; Id.HF376

ποικιλόπτερος.definition: with wings of changeful hue, Id.Hipp.1270 : metaph., Pratin.Lyr.1.5

ποικιλόστολος.definition: of a ship, with variegated prow, S.Ph.343

ποικιλοφόρμιγξ.definition: accompanied by the various notes of the lyre, Pi.O.4.3

ποικιλόφωνος.definition: with varied tones, Nonn.D.2.510; Tz.ad Hes.Op.201; Sch.Pi.O.3.11: metaph., = Clearch.26

ποικιλόχειρος.definition: with changeful hands, of Fortune, prob. in Lyr.Alex.Adesp.34.1

ποικιλτής.definition: broiderer, pattern-weaver, Aeschin.1.97, Arist.Mete.375a27, LXXEx.28.6, BGU34 ii 24 , Chor.in Hermes 17.226, etc.:—fem. Str.17.1.36

ποίμνη.definition: flock, Od.9.122; prop. of sheep; metaph. of persons, A.Supp.642 , Eu.197; of mankind, Pl.Plt.267c

ποιμνήϊος.definition: Ep. Adj. of a flock or herd, Il.2.470, Hes.Op.787

ποίμνιον.definition: = esp. of sheep, Hdt.2.2, 3.65; metaph. of disciples, Ev.Luc.12.32, al.; 1 Ep.Pet.5.2

ποιναῖος.definition: punishing, avenging, Keil-Premerstein Erster Bericht p.9 ; AP5.253.6 ; Aristaenet.1.10; Lyd.Mag.3.16

ποινάομαι.definition: Med., avenge oneself on one, . . E.IT1433

ποινηλασία.definition: pursuit by the furies, madness, Lyd.Ost.28

ποινηλατέω.definition: pursue like an avenging fury, S.E.M.11.117:—Pass., to be so pursued, Id.P.1.27, 3.237, Heph.Astr.3.8 .151), Eun.Hist.p.248 D., Herm.in Phdr.p.111A

ποινίζομαι.definition: Arc. aor. 1 inf. exact a penalty, IG5.261.14

ποινίς.definition: perh. = , Theognost.Can.23; cf. in if from

ποινοστροβέομαι.definition: Pass., to be routed, of an army, BCH55.85

ποιολογέω.definition: put up corn in sheaves, Theoc.3.32

ποιολόγος.definition: picking up grass or herbs, Arist.Fr.351

ποιόω.definition: make of a certain quality, Thphr.CP2.1.5:—Pass., to be endowed with quality, Stoic.2.220, S.E.M.1.108; Plot.1.1.11, cf. 4.3.26; Sor.1.95

ποίφυγμα.definition: blowing, snorting, A.Th.281, cf. Epic. in Arch.Pap.7.6

ποιφύσσω.definition: trans., blow up, Lyc.198; puff out, AP7.215

ποιωτίζομαι.definition: Pass., to be endowed with quality, Antyll. ap. Orib.10.2.1

ποκάριον.definition: Dim. of Sch.Theoc.15.18, Hippiatr.26: pl., Sammelb. 7247.21

ποκοειδής.definition: like undressed wool: rough, crude, Longin.15.5

ποκόομαι.definition: Pass., to be covered or clothed with down, AP6.102

πολεμάρχειος.definition: of or belonging to the polemarch, Polem.Hist.58; his residence, X.HG5.4.6, Plb.4.79.5; IG12 .279

πολεμαρχέω.definition: to be polemarch, Hdt.6.109, cf. Cratin.458 , X.HG5.2.25; Boeot. IG7.4127 , etc

πολεμαρχία.definition: office of polemarch, Polem.Cyn.18, Vett. Val.213.1, al

πολεμέω.definition: Ion. Iterat. Acus.22J.: fut; fight, do battle, Pl.Prt.350a; X.Cyr.7.1.49; but what our means of war are, And.3.16

πολεμήϊος.definition: Ep., Ion., and Lyr. Adj.warlike, freq. in Hom. , Il.2.338, al.; 7.193, Hes.Sc.238; = v.l. in Hdt.5.111; war-note, of the trumpet, B.17.4

πολεμητόκος.definition: bringing forth war, Nonn.D.4.425, etc.; of Athena, Orph.H.32.10

πολέμιος.definition: more freq. of or like an enemy, hostile, Pi.P.1.80; Id.N.4.55; A.Th.588; ib.216, etc.; S.Ph.1302; ib.1323; hostile to one, Hdt.1.4, E.Hec.1138; Hp.Art.11

πολεμιστής.definition: war-horse, charger, D.S.2.41 , Str.15.1.29, Plu.Fab.20; are prob. racehorses trapped as chargers, Theoc.15.51, cf. IG22.2316.29, SIG697 H3 , Phot. s.v

πολεμογράφος.definition: describing wars, of an historian, IG 42.687

πολεμοκέλαδος.definition: exulting in the din of war, Lyr.Adesp.108

πολεμόκλονος.definition: raising the din of war, Batr.4; ib.275, Orph.H.32.2

πολεμοποιέω.definition: c. acc., make war on, Hp.Ep.17

πολεμόω.definition: make hostile, make an enemy of, v.l. in LXX4 Ma.4.21:—Med., surely you will make them your enemies, Th.5.98:—Pass., to be made an enemy of, Id.1.36; . . ib.57: —in other passages it is doubtful whether the word should…

πολέω.definition: intr., go about, range over, haunt, A.Pers.307; E.Alc.29 ; Id.Or.1270 :—Med., A.Pr.645 , cf. Ar.Av.181: abs., Lex.Sol. ap. Lys.10.19

πολιά.definition: greyness of hair, Men.Mon.705; as a disease, Arist.GA784b13, Pr.894b9, Fr.235; LXX4 Ma.7.15, cf. Plu.2.4ib, Chor.p.15B., al.; AP5.219 : concrete, Chor. in Lib.4.516R

πολιαίνομαι.definition: Pass., grow white, of the foaming sea, A.Pers.109

πολιανομέω.definition: hold office of Pl.Ep.363c; at Rome, to be aedile, D.C.43.48

πολιανόμος.definition: a civic magistrate; = Lat. aedilis, D.C.43.28,48

πολιαρχέω.definition: to be praefectus urbi, D.C.53.33, Malch.p.410 D., Lyd.Mag.3.38

πολίαρχος.definition: ruler of a city, prince; = Lat. praefectus urbi, D.C.40.46, al., Lyd.Mag.1.49 : as Adj., ib.2.19; Thess. IG9.1233

πολιάτας.definition: Aeol. and Dor. for opp. Alc.Supp.14.6, Id.Oxy.1233 Fr.22.3, Pi.I.1.51, Leg.Gort.10.35, Isyll.21

πολιήτης.definition: Ep. and Ion. for citizen, Il.2.806 , Simon.137, twice in Trag., A.Pers.556, E.El.119 ; constantly in Hdt. :—fellow-citizen, countryman, ib.37,120, al., cf. A.R.1.867: as Adj., sands on my country's shore, E.Hipp.1126

πολιορκέω.definition: fut. X.Cyr.7.5.12:aor; metaph., Porph.Chr.28:—Pass., to be besieged, pestered, Pl.Alc.2.142a, cf. R.453a, X.Mem.2.1.13, UPZ6.33 ; of a banker, PCair.Zen.624 : in Medicine, to be blocked, Dsc.5.6.13

πολιορκητής.definition: taker of cities, surname of Demetrius son of Antigonus, Phld.Hom.p.55 O., D.S.20.92, Plu.Demetr.42, Arist.6 , etc

πολιοφυλακέω.definition: of an army, keep within the city, opp. taking the field, Plb.18.39.4

πολιόω.definition: turn grey, Dsc.1.30, Eup.1.94:—mostly in Pass., to be or become grey, Arist.GA780b4, cf. Gal.12.441; Arist.HA518a16, cf. Plu.Fr.inc.149; of things, J.AJ10.11.7

πόλισμα.definition: buildings of a city, town, sts. = sts. difft. from it; of Ecbatana, Hdt.1.98; ib.57, cf. 6.6; of Thebes, A.Th.63, al.; of Troy, S.Ph.1424; of Athens, Id.OC1496 , cf. Ar.Av.553, 1565; Men.Sam.110: pl., Call.Aet. Oxy.20…

πολισμάτιον.definition: Dim.of foreg., Ephor.27 J., Plb.1.24.12, Str.6.3.9, J.AJ15.9.6, Plu.Them.26

πολισμός.definition: building of a city, D.H.1.57,59; Lyd.Mag.1.2

πολιτάρχης.definition: civic magistrate, at Thessalonica, Act.Ap.17.6; at Lete, SIG700.2 ; in Egypt, POxy.745.4 :—also Aen.Tact.26.12

πολιτεία.definition: Ion. condition and rights of; the daily life of a citizen, And.2.10, D.19.184; Id.20.122; life, living, Plb.18.43.6; so perh. Ep.Eph.2.12

πολίτευμα.definition: business of government, act of; the concrete of III, the government, Arist.Pol.1278b11, cf. 1279a26, 1283b31, etc.; the citizens, ib.1303b26, cf. 1305b34; Aeschin.2.172; Plb.5.9.9, cf. 4.25.7 ; Id.1.13.12, D.H.1.41; f…

πολιτεύω.definition: have a certain form of government, administer the state, Th.1.19, 3.62; Id.4.130; Id.2.65; X.HG1.4.13; Th.2.37:—Pass., of the state, to be governed, Isoc.6.35, cf. Pl.R.427a, etc.; X.Mem.4.4.16; the measures of their …

πολιτικοπραιτώριος.definition: in accordance with jus civile and praetorian law, PMasp. 151.44

πολιτογραφέω.definition: enrol as a citizen, D.S.11.49, Philisc.Com.5: abs., act as registrar, OGI547.4 :—Pass., to be admitted to citizenship, ib.229.54 , cf. Plb.32.7.3, Phld.Acad.Ind.p.35 M., D.S.11.72,86; IG9 .517.41

πολιτοκάπηλος.definition: jobber in public offices, Malch. ap. Suid. s.v

πολιτοφύλαξ.definition: warden of the citizens, title of a magistrate, Arist.Pol.1268a22; at Larissa, ib.1305b29

πολλαπλασιασμός.definition: multiplication, Plu.2.388c, Gal.7.509, Procl.in Euc.p.151 F

πολλαπλασιεπιμερής.definition: containing a number a number of times with more than one aliquot part over , and containing a number a number of times with one aliquot part over , Nicom.Ar.1.23

πολλαπλασιότης.definition: the being a multiple, Theol.Ar.52, Iamb.in Nic.p.38 P.,al

πολλαπλασίων.definition: gen. = Num.Chron.1905.114 , Plb.35.4.4, Plu.2.215b: c. gen., Phld.Sign.9. Adv. Poll.4.164

πολλοστημόριος.definition: a number of times smaller, opp. Arist.Top.147a26, Metaph.1020b28; Id.Pol.1308b2; fraction, Id.Top.125a9; Luc.DDeor.1.1, cf. Phld.Mus.p.110 K

πολογραφία.definition: Ion. description of the heavens, title of a treatise by Democritus, Hp.Ep.18, D.L.9.48

πολτάριον.definition: Dim. of little porridge, poor bad porridge, Dsc.2.92, Philum. ap. Orib.45.29.3

πολτοποιέω.definition: make into porridge, Orib.Fr.75:—Pass., to be made into porridge, Dsc.2.106

πολυάγκιστρος.definition: with many hooks, Opp.H.3.78; night-line, Arist.HA532b25, 621a16

πολυαδελφία.definition: possession of many brothers, Sch.Ptol. Tetr.102:—also Cat.Cod.Astr.6.70

πολυάδελφος.definition: with many brothers, Vett. Val.16.29, Poll.6.171, Paul.Al.L.3, Sch.S.Ant.1

πολύαθλος.definition: of many labours, epith. of Heracles, Luc.DDeor.10.1

πολυαιμέω.definition: to have much blood, Arist.PA648a30, GA765b18

πολύαιμος.definition: full of blood, of a full habit, Hp.Flat.14, Arist.HA515a20, 520b27 ; Id.PA669a27

πολυαίνετος.definition: = sq., E.Heracl.761 , BCH29.412 :—also IG42.616.5 ; to be restored in BCH21.599

πολύαινος.definition: much-praised, Homeric epith. of Odysseus, Il.9.673, 10.544, 11.430, Od.12.184; but expld. alternatively by Hsch. as =

πολύαμμος.definition: abounding in sand, sandy, Hsch. s.v

πολυάμπελος.definition: with many vines, B.7 , Sch. D Il.2.507, etc

πολυανάλωτος.definition: prodigal, Vett. Val.48.25; causing much expense, very expensive, gloss on EM750.47

πολυαναφορία.definition: Astrol., slowness in rising, Sch.Ptol. Tetr.118

πολυανάφορος.definition: Astrol., slow in rising, Vett. Val.227.12, Sch.Ptol.Tetr.118

πολυανδρεῖον.definition: common burial-place, IG22.1035.33, al., Favorin. in PVat.11.8.20; SIG826 E iii32 ; cf. II.2

πολυανδρέω.definition: to be full of men, to be populous, Th.6.17, cf. Str.8.7.1, Sammelb.7462.7 :—Med., D.S.8.1, Ocell.4.4, Ael.NA5.13

πολυάνδριος.definition: of or connected with many men; Subst. place where many people assemble, Plu.2.823e

πολύανδρος.definition: of places, full of men, populous; of persons, many, numerous, A.Pers.533 , cf. Ag.693 ; Tim.Pers.194; Onos.21.5; much experience of men, Vett. Val.172.25

πολυάνθεμος.definition: rich in flowers, Sapph.Supp.25.11; Anacr.65.3; Pi.O.13.17: in later Prose, Plu.2.294f

πολυανθής.definition: blooming, Od.14.353; h.Hom.19.17; Mosch.2.59, cf. Opp.C.1.320, al.: in later Prose, Gp.15.4.4; parti-coloured, D.S.31.8, cf.5.30: poet. fem. Nic.Th.877

πολυανθρωπέω.definition: to be populous, J.AJ1.4.1 , St.Byz. s.v

πολυανθρωπία.definition: large population, multitude of people, X.HG5.2.16, Vect.4.49, Arist.Pol.1326b20, D.S.1.73, etc

πολυάνθρωπος.definition: populous, Hp.Art.72, Th.6.3; much-frequented, crowded, Luc.Peregr.1

πολυάργυρος.definition: rich in silver, of persons or places, of the Lydians, Hdt.5.49, cf. Ph.2.30; D.S.5.36; Plu.Comp.Lys.Sull.3

πολυάριθμος.definition: numerous, manifold, Callicrat. ap. Stob.4.28.16; D.S.14.25

πολυαρμόνιος.definition: capable of being played upon in many modes, Pl.R.399d

πολυαρχία.definition: command or government shared by many, Th.6.72, cf. X.An.6.1.18, J.AJ4.8.41, Plu.Cam.18, etc

πολυάρχιος.definition: invented by the physician Polyarchus, Sor.2.32, Gal.13.184

πολυαχθής.definition: very grievous, Q.S.3.421; Id.10.38, cf. Sch.Nic.Al.322

πολυβαφής.definition: much-dipped, of drowned men, A.Pers.275 , but v

πολύβιβλος.definition: in many books, Ath.6.249a; Gal.1.409, cf. IGRom. 4.1655

πολυβλαβής.definition: very hurtful, EM1.22, Sch.A.R.2.232; Pass., easily hurt, Plu.2.1090b

πολυβλαστής.definition: shooting vigorously, Thphr.CP3.7.4, v.l. for ib.3.19.2

πολυβόειος.definition: covered with many oxhides: Ep. fem. Q.S.3.239

πολυβόητος.definition: much-talked-of, gloss on Sch.A.Supp.532; much-sounding, gloss on Sch.E.Alc.918

πολυβόρος.definition: much-devouring, voracious, Pl.Criti.115a ; opp. Hp.Aër.4; Gal.UP4.18

πολυβότειρα.definition: fem. Adj., much- or all- nourishing, in Ep. form epith. of Il.3.89, al.; of 11.770

πολύβοτος.definition: much-nourishing; having much pasture, Tim.Pers.153; D.H.1.37

πολύβοτρυς.definition: abounding in grapes, of places, Hes.Fr.122, Simon.53, Theoc.25.11; E.Ba.651

πολυβούτης.definition: rich in oxen, . . Il.9.154, Hes.Fr.134.3:—also in form Carm.Naupact.2

πολύβροχος.definition: freshly infused several times, Dsc.1.128.6, al; with many nooses, E.HF1035

πολύβυρσος.definition: of many hides or skins, gloss on Sch.A.R.3.1231

πολύβωτος.definition: prob. from many-feeding, ferlile, as ironical epith. of the barren island of Seriphos, Cratin.211

πολυγάλακτος.definition: with much milk, Arist.PA688b3: poet. Sup. AP9.224

πολυγαμία.definition: polygamy, Ph.1.568; frequent marriage, Vett. Val.119.22

πολύγαμος.definition: often-married, or, living in polygamy, Poll.3.48, Ptol.Tetr.183

πολυγέλως.definition: gen. pl. f.l. for in Plu.2.552a

πολυγενής.definition: of many families, Poll.9.21; PMich. in Class.Phil.22.9

πολυγηθής.definition: Dor. much- cheering, delightful, gladsome, Il.21.450; Hes.Th.941, Op.614, cf. Pi.Fr.29.5; Id.P.2.28; AP9.189, etc.: also voc. Orph.H.10.10

πολύγληνος.definition: many-eyed, Nonn.D.3.272, AP5.261; with many meshes, Opp.C.1.157

πολύγλωσσος.definition: Att. many-tongued; speaking many tongues or languages, Lyc.1377, Luc.JTr.13, Gal.8.585; Tryph.24

πολύγναμπτος.definition: much-bent, much-twisting, Pi.O.3.27; AP9.191; Q.S.1.286; curly, Theoc.7.68

πολυγνώμων.definition: gen. very sagacious, Pl.Phdr.275a, D.C.76.16 ; sententious, Philostr.VS1.16.4. Adv. Poll.4.23

πολύγομφος.definition: with many nails, well-riveted, Hes.Op.660, cf. Ibyc.Oxy.1790.1.18, A.Pers.71

πολυγόνατος.definition: having many joints, Dsc.1.14, al; Subst. sealwort, Polygonatum multiflorum, Id.4.6

πολύγονος.definition: producing much offspring, prolific; of the Nile, much-producing, fertilizing, Id.Fr.159 , D.S.1.10:—Ep. Opp.C.3.519

πολυγράμματος.definition: marked with many letters, =; of words, composed of many letters, Phld.Po.Herc.994.32, al

πολυγραφέω.definition: write much or at length, Ath.Mech.4.9, Apollon.Cit.3

πολυγραφία.definition: writing much, D.L.10.26, dub. in Phld.Rh.1.143S

πολυγράφος.definition: writing much, Id.Ind.Sto.32, Ath. Mech.6.2: Sup. Cic. Att.13.18, D.L.10.26

πολυγύμναστος.definition: of much experience, of a woman, Luc.Tox.14

πολύγωνος.definition: polygonal, Id.Sens.442b20, Plu.2.1121c: Subst. polygon, Antipho Soph.13, Gal.Anim.Pass.2.3

πολυδαίδαλος.definition: highly, richly wrought, chiefly of; Act., working with great art or skill, very skilful, Il.23.743, APl.4.80

πολύδακρυς.definition: of or with many; of persons, much-weeping, Id.Ph.366, Supp.Epigr.4.719

πολυδάπανος.definition: causing great expense or; of a person, expensive, extravagant, Id.Ap.19, Vett. Val.90.15. Adv. D.S.1.52, Plot.1.4.7; at great expense, IGRom. 4.1241, 1242, 1273, JHS37.108

πολυδέγμων.definition: gen. containing or; like a name of Hades, h.Cer.17.31, prob. in Orph.H.18.11, cf. Fr.49iv64,v69

πολυδειράς.definition: with many ridges, Il.1.499,5.754; many-necked, Q.S.6.212

πολύδενδρος.definition: abounding in trees, of a country, Str.17.3.4: heterocl. dat. pl. E.Ba.560

πολύδερμος.definition: = EM395.56 (v.l; with several layers, of the abdominal wall, Gal.8.952

πολύδεσμος.definition: fastened with many bonds, strong- bound, Od.5.33, v.l. ib.338

πολυδίψιος.definition: very thirsty, of ill-watered countries, Il.4.171, Q.S.3.570. , much-destroyed.)

πολύδιψος.definition: making very thirsty, Xenocr. ap. Orib.2.58.91

πολύδοξος.definition: having various opinions, Stob.2.7.4a; famous, BCH21.599 , Timo44; IG14.2124

πολυδύναμος.definition: with many powers or faculties; powerful, Eust.916.21

πολυεθνής.definition: many-peopled: numerous, Oenom. ap. Eus.PE5.29, Orph.H.78.11, A.430

πολυειδής.definition: of many kinds or forms; name of a lozenge, Aët.12.64 bis

πολύειδος.definition: name of various plants, e.g; Adj. = I, Zos.Alch.p.113 B

πολυέλικτος.definition: much convoluted, Gal.2.572; the pleasure of the mazy dance, E.Ph.314 ; Ep. Nonn.D.21.185

πολύεργος.definition: hardworking, Nic.Th.4, cf; Pass., highly-wrought, elaborate, Ph.1.665

πολυέταιρος.definition: with many fellows or comrades, Poll.3.62

πολυετής.definition: after many years; lasting many years, OGI383.22 ; Ph.2.364, 1.677; Luc.Merc.Cond.17; Sor.1.33; full of years, LXXWi.4.16; old, Hld.10.25; Dsc.2.76; keeping for many years, of a remedy, Aët.9.24

πολυετία.definition: length of years, Ph.1.393, al., Gal.6.357, D.L.1.72, D.C.66.18

πολύευκτος.definition: much-prayed-for, much-desired; Act., with many prayers, Nonn.D.40.66

πολύζηλος.definition: full of emulation, S.OT381; much admired, B.10.63; S.Tr.185

πολυζήλωτος.definition: much admired or revered, B.7.10, al.; E.Hipp.168 , cf.IG4.491.3 , Hymn.Is.16

πολυζωέω.definition: to be full of life, of Isis, IGRom.1.1310

πολυηγόρος.definition: much-speaking, Philisc. ap. Plu.2.836c, cf. Orph.A.489

πολυήκοος.definition: having heard much, much- learned, Pl.Lg.810e; Id.Phdr.275a

πολυήμερος.definition: lasting many days; full of days, aged, LXXDe.25.15, al

πολυήρατος.definition: much-loved, very lovely; of persons, Hes.Fr.192.1; Plu.2.767f; of Caracalla, Opp.C.1.2

πολυηχής.definition: many-toned, of the nightingale's voice, Od.19.521; AP9.504; much or loud-sounding, Il.4.422; A.R.4.609,963

πολύηχος.definition: = Ph.1.373, Sch.S.Aj.695: metaph., Ph.1.372; noisy, Epict.Gnom.1. Adv. Ael.NA12.28

πολυθαμβής.definition: much frighted or astonished, ib.418, al

πολυθεάμων.definition: gen. having seen much, c. gen., Pl.Phdr.251a

πολύθερμος.definition: very hot, Plu.Alex.4, cf. Heliod. ap. Orib.49.8.11, Gal.17.201, Theo Sm.p.187 H

πολύθηρος.definition: with much game, full of wild beasts; mighty huntress, epith. of Id.Hipp.145

πολυθρέμμων.definition: gen. feeding many, epith. of the Nile, A.Pers.33 ; Orph.H.51.13

πολυθρήνητος.definition: lamentable, AP7.334.15, cf. IG12.445.6 ; gloss on Sch.S.Tr.848

πολυθρόνιος.definition: = Androm. ap.Gal.14.32: is f.l. in Nic.Th.875

πολυθύσανος.definition: with many tassels, epith. of Artemis, Poet. ap. Hsch. , rushing violently)

πολύθυτος.definition: abounding in sacrifices, Pi.P.5.77, N.7.47; S.Tr.756; E.IA185 ; Id.Heracl.777

πολυϊδρεία.definition: much knowledge or wisdom, in pl., Od.2.346, cf. 23.77 ; Thgn.703 codd.: later in sg., Call.Aet.3.1.8

πολύϊδρις.definition: Ion. gen. Att. of much knowledge, wisdom, Od.15.459, 23.82, Hes.Th.616, Alc.Supp.7.7, Ar.Eq.1068 ; Arist.HA616b24, etc.; dat. Sapph.166

πολύϊππος.definition: rich in horses, Il.13.171, D.P.308, Tryph.171

πολυϊστορία.definition: great learning, erudition, prob. in Phld.Rh.1.143 S

πολυΐστωρ.definition: very learned, D.H.Din.1, Str.3.2.12, Gal.17.605; esp. as epith. of Alexander Polyhistor, J.AJ1.15.1, etc.; AP9.280 :—also Sch.Lyc.5

πολυκαισαρίη.definition: a plurality of Caesars, formed after Arius ap. Plu.Ant.81

πολυκάλαμος.definition: of or with many stalks, Thphr.HP8.9.2, cf. CP4.11.3; D.S.3.58

πολυκαμπής.definition: with many curves, Thphr.Sens.65, CP6.10.3, AP6.297 , etc.; Plu.2.649b; of a zigzag route, ib.615c: metaph. of music, with many flourishes, Phrynis ap.Poll.4.66

πολυκανής.definition: much-slaughtering, with slaughter of many beasts, A.Ag.1169

πολυκαρπία.definition: abundance of fruit, IG12.76.45, X.Mem.3.14.3, Thphr.CP4.8.1, Sammelb.6944.14 , Sm.Ps.64.10

πολύκενος.definition: containing much void, porous, Arist.Pr.940a4; Epicur.Ep.2p.37U.; Id.Nat.2.9, cf. Dsc.5.108, Plu.2.721c, Gal.9.181

πολυκέντητος.definition: gloss on Hsch., Suid., cf. EM506.49, Eust.425.24

πολυκέρδεια.definition: great craft, Od.23.77,24.167; is v.l. in Adam.Phgn.2.37

πολυκερδής.definition: very crafty or wily, Od.13.255; shrewd in business, money-making, Man.1.132, Polem.Phgn.8; gainful, Opp.H.2.15

πολυκέφαλος.definition: many-headed, Pl.R.588c; Id.Sph.240c, cf. Arist.GA769b27; of plants, interpol. in Dsc.2.152; LXX4 Ma.7.14; a celebrated air on the flute, so called from its expressing the hissing of the serpents round the Gorgon's hea…

πολυκηδής.definition: full of care, grievous, Od.9.37,23.351; Plu.Nob.2 ; Q.S.8.31; of persons, A.R.4.734, cf. Q.S.10.310

πολυκίνδυνος.definition: very dangerous, Isoc.10.17 as; conversant with danger, TeucerinCat.Cod. Astr.7.198

πολυκίνητος.definition: full of movement, Plu.2.681a, cf. Gal.UP16.6; restless, Id.8.131; Iamb.Myst.3.2; Arist.Mu.400b9

πολύκλαυστος.definition: Act., much-lamenting, Emp.62; Mosch.3.73; IG14.607; swollen with tears, Arat.360; causing much lamentation, Q.S.10.141

πολυκλήϊς.definition: with many benches of rowers, in Hom. always in dat., as epith. of ships, Il.7.88, Od.20.382; Il.2.74, cf. 175, al.; Hes.Op.817

πολύκληρος.definition: with a large portion of land, exceeding rich, Od.14.211, Theoc.16.83

πολύκλητος.definition: called from many a land, of the allies of the Trojans, Il.4.438,10.420

πολύκλινος.definition: with many couches or seats, Hld.5.18

πολύκλυστος.definition: much-dashing, stormy; Pass., washed by many a wave, Hes.Th.199; A.R.1.597

πολύκλωνος.definition: with many branches, Thphr.HP6.2.6 , Dsc.3.33; = 4, Ps.-Dsc.3.113: neut. name of a plant, Gp.12.1.2

πολύκμητος.definition: wrought with much toil, Hom; later, laborious, AP9.656.6; Q.S.7.424

πολύκνημος.definition: with many mountain-spurs; field basil, Zizyphora capitata, Hp.Mul.1.65, Nic.Th.559,Al.57, Dsc.3.94

πολύκοινος.definition: common to many or to all; promiscuous in sexual relations, Ptol.Tetr.172, Cat.Cod.Astr.8.176

πολυκοιρανία.definition: Ep. rule of many; rule over many, Rhian.1.10

πολυκοιτέω.definition: lie with many women or men, Vett.Val.118.5

πολύκοιτος.definition: lying with many women or men, Id.75.9, al

πολύκολπος.definition: with many sinus, Gal.2.890; of a fistula, Heliod. ap. Orib.44.23.68

πολύκρημνος.definition: with many steeps or mountains, B.1.11, cf. Call.Fr.477

πολύκριθος.definition: abounding in barley, B.10.70, cf. Euph.51.14, Suid. s.v

πολυκρότητος.definition: much struck or beaten, Hsch. s.v

πολύκροτος.definition: also , ringing loud or; sly, cunning, wily, v.l. in Od.1.1, cf. Hes.Fr.94.22, Anacr.90.2

πολύκρουνος.definition: with many springs, fountains many-gushing, AP9.669.4 ; with many mouths, Aristid.Or.17.22

πολυκτήμων.definition: gen. with many possessions, exceeding rich, Il.5.613, S.Ant.842 : in later Prose, Eus. Mynd.59, Alex.Aphr.in Top.147.14: c. gen., E.Ion581

πολύκτηνος.definition: rich in cattle, Alex.Polyh. ap. Eus.PE9.25

πολύκτητος.definition: of large possessions, wealthy, E.Andr.769 , v.l. in Sch.S.El.508

πολυκυλίνδητος.definition: much or often rolled, Eust.1471.7, Hsch

πολυκύματος.definition: swelling with many waves, Hsch.s.v. , EM545.15

πολυκύμων.definition: bringing forth much, gloss on Sch.A.Ag.119

πολυλάλητος.definition: often repeated, of a common epithet, Eust.861.33

πολύλαλος.definition: talkative, Cleobul. ap. Stob.3.1.172; Plot.6.2.21, cf. Sm.Jb.11.2, Sch.Ar.Nu.1363, Sch.S.Ant.324

πολυλήϊος.definition: with many cornfields, Il.5.613, Hes.Fr.134.1; prob. in B.9.34; fruitful, Arat.1058

πολυλίμενος.definition: with many ports, Artem. ap. Eust.287.34

πολύλιμος.definition: ravenous hunger, coined as etym. of prob. in Plu.2.694a

πολύλλιστος.definition: also Orph.H.32.14, al.: :— sought with many prayers, Od.5.445; temples much frequented by suppliants, h.Ap.347, cf. h.Cer.28; B.10.41: later in act. sense, Procl.H.7.51 :—also Simon.45, cf.IG3.171 iii 12

πολυλογέω.definition: talk much, Gal.18.792, Vett.Val.175.31, al., Poll.10.51, Alex.Aphr.in Top.433.19

πολυλογία.definition: loquacity, much to say, Pl.Lg.641e, X.Cyr.1.4.3, Arist.Pol.1295a2, LXXPr.10.19, etc

πολύλογος.definition: loquacious, Democr.44, Pl.Lg.641e, X.Cyr.1.4.3 . Adv. Poll.4.24

πολυμάθεια.definition: = , Arist.Fr.62, Str.1.1.1, Ph.1.652, Luc.Salt.37: as pr. n. of a Muse at Sicyon, Plu.2.746e

πολυμαθής.definition: having learnt or knowing much, Ar.V.1175, Democr.64, Pl.Lg.811a: Comp. Aristeas137: Sup. Phld.Vit.p.35J.; Ath.9.398e, cf. Dam.Isid.168, Lyd.Mag.1.5

πολυμανής.definition: Ep. troubled by manifold madness, AP12.87

πολυμάντευτος.definition: on which many oracles are given, Plu.2.292f

πολυμάσχαλος.definition: with many side- branches, Thphr.HP3.8.4, 3.10.2, cf. 3.12.3

πολυμέδιμνος.definition: with many medimni, epith. of Demeter, Call.Cer.2

πολυμέλαθρος.definition: Ep. with many halls or temples, Call.Dian.225

πολυμελής.definition: with many members; many-toned, in form Alcm.1. Adv. Poll.4.57

πολυμέρεια.definition: a consisting of many parts, Ph.1.506, Placit.5.26.4, Porph.Sent.34

πολυμερής.definition: consisting of many parts; of divers kinds, Arist.Pol.1311a33. Adv. in many ways, Ep.Hebr.1.1, Plu.2.537d, Ptol.Tetr.127

πολυμέριμνος.definition: full of care, Arist.Mu.400b10, cf. Vett. Val.2.2,al

πολύμεσος.definition: having several means, of contraries, Olymp.in Cat.137.31, Eliasin Cat.243.31

πολυμετάβολος.definition: very changeable, Lyd.Mens.2.7, cf. Vett.Val.9.2, Procl.in Alc.p.301, Tim.Lex

πολυμετρία.definition: use of a variety of metres, Eust.353.42

πολύμετρος.definition: of many measures: hence, copious; written in many metres, Ath.13.608e

πολύμητις.definition: of many counsels, of Odysseus, Il.1.311, Od.21.274, Ar.V.351; of Hephaestus, Il.21.355; Orph.A.126

πολυμηχανία.definition: Ion. resourcefulness, inventiveness, Od.23.321, Plu.2.233e: pl., Man.6.483

πολυμήχανος.definition: resourceful, inventive, epith. of Odysseus, Il.2.173, etc., cf. S.Ph.1135 ; of Apollo, h.Merc.319; of Nature, Orph.H.10.1; Opp.H.2.54: in later Prose, Aristid.Or.41.2

πολυμιγία.definition: mixture of many components, Plu.2.661e; confusion, Ph.1.426

πολυμίγματος.definition: = Androm. ap. Gal.14.131, Gal.14.283, al., Paul.Aeg.3.48

πολύμισθος.definition: receiving much pay or hire, v.l. in AP5.1

πολυμιταρική.definition: art of weaving Hsch., Suid. s.v

πολύμιτος.definition: consisting of many threads, Cratin.436; damask stuffs, in which several threads were taken for the woof in order to weave in patterns, Plin.HN8.196; damask robes, A.Supp.432 ; Sammelb. 7033.37

πολυμνήμων.definition: gen. remembering many things, Plu.2.292a, Gal.17.605

πολύμνιος.definition: full of moss, v.l. in Nic.Th.950

πολύμορφος.definition: multiform, manifold, Hp.Aër.12; of persons, versatile, Ph.2.47; Id.1.565

πολύμουσος.definition: rich in the Muses' gifts, Plu.2.744a; many-sided in art, Luc.Salt.7

πολύμοχθος.definition: much-labouring, suffering many things; Pass., won by much toil, toilsome, Arist.Fr.675.1; IG3.1374; wrought with much toil, Theoc.28.8

πολύμυθος.definition: poet. Call.Iamb.1.170; Pass., much talked of, famous in story, Pi.P.9.76

πολύμυξος.definition: with many wicks, of a lamp, Mart.14.41 tit

πολύμυχος.definition: with many recesses, gloss on Sch.Call.Del.65

πολύναος.definition: with many temples, Theoc.15.109; Ion. EM32.9

πολυναύτης.definition: Dor. with many sailors or ships, A.Pers.83

πολυνεικής.definition: much-wrangling, Id.Th.830 : freq. as pr. n. on which the Trag. are fond of playing, ib.578,658, al

πολυνέφελος.definition: overcast with clouds, EM7.10; Dor. epith. of Pi.N.3.10

πολύνοια.definition: Ion. thoughtfulness, opp. Pl.Lg.641e, cf. Aristid.Or.50.26, D.C.52.41, Dam.Isid.37; opp. Democr.65

πολύνοος.definition: contr. thoughtful, opp. Plot.6.2.21, cf. Porph.Plot.14; profound, Hierocl.in CA26p.480M., cf. Iamb.in Nic.p.5 P. Adv. Poll.2.230

πολύνοσος.definition: liable to many sicknesses, Str.15.1.43, Cat.Cod.Astr.2.208

πολύνοστος.definition: making much return; of food, very nutritious, Hp.Vict.2.56 : Comp., of seed, producing fuller grain, Thphr.HP8.8.2

πολύξενος.definition: Ion. poet. also; visited by many guests, Pi.O.1.93 , N.3.2; Id.Fr.122.1; E.Alc.569 ; cf. sq

πολυόδους.definition: Ep. with many teeth, Nic.Th.53, Nonn.D.24.253, al

πολυοινέω.definition: to be rich in wine, h.Merc.91

πολυοινία.definition: abundance of wine, Gp.4.1.14, etc; excess in wine, Pl.Lg.666b, Ph.1.351, Plu.2.239a

πολύοινος.definition: rich in wine, of a place, Th.1.138 , Lib.Ep.19.8; of men, X.Vect.5.3

πολύοκνος.definition: delaying much, very tardy, JRS17.52 , Sch.S.Tr.841

πολύολβος.definition: very wealthy, of persons and countries; Act., rich in blessings, Sapph.59, cf. Afric.Cest.28; of the Sun, Epigr.Gr.361

πολύομβρος.definition: very rainy, Cat.Cod.Astr.4.87; gloss on Sch.Nic.Al.288

πολυόμφαλος.definition: with many bosses or shields, of the Roman testudo, Opp.C.1.218

πολυορκία.definition: habit or custom of swearing, Ph.2.196, 271

πολυόστεος.definition: with many bones: =; of fruits, with many seeds, Cat.Cod.Astr.8.251

πολυόφθαλμος.definition: many-eyed, D.S.1.11, Poll.4.141; with many eyes or buds, Gp.5.8.1

πολυοχλέω.definition: to be numerous, D.H.6.64, cf. 5.6:—Pass., to be much-peopled, of a city, Str.8.6.20, D.S.14.95, Timae.inCat.Cod.Astr.1.99, prob. in Ceb.15

πολυοχλία.definition: crowd of people, Plb.10.14.15, LXXJb.39.7; Inscr.Perg.252.22

πολύοχλος.definition: much-peopled, populous; very prolific, Arist.Pol.1291b23; for E.Rh.166 v

πολυοψία.definition: abundance or variety of meats or fish, X.Mem.3.14.3, Plu.2.662a

πολύοψος.definition: abounding in fish, Str.12.3.38; luxurious, Luc.Gall.11

πολυπάθεια.definition: suffering of many calamities; receiving of diverse impressions or sensations, formed after Plu.2.167e, 734a

πολυπαθής.definition: subject to many passions or impressions, Democr.149; Plu.2.97b; full of diverse reactions, ib.171e; poet. much perturbed, AP9.98

πολυπαίγμων.definition: gen. very sportive, v.l. in Od.23.134, so cited by Sch.Ar.Th.954

πολυπαιδία.definition: abundance of children, fecundity, Isoc.9.72, App.BC1.7, Hierocl.in CA24p.472 M., Chor.Proc.6

πολύπαις.definition: with many children, Str.17.3.19, LXX4 Ma.16.10; of swans, Ael.VH1.14: metaph., of Tyre, mother of many colonies, AP7.428.14

πολυπαρθένευτος.definition: having been long a maid, Sch.E.Ph.1732

πολυπάταξ.definition: full of tumult, found in acc., Pratin.Lyr.1.2; dat. Choerob.in Theod.1.377 H., prob. in EM280.1

πολυπάτητος.definition: much trodden, Sch.Call.Jov.26: metaph., common-place, threadbare, Plu.2.514c

πολύπατρις.definition: having more than one country, Eust.4.20

πολυπειρία.definition: great experience, Th.1.71, Pl.Lg.811a, LXXWi.8.8, D.S.5.1, Plu.Sol.2

πολύπειρος.definition: much-experienced, Parm.1.34, Ar.Lys.1109, LXXSi.21.22, D.S.1.1 , Sor.1.4; Epigr.Gr.202 . Adv. Sch.Theoc.15.48

πολυπενθής.definition: much-mourning, Il.9.563, cf. Od.14.386; 23.15; of events, very lamentable, A.Pers.547 : Sup. Plu.2.114f

πολυπευθής.definition: much-inquiring, a day on which many persons consult the oracle, Plu.2.292f

πολυπήμων.definition: gen. causing manifold woe; Pass., much-suffering, Man.1.85,4.49

πολυπῖδαξ.definition: with many springs, many- fountained, Il.8.47, 14.283, etc.; ib.157, 20.59, 218 ; A.R.3.883

πολύπικρος.definition: very keen or bitter: neut. pl. as Adv., Od.16.255: regul.Adv. Eust.1801.35

πολυπλανής.definition: roaming far or long; much-erring , AP9.134; Musae.175. metri gr. in Opp.C.4.358.]

πολυπλάνητος.definition: = foreg., of the; of blows, falling in every direction, A.Ch.425

πολύπλανος.definition: = Id.Pr.585 ; E.Ph.661 , cf.AP6.69 : in late Prose, Paul.Al.M.3

πολυπλασιάζω.definition: later form for multiply, LXXDe.8.1 , Gal.10.352, Hdn.8.2.4 , Jul.Or.4.139a , Them.Or.21.261a; Phlp.in Mete.15.10; Ael.Tact.8.2

πολυπλασιασμός.definition: multiplication, v.l. in Plu.2.388c, 1020c, cf. Aenesidem. ap.S.E.M.10.217; in tactical sense, deepening, Arr.Tact.9.4

πολυπλάσιος.definition: = AP6.152 , LXX2 Ma.9.16, Alex.Aphr.de An.123.33, Them.Or.6.74c

πολυπλασίων.definition: gen. = Isoc.15.177 codd., SIG711 L11 , Them.Or.15.186b

πολύπλεθρος.definition: many in size, far-stretching, E.Alc.687; of persons, rich in land, Luc.lcar.18

πολυπλήθεια.definition: Ion. great quantity or number, Hp.Aër.15, cf. Aen.Tact.3.1; Arist.HA562b29, cf. Ocell.4.5, Aen.Gaz.Thphr.p.47 B., SIG880.40 , etc.:—written S.Fr.667.1 , Hyp.Fr.266 D., ap. Poll.4.163, LXX2 Ma.8.16, Str.16.2.23

πολυπληθέω.definition: multiply, LXXEx.5.5; abound in feet, ib.Le.11.42

πολυπλόκαμος.definition: with many feelers, of the poulp, Marc.Sid.36

πολύπλοκος.definition: tangled, E.Med.481; metaph., tangled, complex, Pl.Phdr.230a; X.Lac.11.5; Simm.26.20; E.IA197 . Adv. D.H.Th.54: neut. as Adv., cj. in Thphr.Sign.40

πολυπόδειος.definition: of a poulp, Poll.6.33,47; , Theopomp.Com.6 , Philyll.13, Mnesim.4.43 , etc

πολυπόδιον.definition: Dim. of f.l. in; polypody, Polypodium vulgare, Thphr.HP9.13.6, Dsc.4.186, etc

πολυπόθητος.definition: much longed-for, as expl. of Str.8.6.7, Ath.10.433e; ibid

πολυποίκιλος.definition: much-variegated, E.IT1149; manifold, Ep.Eph.3.10; Anon.Incred.17; Orph.H.6.11

πολύπολις.definition: Ion. poet. with many cities, Call.Dian.225; a congeries of cities, Ph.2.541

πολύπονος.definition: of men, much-labouring, much-; of things, painful, toilsome, A.Pers.320; S.Ph.777; Id.El.515 ; E.Or.1011 ; Hp.Aff.23; Pl.Lg.633b; E.Hel.199 . Adv. Plu.Alex.63, Phalar.Ep.34

πολυπόταμος.definition: with many or large rivers, E.HF410

πολυποτέω.definition: drink hard, drink much wine, Hp.Prorrh.2.2

πολυπότης.definition: hard drinker, Hp.Aër.4, Ath.10.442f, Cass.Pr.48; poet. AP9.524.17:—fem. Ael.VH2.41

πολύποτμος.definition: of many fates or fortunes, Orph.H.70.9

πολυπραγμονέω.definition: mostly in bad sense, to be a meddlesome, inquisitive busybody, Ar.Pl.913, etc.; Pl.R.433a: c.acc., Democr.80; interfere, IG5.1208.24

πολυπραγμοσύνη.definition: curiosity, officiousness; later, search after knowledge, Plb.5.75.6.—Cf

πολυπράγμων.definition: gen. busy about many; later and rarely in good sense, curious after knowledge, Plb.9.1.4; D.S.1.37, cf. Antig.Mir.24

πολύπρεμνος.definition: with many trunks, A.R.4.161; prob. in Coluth.195

πολυπρόβατος.definition: rich in sheep or cattle, Hdt.5.49 , cf.X.Vect.5.3

πολυπρόσωπος.definition: many-faced, multiform, the; of many persons, J.BJ1.28.4. Adv. of conspirators, Id.AJ16.3.3

πολυπτόητος.definition: poet. timorous, Plu.2.44c, etc.; AP5.289 ; much- agitated, ib.7.624 , cf. Nonn.D.27.189,al

πολύπτυχος.definition: of or with many folds; folded many times, with many leaves, Luc.Am.44; Poll.4.18

πολύπτωτος.definition: with or in many cases, a rhetorical figure, employment of the same word in various cases, Hermog.Id.1.12, Eust.349.39; Id.105.26; alone, Quint.Inst.9.3.37, Longin.23.1

πολύπυρος.definition: rich in corn, epith. of fruitful lands, Il.11.756, 15.372, Od.14.335,al., A.Supp.555 , AP6.258 , Dsc.1.127; Hymn.Is.2

πολυρραγής.definition: epith. of a river, either with many branches, or violent, Nic.Th.59

πολυρραίστης.definition: slayer of many, Opp.H.1.463, v.l. for in Lyc.210

πολυρρήμων.definition: gen. much-speaking, wordy, M.Ant.3.5; LXXJb.8.2; Max.Tyr.31.1

πολύρρηνος.definition: = foreg., of a person, Od.11.257; of a country, A.Eleg.3; Q.S.2.331

πολύρριζος.definition: with many roots, Id.HP9.10.2, Epigr; bearing many i.e. fertile in herbs. Str.5.3.6,15.1.22

πολυρρόθιος.definition: much-dashing, loud-roaring, Q.S.7.395; buffeted by many waves, Arat.412

πολύρροθος.definition: = foreg., the cries of many voices, A.Th.7

πολύρροιζος.definition: with a loud rushing noise, Q.S.1.156; f.l. for Nic.Th.792

πολύρρομβος.definition: with many turns, of a bandage, Sor.Fasc.23,57

πολύσαρκος.definition: very fleshy, Arist.HA583a7, PA656a19; metaph., very stupid, Them.Or.23.288c

πολυσήμαντος.definition: with many significations, Heliod.in EN86.8; Lyd.Mag.2.2; title of work by Orus, Reitzenstein Gesch.d.Gr.Etym.p.336

πολυσημάντωρ.definition: giving commands to many, ruling over many, h.Cer.84, 376, cf. 31

πολυσθενής.definition: of great might, Epic.Alex.Adesp.9 ii 11, cf. Luc.Trag.192, Q.S.2.205, al

πολυσιτία.definition: abundance of corn or food, X.HG5.2.16; much eating, Luc.Par.16

πολύσιτος.definition: rich in corn, of persons, X.Vect.5.3; high-fed, full of meat, Theoc.21.40

πολύσκαρθμος.definition: much-springing, bounding, Il.2.814; or , driving swift horses, but Nic.Th.350; Q.S.5.657

πολύσκιος.definition: very shady, Hp.Aff.60, A.R.4.166, Jo.Gaz.Ecphr.2.289, interpol. in Dsc.1.126

πολυσκύλαξ.definition: with many dogs, in gen. pl. of many dogs' heads, Nonn.D.18.246

πολύσπαστος.definition: drawn by many cords: compound pulley, HeroBel.84.11, Ath.Mech.33.3, Plu.Marc.14, Gal.18.747

πολυσπερής.definition: wide-spread, spread over the; fruitful, Emp.74

πολύσπερμος.definition: abounding in seed, Arist.GA725b29; abounding in seminal fluid, Gal.1.339

πολύσπορος.definition: with many crops, fruitful, E.Tr.748; = II, Ptol.Tetr.72, Cat.Cod.Astr.7.212

πολυστάδιος.definition: many stades long, Eudem. ap. Simp.in Ph.974.5

πολυστάφυλος.definition: rich in grapes, of places, Il.2.507, S.Ant.1133 ; also h.Hom.26.11; Hecat.15J

πολύστεγος.definition: with many ceilings or stories, Id.16.2.23; cj. in Ph.Byz.Mir.5.2

πολυστένακτος.definition: causing many groans, Luc.Trag.2; full of groaning, AP7.155

πολυστέφανος.definition: with many wreaths or crowns; Subst., = Feronia, Gloss

πολυστεφής.definition: decked with many wreaths, A.Eu.39; twisted in many a wreath, Nic.Th.378; of a serpent , ib.490

πολύστιος.definition: with many small stones, pebbly, Call.Jov.26; Nic.Th.950, Al.466

πολύστιχος.definition: = sq., Str.17.1.28; of many lines or verses, Ammon.in Int.134.22, Paul.Aeg.Praef

πολύστοιχος.definition: in many rows, Arist.HA505a29; Thphr.HP8.4.2 ; jaws set with many rows of teeth, Lyc.414

πολύστομος.definition: many-mouthed, Hp.Oss.13; of a; uttered by many mouths, Nonn.D.26.275

πολύστονος.definition: much-sighing, mournful, of persons; noisy, f.l. for foreg. in Nic.Th.175; . . Q.S.14.644

πολύστρεπτος.definition: much-twisted, v.l. for in Nic.Al.224, cf. Orph.A.1096, etc.; Lyd.Mens.4.159

πολυστροφία.definition: poet. complication, variety of melody, AP7.198

πολύστυλος.definition: with many columns, Str.15.1.21, 17.1.28; of the Odeum, Plu.Per.13

πολυσύγκρατος.definition: mixed up of many things, Hsch. s.v

πολυσύγκριτος.definition: compounded of many things, Id. s.v

πολυσύνδεσμος.definition: using many conjunctions or connecting particles, Sch.Th.2.41

πολυσύνδετος.definition: = foreg., versus Serv.Dan.ad Verg.A.11.634; Diom.p.447 K., cf. Donat.ad Ter.Ad.301

πολυσύνθετος.definition: much-compounded, Plot.5.9.3; of; the union of clauses by many particles, Rutil.1.14

πολυσφαιρία.definition: multiplication of spheres, Theo Sm.p.201 H

πολυσφράγιστος.definition: Ion. with many seals, well-secured, Nonn.D.4.14

πολυσχημάτιστος.definition: multiform, Poll.5.170; of verses, composed of various metres, Sch.Ar.Eq.322, etc.; Heph.10.4

πολυσχημοσύνη.definition: use of a variety of forms, Eust.1463.27

πολυσχήμων.definition: gen. onos, of many shapes, varied in form, Placit.1.14.4, Poll.6.171, Artem.1.2: Sup. Str.2.5.18. Adv. Poll.4.98

πολυσχιδής.definition: split into many parts; much-cloven, opp. of certain figs, Arist.Pr.930b33; of a deer's antlers, branching, Id.HA517a24, cf. PA663a10; of the lungs, Id.HA495b1; of leaves, Thphr.HP3.12.5; Dsc.2.185; of a mountain range…

πολυσχιδία.definition: Ion. a splitting into many parts: manifold division, Hp.Acut.3; diversity, Id.Praec.13

πολύσχιστος.definition: split into many parts, branching, S.OC1592

πολύσχοινος.definition: of many cords, of a net, Marc.Sid.92

πολυσώματος.definition: with many bodies, D.S.1.26, cf. Plu.2.427b, Poll.2.235; composed of many corpuscules, Placit.3.3.4 , cf. Gal.19.482

πολύσωρος.definition: rich in heaps of corn, of Demeter, AP6.258

πολυτάλαντος.definition: worth many talents; possessing many talents, Luc.Tox.14, cf. Poll.9.54

πολυτάραχος.definition: tumultuous, Sch.D Il.1.34, Hsch. s.v. Erot. s.v

πολυτειρής.definition: wearying much, Q.S.4.120,5.314; rich in stars, Arat.604

πολυτεκνέω.definition: have many children, Arist.Pol.1272a24, Ephor.216 J

πολύτεκνος.definition: bearing many children, prolific; consisting in many children, Nonn.D.25.561

πολυτέλεια.definition: Ion. great expense; costliness, X.Lac.7.3, etc

πολυτελής.definition: very expensive, costly, opp; of persons, lavish, extravagant, coupled with Men.615; Id.325.7; Id.824; Antiph.80.5. Adv. Eup.335, Lys.7.31, X.Mem.3.11.4: Sup., in the costliest manner, Hdt.2.87

πολυτεχνία.definition: skill in many arts, Pl.Alc.2.147a, Aristeas51, v.l. in D.S.1.64: in pl., Perict. ap. Stob.4.28.19

πολύτεχνος.definition: skilled in many arts; the work of many craftsmen, D.Chr.78.24

πολυτιμητίζω.definition: esteem highly, Numen. ap. Eus.PE14.5, Hsch.:— Pass., to be addressed as Com.Adesp.1120

πολυτίμητος.definition: at a high price, very costly, Epich.71, Ar.Fr.387.9, Alex.Trall.1.15; with play on signf. I, Ar.Ach.759

πολύτιμος.definition: much-revered, Men.109.1; highly priced, Hp.Nat.Puer.13; very costly, AP5.35.5 , Babr.57.9. Adv. Plb.14.2.3

πολύτλας.definition: much-enduring, epith. of Odysseus, Hom. and S. only in nom., Il.8.97, al.; ironically, S.Aj.956 ; gen. Eust.700.32; acc. Antisth.Od.14 codd., Man.5.268

πολυτλήμων.definition: much-enduring, Il.7.152; of Odysseus, Od.18.319; Ar.Pax236

πολύτλητος.definition: having borne much, miserable, Od.11.38, cf. Orph.Fr.354, Q.S.1.135, al.; also Id.11.25; Id.2.341

πολύτμητος.definition: much-cut, lacerated; Act., cutting much or deeply, of sharp pain, Id.H.5.288

πολυτοκέω.definition: to be prolific, Arist.HA558b20, GA750a27, Thphr.CP1.22.1

πολυτόκος.definition: bearing more than one child; bringing forth many children or young ones, prolific, Arist.PA688a34, GA749b31 , Porph.Abst.4.14

πολυτράχηλος.definition: with large or stubborn neck, Heraclit.All.17 codd

πολύτρητος.definition: poet. much-pierced, full of holes, porous, Od.1.111, 22.439; Cratin.213; Dsc.2.182; of the flute, AP9.266 , 505.5; ib.6.101 ; of honeycombs, ib.9.363.15 ; Luc.Epigr.12; of the lungs, Aret.SD1.10; Str.12.8.16

πολύτριπτος.definition: rubbed very fine, Nic.Th.104; much-trodden, frequented, Opp.H.3.502

πολύτριχος.definition: very hairy, bushy; = Dsc.4.134, Sammelb.7350.8 , Phot. s.h.v., AB343

πολυτροπία.definition: Ion. versatility, craft; multifariousness, variety, Hp.Acut.3 , D.H.Amm.2.3, Corn.ND25, M.Ant.12.24

πολύτροπος.definition: much-turned, i.e. much-; turning many ways: metaph., shifty, versatile, wily, of Hermes, h.Merc.13,439; Pl.Plt.291b; and in this sense Plato took the word as applied to Odysseus, Hp.Mi.364e , al.; their versatility of…

πολύτροφος.definition: well-fed, plump, Thphr.CP4.3.5; parox. Act., supplying food, Call.Cer.2; Mém. Miss.Arch.Perse20.90

πολύυλος.definition: abounding in forests, Gloss; abounding in materials, Poll.6.171; plethoric, Antyll. ap. Orib.9.13.2, cf. Heliod. ib.46.20.7

πολυύμνητος.definition: much-famed in song, Pi.N.2.5, M.Ant.7.6, Chor.inJahrb.9.187

πολύυμνος.definition: abounding in songs, much sung of, famous, of Dionysus, E.Ion1074 , cf. h.Hom.26.7; Anacr.159; Ar.Eq.1328; Tim.Pers.244

πολυφαγία.definition: excess in eating, Arist.GA768b29, Ph.1.686, Plu.2.624a, Iamb.Protr.2

πολυφάγος.definition: Ion. eating to excess, Hp.Vict.2.49, Arist.Fr.520

πολυφάρμακος.definition: knowing many drugs or charms; given to the use of drugs, Gal.10.169

πολυφάσματος.definition: of many appearances, multiform, Orac. ap. Lyd.Mens.3.10

πολύφατος.definition: much spoken of, famous, Pi.P.11.47; excellent, noble strain, Id.O.1.8, cf. N.7.81

πολύφημος.definition: Dor. abounding in songs; many-voiced, wordy, Od.2.150; to bring it forth to the many-voiced, i.e. the agora , Orac. ap. Hdt.5.79

πολυφήτωρ.definition: = foreg. II, as gloss on Sch.Il.9.404

πολυφθερής.definition: subject to many forms of destruction, Emp.113

πολύφθογγος.definition: of many notes, Plu.2.827a, cf. 973c, Ael.NA5.51

πολύφθοος.definition: epith. of a day at Delphi, on which the oracle was much consulted, Plu.2.292f

πολυφθόρος.definition: destroying many, fraught with death or; proparox. Pass., utterly destroyed or ruined, S.Tr.477, El.10

πολυφιλία.definition: abundance of friends, Arist.Rh.1360b20, Pol.1284a20, al.; . . ib.1293a31, cf. Lib.Or.25.59

πολύφιλος.definition: having many friends, dear to many, Pi.P.5.4, Lys.8.7, Arist.EN1170b23, Rh.1372a13, Him.Or.8.6

πολύφιλτρος.definition: suffering from many love-charms, love-sick, Theoc.23.1

πολυφλέγματος.definition: having much phlegm, Ptol.Tetr.151, Antyll. ap. Orib.6.8.3

πολύφλοιος.definition: with much or thick bark, Hsch.s.v

πολύφλοισβος.definition: loud-roaring, Il.1.34, Hes.Op.648, Archil.9.3, Diph.126.4, etc.; confused dissertation, Olymp.Alch.p.92 B

πολύφορβος.definition: also Il.9.568, Hes.Th.912: :—feeding many, bountiful, Il.14.200,301; Hes.l.c

πολυφόρητος.definition: bearing much, Phot. and Suid.s.v; carried about, well-known, An.Ox.3.187

πολυφραδέω.definition: to be very eloquent or wise, only in part. = sq., Hes.Fr.197

πολυφραδής.definition: very eloquent or wise; much talked of, famous, IG14.2012 A 26

πολύφραστος.definition: = very wise, Parm.1.4; so shrewd, Opp.C.4.6; Nonn.D.4.275

πολυφρόντιστος.definition: thoughtful, AP7.84; very anxious, Sch. S.Tr.109, Suid.s.v. Adv. IG22.1042b21

πολυφροσύνη.definition: fullness of understanding, great shrewdness, Democr.40: pl., Thgn.712

πολύφυλλος.definition: with many leaves, thick-leaved, of the yew, Eup.14.3, cf. Thphr.HP1.10.8, etc

πολύφυλος.definition: consisting of many tribes, Orph.H.62.3; epith. of Egypt, Timo12

πολυφωνέω.definition: sound or speak much, gloss on Eust.751.11

πολυφωνία.definition: variety of tones, Plu.2.1141c, cf. 674f; D.S.2.56; variety of speech, J.AJ1.4.3

πολύφωνος.definition: having many tones; having many voices, Plu.2.411e; loquacious, talkative, ib.715a, cf. Luc.Hist.Conscr.4

πολύχαλκος.definition: abounding in copper or bronze; wrought of bronze, brazen, 5.504, Od.3.2; Parm.1.18

πολυχανδής.definition: wide-yawning, capacious, Orph.Fr.56; Stud.Ital. 2.398 ; Theoc.13.46; Nic.Th.951; Nonn.D.11.162; Q.S.1.527; Tryph.535: in late Prose, Them.Or.23.299c

πολυχαρής.definition: feeling or causing much joy, An.Ox.3.138, Hsch. s.v. graceful, Phld.Lib.p.26 O

πολυχειρία.definition: multitude of hands, i.e. workmen or; possession of many hands, Polem.Cyn.43

πολυχίτων.definition: having many coats, Thphr.CP3.21.2, 5.18.2, etc.; of the eyes, Hp.Ep.23

πολυχορδία.definition: the use of many strings in the lyre, Pl.R.399c, Phan.Hist.17, etc.: pl., Plu.2.661d

πολύχορδος.definition: many-stringed, Theoc.16.45; many-toned, of the flute, Simon.46, cf. Pl.R.399d ; E.Med.196 ; the sound of many strings, Id.Rh.548 : metaph., Plu.2.827b

πολύχορτος.definition: with much grass, gloss on Eust.743.30

πολυχρηματέω.definition: abound in money, prob. in Str.9.2.40

πολυχρηματία.definition: greatness of wealth, opp. X.Smp.4.42, cf. Poll.3.110

πολυχρηματίας.definition: man of great wealth, v.l. in D.L.6.28

πολυχρήματος.definition: very wealthy, Str.16.4.22, al., Eus.Mynd.17; characteristic of wealth, Phint. ap. Stob.4.23.61a

πολύχρηστος.definition: useful for many purposes, very useful, Arist.GA789b9, Pol.1337b26, Dsc.1.1, Gal.6.534, 480 ; Corn.ND9: Comp., Muson.Fr.20p.112H., Alex.Aphr.in Top.277.4. Adv. v.l. in Paul.Aeg.7.16

πολύχροια.definition: variety of colour, Arist.Pr.963b37, Ael.NA in epilogo

πολυχρονίζω.definition: fut. prolong, LXXDe.4.26: abs., live long, Ptol.Tetr.132

πολυχρόνιος.definition: of olden time, ancient, h.Merc.125; of long standing, Sammelb.6026

πολυχρονιότης.definition: long duration, Phld.Herc.1251.4, Ptol.Tetr.10, etc.; longevity, Phld.Sign.17, Sch.Ar.Av.604; keeping quality, Thphr.Od.19

πολύχροος.definition: contr. many- coloured, variegated, Emp.23.3, cf. Arist.Pr.963b37, Opp.C.1.348; Arist.HA492a5: poet. Opp.C.4.389

πολύχρυσος.definition: rich in gold, of persons, cities; as epith. of Aphrodite, = Hes.Op.521, Fr.143.3, h.Ven.1

πολύχυλος.definition: with much juice, Ath.Med. ap; = I.2, Dsc.1.26, 5.96

πολύχυτος.definition: capable of great diffusion, Orib.Syn.2.56.77; widely diffused, Plu.Cat.Mi.25; Id.2.423a, etc

πολυχώρητος.definition: capacious, spacious, PMag.Par.1.2828, cf. Sch.Theoc.13.46; of large area, Sophon.in de An.9.17 : Comp., of larger area or of greater cubic content, Simp.in Cael.414.15, in Ph.291.18: Sup., Damian.Opt.3

πολυψηφία.definition: number or diversity of votes, Th.3.10, Ph.2.567

πολυψήφις.definition: with many pebbles, pebbly, of river-beds or the sea-shore, Orac. ap. Hdt.1.55; Naumach. ap. Stob.4.31c.76: Ep. Opp.C.1.292

πολύψηφος.definition: = foreg., Sch.Call.Jov.26; with many votes, Luc.Harm.3

πολυώδυνος.definition: Pass., suffering great pain or distress, APl.4.111 ; AP11.386

πολυωνυμία.definition: poet. multitude of names, Democr.26, Call.Dian.7

πολυώνυμος.definition: poet. Mém. Miss. Arch; of divinities, worshipped under many names, h.Cer.18, B.Epigr.1.1, S.Ant.1115 , Ar.Th.320 , Theoc.15.109; Arist.Mu.401a12; Secund.Sent.3

πολυώνυχος.definition: with many claws, of birds, Arist.HA504a5; dividing the hoof, Id.Pr.895a38

πολυωρέω.definition: treat with much care, c. gen., Supp.Epigr.2.257.12 , PCair.Zen.38.23 , D.L.6.9: Dor. aor. IG4.497.8 : later c.acc., having observed her carefully, D.S.18.65; PCair.Zen.462.10 : abs., Test. ap. Aeschin.1.50, Corn.ND1; …

πολυωρία.definition: care, attention, consideration, Chrysipp. Stoic.3.187, Delph.3.88 , PCair.Zen.527 , etc

πολύωρος.definition: many years old, Dius ap. Stob.4.21.17

πολυώροφος.definition: of many roofs or stories, Eust.640.1:— written in Str.16.2.13

πολυωφελής.definition: very useful, Arist.EN1095a11, D.H.1.36, etc.: Comp., SIG1164 : Sup., Ael.NA Praef. Adv. Ar.Th.304: Sup. X.Eq.Mag.1.1

πομπαῖος.definition: escorting, conducting, a; epith. of Hermes, who escorted the souls of the dead to the nether world, A.Eu.91, S.Aj.832, E.Med.759 , D.L.8.31

πομπευτήριος.definition: of or for a procession, D.H.Dem.32

πομπευτής.definition: = 2, Id.7.72: as Adj; organizer or marshal of a procession, Luc.Nec.16

πομπίλος.definition: a fish which follows ships, Gasterosteus ductor L., Erinn.1, A.R.Fr.9, et alii ap. Ath.7.282e, al

πόμπιμος.definition: also E.Hipp.578 , Ph.1711; Pass., sent, conveyed, to one, S.Tr.872, cf. E.Hipp.578

πομποστολέω.definition: conduct a procession, IG2.1325; c. acc., lead or carry in procession, Str.14.2.23; Luc.Am.11

πομφολυγίζω.definition: bubble up like boiling water, Dsc.1.68.4, 5.74, Simp.in Ph.460.22

πομφολυγόω.definition: cause to bubble or boil, Arist.Pr.931b34:—Pass., form bubbles, Herod.Med. in Rh.Mus.58.76, Dsc.5.126

πομφολύζω.definition: or bubble or boil up, tears gushed forth, Pi.P.4.121

πονήρευμα.definition: Medic., in sg., bad state or condition, Gal.19.138

πονηρεύομαι.definition: to be in a bad state, Hp.Coac.194; act wickedly, play the knave, Heraclit.125a, Arist.Rh.1411a17, Men.Epit.133; D.19.32, cf. Phld.Rh.1.43 S., Plu.Cat.Ma.9, etc.: c. dat., towards or against . . , Thd.Su.61: with Preps…

πονηρία.definition: bad state or condition; in moral sense, wickedness, vice, knavery, . . S.Fr.925, cf. Ar.Th.868, Lys.22.16; turns again to vice, X.Cyr.7.5.75: in pl., knavish tricks, rogueries, D.21.19, Arist.Rh.1389a18

πονηροκρατέομαι.definition: Pass., to be governed by the III, Arist.Pol.1294a2, D.H.8.31

πονηρόπολις.definition: Roguetown, a nickname given to some place by Philip, Theopomp.Hist.107, Plu.2.520b

πόνησις.definition: toil, exertion, D.L.6.70: pl., f.l. in CritiasFr.25.30

Ποντάρχης.definition: president of the provincial council; epith. of Achilles at Olbia, IPE12.134, al

ποντιάς.definition: poet. fem. of Pi.N.4.36; i.e. the Isthmus, Id.I.4.20; E.Hec.444 ; Crates Com.29

ποντίζω.definition: plunge or sink in the sea, A.Ag.1013 :—Pass., S.El.508

πόντιος.definition: of sponges or fragments of such, Trag.Adesp.258; in the sea, of islands, Pi.N.8.18; esp. of those far out to sea, opp. Arist.Mete.368b33, cf. Thphr.HP4.6.2,8.6.6; of ships, A.Pers.553 ; E.IA253

ποντόβροχος.definition: drowned in the sea, LXX3 Ma.6.4, Phot

ποντογενής.definition: seaborn, Orph.H.55.2, 81.1:—fem. poet. formed like Opp.C.1.33

ποντοθήρης.definition: one who fishes in the sea, AP6.193

ποντομέδων.definition: lord of the sea, of Poseidon, Pi.O.6.103, A.Th.131 , E.Hipp.743 , Ar.V.1532, IG12.706; Hes. in PMich.11.17; of Priapus, AP10.16 :—heterocl. gen., Orac. ap. St.Byz.s.v

ποντοπαγής.definition: fixed, founded on the sea, Nonn.D.41.15

ποντοπόρος.definition: seafaring, of ships, Il.1.439, 2.771, Od.12.69, S.Ph.721 , Aj.250 ; Hom.Epigr.8.1, cf. Opp.C.1.120; Mosch.2.49

ποντοχάρυβδις.definition: seagulf, whirlpool, Com. epith. for a glutton, Hippon.85.1 . cf

πόπανον.definition: round cake, used at sacrifices, Ar.Th.285, al., cf. Pl.R.455c, Arist.Fr.489, IG2.1651, Men.129.4, PCair.Zen.569.86 , Dieuch. ap. Orib.4.7.32, Porph.Abst.2.16; cj. in Thphr.Char.16.10

ποππύζω.definition: onomatop. word, smack the lips or cluck: hence, I. call to horses, etc., Ar.Pl.732, cf. D.S.1.83:-Med., call to a horse, S.Fr.878: com., call to a man, Timocl.21.7; Thphr.Char.20.5; title of play by Alexis; . . Ar.V.6…

πόππυσμα.definition: smacking of lips, clucking, Dexipp.in Cat.11.27: Lat.poppysma, Juv.6.584

ποππυσμός.definition: = foreg., X.Eq.9.10, Plu.2.713b , Poll.1.210, v.l. in D.H.Comp.14; Nicom.Harm.6, cf. PMag.Leid.W.1.37; of applause, Plu.2.545c : Lat. poppysmus, of the sound made on seeing lightning, Plin. HN28.25 ; . . PMag.Leid.W.2.1

πορεία.definition: mode of walking or running, gait; journey, A.Pr.823, al.; Pl.Phd.107d; Id.Cra.420e; Isoc.1.19; Pl.Phd.115a, X.Cyr.8.5.1: metaph., processus ad infinitum, Phld.Mort.19

πορεῖον.definition: means of conveyance, carriage, GDI5043; load, PPetr.2p.128 , etc.; written PTeb.195 , etc

πόρευμα.definition: place in which one walks; means of going, carriage, a fleet, E.IA300

πορεύσιμος.definition: also Them.Or.6.83c:—that may be; Act., able to go or travel, Pl.Epin.981d

πορευτέος.definition: to be traversed, S.Ph.993; neut. one must go, S.Aj.690, E.Heracl.730, Pl.R.452c

πορεύω.definition: fut. E.Hec.447 , etc.: aor; Act., make to go, carry, convey, by land or water, Arion 1.13, Pi.O.1.77, P.11.21, etc.; S.Ph.517 ; . . Id.OC1476; E.Tr.1086 ; . . Id.Hec.447 ; Id.Med.181 ; Th.4.132, etc.: c. dupl.acc., ca…

πόρθησις.definition: sack of a town, D.18.70, Plu.Sull.33, etc

πορθμεία.definition: ferrying across a river, SIG1262.10; conveyance by water, Str.5.3.7

πορθμεῖον.definition: Ion. place for crossing; passage-boat, ferry-boat, Id.7.25, X.HG5.1.23, Antiph.86.4, Luc.DMort.10.1; IG12.890

πόρθμευμα.definition: passage, ferry, of the river Acheron, A.Ag.1558

πορθμεύς.definition: Ion. ferryman, Od.20.187; generally, boatman, seaman, esp. as one of the crew of a passenger-ship, Hdt.1.24, Ar.Ec.1086, Theoc.1.57

πορθμεύω.definition: carry or ferry over a strait, river, etc; Act.intr., pass over, Pl.Ax.371c; AP7.68 ; Epigr.Gr.522.1 ; E.IA6

πόρθμιος.definition: epith. of Poseidon at Carpathos, IG12.1032.34, 1036.12

πορθμίς.definition: = sq., D.P.80,344; = II, ship, boat, E.Hipp.753 , Hel.1061, IT355, etc.; load this boat for yourself alone, Id.Cyc.362; Paus.8.25.13

πορίζω.definition: bring about, furnish, provide, Hom.Epigr.14.10; etc., Ar.Eq.593, Ec.236, Democr.78, IG22.834.14, etc.; Ar.Fr.81; Isoc.12.82; Pl.Phdr.275a: abs., E.Med.879: freq. with a notion of contriving or inventing, Id.Alc.222 , …

πορισμός.definition: providing, procuring, Plb.3.112.2; earning a living, Chrysipp.Stoic.3.172; Phld.Oec.p.44J.; J.BJ2.21.3: abs., Man.4.448 ; money-getting, Plu.2.524d, 92b , 136c , etc.; means of gain, Chaerem. ap. Porph.Abst.4.8; Plu.C…

πορνεύω.definition: prostitute, mostly in Pass., of a woman; intr. in Act., = Pass., LXXDe.23.17,Luc.Alex.5, Phalar.Ep.121, fornicate, 1 Ep.Cor.6.18

πορνίδιον.definition: Dim. of foreg., Ar. , etc. Ar.Nu.997, Men.Pk.150, Com.Adesp.120, but , Ar.Ra.1301.]

πορνοβοσκέω.definition: keep a brothel, Ar.Pax849, Hyp.Ath.3; waste one's substance on harlots, Palaeph.6

πορνοβοσκία.definition: trade of a brothel-keeper, Aeschin.3.214, Stoic.3.36

πορνοβοσκός.definition: brothel-keeper, Myrtil.4, Aeschin.3.246, D.59.30, Arist.EN1121b33: title of plays by Eubulus, Anaxilas, and Posidippus, and mime by Herodas

πορνοκόπος.definition: one who has commerce with prostitutes, fornicator, Men.1057,LXXPr.23.21

πορνοτελώνης.definition: at Athens, farmer of the Philonid.5: nickname for tax-gatherers, Poll.9.29

ποροποιέω.definition: open the pores, Dsc.5.6; provided with pores, S.E.M.8.309

ποροποιία.definition: state of the pores, term in 'Methodic' medicine, Gal.10.268, Cass.Pr.79

πορπακίζομαι.definition: Med., grasp a shield by the handle, bear a shield, Ar.Lys.106

πόρπαμα.definition: garment fastened with a; = IG 22.1126.31 .—E.ll.cc. preferred the Dor. form v.l. in Suid

πορπαφόρος.definition: wearing a brooch, S.Inach. in PTeb.692ii 16

πόρπη.definition: = brooch, clasp for fastening dresses, esp. on the shoulders; used for piercing the eyes, E.Ph.62, Hec.1170: mostly pl., of the fastenings for women's dresses, Il.18.401, h.Ven.163, E.El.318, etc.; worn as emblem of r…

πορφύρα.definition: Ion. purple-fish, Murex; purple dye obtained from it, Sapph.44, Hdt.3.22, Isoc.12.39, Pl.Lg.847c; Phylarch.45 J., etc.; Ael.NA4.36; used as an application, Orib.Eup.3.2

πορφυρανθής.definition: with purple blossom, Thphr.HP6.6.3; = Ps.-Dsc.3.122; = Id.4.62

πορφυρεύς.definition: fisher for purple fish, Hdt.4.151, Arist.Pr.966b25, Ph.1.35, prob.in E.Fr.670

πορφυρεύω.definition: catch purple fish, Philostr.VA1.24:—Med; dye purple, in Pass., Acus.37J

πορφυρίζω.definition: to be purplish, Dsc.3.36, Apollod.Ath. ap. Ath.7.281f; of the sea, Arist.Mir.843a26:—Med., Apollon.Lex.s.v

πορφύριον.definition: Dim. of Arist.HA546b32; purple-dyed stuff, PLond. 3.899.3 , etc

πορφυρίς.definition: purple garment or covering; a purple-coloured bird, Ibyc.4, cf. Ar.Av.304, Call.Fr.100c2

πορφυρίτης.definition: like purple, porphyry, Plin.HN36.57, cj.in D.C.76.15: as Subst., porphyry-quarry, Ostr.951 ; columns of porphyry, IGRom.4.1431.42 : in fem., the porphyry quarry, Aristid.Or.36.67

πορφυροβάφος.definition: dyer of purple, Inscr. Délos400.7 , IGRom.4.816 , Ath.13.604b

πορφυροειδής.definition: purply, A.Supp.529 ; E.Tr.124 , cf. Arist.Col.792a17. Adv. Dsc.1.73

πορφυρόζωνος.definition: with purple girdle, B.10.49, cf. Hsch. s.v

πορφυροπώλης.definition: dealer in purple, IG Rom.4.1071 , Judeich Altertümer von HierapolisNo.156: fem. IGRom. l.c. , Act.Ap.16.14, PFlor.71.641 :—hence , their trade, AB379, Harp. s.v

πορφυροφορία.definition: wearing of purple garments, Jul.Laod.inCat.Cod. Astr.5.189

πόσθη.definition: membrum virile, Id.Nu.1014; foreskin, Dsc.4.153, Ruf.Onom.102, Orib.Fr.84

ποσόω.definition: reckon the quantity of, count; quantify, Plot.6.6.16:—Pass., to be quantified or quantitatively determined, Dam.Pr.54, Eliasin Porph.154.35, Ascl.in Metaph.104.36, Phlp.in de An.543.31

ποσσίκροτος.definition: struck with the foot in dancing; Act., striking with the feet, Orph.H.31.2

ποταμεύς.definition: name of the East wind at Tripolis, Arist.Vent.973a13

ποταμήϊος.definition: Ion. and poet. for Nonn.D.11.309, al

ποταμηπόρος.definition: crossing rivers, Opp.C.2.178; going to the river, ib.4.84

ποτάμιος.definition: also E.El.309, but cf. 56:—of; of cities, on a river, Pi.P.6.6; Str.11.3.2, al

ποταμίτης.definition: water-finder, Lat. aquilex; worker employed by the Nile conservancy, BGU14ii19 , PSI1.83.11 : dat. pl. spelt PMasp.p.53

ποταμοφόρητος.definition: carried away by a river, Apoc.12.15, PMag.Par.1.876, Cyran.39; PStrassb.5.10

ποταμοφυλακία.definition: office of river-guard, CIL2.1970 , prob. in PAmh.2.32.13

ποταμόχωστος.definition: deposited by a river, Ephor.65 J., Str.13.3.4

ποταποφωνέω.definition: Dor. for declare in addition, Chron.Lind.D.45

ποτηροπλύτης.definition: = foreg., PLond.5.1657 , Ostr.1218; gloss on Sch.Luc.Lex.7

ποτιδέρκομαι.definition: Ep. and Dor. for Il.16.10, Od.17.518, Theoc.1.36

ποτίζω.definition: Att. fut. Gp.17.12.3: :—give to; c. dupl. acc., gave them nectar to drink, Pl.Phdr.247e; LXXGe.24.17; Ev.Marc.9.41, cf. 1 Ep.Cor.12.13

ποτιπτήσσω.definition: = , crouch or cower towards, verging towards it, so as to shut it in, Od.13.98

ποτισμός.definition: = foreg., Call. Fr.anon.121, BGU912.20; irrigation, PCair.Zen.268.36 , PAmh.2.91.11 , etc

ποτιστής.definition: one who gives to drink, Aq.Ge.40.5

ποτίστρα.definition: watering-place, drinking-trough; conduit or channel, CPR121.1 , PTeb.374.14 , etc

ποτιψαφίζομαι.definition: Med., Dor. for vote in addition, Mélanges Glotz290

ποτνιάομαι.definition: cry hence generally, cry aloud in; c. acc., implore loudly, Ph.1.391: c. inf., Id.2.227: abs., ib.65, al

ποτοπτάζω.definition: Dor. Verb, = AP6.353 : also prob. in Dius ap.Stob.4.21.17

πραγματᾶς.definition: = agent or official of a religious guild, IPE2.61, al

πραγματεύομαι.definition: to be engaged in business, spend one's time in business, all night long, X.Cyr.2.4.26; Arist.EN1176b29, cf.1122a9; simply, conduct a business, PCair.Zen.199.11 ; transact business, of clerks, ib.647.11 ; make money by…

πραγματευτέος.definition: to be laboured at; one must treat, Id.Top.105b31, cf. 106a2, Ruf.Ren.Ves.13.11

πραγματευτής.definition: business representative, = Lat. actor, Plu.2.525a, PColumb. in JEA18.16 , PMasp.158.17 , etc.; his agent or attorney, CIG4299 , cf. 3104 , IG14.2057, OGI525.3 , PTeb.357.5 , etc

πραγμάτιον.definition: Dim. of trifling matter, petty lawsuit or business, Ar.Nu.197,1004, Arr.Epict.1.27.16, POxy.746.6 , etc

πραγματοδίφης.definition: one who hunts after lawsuits, pettifogger, Ar.Av.1424

πραγματοκοπέω.definition: meddle in business, to be meddlesome, seditious, Plb.29.23.10, 38.13.8, Phld.Rh.2.53S

πραγματολογέω.definition: narrate facts, Arist.Rh.Al.1438b20; quarrel, argue, D.L.9.52

πραγματομαθής.definition: skilled in business, Anon. ap. Suid

πραιδεύω.definition: = Lat. praedor, Petr.Patr. in Boissevain Dio Cassius iii p.746, Hsch. s.v. written PLond.5.1674.91 , etc

πρακτεῖον.definition: post, official position, Princeton Exp.Inscr. A3 No.562

πρακτέος.definition: to be done, Pl.Prt.356c; one must do, S.OT1439, Pl.Prt.356b, etc

πράκτης.definition: = I. Suid. s.v. Ion. treacherous person, Hp.Ep.19

πράκτιμος.definition: liable to a money-penalty, SIG671 A12

πρακτόρειον.definition: office of the II.1; tax-collector's office, Ostr.517

πράκτωρ.definition: = one who does or executes; official who executes a judgment for debt, esp. public debt, bailiff, IG12.75.49, al., Antipho6.49, Decr. ap. And.1.77, D.25.28, IG12.51.9 , OGI 483.7 , Ev.Luc.12.58; PSI4.335.2 ; PTeb.5.222

πρανής.definition: Ion. (also in Arist.Mete.350a11; of parts of animals or man, that part which is uppermost and visible when the animal or man is in the position , the back part, . . Arist.PA658a17, cf. HA498b20, 519a21, 540a2, GA717b30

πρανίζω.definition: Ion. aor. = Euph.18, Nonn.D.4.340, al.:—Pass., capsize, AP7.532 ; Phot., cf. Hsch.: plpf. Nonn.D.30.86

πραξικοπέω.definition: take by surprise or treachery; overreach, outwit, Id.2.46.2, OGI315.7 , cf. Supp.Epigr.4.671

πρασίζω.definition: to be greenish, Dsc.3.80.2, 4.150.5, Ruf. ap. Orib.8.24.64, Gal.6.742

πρασινίζω.definition: = interpol. in Dsc.3.54, cf. Sch.rec.A.Pers.617, DavidProll.163.27

πράσινος.definition: leek-green, light green; the green faction in the Circus, Mart.11.33.1, POxy.145.2 ; J.AJ19.4.4; cf

πρασοκουρίς.definition: a creature which destroys leeks, Stratt.66.1, Arist.HA551b20, Thphr.HP7.5.4

πρατήρ.definition: the stone on which slaves were sold, Poll.3.78

πρατήριον.definition: Ion. place for selling, market, Hdt.7.23, Aen.Tact.10.14, PTeb.701.7 , Plu.2.972d, D.C.59.14

πραΰγελως.definition: Ion. softly- smiling, Licymn.4, AP9.229 ; ib.10.4

πραϋλόγος.definition: gentle in speech, Erinn.2 in PSI9.1090.32

πραϋμενής.definition: of gentle spirit, Hsch., in Adv. in form IG14.2012 A40 ; more freq. in the contr. form

πραΰνοος.definition: Ion. of gentle mind, Orph.H.69.13; AP7.592, etc.; with v.l. ib.9.769

πραΰνω.definition: tame wild animals, Hes.Op.797, X.Mem.2.3.9; Ael.NA10.10:—Pass., ib.4.16; opp. of horses, X.Eq.9.10; Euph.177

πραϋπάθεια.definition: gentleness of temper, Ph.2.31, Hsch.; written 1 Ep.Ti.6.11

πραϋπαθέω.definition: to be gentle in temper, Ph.1.547

πρεῖγυς.definition: Cret., = old man, ib.4992a iii 2; also in Comp., acc. sg. older, Leg.Gort. 12.34, cf. Supp.Epigr.1.414.9 , and Sup. oldest, Leg.Gort.7.23, al.—Cogn. forms are = Supp.Epigr.4.599.13, 17 , GDI 5148.12, 5167.11; = presid…

πρεμνίζω.definition: stub up, root up, Test. ap. D.43.70 , Poll.7.146, Phot

πρεσβεῖον.definition: Ion. and Ep. gift of; privilege of age, Plu.2.787d, cf. D.39.29: hence, generally, privilege: pl., prerogatives, c. inf., give him as a privilege, to . . , Pl.Grg.524a; Arist.EE1242a6: c. gen., chief share or sovereig…

πρέσβειρα.definition: fem. of h.Ven.32; E.IT963; opp. Ar.Lys.86; Com. of a large eel, Id.Ach.883

πρέσβευμα.definition: ambassador, in pl., E.Supp.173, cf. Rh.936; collectively, the embassy, Plu.Tim.9; but, embassies, missions, Id.2.541e

πρεσβεύς.definition: ambassador, acc. sg. Hoffmann Griech. Dialekte ii No. 160.31 ; dat. pl. Lyc.1056, v.l. in Anon.in EN200.14; nom. dual Ar.Fr.639: Sch.Ar. denies that Ar.Ach.93 is gen. of this word: Boeot. pl. IG7.2418.6, 18 , 1720.6

πρέσβευσις.definition: dispatch on an embassy, Th.1.73, D.C.42.46; poet. acc. to D.H.Amm.2.3

πρεσβεύτειρα.definition: prop. fem. of only metaph., of the scent of hounds, Opp.C.1.464

πρεσβευτής.definition: agent or commissioner, D.45.64; = Lat. legatus, staff officer, etc., Plb.35.4.5, Plu.Mar.7, etc.; = legatus pro praetore, IG 14.1121, etc

πρεσβεύω.definition: intr., to be the elder or eldest, S.OC1422; Pl.Lg.951e: c. gen. pers., to be older than, be the eldest of a number, Hdt.7.2; Timae.114; to be his eldest son, Th.6.55; of wine, . . Archestr.Fr.60.2; Ath.1.19a: hence

πρεσβηΐς.definition: = highest or most ancient honour, h.Hom.29.3

πρέσβις.definition: ambassador, Prov. ap. Sch.Il.4.394; alleged as the word of which is gen., Choerob.in Theod.1.233, Sch.Ar. l.c., Suid

πρέσβιστος.definition: poet. Sup. of eldest, most august, most reverend, h.Hom.30.2, A.Th.390, S.Frr.582, 605; Lyr.Alex.Adesp.35.2; Ti.Locr.104b; Sardis7.13: irreg. form Nic.Th.344

πρεσβυγένεια.definition: Ion. seniority of birth, Hdt.6.51, Plu.2.636e

πρευμενής.definition: of events, favourable, . . Id.Ag.1647; . . Id.Supp.140 ; . . E.Hec.540

πρημαίνω.definition: blow hard, Ar.Nu.336: later c. acc., Herod.7.98

πρηστηριάζω.definition: burn up as with lightning, Hdn.Epim.111

πριαμόομαι.definition: Med., to have one's head shaven, because Priam was represented on the stage with a bald head, Com.Adesp.1123

Πριάπειος.definition: Ion. of Priapus, AP6.254 ; Heph.10.4; D.H.Comp.4, Str.8.6.24

Πριαπίζω.definition: Ion. to be lewd, APl.4.237 ; to be ithyphallic, prob. in IG22.1388.62

Πριαπίσκος.definition: Dim. of dilator or; perineal peg, in the Hippocratic bench, Ruf. ap.Orib.49.26.6

πρίνινος.definition: metaph., oaken, i.e. tough, sturdy, Ar.Ach.180; Id.V.877; Luc.Hist.Conscr.8, cf. AP7.37

πρισματοκαύστης.definition: slow burning fire of sawdust, Ps.-Democr. forming such a fire, Zos.Alch.p.143B

προαγγέλλω.definition: declare, announce beforehand, X.Cyr.5.3.12; Plb.3.20.8; X.Cyr.3.3.34:—Pass., Th.7.65; Berl.Sitzb. 1927.170

προάγγελος.definition: announcing beforehand, c. gen; Subst., harbinger, Plu.2.127d

προαγκτηριάζω.definition: tie with a ligature beforehand, Gal.12.521, Aspasia ap. Aët.16.102

προαγνεύω.definition: pf. purify beforehand, J.BJ4.3.12, cf. Arr.Epict.3.21.14

προαγνοέω.definition: to be ignorant of before, PTeb.23.12 , f.l. in Gal.2.231

προάγνυμι.definition: break before or in advance, Od.5.385

προαγορανομέω.definition: to be i.e. aedile, before, D.C.53.33

προαγόρευσις.definition: foretelling, Arist.Po.1454b5; proclamation, App.BC1.26; warning, prohibition, J.AJ18.8.2, 18.9.2, Poll.8.66

προαγορεύω.definition: aor. Hdt.1.74, 125: pf; foretell, prophesy, X.Smp.4.5

προαγρέω.definition: Aeol. for pf. part. Med. having decided, IGRom.4.1302.6
